title: History Says Bills' Josh Allen Will Outperform Chiefs' Patrick Mahomes on Thanksgiving
full_text:
The NFL table has been set for Thanksgiving , and the games this Thursday across the league are about as juicy as it gets.
And, with that in mind, no contest is seemingly more enticing to dive into this holiday than the primetime matchup between the Buffalo Bills and the Kansas City Chiefs at Highmark Stadium.
With the contest slated for 8:20 p.m. ET in Orchard Park, though, fans from both sides will have to wait a little longer for the main course of the festivities.
Undoubtedly, it will be worth the wait as both squads possess the top two records in the AFC entering Week 12 . . . as well as arguably the top two quarterbacks in all of professional football: Josh Allen and Patrick Mahomes.
In 10 total head-to-head meetings since 2020, which includes six games in the regular season and four in the playoffs, the two perennial contenders have split the matchups at five victories apiece.
However, in the end, it’s been Mahomes and the Chiefs who’ve gotten the last laugh in the postseason as they’ve bid Buffalo farewell four times in January since first meeting in the 2020 AFC Championship at Arrowhead Stadium.
Now, with first place in the conference on the line as the calendar inches toward December, the 11th all-time matchup between the two quarterbacks could set up to be the best of the bunch.
But, who has the upper hand statistically entering the highly-anticipated game ?
Historically, it’s been Allen who’s performed the better of the two in each matchup as he’s outshined Mahomes in just about every important category imaginable since their first meeting six years ago.
For his career against Kansas City per StatMuse , Buffalo’s former 2024 MVP gunslinger has completed 232 of 359 passes for 2,573 yards, 20 touchdowns, and just four interceptions through the air while also adding 100 carries for 506 yards and seven touchdowns on the ground throughout the years.
On average, it equates to a stat line each game of 307.9 total yards, 2.7 total touchdowns, and just 0.5 turnovers ( 4 INTs, 1 fumble lost ) from Allen, which is quite impressive.
For comparison—in those same 10 games with Buffalo—Mahomes has completed 239 of his 361 passing attempts for 2,715 yards, 19 touchdowns, and eight interceptions in addition to adding 53 carries for 267 rushing yards and three touchdowns on the ground, which equals a single-game average of 298.2 total yards, 2.2 touchdowns, and 1.0 turnovers per matchup ( 8 INTs, 2 fumbles lost ).
So, while it’s been close, Allen clearly has the edge on Kansas City’s superstar quarterback when it comes to overall head-to-head record in the regular season and in overall stats. But, will that continue on Thursday night when fans across the nation are settling in to watch the game unfold after their Thanksgiving meal?
Entering the matchup, it appears that Mahomes actually might have the hotter hand . Currently, he’s rattled off four consecutive games with at least two passing touchdowns and no interceptions, pushing his stat line for the month of November to 102-of-146 passing ( 69.9% comp. ) for 1,235 yards and 13 touchdowns through the air. He’s also added 29 rushing yards on just six carries.
Contrastly, despite helping keep Buffalo afloat on top of the NFL standings this month, Allen has had a bit of a rough stretch over the last few weeks with a stat line that reads as follows: 80-of-131 passing ( 61.1% comp. ) for 1,023 yards, five touchdowns, and five interceptions; 18 carries for 50 yards and three touchdowns.
Needless to say, it’s very apparent that Mahomes is outplaying Allen this month, but who knows?
The 6-foot-5, 237-pound playmaker usually has a few tricks up his sleeve any time that he goes up against the Chiefs . . . and Thursday’s critical AFC matchup could provide some similar fireworks in primetime.

title: Everything Buffalo Bills Have to Fear About Kansas City Chiefs in Week 12
full_text:
In what will be arguably the biggest matchup of the entire Week 12 slate, the Buffalo Bills and Kansas City Chiefs will cap off Thanksgiving with a showdown on Thursday night.
This is a massively important game for both teams, as not only is this a measuring stick game for the Chiefs and Bills, but the Chiefs could walk out of Highmark Stadium as the No. 1 seed entering Week 13 if they beat Buffalo and the Denver Broncos lose.
Both teams have a head of steam going into this contest, with the Bills riding a six-game winning streak and the Chiefs having won three in a row.
Now, three things the Bills have to fear the most about the Chiefs ahead of Thursday's crucial matchup.
No quarterback in the NFL is playing better football than Patrick Mahomes, who has been on a legendary heater the last four weeks.
In that span, Mahomes has completed 69.8% of his passes for 1,235 yards and 13 touchdowns to no picks. The addition of Josh Downs at the trade deadline has no doubt helped Mahomes, but Travis Kelce and Rashee Rice have been playing pretty good football, also.
It's fair to point out that those showings have come against the likes of the Denver Broncos, New York Jets, Atlanta Falcons and Arizona Cardinals, but it's not like the Bills have some vaunted defense.
In fact, Buffalo sported the worst pass defense in the NFL before its recent four-game stretch that has seen improved play on defense, although those showings have also been against quarterbacks who couldn't shine Mahomes' shoes .
We're going to find out just how legitimate the Bills' defense is when Mahomes comes to town on Thursday night, assuming weather doesn't completely wreck the game , which it might.
Kenneth Walker has looked like an MVP candidate this season as he puts together the best campaign of his career. In eight games, Walker has 872 rushing yards, 172 receiving yards and 11 total touchdowns.
To put into context just how good those numbers are for Walker, the Chiefs running back needs 155 rushing yards, 127 receiving yards and 265 scrimmage yards to top his career-high marks.
He has already surpassed his personal best in total and receiving touchdowns and needs three more on the ground to surpass that career-high mark.
All that said, Walker is not guaranteed to play in Week 12 because of a groin injury that has kept him out the last two games. But, that isn't as big a problem as it would be for most teams because the Chiefs have an electric rookie behind him in Emmett Johnson.
In Walker's stead, Johnson has ripped off two consecutive 100-yard showings, and he has 108 yards through the air and three total touchdowns in that span.
Whether it's Walker, Johnson, or both, the Chiefs' rushing attack is going to give the Bills' top-10 run defense all it can handle.
The Chiefs' defense is going to present a stiff challenge for the Bills' offense.
Kansas City ranks top 10 in all major categories, including total yards (No. 5), passing yards (No. 7), rushing yards (No. 9) and points (No. 2) allowed per game.
What makes the Chiefs' success against the pass a bit surprising is they haven't been all that good at getting after the quarterback, with Kansas City ranking tied for 25th in sacks and 22nd in pressures.
That's a testament to how well Chiefs cornerbacks like Mansoor Delane and Nohl Williams, among others, have played in 2026.
But that doesn't mean there's nobody to fear along the Chiefs' line, as both George Karlaftis (eight sacks) and Chris Jones (3.5 sacks) are fully capable of wrecking a game.
We also know that defensive coordinator Steve Spagnuolo isn't afraid to bring the blitz, which can help generate more pressure against Josh Allen.

title: Bills Get Positive Injury News Across Board for Thanksgiving Night Game vs. Chiefs
full_text:
The Buffalo Bills have 14 players officially dealing with some sort of injury, but it's seemingly more and more feasible that the entire group is available for Thanksgiving night despite the short week.
Continuing preparations to host the Kansas City Chiefs only four days after disposing of the Miami Dolphins, the Bills held a walkthrough practice on Tuesday. All 14 injured players participated in some capacity.
"I know it's walkthrough today, but everybody will be out there today. We'll kind of just continue to evaluate it through Thursday. Obviously, not practicing today, but everybody seems like they're in as good of a place as we can be right now," said Bills' head coach Joe Brady on Tuesday afternoon in Orchard Park.
That news is nothing less than encouraging for the three Week 12 additions to the injury report coming out of the November 22 win over Miami.
Right tackle Spencer Brown, right guard O'Cyrus Torrence and outside linebacker Greg Rousseau, all starters, popped up on Monday's injury report. While the Bills did not practice on Monday, all three earned limited designations with practice status estimations required by the NFL.
Rousseau totaled 34 snaps, matching Bradley Chubb for most amongst players in the Bills' front seven, against the Jets on Sunday. He made 2.0 sacks, earning a game ball from Brady afterwards.
Listed with a back injury, Rousseau did not appear in any abnormal discomfort while addressing reporters in the locker room . He also entertained a media scrum following Tuesday's walkthrough.
Tuesday marks a positive step forward for starting cornerback Christian Benford, who was forced out during the second half against the New York Jets on November 15.
Having injured his groin, Benford did not practice at all leading up to the November 22 home game. The Bills ruled him out on Friday .
On Tuesday, he finally returned to the practice field. Benford and the Bills have said they're taking a day-by-day approach, but it may be overly optimistic to think the cornerback can fully recover from a groin issue in 11 days.
Brown has a history of back problem that dating back to his rookie season. He left early due to a flare-up on October 12 against the Los Angeles Rams.
Returning to play a full game against the Las Vegas Raiders on October 18, Brown did not respond well during the Week 7 bye. He sat out the November 1 win over the Baltimore Ravens.
With the back seemingly an issue that Brown will have to manage moving forward, his presence on the injury report is likely due to the fact he's seeking treatment. Brown addressed reporters from the podium on Tuesday, and he did not give any reason to think he would not be available this week.
Torrence popped up with an ankle injury one day after playing 99 percent of offensive snaps in Week 11. The rock-solid hog molly will be available to face the Chiefs if history is any indication. He has not missed a start since being drafted in 2023.
Kincaid missed a game for the first time this season, sitting out the November 22 home win due to a thumb injury. He was a non-participant throughout the practice week and carried a doubtful designation into game day .
When asked if Kincaid was close to being available to face the Dolphins, Brady said "yeah" at the conclusion of his postgame press conference.
In a positive development, Kincaid returned to practice this week albeit in a limited capacity. Furthermore, the tight end  reportedly mentioned that he thinks he'll be ready to play Thursday night (h/t WGRZ's Jon Scott ).
The injury occurred midway through the third quarter against the Jets on November 15 when Kincaid got tangled up with linebacker Demario Davis on a red zone play.

title: Bills Must Address QB Deficit After Colts Poach Trusted Josh Allen Understudy
full_text:
The Buffalo Bills need a new emergency quarterback for the season's stretch run.
Committing only two 53-man roster spots to quarterbacks, the Bills have stashed third-stringer Shane Buechele on their practice squad for the past few years.
On Tuesday, however, the Indianapolis Colts signed Buechele off the Bills' practice squad and onto their active roster. The Colts were down to two quarterbacks in their building after releasing veteran starter Daniel Jones last week.
The 28-year-old Buechele becomes the third signal caller on Indianapolis's 53-man roster, joining Anthony Richardson and Riley Leonard.
Meanwhile, the Bills will roll into their Thanksgiving game with quarterback Josh Allen as the starter and Kyle Allen as the lone reserve.
In terms of adding another quarterback, Buffalo will have to scan the free-agent market presuming the front office is unwilling to dedicate a 53-man roster spot to the position. The only way one can claim a player off another team's practice squad is by guaranteeing the player an active roster spot.
Buechele, who initially entered the NFL as an undrafted rookie with the Kansas City Chiefs in 2021, was is his fourth season as the Bills' third quarterback.
It's known that Buechele has developed a friendship with Allen over the years in addition to their working relationship in a close-knit quarterbacks room.
"It's a room that we've all been in together. We're obviously very good friends. We do a lot of hanging out outside the facility," said Allen this past summer.
Buechele and Kyle Allen battled valiantly for second-string duties throughout training camp with the latter squeaking by .
"I think that they both bring a ton of value, not only on the field, but what they bring to the meeting room, their relationship with Josh, their ability to communicate with him, and kind of from their vision to what they see," said offensive coordinator Pete Carmichael.
Over three preseason appearances this past summer, Buechele went 37-of-57 passing (64.9) for 357 yards and one touchdowns. He also ran for 15 yards and one touchdown.
Buffalo made Buechele a practice squad elevation for the Week 10 road contest against the New York Jets. Despite being scratched prior to kickoff, the call-up allowed him to earn a game check.
Late last season, the Chiefs, who were without starter Patrick Mahomes at the time, snatched Buechele off the Bills' practice squad for their Week 18 finale.
Making his NFL debut, Buechele split QB duties with Chris Oladokun for the Chiefs' regular season finale against the Las Vegas Raiders on January 4, 2026. He went 7-of-14 passing for 88 yards and added one four-yard rush.
The Chiefs cut Buechele loose following the Week 18 loss, and the Bills subsequently signed him back to the practice squad for their postseason run.

title: 3 Reasons the Panthers Won’t Be Embarrassed by Buccaneers Again
full_text:
The Carolina Panthers have their biggest game of the season on Monday. A primetime, divisional showdown on the road against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers .
This is the Panthers' final primetime game, completing the trifecta of playing on Thursday, Sunday, and now Monday Night Football on ESPN. Entering Week 12 at 5-5, the Panthers have a two-game lead atop the NFC South, with both Tampa Bay and the New Orleans Saints losing on Sunday.
Tampa Bay is widely regarded as the next-best team in the division, which isn't saying much. That said, being swept by the Buccaneers is a nightmare scenario for the Panthers and needs to be avoided at all costs.
Carolina has found life as of late, winning two straight and moving to 5-5 on the season. Now that momentum has to continue, and theres plenty of reason to believe it can continue against the Buccaneers on Monday. Here are three reasons why Carolina will remain competitive against Tampa Bay on the road.
Against the Ravens, Young was elite under pressure , completing 10-of-15 passes for 173 yards and 2 touchdowns. His passing yards under pressure are a career high for Young, and he'll need to maintain that type of accuracy against the Buccaneers.
Tampa Bay ranks No. 7 in the NFL in pass-rush win rate; they will be pressured early and often. Carolina will be better prepared after what should've been a wake-up call in Week 7.
The run defense isn't fixed, but in two of interim defensive coordinator Todd Wash's three games at the helm, it's been better.
Against the Denver Broncos and New Orleans Saints, Carolina allowed just 126 rushing yards total and gave up 2.6 yards per carry. It's just a two-game sample size, but that's a massive improvement and suggests the change in defensive coordinator has been the right move so far.
The most embarrassing part of Carolina's Week 7 loss to the Buccaneers was that the Panthers allowed 43 points, with Baker Mayfield completing just 7 passes for 64 yards and 1 touchdown.
It seems highly unlikely that Carolina is that inept at run defense again. That said, there will be crucial moments when Baker Mayfield has to beat Carolina with his arm, and so far this season, the Tampa Bay pass offense has been putrid.
The Buccaneers are the NFL's 32nd-ranked pass offense, which is dead last. Carolina recently got reinforcements back in the secondary, with Will Lee III and Mike Jackson back in the lineup. Those additions will be key to limiting a struggling passing game.

title: Dave Canales’ Jonathon Brooks Admission Raises Questions on Draft Pick and Future
full_text:
The Carolina Panthers are anticipating getting Jonathon Brooks back soon. The oft-injured running back had surgery earlier this season, and the Panthers opened the return window on November 11. They had three weeks from then to actually activate him.
In the past, that would have been considered a big boost. When Brooks finally got healthy enough to make his NFL debut in 2024, there was plenty of excitement. Then, when he was ready to go in Week 1 of this season, the hype was massive.
This time, though, Dave Canales had a strange admission about Brooks' role on this team and it raises plenty of questions.
Lost in the shuffle of a pretty exciting and crucial win on Sunday was the fact that Trevor Etienne had a really solid day as the backup running back. He had only a few touches, but he did well with them.
He's also been pretty great, excluding a bad choice to let the first punt of the game roll, on special teams all season. He and Tre Tyus, another running back, have been really good on returns this year.
That, according to Dave Canales, makes it very difficult to find a place for a healthy Jonathon Brooks. He has to be activated in about a week, but the Panthers don't seem to have a spot for him.
Dave Canales: Trevor Etienne’s production and Tre Tyus’s special teams value making it challenging to find a spot for Jonathon Brooks, whose return-from-IR window is open for another 8 days. pic.twitter.com/1qfOg7nXA8
Brooks is a talented player, but he doesn't fill a need right now. Etienne is both a return man and a receiving back out of the backfield. It would seem that, for now, Brooks lost his spot to Etienne.
This raises all sorts of questions. The simple fact that the head coach is wary about where to put him speaks volumes about his high draft selection and his future with the team. Brooks' contract ends after next season. Is there any world he gets extended?
Dan Morgan has generally drafted pretty well during his tenure, but he got off to an abysmal start. Just look at the 2024 draft class:
Is it crazy to say that Smith-Wade is the best player there? Legette is healthy but running zero routes. Brooks can't stay healthy and lost his position to a fourth-round running back. Sanders has been healthy scratched every week but one.
Brooks was arguably the high-profile addition. The ACL injury dropped him to the second round, but he was a first-round pick before that. The Panthers seemed to think they got a steal, but he has not been on the field much and hasn't made an impact.
It's troubling for a player the Panthers invested so much in, to say the least.

title: Baker Mayfield's New Contract Could Create a Major Offseason Dilemma for Panthers
full_text:
The Tampa Bay Buccaneers are in the NFC South division with the Carolina Panthers. The Bucs just signed quarterback Baker Mayfield to a three-year, $165 million contract.
The Buccaneers signed Mayfield to the extension on Tuesday, Sept. 8, averaging $55 million per year.
The Panthers are still considering their options with Young. He has played better than expected this season and has put himself in a good position to negotiate a contract with the team.
Mayfield's contract could serve as a comparison for future contract negotiations between the Panthers and Bryce Young.
Young completed 22 of 30 passes for 254 yards and two touchdowns in Sunday’s 35-33 win over the Baltimore Ravens. Young has thrown for 2,651 yards and 18 touchdowns with seven interceptions in 10 games this season.
Bryce Young, the fourth-year quarterback for the Carolina Panthers, had another great game Sunday. There are still many areas in which Young can improve, but the Panthers have seen enough to pick up the fifth-year option on his contract for the 2027 season.
The average annual value of Baker Mayfield’s new contract is $55 million. As long as Young continues to develop as Carolina believes he can, the Panthers could be looking at a similar commitment in the future.
The Panthers have some time to decide on an extension for the fourth-year quarterback, as they exercised his fifth-year option for the 2027 season earlier this year.
The Panthers don’t have to rush into signing Young to a long-term contract extension. He could become even more valuable to the team as the market for quarterbacks increases over time.
Young has shown improvement in several areas since late last season, and the Panthers believe he can be the franchise quarterback for several years to come. In addition, the price for a franchise quarterback could increase as the Panthers compete in the NFC South.
But I’m not saying that Young should make $55 million a year. All I’m saying is that Baker Mayfield’s contract with the Buccaneers can be used as a comparison in future contract negotiations with the Panthers.
After making so many investments to try to find a franchise quarterback, the Panthers must wait and see if Young can develop into that player and then make the right decision about his contract.

title: Panthers Catch Major Break After Jalen Coker Injury Scare Against Ravens
full_text:
The Carolina Panthers received some encouraging injury news on Monday f ollowing their 35-33 win over the Baltimore Ravens on Sunday. Wide receiver Jalen Coker was hit hard in the fourth quarter and was taken to the medical tent to be evaluated for a concussion.
Coach Dave Canales provided more good news on Monday, revealing that Coker had been cleared through concussion protocol. He will be available for the Panthers’ Week 12 matchup against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers on Monday night.
Dave Canales: Jalen Coker has been cleared, so he's not in the concussion protocol entering Week 12.
Coker was taken to the locker room for evaluation after getting hit by linebacker Roquan Smith late in the fourth quarter. He had just caught a 6-yard pass on Carolina’s go-ahead drive.
The Panthers were able to hold on to the lead and seal the win, but losing Coker for an extended period of time would create more issues for an offense that has struggled to be consistent in the passing game.
Coker had some big plays prior to his injury, including a 35-yard reception in the first quarter that set up Mitchell Evans’ touchdown on the next play. He finished the game with 4 catches for 47 yards.
The third-year wide receiver has been a steady contributor for the Panthers this season, catching 35 passes for 440 yards and 3 touchdowns in 11 games. Only rookie Tetairoa McMillan has more receptions than Coker for the Panthers this season.
This is great news for the Panthers, who are set to play the Tampa Bay Buccaneers in Tampa on Monday night. This is also a divisional game, which the Panthers can use to increase their lead in the NFC South division as they look to secure a playoff spot in the latter part of the season.
The Panthers are currently two games ahead of the Buccaneers in the NFC South division standings. They can add to that lead in Week 12 when they play Tampa Bay on Monday night.
With Coker back in the fold, Carolina’s offense will have another weapon at its disposal and Young another quality target to throw to. The Panthers will look to build off of their impressive win against the Ravens on Sunday in order to carry that momentum into their next game against the Buccaneers on Monday night.
The Panthers are trying to maintain as many offensive players as possible for the remainder of the season, and keeping the wide receiver healthy is great news for Carolina.

title: NFL Week 12 Odds Paint Picture of Panthers’ Revenge Chances vs. Buccaneers
full_text:
The Carolina Panthers got embarrassed by the Tampa Bay Buccaneers last time the two teams faced off. Carolina got run all over to the tune of over 250 yards. Baker Mayfield attempted 11 passes in a 30-point win in Carolina .
This week, the Panthers have a chance for revenge. They'll head to Tampa Bay on Monday night to try and maintain their two-game NFC South lead and exorcise some of the demons that have haunted them against the Bucs.
A 5-5 team versus a 3-7 team would lead you to believe that the 5-5 team would be favored, but they are not. The Panthers are underdogs this week against the Buccaneers.
The fact that Carolina's going on the road doesn't help, nor does the fact that the Buccaneers dominated them a few weeks ago. Per DraftKings , the Buccaneers are -153 on the moneyline. The Panthers are +129 to win outright.
The spread currently sits at three points. The Bucs are -102 to cover, while the Panthers are -117 to cover. The total is set at 43.5, and the over is -110. The under is -109. These two teams combined for 56 points last time.
That means that oddsmakers believe that the Buccaneers will beat the Panthers 23-21, roughly.
Now, there's also reason to believe this matchup will be different. Ejiro Evero is gone, and the run defense has been significantly better since his firing. It's hard to envision Bucky Irving running quite as wild.
Plus, the Buccaneers' rushing attack focused on two key areas of weakness in that particular matchup. They wanted to attack the edges and get up against cornerbacks because the Panthers were missing Jaelan Phillips, Jaycee Horn, and Mike Jackson.
Phillips and Jackson are back. Horn could be, although it's a real long shot. Will Lee is playing a lot better now. So, those two areas can't be exploited that badly, which could force Baker Mayfield to throw a lot more than he did last time.
And Mayfield has not been putting out good QB play recently. Truly, he hasn't put any out at all this season. His last three outings since that contest:
He has two touchdowns and two interceptions in those games. He's lost a fumble and been sacked nine times in those three games. It has been ugly, so if the Buccaneers can't run all over the place, things get dicey for them.

title: Bryce Young Thrived Under Pressure, a Good Sign for Panthers Next Week
full_text:
It was a wild game, but the Carolina Panthers came out on top, taking a two-game lead at the top of the NFC South. Carolina's Week 11 win over the Baltimore Ravens saw Carolina's offense get back into rhythm, leaning on Chuba Hubbard in the run game and pushing the ball downfield to Tetairoa McMillan, Darren Waller, and others.
Bryce Young had moments he'd want to take back, such as the first-quarter safety and the third-quarter interception in the endzone, which led to Baltimore taking the lead in the fourth quarter. However, outside of those two mistakes, Young was outstanding , completing 73% of his passes and throwing two touchdowns.
What was most impressive about Young's performance was his poise in the pocket, and his ability to operate under pressure, of which there was plenty.
Young completed 22-30 passes for 254 yards. According to Next Gen Stats, 173 of those passing yards were under pressure, a career high for Young. Furthermore, both touchdown passes came under pressure as well; that's elite production under those circumstances, with the offensive line being as bad as it's been throughout the season.
Bryce Young threw for a career-high 173 yards under pressure against the Ravens, completing 10 of 15 passes with 2 TDs and an INT. Young led his 14th career game-winning drive, tied for the most by a QB age 25 or younger since at least 1950. @BALvsCAR | #KeepPounding pic.twitter.com/X9HkXey0P8
As far as pressure goes, it's not going to get any easier for Young, as Carolina is back on the road this week, facing the division rival Tampa Bay Buccaneers.
The Buccaneers are No. 7 in the NFL in pass rush win rate. In Week 7 against the Panthers, the Bucs posted 17 pressures and five sacks. It was Carolina's worst offensive line performance of the season, which is saying something considering how bad it's been all season.
With Young handling pressure better than at any point in his career, he'll need to continue that against Tampa Bay. Carolina cannot afford another game like Week 7, when Young was essentially fighting for his life the entire game and had no room to operate.
Carolina's season could be in the balance on Monday Night Football. The Panthers lead atop the division by two games after Week 11, but falling to 0-2 against Tampa Bay would be disastrous. With how close this NFC South race is trending towards being, Carolina needs as much breathing room as possible, and being swept by the next best team in the division would be disastrous.
Carolina had to bank on the Falcons beating the Saints to win the division in 2025. If the Panthers don't want their fate decided by tiebreakers this season, then a win on Monday Night Football is desperately needed.

title: Examining Panthers’ Playoff Chances After Taking 2-Game Lead in NFC South
full_text:
The Carolina Panthers created some separation on Sunday, beating the Baltimore Ravens 35-33 in a wild back-and-forth game. The game featured seven lead changes, muffed punts, turnovers on both sides, and yet both offenses were awesome.
Stepping away from the game itself, this was the Panthers' biggest win of the season. That may sound weird, considering they beat the 4-6 Baltimore Ravens with no Lamar Jackson, but the division is firmly Carolina's at present.
With the win, Carolina takes a two-game lead at first place in the NFC South . The Panthers were the only team to win on Sunday; the Saints lost to the Chicago Bears, and the Buccaneers lost to the Detroit Lions.
It's a perfect weekend for the Panthers, and before the game, head coach Dave Canales emphasized the importance of a Week 11 win was.
"I wanted the guys to be comfortable in this position so they could say, 'Hey, when you have a chance to start to create some distance, how do we respond to that?' And, uh, just to create that, you know, little added pressure."
Now that Carolina has come through and responded as Canales wanted, their playoff outlook has completely changed.
The Athletic updates its NFL playoff simulator as the season progresses. After Week 11, the Panthers now have a 40% chance of securing the No. 4 seed and hosting a wild-card game, as they did last season. Right below the Panthers are the Buccaneers and Falcons, sitting at 28% and 10%
Furthermore, the No. 3 seed is still in play. The playoff simulator has Carolina sitting at 13% for the No. 3 seed, second behind the New York Giants at 56%, and deservingly so because the Giants are in almost as bad a division as Carolina and picked up a huge win against the Jacksonville Jaguars.
None of this means the Panthers are objectively good; they're not right now. Carolina is inconsistent and has a horrible defense. That said, the rest of the NFC South is just as inconsistent, and has just as bad of flaws as Carolina's defense.
Carolina faces the Tampa Bay Buccaneers on the road this week; it's the season's most important game of the season and could create an even bigger lead in the NFC South title race. Carolina got walloped by the Buccaneers in Week 7, losing 43-13, with Baker Mayfield completing 7 passes for 64 yards.
Monday night's game against Tampa will potentially be what gets Carolina into the playoffs or not.

title: Panthers' Surprising Xavier Legette Decision Raises Major Questions
full_text:
Carolina's wide receiver Xavier Legette was expected to play a big part in the Panthers' passing game this season, but things haven't panned out that way for the former first-round pick, even after he returned from a knee injury that forced him to miss six games.
Despite returning from injury a few weeks ago, Legette has found himself on the outside looking in when it comes to Carolina's passing game.
On Sunday against the Ravens , Legette was on the field for nine special teams plays, but none on offense. According to Next Gen Stats, Legette didn't run any routes against Baltimore.
As a first-round pick in the 2024 NFL Draft, Legette was expected to play a major role in the Panthers' passing game this season.
His first game back against New Orleans was less than stellar, as he was on the field for just two offensive snaps and wasn't targeted. Through two games since returning from injury, Legette has not had a single pass thrown in his direction.
This scenario is even more peculiar because the Panthers have previously said they want to get more out of the young receiver.
After the Saints game, Canales said that getting back on the field after missing six games was an adjustment for Legette. He added that he wanted to see more from the young receiver.
"I want to see Xavier out there more," Canales said , according to the team's official website.
In contrast, when asked about Legette's role following Sunday's game, Canales' comments were somewhat different.
"Xavier's just continuing to battle to show us how he can help the team, and was able to get out there on some coverage units," Canales said Monday.
The situation for Legette is even more complex, however, as John Metchie III and Brycen Tremayne have had opportunities to establish themselves on offense while Legette was recovering from his injury. Metchie, in particular, has benefited from building chemistry with Bryce Young during Legette's absence.
Even though Carolina is winning games right now and the receiving rotation is becoming more consistent, it is still worth noting the lack of playing time for a former first-round pick who was expected to be a key part of Carolina's receiving game this season.
Legette has only caught two passes for 64 yards this season, with his best play coming on a 55-yard reception against Atlanta before his injury.
The Panthers are winning, and their receivers are starting to get on a roll. But Carolina still has to decide if there is an offensive future for Xavier Legette.
His lack of involvement is quickly becoming one of the most interesting aspects of the Panthers' offense.

title: Bryce Young's Latest Performance Could Force Panthers Into Major Contract Decision
full_text:
Bryce Young gave the Carolina Panthers another reason to feel good about their investment in him after leading the team to a dramatic win over the Baltimore Ravens in Week 11. With the quarterback continuing to show growth, the question surrounding his future in Carolina is becoming increasingly interesting.
Young went 22 of 30 for 254 yards and two touchdowns on Sunday as the Panthers beat the Baltimore Ravens 35-33. He also helped the team with a 12-play, 55-yard drive that ended with a game-winning 37-yard field goal from Ryan Fitzgerald with 1:44 remaining.
His play on Sunday was another step in Young’s development as the Panthers’ long-term quarterback. However, the Panthers have yet to make a decision on whether to extend the contract of the quarterback.
For now, the Panthers have already taken one step to keep Young in Carolina. In April, the Panthers exercised the fifth-year option on Young’s rookie contract , which means he is under contract with the team through the 2027 season.
The Panthers can wait and see how Young progresses before offering him a big contract in the future. His salary in the 2027 season would be $25.9 million, giving the Panthers plenty of security at the position while they continue to look at Young’s future.
In August, executive vice president of football operations Brandt Tilis said that contract talks would be internal and that he was “very pleased” with the progress that Young was making.
That leaves the Panthers with some flexibility. They can pursue an extension before Young reaches the end of his current deal, but there is no immediate need to rush into negotiations.
The Panthers are in a good spot with Young’s contract for now and can wait until the time is right to offer him an extension.
On Sunday, Young led the Panthers to another close victory as he delivered in the clutch for Carolina. He now has 14 career game-winning drives, tied for the second-most in the NFL since he entered the league in 2023. The Panthers will have to take that into account when considering his long-term future with the team.
It is only one game, however. Carolina will look for the same level of performance from Young in the coming weeks as he continues to develop.
The Panthers have Young under contract through the 2027 season, so there is no rush to negotiate a new deal. If he continues to play at a high level and lead the team to victory, however, an extension will likely be on the table.

title: Panthers Make Surprising Move in Latest Super Bowl Rankings After Ravens Win
full_text:
The Carolina Panthers are getting more recognition as the NFL heads into the final stretch of the season and towards the playoffs. The Panthers’ latest win was another step in the right direction for the team.
Carolina’s Super Bowl-odds power rankings position rose two spots to No. 15 on Sunday after the Panthers’ 35-33 win over the Baltimore Ravens , according to Sports Illustrated.
While the Panthers are still a long shot to win the Super Bowl this season, Carolina is currently listed at +7,400 to win the Super Bowl.
The Panthers are still a long shot to win the Super Bowl, but the recent success of the team is certainly making them more recognizable. This is another small step for the Panthers toward being recognized for their play on the field.
The Panthers fought back from an early deficit to claim a victory on Sunday.
Carolina fell behind 12-0 in the first quarter but responded with a strong second quarter from Bryce Young and the offense . Chuba Hubbard had a big day on the ground with 120 yards and two touchdowns on 15 carries. Young threw for 254 yards and two touchdowns on 22 of 30 passing.
The lead changed hands seven times during the game. Ryan Fitzgerald connected on a 37-yard field goal with 1:44 remaining in the game to give Carolina the lead. The Carolina defense sealed the win with an interception on the Ravens’ final possession.
This is the second consecutive game that the Panthers have come away with a win in the final minutes of a game that was not played at its highest level.
With the win, the Panthers move to 5-5 on the season and take a t wo-game lead over the rest of the NFC South . Tampa Bay, Atlanta, and New Orleans all lost in Week 11.
The Panthers still have plenty of work to do in order to become serious Super Bowl contenders.
At +7,400, they still are a long shot to win the championship this season. To become a serious threat to win the Super Bowl, the Panthers must continue to play well in the remaining games of the regular season and be able to compete with the best teams in the league.
With 7 games left in the regular season, the Panthers have a chance to build upon their current lead in the NFC South and try to make the playoffs.
Carolina’s next game will be against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers, a team that the Panthers can further pull away from in the NFC South.

title: Chicago Bears and Detroit Lions: Who Wins and Why for Week 12
full_text:
When the season began, Ben Johnson and Bear players on offense talked about league setting scoring and yardage records. Their 59-point opener emboldened everyone.
Now they reach a critical juncture in their schedule tied for first place and have fortified their defense with a defensive player of the year level monstrosity, Jeffery Simmons. Yet, the offense is sputtering badly for one main reason and it's at a very basic level.
They're having trouble running the football.
"We're going to continue to stress that running game," Johnson said. "We've got too many good players for it to be lagging behind like it is right now. We've got to continue to sink into that. It's a big part of what we do and who we are."
The last time Ben Johnson took the field in Detroit… I suppose he should expect another warm welcome on Thursday pic.twitter.com/RuHL6QywsN
The can look at individual backs. D'Andre Swift has had some fumble issues and Kyle Monangai returned from a five-week injury absence without making an impact. The simple truth is it isn't getting opened the way it did last year or earlier this year, and it's on their line to provide the running room.
Noon kickoff: Bears at Lions on Thanksgiving on CBS
A year ago the Bears led the NFL at 3.1 yards before contact for rushing attempts. This year, they're 13th at 2.5. They had a change at center to Garrett Bradbury. Theo Benedet took over at left tackle after Braxton Jones' injury three games in, and with Ozzy Trapilo not ready yet after his knee surgery they've had to cope with more change. Now tight end Cole Kmet is done for the year and he's their biggest blocking presence in the attack at his position.
The Bears traded two first round picks for Jeffery Simmons, and he's already showing why he's worth it. 52 TKL, 12 TFL, 9 SACK, 14 QBH, 6 PD, 1 FF in 10 games. Simmons is now the second favorite to win DPOY behind Will Anderson Jr. https://t.co/sWxKELz7Xr pic.twitter.com/aefGhdhrGD
Then there are the backs. It's hard being a power back when your foot is an issue like it is for Kyle Monangai. D'Andre Swift's problems haven't been specified beyond Johnson's comment: “He just needs to hold on to the ball and we'll be fine.”
Without the running game as a basis, there are no scoring or yardage records and it's not going to be easy to keep up with a high-powered offense like Detroit has. Simmons is going to need to be even more impactful if the defense is going to need to carry the Bears to Johnson's first win over his old team.
It's the Bears and Lions in an NFC North first-place showdown at Ford Field at noon on Thanksgiving, here's who wins and why.
Bears beat Detroit tomorrow: 97% playoff chance and sole 1st in the NFC North Bears lose to Detroit: 82% playoff chance and 0-3 in the division pic.twitter.com/AJDqYH7dtL
Defensive tackle Alim McNeill is making the run very tough for Detroit opponents as only the Bills ran for more than 127 yards on them and seven of the Lions' 10 opponents failed to gain more than 91 rushing yards. The Bears have run into seven top 10 rushing defenses and it's slowed them down, but the Detroit defense they face this week is without both Aidan Hutchinson and Jack Campbell, and both were critical in stopping the run, as well. No Edge
The Detroit Lions defense is held together with tape and glue right now, making the Bears a solid pick tomorrow pic.twitter.com/Togu5dvAqq
Caleb Williams is coming off two down games following a surge after his hamstring injury. He has had good success against Detroit, with a 96.8 passer rating, nine TDs, just two interceptions, and 252.2 yards per game. But he's 0-4 as a starter against Detroit. The Lions' secondary is getting back to full health with safety Joseph Kerby back but without Hutchinson applying pressure that might not be enough. The Lions are 27th in pass defense and have given up more TD passes than all but one other team despite their recent surge on that side of the ball. Williams' scrambling is part of their passing game even if it counts for rushing yards and can be an edge against a defense playing as much man-to-man coverage as Detroit does. Edge to Bears
Lions offense vs. Bears defense: Detroit ranks 5th in EPA per dropback, and the Bears defense ranks 7th in EPA per play allowed (Weeks 1–11) #DaBears pic.twitter.com/SR6kGZFOxT
Jahmyr Gibbs leads the NFL in rushing and is a back who can be stopped five or six times in succession but suddenly breaks off a big play. It's difficult to keep him down all game, and the Bears' run defense has had occasional problems leaking all year despite being seventh overall in rushing yards allowed. They are 25th in yards allowed per carry because of the big plays they give up. One Gibbs big run can switch momentum and turn a game. Edge to Lions
The @NFL has released their game picks for Bears vs Lions on Thanksgiving and it’s majority Chicago for this NFC North battle. 👀 Bears the favorites heading into this highly anticipated matchup. 🐻⬇️ pic.twitter.com/aFIhzvYCsX
Simmons' big rush can come from up the middle or the edge, as he showed in each of his three games, but Detroit's offensive line has been fortified this year and they're doing a solid job of protecting Jared Goff. The misnomer is Goff gets rid of the ball so fast the Bears' rush can't get there -- he's actually taking longer (2.84 seconds, per NFL Next Gen Stats) to get rid of it than any year since he led the Rams to the Super Bowl in 2018. He's getting time to find Amon-Ra St. Brown, Jameson Williams and Sam LaPorta. Detroit is using . This is one game where the absence of Kyler Gordon in coverage is huge for the Bears. The speed of Detroit's receivers on their artificial surface helps make for better separation and big plays, and they have a good speed advantage over the Bears' secondary. Edge to Lions

Bears punt returner Kalif Raymond gets a chance to face his old team looking for a big play. His 10.0-yard average is up 2.5 yards over his last Lions season but well below the 11.3-yard average over the course of his Detroit years. Zavion Thomas broke big Bears plays in the offense last week and doing it on kick returns is needed. The Lions have had only 13 punt returns this season as they're sixth in fair catches with 15. The Bears have had two punts deflected this year, not blocked. The difference from a block is both went beyond the line of scrimmage but easily could have been complete blocks. No NFL team has had two blocks, so it doesn't say much for Chicago's protection. No Edge
The Bears have outscored opponents 62-0 in the first quarter of their last seven wins and scored on their opening drive five straight games. Ben Johnson effect. pic.twitter.com/uvv82NlZ7R
Johnson's wizardry doesn't seem to work against his old boss, or the NFC North overall. He has three wins against NFC North teams, two over Matt LaFleur and the Packers, none over Detroit. Dan Campbell seems to have found a way to fix the offense that appeared broke after Johnson left Detroit. He imported Johnson's good friend Drew Petzing and they have it clicking in the running game and passing game. No Edge
Trying to win at Detroit on Thanksgiving is normally not a huge problem for Lions opponents as Detroit has lost eight of its last nine Thanksgiving games. The one win cost Matt Eberflus his Bears head coaching job, though. Prep time for the Bears is reduced even more because they go on the road for a Thursday noon game. The Johnson homecoming factor was not something in the Bears' favor last year but that was only the second game he had coached in Chicago. No Edge

title: Ben Johnson Addresses Possible D'Andre Swift Fumble-Related Punishment Before Bears-Lions
full_text:
In what has been uncharacteristic for his career, Chicago Bears running back D'Andre Swift has experienced fumbling issues in 2026.
In 10 games this season, Swift has coughed up the rock three times, matching his career-high mark with seven games left to play.
His first fumble came in Week 2 against the Minnesota Vikings , and he followed that up with another in Week 4 versus the New York Jets. His most recent fumble occurred against the New Orleans Saints in Week 11.
After the game, head coach Ben Johnson offered up a simple "no" when asked if he had to say anything else to Swift after previously addressing the fumble issue with his starting running back, which led us to believe that not only was Johnson angry, but he might plan on punishing Swift , also.
However, that is not going to be the case, as Johnson told reporters there is no punishment planned for Swift for the Thanksgiving Day contest against the Detroit Lions.
"No, he just needs to hold on to the ball and we'll be fine," Johnson said, according to ESPN's Courtney Cronin .
It wasn't outlandish to think that Swift might at least see a reduced role, something the Bears have the option of doing now that Kyle Monangai has returned from his turf two.
After all, Johnson has punished Swift before after he benched the veteran running back for an entire half as a result of his fumble in Week 4.
But this is a very different situation in Week 12, as the Bears are playing the biggest game of their season against the Lions, who sit ahead of them in first place . With a win, the Bears would move into first place in the NFC North going into Week 13.
That means all hands on deck and having the duo of Monangai and Swift will be huge for Chicago's offense.
It certainly has not been an ideal year for Swift, his three-year, $33.75 million contract extension notwithstanding.
While the Bears running back is on pace for 1,000 yards on the ground once again, he is also averaging just 3.7 yards per carry, which isn't all on the offensive line because Monangai is running behind the same group and has averaged five yards per tote.
Swift's struggles have been part of the frustration Johnson has had with his running game as a whole, which he says lacks adequate efficiency.
"We weren't as consistent running the ball as we had wanted to be coming off the bye, that was a point of emphasis for us," Johnson said after the Week 11 victory. "When I looked at our runners, they were under four yards a carry. That efficiency stat that we talked about, we weren't hitting that."
Righting the ship on the ground might prove difficult this week, though, as the Lions sport the sixth-best run defense in the league.

title: Chicago Bears Week 12 Keys to Victory: Offense Must Feast on Vulnerable Lions
full_text:
The NFL has been playing games on Thanksgiving Day since the beginning of the league, but we may be about to watch the greatest Thanksgiving game of all time. The Chicago Bears are traveling to Ford Field to take on the Detroit Lions with control of the NFC North on the line. Whoever wins will move to 9-2 on the season, stand alone atop the division, and hold a tiebreaker. The stakes could hardly be higher.
Both teams are red-hot entering Week 12. In fact, this is the first Thanksgiving game in NFL history in which each team is riding a win streak of at least five games. Lions running back Jahmyr Gibbs is putting together a strong case to be the 2026 Offensive Player of the Year while Jeffery Simmons' three-sack game in Week 11 made him a favorite to win Defensive Player of the Year.
Any way you look at it, this game is as close to a true toss-up as it gets. The Bears can absolutely win this one and head into another mini-bye with legitimate Super Bowl aspirations, especially if they hit these keys.
Turkey legs and stuffing shouldn't be the only thing that the Bears feast on during Thanksgiving. They need their offense to get its mojo back against Detroit's wounded defense. They had already lost star pass rusher Aidan Hutchinson for the season in Week 10, but on Sunday they also learned that standout rookie defensive tackle Skyler Gill-Howard is out for the season , too. Linebacker Jack Campbell is also still out after his terrifying neck injury earlier in the month.
Detroit's defense still has plenty of firepower, such as defensive tackle Alim McNeill, but it's vulnerable right now and the Bears' offense must take advantage after back-to-back unimpressive games. I'm not saying they need a repeat of their 59-point outburst in Week 1, but I have a hard time believing they'll win with any less than 30 points.
The Lions' offense is humming right now, and a lot of credit for that goes to Jared Goff's steady, unwavering level of play. Offensive coordinator Drew Petzing's offense fits him like a glove, and he's only gotten better as he's become more comfortable. It's up to the Bears, therefore, to make him uncomfortable.
If the Bears' defensive line can get to Goff and bring him down at least three times in the first half, he'll likely be rattled enough to get a little jumpy. He may fire the ball too early and create interception opportunities or throw the ball out of bounds when perhaps a play could have been made.
As aforementioned, Gibbs is currently a strong candidate to finish the season as the NFL's Offensive Player of the Year. He currently leads all running backs in carries (222), yards (1,098) and touchdowns (13). He is the engine of Detroit's offense, and the Bears have to find a way to slow him down. Luckily, they already found a blueprint for doing exactly that earlier in the season.
In my Week 6 keys to victory for the Bears , I said that they needed to hold superstar running back Bijan Robinson to less than five yards per carry. They failed in that regard, but they held him to just 61 rushing yards for the game. How? By starting out hot on offense and forcing Atlanta to keep Robinson on the sidelines.
That's how Chicago can throw the brakes on the Gibbs train. Jump out to an early lead, force a couple of three-and-outs, and Detroit will have to play catch-up through the air. That's when the defensive line will have their chance to hit my second key and make Goff's life miserable for 60 minutes.
Unfortunately for Bears fans, I think my keys to victory are asking too much of this Bears team against the Lions on the road on a short week. When I predicted the Bears' final games of the season , I had them losing this one and I stand by it. However, it will be a close one, and the players will be able to hold their heads high during the mini-bye.
After losing this game, I expect the Bears to finish the season 13-4, including a victory over the Lions at Soldier Field in Week 17. They'll get their revenge, but it won't happen on Thanksgiving.

title: Bears vs. Lions Thanksgiving Game Will Make NFL History and Chicago's Super Bowl Omen
full_text:
The Week 12 game between the Detroit Lions and Chicago Bears could very well be the biggest in the storied histories of two franchises that have been facing off since 1930.
With both teams sitting at 8-2, the Lions and Bears are not only in contention for the NFC North (the winner will leave in first place), but also the conference's No. 1 seed.
As The Athletic's Kevin Fishbain noted, the only two times the Lions and Bears made the playoffs in the same season came in 1994 and 1991, so we could see something very rare in 2026, which only adds more juice to the upcoming contest.
According to Pro Football Talk's Michael David Smith , when the Bears and Lions meet on Thursday, it will be the first time in NFL history that two teams face off on Thanksgiving amid winning streaks of five games or more.
The Lions have actually won six straight with victories over the Arizona Cardinals, Green Bay Packers, Minnesota Vikings, Miami Dolphins, New England Patriots and Tampa Bay Buccaneers.
Chicago is a winner of five consecutive games, with victories over the Atlanta Falcons, Patriots, Seattle Seahawks, Buccaneers and New Orleans Saints.
During their five-game winning streak, the Bears have not trailed once in any of those games, which is quite impressive.
You'd have to go back 41 years to 1985 for the last time that happened, according to Larry Mayer of ChicagoBears.com .
Of course, 1985 was the only time the Bears won a Super Bowl with one of the greatest defenses in league history, which makes Chicago's current streak a great omen for a team that has legitimate Super Bowl aspirations this season.
The streak came in the final three weeks of the regular season and first two weeks of the playoffs that season before it was snapped in Super Bowl XX when the Patriots took a 3-0 lead before the Bears blew them out, 46-10.
The five-game winning streak began when Caleb Williams made his return to the field following a three-game absence due to a hamstring injury. He also returned one week after the Packers crushed the Bears at Lambeau Field, 31-7.
Three of the five wins have also featured Jeffery Simmons, who was acquired before the trade deadline and made his debut in Week 8. Simmons has been every bit of the difference-maker Chicago hoped he would be.
The Bears are going to need both Simmons and Williams at their very best in what will be one of Chicago's toughest games of the entire 2026 season against a very good Lions squad.

title: Slowing Jahmyr Gibbs and Lions Attack Requires a Missing Bears Element
full_text:
Defensive coordinator Dennis Allen cited the real problem facing the Bears as they try to figure out a way to contain Amon-Ra St. Brown, Jameson Williams, Jahmyr Gibbs and the Detroit Lions offense.
They knew this even before the offseason began, as far back as the 52-21 rout Detroit pinned on Ben Johnson in his return to coach against his old team. It was a key reason they sought specific players in free agency and the draft.
“I think the No. 1 thing is speed," Allen said. "They run every route as if they're getting the ball. They really stress the defense with the speed that they have. I think they've got a really good scheme. They execute it really well. The quarterback executes at a high level. Again, like I said, it's going to be a tremendous challenge for us. This is a really, really, really good offensive football team that we're facing. We've got to be on it.”
Gibbs' league-leading rushing total of 1,098 yards says he's both using his speed and being relied on now as a load-type back. He already has 222 rushing attempts, only 28 away from his career high.
Containing Jahmyr Gibbs is a really difficult task, but the Bears need to find a way to prevent him from making big plays in their showdown against the Lions on Thanksgiving Day. pic.twitter.com/TUf5Nb9Lyi
"With this offense is, if you want to have some type of success against a team like this, you got to stop Gibbs," Bears defensive tackle Jeffery Simmons said. "I feel like a lot of stuff is ran through him."
When Ben Johnson coordinated the Lions offense, he had a close-up look at the issues Gibbs causes for defenses.
"The talent is on another level," Bears coach Ben Johnson said. "Just the speed, the ability to burst and make guys miss, all that. But from afar, not in the building, it looks like he's added a little bit of size and mass to handle that workload. And so I know how many times he's touched the ball so far this year, but like I said before, I don't know why you wouldn't continue to feed him and feed him because as the game goes on, it just seems like ... eventually he's going to break through and end up having some big plays for you.
Jahmyr Gibbs just tied Barry Sanders for the most rushing touchdowns in NFL history before turning 25. 23 CAR, 98 RUSH YDS, 2 TD, 4 REC, 20 REC YDS vs Buccaneers. Gibbs remains the OPOY favorite, with JSN right behind him. https://t.co/sh6pfsYxuG pic.twitter.com/g4cJLVE7UB
"So they're doing a great job. I think Hank Fraley is one of the best O-line coaches in the business and that plays a big part of Gibby's success. But, certainly, he's a unique talent in his own regard and big challenge for us."
St. Brown's quickness, route running and hands have made him a Bears killer since back when he came into the league before Johnson was Lions offensive coordinator in 2021. Last season, he had 20 catches for 254 yards and three touchdowns in the two games against the Bears.
Tom Thayer: Jared Goff & Amon-Ra St. Brown Are a NIGHTMARE for Defenses! LINK: https://t.co/WfNzSm5OGu Brought to you by @advantagechevybridgeview Find your Advantage at Advantage Dealer Group @carmendefalco @jurko64 #ChicagoBears #DetroitLions #AmonRaStBrown #JaredGoff … pic.twitter.com/hvlYLmhBw8
Williams is the field stretcher and had 10 catches for 182 yards last season in two games against his old coordinator's team.
"I do think it starts with Gibbs though," Johnson said. "If he's not the offensive player of the year right now, then he's gotta be top three. He's all over the place. He's leading the league in scrimmage yards and run game, pass game, it just seems like they can't get the ball to him enough. We've got our hands full with him."
So here are the Bears back face to face with the Lions' offense and quarterback Jared Goff has his speed targets. And where are the Bears defensively?
Throwback to Amon-Ra St. Brown showing off his INSANE burst 🔥 pic.twitter.com/Inko6j1FWA
If Jeffery Simmons, Montez Sweat and Austin Booker can't get to Goff, their coverage is challenged. They brought in Coby Bryant because of the speed he added at safety and he hasn't played a down due to his knee/leg injury. They finally got Kyler Gordon back from injuries and he played five games, but now he's on the verge of being ruled out for a second straight game due to a shoulder injury.
Devin Bush and Dillon Thieneman are the speed additions left and still playing. So much will depend on the rush getting the heat on Goff or at least getting in his face to force him off his throwing point and disrupt timing.
Jeffery Simmons is a force multiplier along the defensive line who is unstoppable in 1-on-1 situations He can power through double-team blocks to make plays, and he creates opportunities for his teammates. He’s playing at a DPOY caliber #Bears pic.twitter.com/tqQrNTzyTv https://t.co/KXyraH84sw
"When you have a lot of playmakers and you're not affecting the pocket, bad things happen," Simmons said.
Fortunately for the Bears, they have the player who can affect the pocket.
Simmons is only one player, though, and he's a defensive lineman at that. He can be double-teamed. It only takes a few passes to get out when a team brings as much speed to bear against a defense as Detroit does.
Jeffery Simmons definitely sacking Jared Goff at least twice and that’s bare minimum

title: Caleb Williams Attempts to Regain His Touch on a National Stage
full_text:
Caleb Williams knows his last two games failed to meet the standard of his first three games back after a hamstring injury.
Rectifying this against the Detroit Lions is essential if the Bears are going to have a chance to win their Thanksgiving showdown at Detroit and retain first place in the NFC North. It might be a matter simply of being more decisive, he said Tuesday at Halas Hall.
"Yeah, I think last game just not as decisive as I wanted to be," he said Tuesday. "There was times where just getting through the reads maybe too fast or maybe a little too slow and you're missing opportunities and things like that. So just pulling the trigger, being decisive, I think that's something I always harp on."
Just as the Bears running game has been struggling of late, Williams' completion percentage has been coming down from its peak around 72%. It's come down as teams have amped up the blitzing against Williams. He's at 61.7% completions in the last two games and his passer rating was 72.9 after he had a 111.3 rating and 73.8% completions in his first three games after his hamstring injury.
"The Bears & their GM followed a very pragmatic, simple formula. Sometimes when you see this in life, business, & sports you're like: Why doesn't everybody do it that way?" @colincowherd breaks down how Bears GM Ryan Poles quickly built a winning team around Caleb Williams pic.twitter.com/YEl5b3J9F2
"We've been in the 60 ranges of completion percentage and we want to get back up to the 70s, obviously, as an offense," he said. "And so a big part of that is me knowing where the guys are, knowing the defense, knowing where we want to go with the ball, and if it's not there, just checking the ball down and living to fight for another down."
The Lions could wind up being surprised by a new Bears weapon. That's receiver Zavion Thomas. The speed demon had a 30-yard reverse, then made catches of 40 and 16 yards against Tampa Bay as the Bears turned to him for a more extensive look for the first time.
Caleb Williams has been pressured more than any other QB in the NFL but still has been surgical against it. #18 has been unfazed pic.twitter.com/Hu5aOEbXrB
Williams recalled one Saints reaction to Thomas' 4.28-second speed from during the game.
"Yeah, it was funny," Williams said. "Somebody came up to me mid-game and was like, 'He wasn't on the scouting report,' of him being that fast, and so it's awesome to be able to have the young rook step up in big moments.
"He stepped up on that sliding catch he had, he stepped up on the 40-yard pass that we ended up having. He's doing a good job. We gotta keep encouraging him to be at his best, because that's what we need. It's a long season and guys are gonna have to step up and show up in big moments, regardless of how much playing time you had or having."
Caleb Williams reaction after throwing a block 😂 pic.twitter.com/LOMbM1DyPr
Finding Thomas or any of the receivers might not be as easy as in past games against Detroit as their secondary has begun to reform with the return from a knee injury by safety Joseph Kerby last week. The Bears also must contend with the pass rush of defensive tackle Alim McNeill, who has become the Lions' version of Jeffery Simmons. In fact, Simmons and McNeill are tied for 10th best defensive tackle in the game on Pro Football Focus' grading, which can be a bit subjective.
"In their first couple games, maybe not so much, but their past five games they've been pretty damn good with getting teams into, third-and-long, seven plus, and a lot of times that's obviously in the defenses favor," Williams said. "So we’ve got to try and stay on track on normal down and distances and then from there when those moments do come up and we're at third-and-seven we’ve got to have answers, we got to be able to adjust throughout the game and go out there and make plays when the ball is in the air or if we're running it.”
Whatever they do, it needs to be sharper than against both Tampa Bay and New Orleans in wins. They've got to pull this off on a short week of work, without a real practice.
“The greatest challenge is obviously the full speed," Williams said. "You put in specific plays for defenses and you want to be able to see them and throw them at full speed as a quarterback, even just overall just as an offensive line or running back; being able to see the gaps and the holes and things like that, blocking wise, how they're blocking certain runs and things like that.
"That felt like last year." @robertmays weighs in on an up and down performance from Caleb Williams and the Chicago Bears offense in Week 11. pic.twitter.com/M8TjDKrzED
"I think that's the biggest challenge but we’ve got a bunch of pros in this locker room, guys throughout the walkthroughs in the short weeks are asking questions, we're reloading stuff whenever we need to reload it. If it takes a little bit longer, it takes a little bit longer."
Getting it all down this week rapidly can make for postgame celebration with turducken against a Lions team that is 1-8 in its last nine Thanksgiving games.
“Appreciate you Poles, Ben.” Caleb Williams had to give props to Jeffery Simmons and everyone who brought him to Chicago 🤝 @insidethenfl Week 11 Mic’d Up on X pic.twitter.com/kEbHb1tP9F

title: Revisiting the Bears' Last Thanksgiving Game vs Lions and How Much Has Changed
full_text:
Chicago Bears fans have seen a lot of bad football in the decades since their last Super Bowl win, but arguably none worse than the Matt Eberflus era. As head coach of the Bears for two and a half seasons, Eberflus oversaw the longest losing streak in franchise history (14 games), finished with the second-lowest winning percentage (.304), and became the only head coach in franchise history to never beat the Green Bay Packers.
This era of failure culminated in Chicago's humiliating loss to the Detroit Lions on Thanksgiving Day of 2024, a game that lives in infamy. The Bears trailed 20-23 in the game's final minute as Caleb Williams was sacked at midfield with 36 seconds remaining. Eberflus inexplicably declined to call a timeout as the offense seemed unaware of the running clock. The ball was snapped with seven seconds left, Williams threw a pass to Rome Odunze, but it fell incomplete as the clock hit zero.
The Bears fired Eberflus after this Thanksgiving disaster , the first time in franchise history that the Bears fired a head coach midseason. It was more than warranted as Eberflus seemed to have lost the locker room entirely. Multiple reports alleged that Bears players confronted Eberflus openly about failing to call a timeout late in the game.
However, this catastrophic loss proved to be a blessing in disguise. Three months later, the Bears hired Ben Johnson as their next head coach , and he's led the Bears to a 20-9 record, including the playoffs, since then. Now, in Week 12 of his second season, Johnson has a chance to avenge the Bears of a loss which he helped deliver. The Bears face the Lions on Thanksgiving again this year with control of the NFC North on the line.
The 2026 Bears could not be more different from the team that took the field for what ended up being Eberflus' final game with the franchise. Instead of riding a five-game losing streak into this holiday showdown, the Bears have won their last five games. Even better, they haven't trailed for a single second in any of those games.
In 2024, Caleb Williams was an overwhelmed rookie trapped behind a shoddy offensive line in a stale offense. Today, Williams leads one of the best offenses in the league with an offensive line that includes the inaugural Protector of the Year . The old Bears defense struggled to get after the quarterback, but these Bears are currently Top 4 in total sacks and only six behind the leaders.
I say all that to say this: nothing from the last Thanksgiving matchup between these two teams can inform us about what's going to happen on Thursday. Not even last year's games, the first under Ben Johnson, can tell us much about what to expect.
I'll have more to say about what the Bears' gameplan for Thursday should be as we get closer to kickoff. For now, suffice it to say that the Bears are going to have to lean on Caleb Williams to get the job done. The running game has stagnated, and the Bears' defense, while much improved, hasn't faced an offense as potent as Detroit's. Meanwhile, Williams has grown by leaps and bounds in his third NFL season.
That's exactly what should give Bears fans hope. Two years ago, relying on Williams to carry the team would have been a fool's errand. Now, that's just what's expected of him as the franchise quarterback. We saw him do it against the defending champs in Week 8, he just needs to do it again to put the Bears in the driver's seat of the division.

title: Bears Claiming Former Commanders CB With Ties to Dennis Allen is Bad Sign for Kyler Gordon
full_text:
The Chicago Bears made a roster move on Tuesday with just two days to go before the Week 12 game against the Detroit Lions .
According to the league's transactions wire , the Bears claimed former Washington Commanders cornerback Isaac Yiadom. Players claimed off waivers go the active roster.
Yiadom was cut loose by the Commanders on Monday with the team needing to make room for running back Jacory Croskey-Merritt, who was activated off injured reserve.
Despite being with the Commanders since September, Yiadom did not play any snaps on defense and appeared for 55 on special teams.
A former third-round pick of the Denver Broncos in 2018, Yiadom has 121 games under his belt over eight-plus seasons, including 34 starts, and has played in games with the Broncos, New York Giants, Green Bay Packers, New Orleans Saints, San Francisco 49ers and Commanders.
Yiadom's stint in New Orleans overlapped with Bears defensive coordinator Dennis Allen's when he was the head coach there after serving as defensive coordinator.
Yiadom has tallied 230 tackles (170 solo), including two for loss, 0.5 sacks, one QB hit, 32 passes defensed, three interceptions and three forced and recovered fumbles during his career.
In coverage, the veteran has surrendered a completion rate of 62.4% and a passer rating of 102.9 on 258 targets.
Yiadom brings a bit of versatility with experience playing in the slot, out wide and at safety, although he will likely contribute on special teams only in Chicago, barring more injuries.
Yiadom is the second defensive back the Bears have added in as many days after the team reunited with Marlen Sewell, who was added to the practice squad on Monday. Undrafted rookie quarterback Miller Moss was cut loose to make room.
The two additions come amid the Bears dealing with injuries in the secondary, as both slot cornerback Kyler Gordon and safety Elijah Hicks are both hurt. The addition of Yiadom could be a sign that Gordon is set to miss at least one more game.
Gordon is dealing with a shoulder injury that kept him out of last week's game and he remained sidelined at practice on both Monday and Tuesday (the injury reports were estimations).
Meanwhile, Hicks was unexpectedly added to the injury report on Tuesday and has been ruled out because of a concussion, head coach Ben Johnson told reporters before practice. Sewell is probably the response to Hicks' injury.
Not having Hicks not only cuts into the depth at safety, but it also leaves the Bears without their punt protector, so they'll have to figure out a replacement for that role.

title: Bears Tuesday Injury Report: Status Quo for Kyler Gordon, 1 DB Added & Ruled Out
full_text:
The Chicago Bears have released their second injury report of the week ahead of the Week 12 game against the Detroit Lions on Thursday afternoon.
Because the Bears only held a walkthrough once again on Tuesday, the injury report was an estimation.
The Bears had a new addition to the injury report in veteran safety Elijah Hicks, who head coach Ben Johnson revealed has already been ruled out .
Other than Hicks, it was the same four players who were listed on Monday, including cornerback Kyler Gordon, linebacker D'Marco Jackson, left tackle Theo Benedet and running back Roschon Johnson.
Let's see if there was any change in their respective estimated participation levels on Tuesday.
It isn't clear when Hicks suffered his concussion. There was no report of a head injury during or after Sunday's game and the Bears didn't practice on Monday, as evidenced by the team releasing an estimated injury report.
Hicks' absence leaves the Bears short on depth at safety and without a punt protector.
Adam Hoge of CHGO Bears thinks Chicago could replace him with one of two defensive backs, Marlen Sewell or Skyler Thomas, or running back Salvon Ahmed. All four took snaps as the punt protector during the preseason.
Let's start with the bad news: Kyler Gordon is still sidelined and it looks like he's going to miss his second straight game with his shoulder injury that initially had him labeled as day-to-day, Johnson said last week.
Along with Gordon and Hicks, Roschon Johnson was unable to take part yet again and he remains on track to sit out.
Last week, the Bears deployed Clark Phillips in Gordon's spot and he played well, so it's possible the Bears stick with him.
We could also see Chicago opt to roll with Malik Muhammad in the slot. Cam Lewis would typically be another option but there's less of a chance that happens with Hicks ruled out.
If Johnson sits, Salvon Ahmed will take his place.
With D'Marco Jackson a full participant yet again, he continues to be on track to overcome his elbow injury that he suffered during Sunday's contest.
There was a bit of a mystery with Jackson , who did not play a snap on defense despite not being given a designation after he departed for the locker room to get evaluated.
Chances are the Bears just decided to play it safe with him with a short week ahead of the Lions game on Thanksgiving.
The big news is Theo Benedet going from non-participant to a full practice. Benedet got shaken up in Week 11 but quickly returned, so there wasn't really much concern for him to begin with.
The Bears have Ozzy Trapilo ready to rock in the event that Benedet suffers a setback, but he should be good to go.

title: Zac Taylor Updates Dalton Risner's Health, Shemar Stewart's Lacking Impact Entering Saints Week
full_text:
Zac Taylor returned to the podium on Wednesday for the first time since the Bengals' five-game win streak ended against the Commanders.
The 22-20 loss featured one of the worst rushing performances in team history (14 carries for 31 yards), and Jalen Rivers' 58 snaps at right guard had something to do with it.
The backup right guard filled in for Dalton Risner (knees) and only notched a 55.3 Pro Football Focus grade (50.5 run-block grade). Getting Risner back to complete the offensive line continuity this week would be massive.
Taylor updated his status.
"He'll be day to day, so we'll see," Taylor said about Risner. "Just talked to him this morning, and we'll just take it day to day and see where he ends up on Sunday. Today's a walkthrough-only day, so I wouldn't read too much into how that goes today."
Bryan Cook suffered an injury in the first half of the game but ended up playing 64 snaps and should be good to go this week. Taylor said he is just "sore" after the recent loss. Meanwhile, Cincinnati desperately needs help at defensive end amidst Shemar Stewart's shutout from the lineup.
He didn't play a snap Monday, and the week prior, he didn't enter the game until the Bengals were up 31-3. The three weeks prior to that, he played five, six, and zero total snaps.
"I've been pleased with Shemar," Taylor said, noting the game flow led to no snaps for Stewart because Boye Mafe and Myles Murphy didn't play a lot in the first half. "I know I sound a little bit like a broken record up here, and then he doesn't take a snap, so I get that. But he's controlling everything he needs to control. He's in a positive spot right now for us. We'll provide him some opportunity to go make some plays for us, and I like where he's at. So just the way it unfolded last week wasn't any sort of indictment on it."
We will see if the Bengals put weight behind Taylor's words by actually playing Stewart a significant snap diet this week.
All in all, Cincinnati is pretty healthy entering Week 12 as they get their first normal game week in nearly a month to enjoy at home.
Looking a bit deeper into this, the data matches the eye test on Boye Mafe/Myles Murphy usage. The Bengals have continued to rely more heavily on them with last night being the most all season.
