title: Referee Report: Bengals, Saints Should Expect Lots of Flags in Sunday's Game
full_text:
Not only are the Cincinnati Bengals wearing the same uniform combo they wore when they blew a 15-point lead against the New York Jets last year, they’ll also have the same referee they had that day.
Scott Novak will be on the call for Sunday’s game against the New Orleans Saints at Paycor Stadium, marking his first Bengals game since the team’s infamous 39-38 loss in Week 8 last year.
Novak has been a head referee since 2019 and has been an NFL official since 2014.
The Bengals are 3-5 with Novak. The Saints also are 3-5 with him.
Novak and his crew are averaging 17.4 accepted penalties per game, which is a close second to Craig Wrolstad (17.44) for second most in the league.
Last year Novak ranked 11th (11.82), and in 2023 he was 10th (12.24).
Novak and his crew have called 46 offensive holding penalties this year, most in the league. The next highest number is 37 by Alex Moore, who has only worked nine games this season to Novak’s 10.
The next highest number for a referee that has worked 10 games is 32 by Shawn Smith.
Novak and his crew also lead the league with 13 unnecessary roughness penalties, which is almost 50 percent more than the next highest total, which is nine by Shawn Hochuli.
In Week 4, Novak’s crew had 30 accepted penalties for 280 yards.
The penalties are the most this season, and the yards are second most behind 289 in a Week 2 overtime game between the Packers and Jets, which Novak also worked.
Novak has one career playoff assignment, which was an NFC Wild-Card game between the Buccaneers and Commanders way back in 2020.
Here is the full list of eight Bengals games Novak has worked:
Week 8, 2025: Jets 39, Bengals 38
Bengals 2-15; Cowboys 4-25
Week 14, 2024: Bengals 27, Cowboys 20
Bengals 10-77; Cowboys 4-36
Week 8, 2024: Eagles 37, Bengals 17
Week 14, 2023: Bengals 34, Jaguars 31
Bengals 6-35; Jaguars 7-55
Week 5, 2022: Ravens 19, Bengals 17
Week 9, 2021: Browns 41, Bengals 16
Bengals 4-31; Browns 10-84
Week 8, 2020: Bengals 31, Titans 20
Week 10, 2019: Ravens 49, Bengals 13

title: This Week's Cincinnati Bengals Uniform Combination Will Send Shivers Through Fan Base
full_text:
If you tie memories to Cincinnati Bengals uniform combinations, prepare to be uncomfortable.
The Bengals will wear black jerseys, orange pants with black stripes and black socks Sunday afternoon at Paycor Stadium against the New Orleans Saints.
They’ve only worn the combination three other times, and two of them were losses that stuck with fans long after the clock hit 0:00.
The uniform combination debut came in Week 5 of 2024 against the Baltimore Ravens. The Bengals blew up a 10-point fourth-quarter lead to go to overtime, where holder Ryan Rehkow dropped the snap on what would have been a 53-yard field goal attempt to win the game.
One play later, Derrick Henry ripped off a 51-yard run, followed seconds later by Justin Tucker’s 24-yard field goal for a 41-38 victory that dropped the Bengals to 1-4.
Later that season, with the Bengals riding a two-game winning streak, they wore it again for a home game against the Cleveland Browns, and the Bengals won easily, 24-6.
But last year in Week 8, the uniform combination returned for one of the games that encapsulated the disaster the 2025 Cincinnati defense was – a 39-38 loss to the New York Jets.
The Bengals led that game by 14 twice in the second quarter and took a 15-point lead into the four quarter, only to watch the Jets outscore them 23-7 over the final 14 minutes to pull off a stunning win.
It also was Trey Hendrickson’s final game with the team as he asked off the field due to an injury in the second quarter.
The following week, the Bengals blew another late lead against the Chicago Bears.
Breaking down the individual elements of the uniform combination, Cincinnati is just 3-7 while wearing orange pants, although they snapped a three-game losing streak in the britches a few weeks ago in Madrid with a 34-17 win against the Atlanta Falcons.
Conversely, the black socks had been lucky. The Bengals had won five in a row with them and 9 of 11 before losing Monday night at Washington.

title: Shemar Stewart Off to a Historically Bad Start in His Young Career
full_text:
There's always a game every fan base would like to have back at the end of a season. For Cincinnati Bengals fans, that game happened on Monday night.
The Bengals had a chance to take care of business on the road in a Monday night showdown with the Washington Commanders. Instead, the rest of the week is being spent wondering how the Bengals allowed the Commanders to grab the 22-20 win.
The offense was a shell of itself for most of the first half, while the defense crumbled during crunch time. The pass rush was solid in the first half, earning three sacks, but looked a little gassed in the second half, resulting in zero sacks. Which begs the question: where is Shemar Stewart?
The Bengals' 2025 first round pick has been non-existent for the franchise this season. On Monday night, Stewart didn't even play a snap. Looking at his performance this season, Stewart has only played 52 snaps for the Bengals.
A team that is looking for help in the pass rush is not getting it from a player who was selected in a premium spot just two drafts ago. To make matters worse, Stewart is on a path to being one of the worst pass rushers to be selected in the first round in the last twenty drafts.
According to Gridiron Grading , Stewart is off to the slowest start of any edge rusher drafted in the first round in the last 20 years. This chart was created using each player's Pro Football Focus grades.
Sure, Stewart should take some blame for not being able to translate his game at the NFL level. However, the Bengals front office had to know this pick could have always been a high-risk, high-reward situation.
Stewart was not known as a player to rack up sacks during his college career. In three seasons with the Texas A&M Aggies, Stewart had just 4.5 sacks.
The current pass rush situation also can go back to the team not making any moves prior to the trade deadline. Well, they made one move, then decided it wasn't the right move, but let's just leave that in the past.
Now, the Bengals are hoping for edge depth and a running back who can show any life in the backfield as they quickly approach the end of the season. The only problem is that the team will have to make do with what they currently have.

title: 'Showing My Love To The Cincinnati Zoo And Fiona' - Tee Higgins Honors Famous Cincinnati Hippo
full_text:
Tee Higgins walked into Monday Night Football sporting a nice gesture toward Fiona the Hippo and Cincinnati. The Cincinnati Zoo lost its prized, cute hippo this past week due to health complications from Fiona eating a knit hat that accidentally got launched into her exhibit.
Higgins rocked a Fiona sweatshirt walking into the stadium for the game.
The whole Cincinnati community has taken the news pretty hard. Fiona was consistently voted as the city's best "Cincinnatian" in the annual CityBeat best of Cincinnati awards. She is the reigning queen, earning the honor in 2025 over names like Joe Burrow and Bob Herzog.
She would've turned 10 years old in January.
Higgins caught a touchdown in the loss to Washington, but was largely quiet with two catches for 43 yards and the score.
“Yeah, I mean, obviously, Cincinnati is mourning pretty hard about that one. I felt it from them. I love Cincinnati, so just showing my love to the Cincinnati Zoo and Fiona," Higgins said about the outfit.
The Bengals couldn't keep the good-hippo luck rolling after no major Cincinnati sports team had lost since Fiona passed right before the weekend began.
Cincinnati didn't execute nearly well enough to pull off a road victory against a good quarterback like Jayden Daniels.
"What did they have, field goals? I don't know. They just beat us. I think you have to own that as a team. We have to come back next week and do what we're supposed to do," Dexter Lawrence said about the outing. "I haven't had a chance to talk to them (rest of the defense). We just have to stay together, you know? It's a tough, tough loss, but we have to stay together, and we have to be better as a team."
Ja'Marr Chase echoed a similar sentiment in pretty brief postgame comments from him and just about every other Bengal.
"One loss doesn't determine nothing. It's the NFL. You got a loss, you learn from it. We learn from our mistakes. That's what we're going to do. We're going to watch the film, we're going to correct it and move on," Chase declared.
Heavy hearts remain in Cincinnati as Higgins's team tries to lift the city this coming Sunday and start a new winning streak.

title: From Pregame to Final Minute, Bengals Mistakes Drive Dagger Into Win Streak
full_text:
The struggle to execute a plan began before kickoff with an aggressive coin flip decision dripping with doubt. And it lasted until the final damning 46 seconds as the Cincinnati Bengals defense dialed back memory banks to a series of failed finishes in 2025.
Quarterback Joe Burrow went from Superman to shaky against the blitz, and Al Golden’s pash rush went from lethal to a David Copperfield Learjet as the Washington Commanders answered four consecutive punts with six straight scoring drives.
From start to finish, failures littered the Northwest Stadium turf in a 22-20 loss that snapped the Bengals’ five-game winning streak.
None were more surprising than the white-hot Bengals failing to secure a final-minute first down that would have left Washington quarterback and hero marksman Jayden Daniels stranded on the sideline.
“Trying to get a first down to win it,” Cincinnati head coach Zac Taylor said. “That way, the walk-off field goal would win the game for us. Make them use their timeouts. Go get the last first down so we can walk off with a field goal.”
Had Burrow found a completion of just 7 yards on one of his final two dropbacks, that is how it would have played out, with kicker Evan McPherson continuing his impressive season with a game ender.
But Burrow missed Chase – the second huge missed chance of the half – on second down and nearly threw a walk-off pick.
Then on third down, he made McPherson’s job much tougher by taking a 7-yard sack when he failed to see open receivers.
Shocked this didn’t go to Tee … https://t.co/hkJTmuID1x
“If you run it twice, then you’re disappointed that you’re in fourth and 9,” Taylor said in a telling admission of how repugnant the rushing attack was throughout the game, with the Bengals managing just 31 yards on 14 carries.
“They’re going to get the ball back with whatever it was,50 seconds left, not counting that injury timeout because you can’t anticipate that,” he added. “But that was the mindset there.”
The Commanders lost their final timeout when cornerback Rasul Douglas didn’t get up following the near interception, whether it be due to injury or disappointment. Had the Bengals run the ball on second and 7, the Commanders would have called timeout.
And the sack Burrow took on third down essentially served as a running play as the clock kept running.
McPherson buried a 56-yard field goal into the net for a 20-19 lead, a kick that would have played on his career highlight reel regardless of whatever accomplishments await in the future.
And while it felt as though the Bengals had cleared dodged a soggy start and sloppy finish, those who lived through the 2024 and 2025 seasons knew 46 seconds might have been too much time left on the clock.
And Daniels proved them right, needing just two passes to Antonio Williams – a 22-yard drive starter and 42-yard game sealer – to set up Drew Stevens for a 26-yard field goal to walk off the Bengals.
“A little disappointment, obviously,” said safety Bryan Cook, who left the game briefly with an ankle injury but gutted it out in the second half.
“We had a chance to win at the end, and we didn’t do that,” Cook added. “But the good teams – the great teams – know how to take a punch and throw another one. I'm excited to see how we respond.”
The defense has been playing with a significant buffer as Burrow boosted his MVP campaign with a historic run of production during the five-game winning streak.
In an attempt to keep that going, the Bengals chose to receive the opening kickoff after winning the coin toss for the second week in a row.
Last week it resulted in a 13-play, 80-yard touchdown drive that set the stage for a 38-18 rout of the Pittsburgh Steelers.
Monday night, the Bengals not only went three and out, but the Commanders were able to get a touchdown with 12 seconds left in the first half and a field goal to open the second half.
They would go on to score field goals on each of their five second-half drives.
Burrow and the Bengals offense scored on their final drives of the first half and opening possession after halftime to take a 17-10 lead.
But they were 0 for 3 on third down after that, including a missed shot on a deep ball that could have been a kill shot and a third-and-10 screen that Chase wasn’t able to advance more a couple of yards.
“Just not good enough to win,” said Burrow, who completed 28 of 40 passes for 300 yards and two touchdowns.
“We made some plays at the end that put us in a good spot, but it’s just not good enough,” he added. “We just didn’t make plays. We need to make plays.”
The usual chemistry connected Burrow and Chase weren’t in sync on the near interception on the final drive, nor were they together on the failed deep ball.
Chase had the defense beat in a play that looked similar to the failed attempt in the Tennessee game. Chase said he was just trying to make a play on the ball for his quarterback but couldn’t even get his hands on it. Burrow said though the ball came out of his hand awkwardly, he thought he put it in a good spot.
Burrow was 11 of 11 for 181 yards against the Pittsburgh blitz.
He was 30 of 33 for 394 yards and five touchdowns against the blitz in the three games prior to Monday night.
Against the Commanders, he was just 8 of 16 for 64 yards and a touchdown.
He’s been able to over a subpar run game all season, but against the Commanders it was even more problematic, and Taylor didn’t have an answer for why in the immediate aftermath.
“I feel like that’s a good question,” he said. “I felt like there was maybe a little bit more of an opportunity than what we took advantage of. It wasn’t like there was major production there, but I thought that there was a little more opportunity, and we’re going to have to watch to see where those errors were.”
In the end, the Bengals got exactly what they wanted, what they thrive on – the ball in Burrow’s hands with a chance to win the game.
But the Commanders blitzed him on second and 7 and Burrow nearly threw a pick. One play later, he took a sack.
The chance to control the outcome was transferred to the defense. But an otherwise solid night – Washington was just 2 of 10 on third down and 1 of 3 in the red zone – will be remembered for Daniels throwing two great passes for 64 yards and a walk-off win.
“Credit to them,” Taylor said. “They played great. They made it really difficult on us in all phases, and we didn’t finish the job.”

title: Joe Burrow Posts Worst PFF Grade in Several Seasons as Commanders Marks Largely Disappoint
full_text:
The Pro Football Focus grades are in after Cincinnati's 22-20 loss to Washington ended their five-game winning streak. Those grades reflected a losing effort as Cincinnati's stars did not keep up their nuclear-level run in recent weeks.
The 64.1 overall team grade was the second-lowest of the season, trailing a 63.7 mark in the Week 3 loss to Pittsburgh. Offensively, only Amarius Mims (81.3) posted an 80-plus grade as he continues his All-Pro level season.
The rest of the top five went in this order (min. 15 snaps): Mike Gesicki (79.4), Jack Endries (76.2), Drew Sample (67.9), and Ted Karras (67.3).
Endries is doing a nice job filling the role of injured Erick All. The rookie posted a career-best grade against Washington. There were plenty of big names at the bottom, including the worst game of the season for Joe Burrow (56.6).
He had the fifth-worst grade, followed by Tee Higgins (56), Dohnte Meyers (52.2), Dylan Fairchild (52.1), and Chase Brown (37.9). Cincinnati needed much more from its top running back in Brown and offensive engine in Burrow, but they didn't answer the call.
It was a shocking performance from Burrow , posting his worst grade since a 50.8 mark in Week 4 of the 2023 season. The Bengals needed the run game to step up around his shaky outing, and it didn't get on the plane for the road outing.
Flipping to defense, Boye Mafe's multi-sack outing had him leading the way again with a 79.6 grade.
The rest of the top five went in this order: TJ Slaton (75.9), Josh Newton (71), DJ Ivey (67.3), and Jordan Battle (65.2).
A whopping seven high-snap players earned 60 grades or lower in the rainy slog. The bottom five went in this order: Myles Murphy (47.4), Dexter Lawrence (48.2), Jonathan Allen (51.2), B.J. Hill (52.3), and Dax Hill (53.9).
A ton of star names in that low group. They need to flush it and be much better at home this week against the Saints.

title: 'Going To Be A Little Clunky' - Zac Taylor, Joe Burrow Dissect Horrendous Bengals Rush Attack
full_text:
The Bengals offense face-planted on Monday Night Football in a pretty surprising way against the Commanders. Washington ranks just 18th in scoring defense (24.3) and 20th in EPA/play allowed, but the Bengals couldn't find any consistency.
Zac Taylor and Joe Burrow dove into why it was so difficult for the offense on a night where the run game was non-existent. Cincinnati needed to bleed out the game in the fourth quarter, but ran for just 31 yards on 14 carries.
The Bengals should be pretty one-dimensional with Burrow at QB, but they can't be entirely one-dimensional.
"I just thought we didn't start very well," Taylor said. "They are a very aggressive defense, and so it's going to be a little clunky at times. They found some momentum earlier in the game, and they came after us. We didn't do a great job answering until about the third or fourth drive. And then we found some momentum. We started on the minus 10, drove it all the way down the field, kicked a field goal, then went down and scored a touchdown to start the second half. So, I felt like we found some momentum there and just didn't finish it the way we wanted to in the second half."
Taylor thought they could've run the ball much better than they did.
It's hard to beat any NFL team averaging 2.1 yards per carry.
"I felt like there was maybe a little bit more of an opportunity than what we took advantage of," Taylor said. "It wasn't like there was major production there, but I thought that there was a little more opportunity, and we're going to have to watch to see where those errors were."
Burrow was pretty short with his comments after a frustrating night. He posted his second-lowest ESPN QBR of the season (58.6, worst against Jacksonville with a 42.6 mark)
"Just not good enough to win. We made some plays at the end that put us in a good spot, but it's just not good enough," Burrow noted about the offense. "We just didn't make plays. We need to make plays. We all can be better, for sure."
According to RBSDM.com, Cincinnati is now heavily favored to host one playoff game as a division winner, but highly unlikely to land the AFC's No. 1 seed (75% chance to host wild card, 7% chance at No. 1 seed). They really needed that victory against a bad Commanders team and now likely have to win out to land that top slot.

title: Winners and Losers from Bengals Last-Second Loss to Commanders
full_text:
The Bengals failed to secure a critical win against the Commanders in Washington on a rainy Monday night in a 22-20 loss. The team now falls to 7-3 after letting a chance to gain a big lead in the AFC North slip away.
Here are five winners and six losers from Monday night.
Mafe provided a game-wrecker like presence in this game from start to finish. He dominated the Commanders offensive line in the first half with three sacks and has emerged as an elite talent on this Bengals team.
With his performance on Monday, Mafe has a new career-high for most sacks in a season with 9.5, and there are still seven games left on the year.
Murphy had a night to forget on Monday as first Jayden Daniels juked him out of his cleats to convert a 3rd & 9 with a 10-yard run that ended with a Commanders touchdown to close the first half. Murphy later committed an offsides penalty that gave the Commanders a first down on a 3rd & 3 in the red zone.
This is the type of game that could ultimately cost Murphy any extension with the Bengals this offseason.
Perine showed that he is a trustworthy player for this offense in inclement weather.
When raining in the first half, Perine routinely flashed whenever he had the ball in his hands. His best play of the night happened at the end of the first half where he took a short pass from Burrow 44-yards downfield to setup the Bengals first score of the night. He finished with 10 touches for 96 yards.
Carter is beginning to make a name for himself as someone consistently inconsistent as a player in the NFL. Along with missed tackles, he again failed to put himself in a position to make a stop in the middle of the field. Jayden Daniels sprinted by Carter on a scramble and instead of potentially stopping Daniels short of the first down mark, Daniels ran for 47-yards down the middle of the field.
It is worrisome that these type of errors are still occurring midway through Carter's second season.
Gesicki led the receiver's tonight with five catches for 77 yards and consistently linked up with Burrow on extended plays where Burrow struggled to find openings in the secondary. He continues to show why Burrow relies on him in the offense even in games where Ja'Marr Chase and Tee Higgins create explosive plays.
The final drive of the game alone lands Golden on this list.
46 seconds and two deep shots in the middle of the field is all Jayden Daniels and the Commanders needed to get in range for the game-winning field goal. Golden clearly failed to establish any sense of urgency in covering the middle of the field in the games final minute. Given this teams struggles over the middle all season that is absolutely unacceptable.
Young has handled much of the dirty work as a blocker at receiver all season, something that the coaching staff noticed and rewarded him for tonight. While he only had one catch for four yards, that catch happened to come at a crucial moment in the red zone. Burrow found himself scrambling out from pressure, and Young made the proper adjustments in the endzone to catch his first career touchdown.
This also comes as Andrei Iosivas is close to returning off of Injured Reserve, so perhaps tonight earned Young more opportunities in the offense as a pass catcher.
While Gesicki and Perine made big plays when they needed to, the Bengals offensive stars failed to do so for much of the night. Outside of a 31-yard touchdown strike to Tee Higgins late in the first half, Joe Burrow, Ja'Marr Chase, and Tee Higgins failed to create many positive plays from start to finish.
It is hard to deny that the weather had a negative impact on the offense, and if they hope to compete in January, they must find a way to overcome the elements.
The Bengals rookie's on offense flashed high potential tonight with Endries catching four balls for 33 yards alongside Young's touchdown. Since Erick All Jr. suffered another unfortunate injury, Endries has consistently seen his role within the offense increase and he has seized the opportunity.
Both Brown and Perine failed in pass-protection in this game, though unlike Perine, Brown did not make up for those mishaps elsewhere. Brown only managed 36 yards on 11 touches and dropped two passes that could have set the offense up in better positions.
The opportunities in front of the Bengals tonight were massive outside of the AFC North. With the Jaguars losing the Giants on Sunday they had a chance to jump a team who beat them earlier in the season. Now at 7-3, it is difficult to see a path to the number one seed in the playoffs with the Bills at 9-1, and the Chiefs and Broncos both at 8-2.
Achieving the number one seed in the AFC Playoffs is still not impossible, but the path towards gaining that privilege just got much more difficult than before.

title: How the Benching of Aaron Rodgers Benefits the Browns
full_text:
The Cleveland Browns are used to bringing dysfunction to the AFC North with their actions both on and off the field.
However, there has not been a peep heard from Berea, and they sit second in the division at 6-4. The stalwart of the division, historically, has been the Pittsburgh Steelers until this season.
The Steelers and coach Mike Tomlin parted ways at the end of last season after 19 years with zero losing seasons. Now the story has changed, as new coach Mike McCarthy benched Aaron Rodgers overnight in favor of Mason Rudolph.
Rodgers has had his lowest completion percentage of his career, but he should still give the Steelers the best chance to win. They are on a two-game losing streak after getting blown out by the Cincinnati Bengals and then dropping a close game against the two-win Philadelphia Eagles.
No matter how Rudolph performs, it looks as though Rodgers is finished in Pittsburgh. He did not show up to the team meeting Wednesday morning, which could signal his end.
Rodgers and McCarthy had a contentious relationship prior to his benching, and the relationship seems to be unsalvageable.
The Steelers’ first team meeting today was scheduled for 8 am, and Aaron Rodgers was not at the team’s training facility at that time. pic.twitter.com/yIYmWfrXKf
The path to the playoffs has now changed for the Browns, as they are the sixth seed in the AFC, one spot ahead of the Steelers.
Both teams are tied, but the Browns have the tiebreaker as of now due to their record within the division.
The Steelers should be underdogs in their next three games, and they play the Baltimore Ravens twice in the last four weeks. The Ravens are having a down year, but the offense has turned around under Jacoby Brissett, and their matchups are always physical. The Browns have the easier schedule for the rest of the season.
The other teams trailing the Browns are the New England Patriots, who lost Drake Maye. Behind them are the Houston Texans at 4-6, and the Browns already beat them head-to-head to win the tiebreaker. The Las Vegas Raiders raced off to a 3-0 start, but have fallen to 4-7. If the Browns can beat them Sunday night, then they will be all but finished .
There is blood in the water for the last wild-card spot, but it’s not the Browns’.
Not only do the benching and fallout with Rodgers benefit the Browns’ playoff hopes, but it also shows the turnaround and shift in the division.
The Browns were on a two-game losing streak, falling to 5-4 and out of a playoff position. Todd Monken did not panic and stuck with Deshaun Watson after missing a week with a concussion.
They fell down 17-0 against the Texans, and fans were ready for Shedeur Sanders to come out and spark the offense. The belief Monken had in Watson paid off as he had his best three-quarters of the season to lead the Browns to a victory and back into the playoff race.
The move to bench Rodgers and his reaction is a typical move the Browns would make in years past, but now the shoe is on the other foot, and the Browns are the ones making responsible decisions. As a result, they are poised to finish ahead of the Steelers in the division. The Browns sit only one game out of the Cincinnati Bengals, and they play each other two times in the last seven games.
The Browns’ roster is so young, and they do not care about the past. Monken has everyone in the organization on the same page, and there has been no discontent .
Rodgers' benching is an alarm that change is coming in the AFC North.
And fortunately, the Browns aren't at the center of negative attention for once.

title: Jared Verse Believes He's Improving, But One Thing Is Still Missing
full_text:
When the Cleveland Browns traded away future Hall of Fame defensive end Myles Garrett, all eyes were on who his replacement would be.
Fortunately, young edge rusher Jared Verse, who was acquired in the trade, quickly emerged during the offseason. He worked with players outside of practice hours, maintained a vocal and standout presence in the media spotlight and seemed poised for a big 2026 season for the Browns' defense.
But through the first 10 games of the year, Verse has struggled . That role he was expected to fill may have been too much pressure for him to handle.
Multiple times now, his public comments have been used as motivation and a competitive edge for opposing teams, all while he has yet to record a sack and is posting career-low numbers across the board in other areas.
Despite the lack of production in the box score, Verse believes his performance against the Houston Texans in Week 10 was a step in the right direction.
On Wednesday, Nov. 25, Verse spoke to the media ahead of the Browns' primetime Week 12 meeting with the Las Vegas Raiders. He was asked how he felt he played against the Texans, whom the Browns beat to improve to 6-4 on the season.
“I think I was my best self that game," he said. "I did exactly what I had to do. I closed the B gap with the tackle, I was able to set the edge, I was able to get to [CJ] Stroud a couple times. Didn’t end up getting a sack but getting in his face, hitting him.
"I won most of my rushes, so I feel like I impacted the game in the aspect I need to.”
Browns DE Jared Verse on his performance against the Texans: “I think I was my best self that game. I did exactly what I had to do. I closed the B gap with the tackle, I was able to set the edge, I was able to get to Stroud a couple times. Didn’t end up getting a sack but getting… https://t.co/pAyktiUzBv
And while it would have been nice to see a sack recorded, the 26-year-old is right; it probably was his best game this year. He registered season-best marks in pressures with five and total pressure rate with 17.9%, routinely getting into the backfield to disrupt the Texans' passing game.
But there is still work to be done, especially as he searches for his first sack of the season.
In the win over the Texans, after allowing 17 quick points, the entire defensive unit anchored down, allowing just seven points across the next 41 minutes of the game . CJ Stroud, surprisingly, was sacked just once, though.
Browns DE Jared Verse registered season-high marks in pressures (5) and pressure rate (17.9%) against the Texans.
Verse has certainly slowly but surely gotten better since the first few weeks of the season, but that ability to get in the backfield and register sacks is something he needs to start doing, not just for the team's ability to shut down opposing offenses, but for his own confidence.
Prior to the Texans game, he revealed that in order to break out of the slump he's in and regain that mindset he once had, he had been seeing team psychiatrist Dr. Mayur Pandya.
“I’m upset with the way I’ve been playing," Verse said back on Nov. 12. "I don’t think it’s physical; there’s nothing wrong with my body. I think it was the mental aspect of the game and I’ve attacked that very well these past couple weeks. But I think this past week is a key thing that I’ve done. I’m very excited for next week."
Coming out of a Week 11 bye , Verse has all the opportunities in front of him to go out there and break his sack-less streak against a rookie quarterback-led Raiders offense.
The Browns and Raiders will meet from Huntington Bank Field on Sunday, Nov. 29, at 8:20 p.m. EST.

title: Browns QB Shedeur Sanders Gives Cleveland Shoppers a Thanksgiving Surprise
full_text:
Pilar Sanders was looking for her son in the aisles of Dave’s Market.
“It’s a pop-up surprise,” she told her Instagram followers as she tried to catch up with him. Two days before Thanksgiving, Cleveland Browns quarterback Shedeur Sanders stopped at the East 61st Street store in Cleveland after practice to pay for shoppers’ groceries.
His mom was there to share the moment.
“And it’s more than just a Thanksgiving dinner, too...So many people are being blessed today. It's so much fun!” Pilar said in her Instagram video .
Thanksgiving can bring the joy of getting everyone around the same table and the worry of figuring out how to pay for what goes on it. For the shoppers Sanders sent to the checkout, one of those worries was taken care of.
In footage from News 5 Cleveland , Sanders told one shopper to get in the middle line, where he’d heard they were giving away free groceries.
“Oh, okay. I need that,” the shopper replied.
“You're ahead of the game now,” Sanders said as he showed the customer where to go.
Kandis Maxwell was among the shoppers Sanders invited to the checkout. She told News 5 Cleveland she had kids and that Sanders was her favorite Browns quarterback. Meeting him was a surprise in itself. Having him pay for her groceries meant something more.
“It just came at a good time and it was unexpected,” Maxwell said. “I’m just thankful.”
Asked what Cleveland had come to mean to him, Sanders talked about the respect people showed one another and how the city had supported the entire team.
“I think that’s just we’re all trending in the right direction here in Cleveland. I’m excited,” he told News 5 Cleveland.
There was still time for a little football talk. When a shopper asked if Sanders would start Sunday against the Las Vegas Raiders, the quarterback pointed to how the Browns were playing .
“You got to think we are winning and we are doing what we got to do,” he told the fan. “Of course I want to play. I’m going to be aggressive when I get out there.”
Sanders threw for 297 yards and two touchdowns in his first start of the season, an overtime loss to New Orleans on Nov. 8. Deshaun Watson returned the following week as Cleveland beat Houston. The Browns come out of their bye at 6–4 and host Las Vegas on Sunday night .
Sanders said he picked this day because he knew plenty of people would be shopping. He also talked about the times someone had shown him an unexpected kindness and how even a few words could change his outlook.
At Dave’s Market, he had a chance to do something for the people right in front of him.
“You don’t know how long you may be alive,” Sanders said. “So you might as well do it while you can.”

title: Todd Monken Warns Browns About Challenge of Facing Raiders' TE Brock Bowers
full_text:
Browns Head coach Todd Monken is a vocal leader. The kind of guy that players love to have in their corner.
All season long, he has shown not only a deep desire to win and succeed on Sundays, but also a commitment to helping both new and veteran players keep improving. Even now, as the head coach of the Cleveland Browns, he is quick to recognize and praise opposing competitors, even those who could stand in the Browns' way of coming away with a win.
On Tuesday, Nov. 24, Monken took time during his media availability to praise Las Vegas Raiders tight end and former Georgia Bulldog Brock Bowers. The Browns are taking on Bowers and the Raiders this coming Sunday, Nov. 29, at 8:20 p.m. EST in a primetime showdown from Huntington Bank Field.
"He's just wired the right way, man. He's unique," Monken said. "He's rare. From the moment he got to Georgia, I always tell the story: we used to mess with him and call him Buddy the Ole' Lab. You could play ball all day, and his tongue would be hanging out, and he never wanted to come out. He would just want to keep playing..."
Monken, the Bulldogs' offensive coordinator from 2020 through 2022, coached Bowers during his freshman and sophomore seasons. He said that from the moment Bowers came into the program, he excelled.
"He got to Georgia, and we were in the stadium. Winter conditioning," Monken continued. "You are doing the old-school run: run the long, walk the short around the football field... You had to run as a group... So, there were groups together, and I will never forget this... On his first day there, they had to meet a certain time; they start running, and he is 10 yards in front of all of them. Now, I could never have done that.
"Here, you are first day; you are going to run with the pack; everyone is going to say you're showboating, you are trying to impress the coaches; that is all he knows. All he knows is one speed and work..."
During Monken's span coaching Bowers, the Bulldogs won back-to-back national championships and Bowers was one of the offensive catalysts, hauling in 119 receptions for 1,824 yards and 20 touchdowns . He also rushed 13 times for 165 yards and four scores.
Browns HC Todd Monken talks about #Raiders TE Brock Bowers who he coached at Georgia pic.twitter.com/oImPaEcus0
Monken went on to joke that he hopes Bowers is still hurt this weekend, which would give the Browns an advantage this weekend in defending the passing attack. Obviously, he doesn't actually mean it, though.
"And uh, hopefully, he is still hurt," he said with a grin.
Bowers has been dealing with both ankle and quadriceps injuries that kept him out of the Raiders' Week 11 loss to the Denver Broncos . Without him in the game, the passing attack leaned more towards Ashton Jeanty and Jack Bech, with the tight end targets going to Ian Thomas and Michael Mayer.
While Bowers is a really important piece to the Raiders' offense, rookie Fernando Mendoza, being so fresh and impressionable, has allowed him to adjust to whoever he ends up getting on the field with.
But as Monken alluded to, if the Browns can match up with the Raiders on Sunday without Bowers on the field, they will be in a much better position to lock down the former No. 1 overall pick.
Cade Cracas is a sports media professional with experience in play-by-play, broadcasting and digital storytelling. He is a recent graduate of Ashland University with degrees in digital media production and journalism.

title: Browns Could Be One Defensive Addition Away From Becoming a Championship Threat
full_text:
The Cleveland Browns’ 2026 season is shaping up to be a memorable one, with the team firmly engaged in the race for the playoffs despite below-average quarterback play and a running game that scares no one.
Coordinator Mike Rutenberg’s defensive unit has been a big factor in the Browns’ surprising season, managing to keep most games close enough for quarterback Deshaun Watson to turn it on late and lead a number of fourth-quarter comebacks.
Cleveland’s defense features several big-time names, including cornerback Denzel Ward, who’s playing the best ball of his life at 29 years old , and second-year wonder Carson Schwesinger , who’s already earned a spot among the league’s top linebackers. Standout rookie Emmanuel McNeil-Warren has also been making noise despite starting just four games this year. And they’ve managed all this despite trading away all-World defensive end Myles Garrett during the offseason.
The Browns are currently ranked fifth-best in passing defense (2,011 yards), second-best in passing completion percentage allowed (58.8), second-best in tackles for a loss (64), and seventh-best in yards allowed after the catch (980) after 10 games.
However solid this group looks week after week, it’s still not part of the truly elite echelon in the league--not by a long shot.
The Browns aren’t so bright in many other aspects of defensive play, including 10th-worst in rushing defense (1,263), 10th-worst in rushing yards per game (126.3), sixth-worst in rushing yards per attempt (4.6), and 10th-worst in quarterback hurry percentage.
And the team is downright mediocre in other spots as well, such as points allowed per game (22.0, tied 14th), takeaways (13, tied 14th), and sacks (27, tied 11th).
Personnel-wise, Cleveland is still waiting for Jared Verse’s breakout game after recording zero sacks, zero passes defended, zero forced fumbles, zero fumbles recovered, and just four tackles for a loss after the first 10 games in a Browns uniform.
Mason Graham started the season on fire, but has since slowed down statistically after knee and ankle injuries forced him to miss two games in October, while Derek Barnett --a late offseason addition to the defensive line-- is also sackless and has one forced fumble and one tackle for a loss in 10 appearances for the club.
Yes, but it won’t be easy. Over the past 15 months, NFL teams have traded away generational talents in their prime, such as Micah Parsons, Jeffery Simmons, and, of course, Garrett.
The Browns own two first-rounders and three fourth-rounders in 2027, two second-rounders in 2028, and two third-rounders in 2029, so there are ample resources to work with if another marquee name should come up available during the next offseason.
A couple of big names to watch in case a trade market materializes are the Niners’ Nick Bosa and the Raiders’ Maxx Crosby.
Bosa is tricky. He hasn’t recorded a sack in five appearances this year, and injuries are clearly piling up. He hasn’t compiled double-digit sacks since 2023, and at 29 years of age, it’s hard to expect him to get substantially better than what we’re seeing right now.
But those numbers, coupled with two remaining years on his deal with no guaranteed money, mean he could be available, with the acquiring team signing an extension to lower projected cap hits of around $33 million and $34 million for 2027 and 2028, respectively. San Francisco would also need to agree to take on a dead cap charge of $49 million by letting him walk, which isn’t impossible.
A Crosby trade had already been agreed upon during this past offseason for two Ravens’ first-rounders, before Baltimore backed out of the deal . Unlike Bosa, it doesn’t seem like Crosby has lost a step, so that figure might still be the going rate for his services, along with about $85 million for the three remaining years on his deal, which only includes about $29 million guaranteed for 2027. That sounds enticing. But if Crosby were put on the trading block again, expect him to have multiple suitors.
A talent like Crosby, coupled with Verse's expected breakthrough, should instantly change the dynamics up front for the Browns, for the better.
A couple of non-elite but still very interesting names to keep tabs on would include the Steelers’ Alex Highsmith and the Eagles’ Nolan Smith. If we’re talking about help on the inside, the Eagles’ Jalen Carter instantly becomes the biggest name out there.
Potential free agent alternatives at edge rusher include the Bills’ Greg Rousseau, Chargers’ Tuli Tuipulotu, and Rams’ Byron Young. While these names would save the team valuable draft capital, the financial burden of an open-market free agent contract could become unbearable in the medium term.
Other names to watch in free agency include Bucs’ YaYa Diaby, Titans’ Jermaine Johnson II, and Giants Kayvon Thibodeaux, with all those names likely commanding deals worth around $20 million and upwards per year. Rams’ Kobie Turner would surely draw a similar figure at the tackle position.
Regardless, expect the Browns to add more bodies to the defensive line via the draft, with a high chance of a top-round pick, depending on what the team decides to do at the quarterback position.
Outside of Crosby, it's hard to find one name that could change it all for Cleveland. Therefore, a multiple-reinforcement strategy looks like the safest bet. Nonetheless, the defensive line should be the top priority on defense.
Rafael brings more than two decades worth of experience writing all things football.

title: Todd Monken Gets Honest About Browns' Week 11 Bye
full_text:
The Cleveland Browns' 2026 bye couldn't have come at a better time.
Following a Week 10 win over the Houston Texans at home, 27-24 , the Browns marched right into a Week 11 bye, giving themselves time to reset and regroup ahead of the back half of the regular season.
Fortunately, while they didn't suit up this past weekend, they got plenty of wins as the Baltimore Ravens, Pittsburgh Steelers and Cincinnati Bengals all lost. Not only does that give the Browns a big opportunity to take the No. 1 spot in the AFC North , but they also now sit in sixth in the playoff bracket.
Head coach Todd Monken spoke to the media on Tuesday, Nov. 24, shedding light on how this bye week couldn't have come at a better time.
"... I told the team this morning. I hope they enjoyed their time away. They earned that," Monken said. "...And we have earned the right to be where we are at, and that same old saying: 'so what, now what.' All we can control is having the best Tuesday that we can today. That's all we can do.
"...All that matters is the day we have today and getting ourselves ready to fight like hell to seven [wins]."
With the entire AFC North losing this weekend, the bye week couldn’t have gone better for Todd Monken and #Browns . pic.twitter.com/KHPvmgarpN
The Browns, unlike many teams this Thanksgiving week, won't have to suit up for a mid-week affair.
The Green Bay Packers play on Wednesday night against the Los Angeles Rams, and the Chicago Bears, Detroit Lions, Philadelphia Eagles, Dallas Cowboys, Kansas City Chiefs and Buffalo Bills all play on Thursday for Thanksgiving.
Monken went on to say that it was nice that the Browns didn't have to change their practice schedule around, especially coming out of the bye.
"It worked out great for us," he said. "In my opinion, having the bye last week, to bring them back today, have today be like a normal Wednesday practice, tomorrow be like a normal Thursday, then Thursday morning we have the ability to basically get ahead of redzone, walk on Thursday... and then really recap what we have installed the first two days and then get the guys out of here.
"Like I said before, it is a unique opportunity here. Because normally you are scrambling to install on Thursday and let the guys have time with their family and friends... Because all have a lot to be thankful for..."
Todd Monken is thankful the #Browns bye week came right before Thanksgiving pic.twitter.com/5ob08fUGS3
While Monken's comments sure are correct, the only hope now is that the players didn't waste the bye week and added free time to their schedules, but instead used it to get ready for a critical stretch of the season.
The Browns return to the field Sunday night, matching up with the Las Vegas Raiders and former No. 1 overall pick Fernando Mendoza. Initially scheduled for a 1:00 p.m. EST kickoff, the game was flexed to primetime and will now be played at 8:20 p.m. EST.
Cade Cracas is a sports media professional with experience in play-by-play, broadcasting and digital storytelling. He is a recent graduate of Ashland University with degrees in digital media production and journalism.

title: This Once Controversial College QB Could Fly Under the Radar as Browns Draft Target
full_text:
The Browns will be in the market for a quarterback during the 2027 NFL Draft. However, Cleveland might be facing a reality that it didn't expect before the season started.
With the Browns sitting at a 6-4 record and possibly heading to the playoffs, they may be unable to draft a quarterback in the top 10. The Browns also have the Los Angeles Rams' first-round pick, but that selection could end up being in the late teens to early 20s, much like Cleveland is projected to be.
If the Browns can't move up to grab their quarterback, they might have to look at someone flying under the radar, and this could be a solution.
Brendan Sorsby hasn't played college football this season because the NCAA ruled him ineligible due to sports gambling violations. Sorsby began his career at Indiana, then transferred to Cincinnati before moving to Texas Tech, where he was supposed to finish his college career.
But his gambling violations became public in April, and it did seem like he wasn't going to play college football again after it became known that he bet on his own teams.
"Sorsby was ruled ineligible by the NCAA after it discovered he had wagered approximately $90,000 on professional and college sports over four years, including 40 bets involving Indiana football when he was a freshman with the Hoosiers in 2022. The NCAA denied Texas Tech's appeal for reinstatement," ESPN's Max Olson wrote in June.
The Browns may have a hard no on adding Sorsby, as bringing in a player with a history of sports gambling is a significant risk. Cleveland could reach out to its neighbors, the Guardians, and see what gambling issues did to their team. Their star closer, Emmanuel Clase, and starting pitcher, Luis Ortiz, are currently on trial for alleged gambling violations involving their own team.
Sorbsy did enter a gambling addiction program in late April, so maybe he did turn the corner, and there is nothing to worry about on that end. If that is the case, Cleveland might have to consider spending a Day 2 pick on him.
CBS Sports draft analyst Ryan Wilson wrote in June that if Sorsby had entered the 2026 NFL Draft, he could've been the second quarterback taken behind Fernando Mendoza, whom the Las Vegas Raiders took No. 1.
"The supplemental draft eliminates any such luxury. It forces teams to decide now, whether they feel ready or not. And after revisiting this most recent quarterback class, here's where I landed: If Sorsby had entered the 2026 NFL Draft, he would've been QB2," Wilson wrote.
Sorsby tried to enter the 2026 supplemental draft, but the league decided not to proceed, which meant Sorsby couldn't enter the league until the 2027 NFL Draft.
Sorsby's gambling violation isn't the only red flag; he hasn't played football all season. The Browns are familiar with the risks of adding a quarterback who hasn't played all season, as they previously traded for Deshaun Watson, who sat out the entire 2021 season with the Houston Texans.
Watson joined the Cleveland Browns in 2022, but the NFL suspended him for 11 games due to violations of the league's personal conduct policy following sexual misconduct allegations.
Watson didn't play for a season and a half, then got thrown into action in December 2022, and he hasn't shown much until this season. He did suffer a few injuries in Cleveland that hurt his playing time as well, but much of the reason he never looked like his old self could have been sitting for almost two years while he was healthy.
Sorsby shouldn't be the Browns' first, second, or even third choice at quarterback.
However, if not enough college quarterbacks entering the draft are viable first-round picks, Cleveland may have to consider someone like Sorsby in the second or third round.
He could have been a top-10 pick if not for his off-the-field issues.
Daniel is a sports writer from Northeast Ohio. He has followed the Browns, Cavs, Guardians, and Buckeyes for years and loves sharing his thoughts on the team.

title: Bengals Loss Puts Browns In Perfect Position To Chase Top Spot in AFC North
full_text:
The Cleveland Browns are alive and well heading out of Week 11.
While they may have gotten a bye, many of the teams the Browns needed to lose did, giving them the best-case scenario heading into the final stretch of the 2026 regular season.
On Nov. 23, in a Monday Night Showdown, the Cincinnati Bengals fell to the Washington Commanders 22-20. The loss moves the Bengals to 7-3 on the season, while the 6-4 Browns now sit just a game behind them for the top spot in the AFC North.
The Bengals, Ravens, and Steelers all lost in week 11 with the Browns on a bye week. The Browns are 1 game back of the Bengals in the AFC North. pic.twitter.com/zqsHvb2xFa
This past weekend, the Pittsburgh Steelers and Baltimore Ravens all lost as well, dropping to 6-4 and 4-7, respectively.
The Browns are now the only team in the AFC North with a winning streak intact heading into Week 12.
Whether the Browns are legit or not, the schedule down the back half of the year favors them tremendously.
In Week 12, the Browns will take on the Fernando Mendoza-led Las Vegas Raiders, a young team that is still trying to find its footing, in a primetime meeting . The Raiders are just 4-7 this year and coming off a 38-24 defeat to the Denver Broncos.
The Browns return from their bye week as the AFC’s sixth seed and are 4.5-point home favorites against the Raiders, per DraftKings.
Over the course of the next five games following the Raiders affair, the Browns will clash with the Bengals, Atlanta Falcons, New York Giants, Ravens and Indianapolis Colts. The Browns and Bengals will play in Week 13 and Week 18.
While the Raiders, Falcons, Giants, Ravens and Colts all appear to be favorable matchups for the Browns, particularly with four of those teams sitting below .500, Cleveland's two matchups against the Bengals could prove to be the most consequential games remaining on its schedule.
Normally pulling headlines because of the state ties, the Browns and Bengals' meetings this season will have more of a say on where the two teams finish in the North than in years past.
In Week 13, it could be the difference between the Browns being stuck in second for the rest of the season or making the No. 1 spot a tug-of-war match. Then, in Week 18, as long as both sides keep their current pace going, that meeting could end up deciding some final seedings.
And along the way, there is still a chance for the Steelers to regain some momentum and make the climb.
Steelers lost. Browns move up to second in the AFC North 😎 pic.twitter.com/bsX5xkjqWL
In a year when the Browns were written off, with plenty of doubt cast on the team's ability to play competitive football on Sundays, led by head coach Todd Monken, they have just found a way to keep winning.
Now, it is all about finishing the year strong and not letting the positives, and rest, that came during the bye week affect their momentum.
Cade Cracas is a sports media professional with experience in play-by-play, broadcasting and digital storytelling. He is a recent graduate of Ashland University with degrees in digital media production and journalism.

title: Why Cleveland’s 6-4 Start Should Change How the Browns Approach the 2027 NFL Draft
full_text:
The Cleveland Browns were expected to be picking high in the 2027 NFL draft, but the young roster and veteran quarterback have raced out to six wins before their bye week .
At the start of the season, there was buzz about a new crop of quarterbacks eligible for the draft. The crowded quarterback class has since thinned out, and if the season ended after Week 11, the Browns would be picking 17th (from the Los Angeles Rams) and 20th.
It was believed that Deshaun Watson got the starting job at the beginning of the season in order to better evaluate the young offensive players and a completely rebuilt offensive line. His veteran presence allowed him to make correct reads and put the players in the best position to succeed.
The Browns could then turn to Shedeur Sanders for their first home game, and he would have the season as an audition.
Winning six games and counting put a kibosh on what this season’s accomplishments could be. The plan was to draft their quarterback for the future, as the rest of the roster is ready to win. Now the draft strategy should be to supplement, rather than build.
They will draft too low to get the first- or second-best quarterback. Watson has played better each week, and he may earn himself a short-term extension in the offseason. The Browns cannot hand the talented roster over to a quarterback who may not be ready to start.
The Browns also have Dillon Gabriel and Taylen Green. Outside of Watson, every quarterback is on a rookie contract, and picking a project at the quarterback position would crowd the room. Not having to choose a quarterback would open the possibilities to draft for depth.
🚨2027 MIDSEASON NFL MOCK DRAFT🚨 1-Titans: Jeremiah Smith, WR, Ohio State 2-Chargers: Colin Simmons, Edge, Texas 3-Dolphins: Drew Mestemaker, QB, Oklahoma State 4-Jets: CJ Carr, QB, Notre Dame 5-Eagles: Dylan Stewart, Edge, South Carolina 6-Jets*: Chris Cole, LB, Georgia… https://t.co/qEY7afiq47 pic.twitter.com/1CDKkfdfOI
In years past, the Browns would need their third- and fourth-round picks to start and play meaningful snaps. Now that the roster is built up and producing, they can draft for depth. The offensive line has two rookie starters, and more should be added early in the draft.
The knock on Spencer Fano coming out of college was his arm-length, and that he may be better suited to play guard. If there is a bigger tackle in the draft, he could move Fano to guard, fortifying an entire side of the line.
The Browns could also draft a wide receiver in the first round. Jerry Jeudy has turned his season around, but his production does not match his contract.
If the Browns choose to move on from Jeudy during the offseason, then they could add a rookie. Andrew Berry picked two wide receivers in the last draft, both of whom are Offensive Rookie of the Year candidates.
The defense has been gashed in the running game, and their leader in sacks is an interior lineman. The Browns need a pass rusher coming off the edge. Alex Wright is out with a season-ending injury, and Isaiah McGuire has been average as his replacement. Jared Verse has been disappointing with zero sacks.
Denzel Ward is having his best season, but he is getting older. He will be approaching his 10th year in the league, and the cornerback position is reliant on speed. They may have to trade up to get one of the better cornerbacks out of college, but they have ammunition.
Later picks can be used for depth pieces. The defensive line and linebackers are top-heavy, and three fourth-round picks can allow them to deepen the positions. They can also draft for specific needs. The offense needs a blocking tight end. The Browns will be in a position to draft the best one, as they do not need to use all their picks on starters.
Cleveland is used to focusing on the draft by October, but the fast 6-4 start has changed that. The best teams in the NFL are deep at most positions, but the Browns have continuously had to draft starters. Now they are in a position to build the back end of the roster .
Graduated from Bowling Green State University with a Journalism degree. Written and contributed to numerous media outlets. Cleveland sports victim.

title: Why the Browns Must Steer Clear of Recently Released 49ers WR Brandon Aiyuk
full_text:
The San Francisco 49ers have released Brandon Aiyuk, potentially giving the Cleveland Browns another opportunity to pursue the veteran receiver.
ESPN sources: the 49ers are releasing WR Brandon Aiyuk today. A first-round pick of San Francisco in 2020, Aiyuk now will move on and wants to resume his career elsewhere after not playing in an NFL game since October 2024. pic.twitter.com/5GB59FBEBt
The veteran receiver has spent his entire career with the 49ers but hasn't played an NFL game since the 2024 season because of off-the-field issues and injuries. San Francisco officially released Aiyuk on Nov. 23, two weeks after the NFL reinstated him from the reserve/left squad list.
But even though he is now available, the Browns should not jump right into the mix to try to land him.
Aiyuk was selected by the 49ers in the first round of the 2020 NFL Draft with the 25th overall pick. Aiyuk quickly lived up to his draft status, recording 748 receiving yards and five touchdowns in his rookie year. His best season as a pro came in 2023, when Aiyuk caught 75 passes for 1,342 yards and seven touchdowns.
Brandon Aiyuk’s last healthy season: - 75 Receptions - 1,342 Yards - 7 TD’s This was in 2023, on just 105 targets Aiyuk put up 1,342 yards.. For context: - Aiyuk’s 1,342 yards ranked 6th in the NFL - Aiyuk’s 105 targets ranked 30th in the NFL Brandon Aiyuk was just entering… pic.twitter.com/FTjQL9UtXo
Following Aiyuk’s best season, a contract dispute the following offseason led San Francisco to explore potential trades.
During the preseason of 2024, the Cleveland Browns and San Francisco 49ers began building the framework of a deal to send Aiyuk to Cleveland. The proposed deal would reportedly have sent Amari Cooper, a second-round pick, and a fifth-round pick to the 49ers. The 49ers entertained trade conversations for Aiyuk at the time due to a contract dispute, as Aiyuk’s rookie deal was near its end.
Aiyuk reportedly rejected the proposed move to Cleveland. He ultimately signed a four-year, $120 million extension with San Francisco, but his relationship with the organization later deteriorated.
Aiyuk tore his ACL and MCL in Week 7 of the 2024 season and has not played an NFL game since. San Francisco later voided $27 million in guarantees after he missed required rehabilitation sessions and team activities.
This situation then spiraled into Aiyuk publicly criticizing and taunting the 49ers. A video of him speeding past the 49ers' home, Levi’s Stadium, even led to him receiving an arrest warrant for an alleged misdemeanor exhibition of speed. The 49ers ultimately released him when his two-week roster exemption expired on Nov. 23.
Brandon Aiyuk has been issued an arrest warrant for speeding and reckless driving next to Levi’s Stadium. pic.twitter.com/4xUkV6LIaM
Despite Cleveland’s past interest, they should steer clear of the once-star wide receiver. Aiyuk’s off-the-field issues could threaten what seems to be a bonded locker room with antics that do not contribute to wins. Furthermore, the Browns are deep at wide receiver.
Rookies Denzel Boston and KC Concepcion have been the backbone of the passing attack, and veteran Jerry Jeudy has settled into his third-option role well, coming up with multiple big catches. There is no reason to take snaps away from the three when they have been successful.
Pursuing a former first-round pick as a reclamation project would fit Andrew Berry’s track record, but it doesn’t make sense for Cleveland now. The Browns have depth at Aiyuk’s position and do not need baggage anymore in their locker room.
While Aiyuk’s past production is intriguing, it is not worth threatening the Browns’ playoff push.
Noah Olson is a Northeast Ohio native and lifelong Cleveland sports fan. He graduated from The College of Wooster with a major in Communications and has been sports writing since 2024. As a writer for BIGPLAY On SI, Noah brings a blend of local pride and an insider’s perspective, focusing on thoughtful analysis and storytelling rooted in Cleveland sports culture.

title: Aaron Rodgers’ Pat McAfee Interview Unveils Major Mike McCarthy Issues With Cowboys
full_text:
Less than 24 hours after getting benched, Pittsburgh Steelers quarterback Aaron Rodgers went scorched earth on head coach Mike McCarthy and revealed several issues he has had with the team while also noting those issues were prevalent during McCarthy's coaching stint with the Dallas Cowboys .
Rodgers made the allegations on "The Pat McAfee Show" in what is one of the most wild situations we've seen in the NFL in quite some time.
Rodgers noted that everything he saw out of McCarthy, which includes some very inexcusable and embarrassing things if true, were issues he had with the Cowboys, and before that, with the Green Bay Packers.
"I looked into what happened in Dallas, and it's the same thing that happened for 10 years in Green Bay," Rodgers said, citing people who worked with McCarthy in both Dallas and Green Bay.
Here's a look at some of the things Rodgers mentioned about McCarthy from their time together with the Steelers.
Among the revelations from Rodgers, he said McCarthy fell asleep in a meeting last week and was even heard snoring. Making matters worse, McCarthy then left the meeting early.
“Last Wednesday, we were in a quarterback meeting. Mike came in late, sat down and within 10 minutes began snoring," Rodgers said. "Woke himself up, was rattling his papers. We all looked around. Five minutes later, you hear the snoring again.
"And less than five minutes after that, he walks out of the room like nothing happened.”
Rodgers also said that McCarthy has missed meetings and walkthroughs.
“Thursday, he misses an offensive meeting. Friday, he doesn’t come to the walk-through. Doesn’t come to the first walk-through, doesn’t come to the protection walk-through on Thursday," he added. "Saturday, he misses the morning meeting, and we don’t have a team meeting Saturday night for whatever reason in Philly."
Rodgers then went on to note that McCarthy admitted he had fallen behind with watching film.
All of that and we haven't even mentioned the most embarrassing part: Rodgers said McCarthy even broke down the team with a "1, 2, 3 Packers" chant that left Steelers players stunned.
"Mike McCarthy broke down the Steelers saying 1, 2, 3 Packers," Rodgers said.
Rodgers claims that other players and coaches on the team can back him up with everything he's saying because he wasn't the only one to witness all of these things from McCarthy.
According to Nick Harris of the Fort Worth Star-Telegram , some of the issues Rodgers talked about with McCarthy in Pittsburgh were indeed prevalent in Dallas.
"If anything wrote the end of Mike McCarthy’s tenure as much as a lack of playoff success in Dallas, it was the things that Aaron Rodgers is talking about here," Harris wrote.
"Laziness when it came to game-planning, outwardly not caring about draft evaluations, players having to confront him (see bye week 2023)," Harris added. "None of this should be a surprise to people that watched the end of his Dallas tenure play out."
Now we're starting to see why McCarthy's tenure in Dallas ended . It's a safe bet the 7-10 record in 2024 wasn't the only reason .

title: Cooper Beebe's Elite Rankings Prove Cowboys Center is Primed For Massive Payday
full_text:
Don't look now, but Dallas Cowboys center Cooper Beebe has quietly been the best center in the NFL this season.
Well, at least according to Pro Football Focus ' metrics that have him as the highest-graded player at his position in the league.
According to PFF, Beebe's 79.3 overall grade ranks first, and he is also top five in run-blocking grade (76.6, ranks fifth) and pass-blocking grade (77.5, ranks fourth).
Those three grades amount to the highest of Beebe's career. And to make his season more impressive, Beebe has not given up a sack, has allowed just 12 pressures while committing just one penalty.
"He has total command of the system," Brian Schottenheimer said of Beebe back in training camp. "I mean, really, total command of the system."
“He’s been a great communicator, I would say, when he first came to the league and had to play young," Schotty added. "He's an elite communicator, and then his ability to control his body and stay connected — really important.
“Cooper Beebe continues to get better and better and better.”
With the way Beebe is playing , the former third-round pick is going to garner himself a hefty contract extension down the road. He is first eligible for a new deal after this season.
The good news for the Cowboys is, they have another year to make a decision on Beebe, as his rookie deal expires after the 2027 campaign.
However, the longer the Cowboys wait, the more expensive Beebe might become if other centers get new deals between now and then.
The current high-water mark for a center contract is Las Vegas Raiders center Tyler Linderbaum, whose three-year deal is worth $81 million, which works out to $27 million per season. The contract also has $60 million fully guaranteed.
But that contract is an outlier because the Raiders went crazy in trying to land a big fish in free agency. Linderbaum's deal leads centers by $9 million in total value and annual average.
The gap between Linderbaum and everyone else when it comes to fully guaranteed money is even bigger at $25 million.
If Beebe were to get paid in 2027, we would expect his contract to be more in line with the second-biggest center deal in the NFL, which comes with Kansas City Chiefs center Creed Humphrey.
Humphrey is on a four-year, $72 million deal, whiich works out to $18 million annually and includes $35 million guaranteed.
Figure something along the lines of four years, $74 million, with north of $30 million guaranteed for Beebe, assuming he keeps playing like an elite center.
But if the Cowboys wait too long to extend him, they could be looking at a deal that inches closer to Linderbaum's.

title: Aaron Rodgers, Mike McCarthy Fiasco Proves Cowboys Ditched Coach At Right Time
full_text:
The Dallas Cowboys may be looking for a new coach if Brian Schottenheimer misses the playoffs in back-to-back seasons. It hasn't been the start that many were hoping for when he took over as head coach, but it's been a much better job than his predecessor is at his new home.
There is plenty of silver lining in Dallas, from a red-hot offense to promising young players on defense that the team can build around. Former head coach Mike McCarthy , however, is watching his team fall apart.
McCarthy's biggest issue stems from a strained relationship with veteran quarterback Aaron Rodgers , who was benched late Tuesday night. But the issue is bigger than Rodgers.
According to reports, frustration with McCarthy is spreading throughout the offense, with the team's inability to air it out and McCarthy's inability to adapt. It looks like McCarthy has lost his touch, and Dallas got out at exactly the right time.
With the downfall in Pittsburgh, the Cowboys avoided a disaster. We have seen Dallas' offense unlocked and thriving, but would that have been possible with McCarthy still at the helm? Looking at the Steelers' offense, CeeDee Lamb and George Pickens would be losing their minds if they were in that situation.
Sure, having an ancient, immobile quarterback doesn't help, but the team isn't even throwing the ball downfield. On Sunday, Rodgers averaged 0.5 air yards per attempt, which is the lowest since ESPN began tracking the stat.
Perhaps that is what led to the frustration in Pittsburgh, which NFL insider Jordan Schultz says is spreading throughout the offense.
"The frustration is not just with Rodgers. Multiple position groups have been upset, and I’m told McCarthy has not been what some offensive players hoped for ," Schultz wrote on X. "Frustration has been growing among everyone for weeks. The Rodgers benching is just the start of what’s being revealed publicly. I’ve also heard players who were used to having Mike Tomlin have struggled with the change."
Things may not be going as well as some may have hoped during the start of the Brian Schottenheimer era, but at least the team isn't falling apart at the seams. Schottenheimer still has the locker room after a season and a half of ups and downs.
Pittsburgh, meanwhile, is crumbling after 11 weeks of Mike McCarthy.
It was time for a change in Dallas, and for once, Jerry Jones made a timely decision that paid off before things were broken beyond repair.

title: NFL Insider Puts Schottenheimer on Hot Seat; Cowboys Demoting Parker Ruffled Feathers
full_text:
If you're a Dallas Cowboys fan who wants to see head coach Brian Schottenheimer gone, you're going to love what ESPN's Jeremy Fowler has to say on the subject.
With the Cowboys sitting at 5-6, Fowler puts Schotty on the hot seat and thinks it will take a playoff berth for the embattled Cowboys coach to keep his job.
Fowler also noted that the vibes coming from Cowboys leadership "are not great," and another interesting nugget was thrown in with his comments on Schottenheimer: Dallas demoting defensive coordinator Christian Parker wasn't a universally-liked move.
"And the vibes out of Dallas leadership are not great. The Christian Parker move was not universally well-received in the building. This might be a case where coach Brian Schottenheimer needs a playoff berth to ensure a third season," Fowler wrote.
Fellow ESPN reporter Dan Graziano agreed with the belief about Schottenheimer's job security.
"And I agree on Schottenheimer," Graziano said. "The Cowboys are more patient with coaches than their reputation would lead you to believe, but they had very high hopes for this season.
"If it fizzles out because they blew the defensive coordinator hire, and Schottenheimer gets to the end of the year with another losing record, I think there would be some smoke there."
It's not surprising to see not everyone loved the Parker decision. We already knew that was the case, at least based on what the Cowboys players were saying about the move .
"Honestly, hurt my heart," rookie defensive back Caleb Downs said. "(Parker is) still one of the people that we're looking to have around, looking to play for, one of our sources of motivation."
"It isn't like he can change what's going on on the field," veteran cornerback Cobie Durant said about senior defensive assistant Mike Pettine, who took over play-calling duties from Parker . "Only we can change that. The play calling is going to be the same… he can't change the 11 guys that're on the field. We have to change that. And that's accountability. We've got to do that."
The Cowboys needed to do something to try and fix their ailing unit, so the move to demote Parker was understandable since Dallas can't do anything personnel-wise.
But that doesn't mean Schottenheimer, Jerry Jones and the rest of the Cowboys' brass don't deserve blame here .
They hired a first-time play-caller knowing there would be growing pains and patience was needed, but they did so ahead of a season in which there was clearly a heightened sense of urgency.
Parker isn't blameless in all of this, but when it comes to being a rookie play-caller, he wasn't in the right situation to begin with.
If it is indeed going to take a playoff berth for Schottenheimer to keep his job, it's not looking good for him.
According to ESPN, the Cowboys are being given a 30% chance to make the playoffs, with a 29% chance to win the division and just a 1% chance to grab a wild-card berth.
It's not hard to see why things are so bleak. Dallas has to make up three games on the New York Giants to finish in first place, and the Cowboys are all the way back in the No. 10 spot in the NFC playoff picture and have to jump the Los Angeles Rams, Seattle Seahawks and Green Bay Packers to get to No. 7.
Making matters worse, the Cowboys have the fourth-toughest remaining slate in the NFL .
If the rest of the season unfolds the way we expect and Fowler is right about Schottenheimer's job security, the Cowboys will be looking for a new coach in 2027.

title: Joe Milton Responds to Dak Prescott's Troll Comment Ahead of Eagles-Cowboys
full_text:
Dak Prescott did a little trolling of Joe Milton before the Dallas Cowboys and Philadelphia Eagles square off on Thursday and Milton has since responded.
During the week when Prescott was asked about Milton, the Dallas signal-caller joked that, in his mind, his former teammate is "still a Cowboy" and he hoped the third-year quarterback will help the Cowboys out in what will be Milton's third career start.
“Very excited. It’ll be fun. Joe knows how I feel about it. He’s still a Cowboy and I’m hoping he helps us out," Prescott said, according to Joseph Hoyt of The Dallas Morning News .
Milton was asked about Dak's comment on Tuesday and made it quite clear that he's all Eagles.
"It was cool, but I'm an Eagle right now, and for the time being, I don't know until my contract is up," Milton said , per Zach Berman of The Athletic. "But as of right now, I'm an Eagle, and that's what it's gonna be. So I'm playing for the Eagles Thursday, and that's what it's gonna be.
"I mean, I respect it, but at the same time, I'm here with these guys, and I'm putting the work in with these guys. I'm grinding blood, sweat, tears with these guys, and just my team right now."
After being drafted in the seventh round by the New England Patriots in 2024, Milton was traded to the Cowboys in 2025 .
Milton, stayed with the team through the 2026 offseason and even made the cut on the team's 53-man roster before he was waived a few days later and brought back on the practice squad.
The third-year signal-caller competed with Sam Howell for the backup job throughout the offseason but clearly did not win because he was cut instead of Howell.
Milton was no doubt frustrated with the decision .
“It was shocking. But it’s life. You got to be able to live with it and deliver blows back when it’s time," Milton said.
Despite his frustration, Milton enjoyed his time with the Cowboys and the coaches were big fans of him, also, so it's conceivable Milton could return to Dallas if things don't work out in Philly.
Milton, who was poached off the Cowboys' practice squad by the Eagles after Jalen Hurts was diagnosed with blood slots, has no doubt struggled over his first two starts in the NFL, which isn't surprising considering his lack of NFL experience.
Milton completed 18-of-34 passes for 169 yards and rushed nine times for 64 yards but didn't find pay dirt in a 19-11 loss to the New York Giants in Week 9.
Then, in Week 11, Milton notched his first win in his second start but only completed 11-of-21 passes for 141 yards scoreless yards.
But Milton has also faced two formidable defenses in a row, and we know the Cowboys don't have one of those, so don't be surprised if it's Dallas who helps Milton to a career-best performance on Thursday.
