title: Worst Quarterbacks To Ever Start Thanksgiving Game For Dallas Cowboys
full_text:
The Dallas Cowboys playing on Thanksgiving is an annual tradition and America's Team will be back in action this week as they host the Philadelphia Eagles . The Week 12 showdown could be huge for the Cowboys, who are 5-6 and desperate to keep their season alive.
Philadelphia has been dealing with a multitude of injuries, and comes into Week 12 with a record of 3-7. They're coming off a win over the Pittsburgh Steelers, a victory that ended a seven-game losing streak.
There will be some added intrigue as former Dallas quarterback Joe Milton III will start in place of an injured Jalen Hurts. While he has the arm strength to make life difficult for the Cowboys' defense, Dallas still has a huge advantage under center with Dak Prescott starting.
Prescott in the midst of a stretch of stellar play, but not every starter on Thanksgiving has delivered for the Cowboys. That said, here's a look at some of the worst quarterbacks they have had to start on Thanksgiving.
A former pitcher who decided to return to football, Chad Hutchinson was signed as a 25-year-old rookie by Dallas in 2002. He started nine games that year and was just 2-7. One of those wins came on Thanksgiving Day as Hutchinson led the Cowboys to a 27-20 victory over Washington.
Hutchinson was just 12-of-25 for 144 yards, but had two touchdown passes and no turnovers. He leaned heavily on Emmitt Smith, who had 144 yards on 23 rushing attempts, which was a smart strategy.
Quincy Carter spent three turbulent seasons with the Cowboys, finally finding success in the 2003 season under head coach Bill Parcells. Carter led Dallas to a 10-6 record that year and a playoff berth. That was also the only year in which Carter started on Thanksgiving Day.
The former Georgia quarterback didn't have a great outing as he took on the Miami Dolphins. Carter was 24-of-40 for 288 yards with two touchdown passes. While those numbers might not be bad, he had three interceptions and a lost fumble. His turnovers were huge in helping the Dolphins win easily , 40-21.
Much like Hutchinson, Drew Henson was a former pitcher who didn't make it in the major leagues and decided to return to football. Henson, who was Tom Brady's former teammate at Michigan, started just one game and it happened to be on Thanksgiving during the 2004 season against the Chicago Bears.
Henson didn't last long as he was benched in favor of Vinny Testaverde after going 4-of-12 for 31 yards with an interception . Dallas won 21-7, but Testaverde and running back Julius Jones deserve the credit for the victory.
It's wild to think there was a time when Ryan Leaf was fighting for the No. 1 spot in the 1998 NFL draft with Peyton Manning. While Manning went on to have a Hall of Fame career, Leaf was one of the biggest busts in NFL history.
After flaming out with the San Diego Chargers, Leaf ended up with the Cowboys, who were desperate for a quarterback. Leaf started three games in 2001 for Dallas, going 0-3 in those starts. That included a loss to the Denver Broncos on Thanksgiving Day.
Leaf went 16-of-32 for 193 yards with no touchdowns, and while he had no interceptions, he did lose one fumble in their 26-24 loss.

title: Dallas Cowboys WRs Catch Huge Break For Thanksgiving Matchup vs Eagles
full_text:
This Thursday, the Dallas Cowboys look for back-to-back wins for the first time since Week 13 of the 2025 season. They know it won’t be easy as they face one of their top rivals on Thanksgiving Day , the Philadelphia Eagles.
Even with Jalen Hurts out, this game could be an interesting one. Joe Milton III is making his third start of the season and will take on the franchise that released him following the preseason. Milton will be out to prove the Cowboys made a mistake, and the Dallas defense has been an easy target for opposing quarterbacks all year.
As concerning as things might be for the Cowboys on the defensive side of the ball, their offense could be in line for another big day. The Eagles pass defense has had its share of struggles, entering Week 12 ranked 17th against the pass .
That already gives the Cowboys an advantage as they enter this one ranked second in offensive passing yardage . Now, the Cowboys receivers gained another advantage as the Eagles ruled out their best cornerback, Quinyon Mitchell, with a hamstring injury.
#Eagles CB Quinyon Mitchell (hamstring) has been ruled out, with a game on Thursday coming.
Mitchell had appeared in all 10 games for the Eagles this season before the injury, recording 41 tackles, 11 pass breakups, and one interception. An All-Pro in 2025, Mitchell currently has a PFF grade of 69.2 overall , which is the 29th highest cornerback grade out of 107 qualified players.
Even if Mitchell were on the field this week, the Cowboys would feel good about their chances to put up a ton of yardage through the air. Dak Prescott, CeeDee Lamb, and George Pickens have been playing lights out over the past three weeks.
Prescott has at least 325 yards in each of the past three games with 11 touchdown passes and just one interception. Pickens was unable to play in Week 9, but in Week 10 he had 11 receptions for 145 yards and three touchdowns. He added 10 catches for 102 yards and a touchdown against the Tennessee Titans.
Lamb has been even more explosive, with 10 catches for 195 yards and one touchdown in Week 9, followed by seven receptions for 72 yards and a touchdown in Week 10, and 11 receptions for 132 yards and a touchdown in Week 11. It's a safe bet that both receivers will threaten to hit triple digits once again this week, especially with Mitchell sitting out.

title: Joey Porter Jr.'s Lockdown Coverage is Forcing Cowboys' Hand on Contract Extension
full_text:
The Dallas Cowboys haven't had much to feel great about on a consistent basis this season. Week after week, negative headlines surround the team, and for good reason.
But one of the lone bright spots for Dallas this year didn't even begin the season on the roster.
Cowboys cornerback Joey Porter Jr. arrived to Dallas prior to Week 4 following a midseason trade with the Pittsburgh Steelers. This marked a fresh start for Porter Jr. following a somewhat messy end to his career with the Steelers.
Though the Cowboys still have some concerning team-wide struggles on defense, Porter Jr. has done everything in his power during the past 55 days since the trade to ensure that Dallas gets things turned around, something that could earn him a new contract in the process.
Porter Jr. is looking to earn a massive new contract this offseason. This dilemma is what led to his holdout with the Steelers, who traded him as a result.
Dallas has a ton of different decisions to make this offseason, but Porter Jr.'s production this year is giving the Cowboys no choice but make his contract extension No. 1 on the list of priorities if he keeps it up.
During his first six games with the Cowboys (all starts), Porter Jr. has allowed just five catches on 15 targets for 35 yards and no touchdowns on 258 defensive snaps, per NFL Pro Stats. This has included 11 total tackles (eight solo), one tackle for loss and five pass breakups.
The possibility of a new contract has been a hot topic of discussion among Cowboys fans, especially when Porter Jr. missed some time due to injury and illness. There was a notion that his absence in Week 5 and Week 9 were a result of another holdout situation.
Porter Jr. made sure to shut that down quickly.
“I don’t know where that narrative came from," Porter Jr. said, per Joseph Hoyt of The Dallas Morning News. "I mean, I get it, it’s the internet, but I don’t really pay no attention to that or do I really care. My goal is to win games and play football.”
A 5-6 record means Dallas still has a ton to play for down the stretch. The Cowboys still have a chance at winning the NFC East in order to clinch a playoff spot. Building momentum starts with Thursday's Thanksgiving Day matchup against the Philadelphia Eagles.
And if Porter Jr. can keep up his impressive play, the Cowboys will have a shot at a second straight win while closing in further on the New York Giants.

title: Cowboys Tuesday Injury Report: 1 Starter Among 2 Upgraded, 3 Players Not Practicing
full_text:
The Dallas Cowboys have put out their second injury report of the week ahead of the Thanksgiving Day matchup against the Philadelphia Eagles on Thursday.
There was a bit of good news to report on Tuesday, as a total of two players were upgraded from estimated non-participants to limited participants, including one starter.
On the flip side, two other starters remained sidelined, and one of the team's wide receivers saw a downgrade in participation from the day prior.
Here's the full injury report for Tuesday.
First, the good news: both linebackers Dee Winters and Jaishawn Barham were upgraded on Tuesday, which gives both a chance to play against the Eagles.
Winters exited the Week 11 game against the Tennessee Titans early with his knee injury and it didn't look good at the time, but clearly it wasn't as bad as initially believed. Barham sat out last week with a hip/groin issue.
Along with those two, more notable good news comes in the form of safety Jalen Thompson, who has now practiced in full for four straight sessions dating back to last week, when he was designated to return from injured reserve .
It looks Thompson has a good chance to get back on the field this week after missing all but three contests in 2026.
Also at safety, the door remains open for P.J. Locke to return from his concussion, although he's going to have to turn in a full practice on Wednesday to have a chance.
Tight end Jake Ferguson and guard Tyler Booker are status quo. Neither one has practiced since suffering their respective injuries and are on track to sit out yet again, which isn't surprising since both were expected to miss multiple games. They have each missed two games in a row.
If Ferguson is sidelined for another game, Luke Schoonmaker and James Mitchell will see increased roles for another week. Mitchell in particular was productive as a pass-catcher in Week 11, with the veteran grabbing two passes for 40 yards.
T.J. Bass will make his sixth start of the season in place of Booker. The veteran guard has not given up a sack this season and has provided solid run-blocking, also.
Wide receiver Jonathan Mingo, who made progress on Monday when he was estimated to be limited, did not take part and is slated to miss his third consecutive game. That would mean increased run for KaVontae Turpin and Camden Brown.
The Cowboys will drop their final injury report of the week on Wednesday, complete with designations for players where applicable.

title: Brian Schottenheimer Praises DeMarvion Overshown For Embracing Reduced Cowboys Role
full_text:
The Dallas Cowboys are making a quick turnaround after their dominant win over the Tennessee Titans in Week 11 . On Tuesday, the team returned to the practice field in pads, and coaches spoke to the media about how they are approaching the week.
Cowboys head coach Brian Schottenheimer was specifically asked about linebacker DeMarvion Overshown, who has seen his role reduced in recent weeks .
Overshown's decrease in usage started after he got an unsportsmanlike conduct penalty for running onto the field and celebrating in street clothes, which led to many wondering whether he was being punished by the team .
Schottenheimer, like Jerry and Stephen Jones, is adamant that the two situations are not related, and instead says it's a way for the Cowboys to maximize Overshown's skillset during a lengthy season.
When asked whether Overshown is in the doghouse and whether that has played a role in his decreased snaps, Schottenheimer said "absolutely not," while praising the linebacker and explaining why the team has been adapting his role.
“ I couldn’t be more proud of the way he's attacking his role ; he's excited about his role," Schottenheimer said. "He's attacking special teams, and again, this is a long season. What we're trying to do is we're trying to utilize as many guys as we can and play to their strengths.
"That's been something that we've been emphasizing over the last couple of weeks.”
Overshown's dynamic speed and sideline-to-sideine ability is a great tool for the Cowboys, but his inability to stay healthy has hurt his ability to become a staple on defense. On special teams, that speed is also an asset, so it's a perfect role as the team aims to get him more involved.
We'll find out how Overshown's role continues to adapt when the Cowboys return to the field on Thanksgiving Day for a showdown with the NFC East rival Philadelphia Eagles . Kickoff at AT&T Stadium is set for 4:30 p.m. ET on FOX.
Kevin Burkhardt and Tom Brady will be on the call for the game, while Pam Oliver and Tom Rinaldi will provide updates from the sideline throughout the evening. Let's hope that Dallas can deliver with another big win and give Cowboys Nation something to be thankful for.

title: Broncos' Jonah Coleman Earns Major NFL Honor After Historic Day
full_text:
It's unfortunate what's happening with J.K. Dobbins and his suspension , but don't let it detract from the Denver Broncos' Jonah Coleman phenomenon.
Coleman rushed for 111 yards and three touchdowns on 24 carries in the Broncos' Week 11 win over the Las Vegas Raiders . The fourth-round rookie running back has been named the AFC Offensive Player of the Week for his historic day against Denver's oldest division rival.
🎩🎩🎩 RT to help us congratulate @jonahcoleman8 on being named AFC Offensive Player of the Week! 👏 pic.twitter.com/dLq30d8EaH
Coleman is the third Bronco to win conference honors this season, joining safety Talanoa Hufanga and linebacker Alex Singleton. Both of those players are veterans, though.
Against the Raiders, Coleman became the first Broncos rookie to rush for 100-plus yards and three touchdowns in a game since Clinton Portis in 2002. Coleman wasn't born until August of 2003, the next summer.
It's been a while since the Broncos have had a running as prolific as Coleman out of the gates. This team went 19 games without a 100-yard individual rusher, but he finally got that monkey off Denver's back.
The last Broncos' rookie running back to make this kind of noise was Phillip Lindsay in 2018, but he didn't have any three-touchdown displays. However, what made Lindsay's emergence so unique was that he was an undrafted rookie, and he'd go on to eclipse 1,000 rushing yards and 10 touchdowns from scrimmage.
Lindsay became the NFL's first undrafted rookie running back to ever be selected to the Pro Bowl. He's also the first undrafted running back to produce back-to-back 1,000-yard rushing seasons to start his career.
As the Offensive Player of the Week, Coleman became just the 12th Broncos running back to earn the award, joining Lindsay (2018), Ronnie Hillman (2015), C.J. Anderson (2014, '15), Knowshon Moreno (2012), Clinton Portis (2003), Mike Anderson (2000), Olandis Gary (1999), Terrell Davis (1996, '97, '98), Gaston Green (1991), Tony Dorsett (1988), and Joe Dudek (1987). The award has only existed since 1984, and a Broncos skill-position player has won it 67 times.
Coleman has a shot at a 1,000-yard rookie campaign, but he'll have to continue producing close to how he did against the Raiders. With 302 yards and six touchdowns thus far, he's got seven games left to try and reach the milestone, and it won't be easy.
In Lindsay's case, he had the entire season to reach 1,000 yards. Coleman started his rookie campaign healthy, but suffered an ankle sprain in Week 2, which landed him a four-week stay on injured reserve.
Since his return in Week 7, though, Coleman has rushed for 263 yards and five touchdowns. If the Broncos' offensive line can continue to block like it did against the Raiders, there's a solid chance the rookie can crack 1,000 yards.
Coleman already leads all rookies with his six rushing touchdowns this season, which is one more than the next-highest guy — Kansas City Chiefs running back Emmett Johnson. I have little doubt that Coleman will rush for double-digit touchdowns as a rookie, but there might not be enough runway left to get him over 1,000 yards, given the four games he missed.
The Broncos are absolutely thrilled with Coleman. He may have gone in the fourth round, but he was one of the few complete backs in the 2026 draft class.
Teams saw a willing and able pass protector and a natural catcher of the football, to go along with Coleman's between-the-tackles vision, power, and burst. He's already caught 17 passes for 146 yards and six first downs, with a long of 51 yards.
Coleman may not have been the fastest running back in a straight line, but his burst is something special. And his jump-cut? Perhaps as potent as RJ Harvey's.
Suffice it to say, the Broncos got an enormous steal in Coleman. They're very fortunate he was still on the board at No. 108 overall. And he's just getting started.
Again, it's too bad that Dobbins is taking his diminished role poorly. But the Broncos aren't letting that get in the way of Coleman's continued rise.
The rookie will be put to the test this week with a Black Friday throwdown with the Pittsburgh Steelers on deck, in their house. The Steelers currently have the NFL's third-ranked rushing defense, and the weather is expected to be cold and rainy.
It's likely to be a Jonah Coleman type of day.

title: Broncos' Biggest Stars Weigh In on J.K. Dobbins Suspension
full_text:
Denver Broncos veteran running back J.K. Dobbins wasn't at practice on Tuesday .
We learned afterward from head coach Sean Payton that he had suspended Dobbins for one game due to "conduct detrimental" to the team. Shortly after Payton spoke, quarterback Bo Nix stepped up to the podium for his presser ahead of this Black Friday's road game against the Pittsburgh Steelers.
Two questions in, Nix was asked what his reaction was to hearing of Dobbins's suspension.
'Well, obviously, I have nothing to do with it, and so we'll just keep finding our way to figure out how to win games," Nix said. "Unfortunately, it has nothing to do with me."
Nix likely knows what's going on behind closed doors, but he's not going to break ranks with Payton and spill any beans or be unprofessional by opining publicly on a very sensitive topic. But Nix has always said good things about Dobbins, and since arriving in June of 2025 as a free-agent signing, the veteran back has contributed to a lot of winning.
After Nix, it was Pro Bowl cornerback Patrick Surtain II's turn at the podium. After being asked about this Steelers matchup, the obligatory Dobbins question followed.
"I ain't got nothing much to say about it," Surtain said. "It's a coach's decision at the end of the day."
It was exactly that, according to Payton: a "coach's decision." Dobbins will serve his one-game suspension, during which, he'll be on a suspended/reserve list, opening up a temorary roster spot.
It would appear that spot will be filled by fellow running back Tyler Badie, whom the Broncos designated to return from injured reserve on Tuesday . Badie practiced in full and is poised to return to the field after suffering a thumb injury in the Broncos' Week 6 overtime win over the Seattle Seahawks.
We didn't learn anything from Payton, Nix, or Surtain about why Dobbins was suspended, but we can only assume that the running back's conduct has something to do with his dissatisfaction over his dwindling role on offense. Since rookie running back Jonah Coleman returned from IR in Week 7, Dobbins has set a new career low in snaps in each subsequent game, culminating in his one snap in Sunday's 38-24 win over the Las Vegas Raiders .
Payton will have to strive to ensure this doesn't become a distraction that unfocuses his team. The Steelers are no joke, sitting at 6-4 and coming off back-to-back losses.
At home in front of the Pittsburgh faithful, the Steelers will be hungry to hand Payton and Nix just their fifth regular-season loss since Week 1 of the 2024 season. Payton is a veteran who's been a head coach for two decades, and he's had to deal with some monumental off-the-field distractions over the years, so if anyone knows how to nip things in the bud, it's him.
But it's still a risk. Dobbins is well-regarded in the Broncos' locker room, and has been a vocal leader since arriving two summers ago, even if he's not a team captain.
Nix was taught by his Oregon head coach — Dan Lanning — the art of avoiding the off-field-distraction trap. Nix may be a team captain, but he's only one voice in Denver's locker room.
"Yeah, it's a part of playing long seasons," Nix said on Tuesday. "You have to limit the distractions, starve the distractions and feed your focus. That's something Coach Lanning taught me a long time ago at Oregon. So for us, it's just about the next game and how we can win it."
Nix's off-field distractions this season have been cacophanous at times. National media types have always loved to criticize him, but following his rough day at the office against the Seahawks, there were actually calls for the Broncos to bench him, including from portions of the fan base and local media.
The noise reached a fever pitch entering Week 7 against the Arizona Cardinals, but it was in that road game that Nix seemed to turn a corner in his recovery from a broken ankle, as he busted off a 62-yard touchdown run and passed for 200-plus yards.
Nix's confidence seemed to come flooding back after that long run, and he's been on the rise in every game since, outdueling Patrick Mahomes in Week 8, Bryce Young in Week 9, and Fernando Mendoza in Week 11.
Do you know what else coincided with Nix's sudden return to pre-injury form? The return of Coleman, who has rushed for 263 yards and five touchdowns in the four games since then.
The momentum that Coleman has given this offense is not a train that Payton wants to stop any time soon. It's unfortunate that it's come at the expense of Dobbins's playing time, but he had six long weeks to help the Broncos produce an effective ground attack, and cement himself — an $8 million/year veteran — as the RB1.
Alas, Dobbins failed to do that, so Payton went looking for a spark from his rookie fourth-rounder. And Coleman has delivered that spark, oxygenating it to a point now where it's become a roaring blaze.
Here's to hoping the Broncos can avoid too many more questions on the Dobbins topic, so they can take care of business against one of the two plus-.500 opponents remaining on their schedule this season.

title: Steelers Make Sudden QB Change Ahead of Broncos Game
full_text:
The Pittsburgh Steelers made a shocking move at quarterback in the lead-up to Friday's game against the Denver Broncos .
In a brief statement released late Tuesday night, the Steelers announced that QB Aaron Rodgers has been benched and longtime backup Mason Rudolph will start the Week 12 contest at Acrisure Stadium.
"The Pittsburgh Steelers have named Mason Rudolph the starting quarterback for Friday’s game against the Denver Broncos. Aaron Rodgers will be inactive," the statement reads.
As of this writing, no reason has been given for Rodgers' benching, which may be related to his recent declining performance. Some have speculated this could be a precursor to Rodgers' release from Pittsburgh or even retirement from the NFL.
Already on record as playing his final season, Rodgers has completed 60.9% of his pass attempts across 10 starts, throwing for 2,241 yards, 16 touchdowns, and six interceptions while leading the Steelers to a 6-4 record.
Rodgers, however, has looked every bit like a soon-to-be 43-year-old quarterback, completely immobile both inside and outside the pocket. He's taken 31 sacks thus far this year, including five amid last week's loss to the Philadelphia Eagles.
Nevertheless, Broncos head coach Sean Payton was anticipating another head-to-head against the future Canton-bound field general — something that occurred regularly during Payton's time in New Orleans.
"They kind of run together," Payton said Tuesday regarding his encounters with Rodgers. "He’s a first-ballot [Pro Football] Hall of Famer. He’s a first-ballot thrower. Just the arm angles, the rhythm, so many things that he’s exceptional at. It was Green Bay for a number of years. They kind of run together, like I said, but the ball comes out quick. He’s got a great throwing motion. There are just so many things that he’s accomplished in his career. Nothing but respect for his skill set and also his staying power. It’s not easy to do.”
For Pittsburgh, there's really nowhere to go but up for an offense that ranks 30th in total yards and 27th in scoring and passing yards per game. Rudolph's insertion could be a green flag for the team's primary pass-catchers, such as DK Metcalf, Roman Wilson, and Pat Freiermuth.
Rudolph, 31, is similar to Broncos backup QB Jarrett Stidham in that he provides a relatively safe floor, though not a particularly high ceiling. Across 38 career appearances, he's thrown for 4,927 yards, 30 touchdowns, and 22 interceptions. He has a career record of 9-9-1 in 19 starts.
Ultimately, Rudolph might not be a central focus of the gameplan in what could be a wet and windy affair in the Steel City. That honor would likely go to Steelers running back Jaylen Warren, who's set for a massive workload on Black Friday.
The Broncos — who executed their own controversial move, suspending RB J.K. Dobbins for the game — will be near full strength on the defensive side, with starting safety Brandon Jones likely to return following a two-week absence.

title: Broncos Dealing With New D-Line Injury Concern Ahead of Steelers Game
full_text:
The Denver Broncos were back at it on Tuesday, practicing for this Black Friday's road game against the Pittsburgh Steelers .
It's a short week, but the Broncos are battle-tested. We saw some new names pop up on the practice report, so let's take a look at where things stand for the Broncos on the injury front early in the week.
After Tuesday's practice, Sean Payton announced that Dobbins has been suspended , which explains why he didn't participate. Fortunately, Badie is eligible to return from injured reserve, and the Broncos designated him to return this week.
Because Dobbins is suspended, he'll go on a reserve list for this one game, which means the Broncos will be able to activate Badie without cutting another player to make room. That makes things a little more awkward, potentially, for Lohner, who is working his way back from the physically unable to perform (PUP) list.
The Broncos started Lohner's clock last week , giving the team 21 days to decide whether to activate him. He's got roughly two weeks of that clock left.
The new injuries to monitor are Bryant, Skinner, Rapp, and Sai'vion Jones. However, both Bryant and Skinner were a full go in practice, while Rapp was limited and Jones didn't participate.
The Broncos worked out four defensive linemen on Tuesday, perhaps anticipating that Jones may not have enough time to recover from his hamstring injury on a short week. Denver worked out Jalen Hunt, Derrick Nnadi, Khalen Saunders, and Ben Stille, but as of this article, none have been signed.
Besides suspending J.K. Dobbins and activating Tyler Badie's practice window from IR, the #Broncos worked out four defensive linemen today: • Jalen Hunt • Derrick Nnadi • Khalen Saunders • Ben Stille pic.twitter.com/x557EDmmow
The Broncos have rookie Tyler Onyedim and veteran Jordan Jackson on the 53-man roster, with nose tackle Jordan Miller on the practice squad, so they have options with Jones banged up and Eyioma Uwazurike on injured reserve.
Now, for some good news: Brandon Jones was a full go on Tuesday. That means, barring an unforeseen setback, he's going to play on Friday, after missing the last two games with a hamstring.
The Steelers are relatively healthy. However, Highsmith is a starter, so his status will be worth monitoring, while Skowronek is a backup.
Pittman hasn't played since October, as we works back from his injury, so the Steelers could activate him this week . Dunker is also working back from injured reserve. Pittman is the name to watch here, beyond Highsmith and Herbig.

title: Broncos Make Move to Maneuver Around J.K. Dobbins Suspension
full_text:
The Denver Broncos are losing a running back for Friday's game against the Pittsburgh Steelers after suspending J.K. Dobbins for conduct detrimental to the team.
But they're also gaining a running back, as the Broncos designated backup Tyler Badie for return from short-term injured reserve, the team announced Tuesday .
Badie missed the mandatory minimum four games after suffering a broken thumb amid Denver's Week 6 victory over the Seattle Seahawks. He was officially listed as a full participant in Tuesday's practice.
The Broncos now have 21 days to activate Badie to the 53-man roster, which appears highly likely before the club departs for Pittsburgh.
Prior to going down, Badie recorded six carries for 22 yards and hauled in six of seven targets for 67 yards across 52 offensive snaps. He also pulled double duty as a special-teamer, returning four kickoffs for 105 yards.
“I think one of the strengths that he has is and this is a valuable trait, you know exactly what you’re going to get from the players," Broncos head coach Sean Payton said of Badie in October. "So you know what it is you might want to do with him, how he is in the protection special teams. It’s harder if you don’t, I think he’s very consistent and that allows us as game planners to know, hey, we’re going to ask him to do this and he’s going to do that very well. There are no surprises and that’s a really good trait.”
Badie was one of two Broncos RBs on injured reserve along with RJ Harvey, who'll be eligible to return for next week's home contest versus the Miami Dolphins.
Even if he weren't suspended this week, it's likely that Dobbins would be further phased out of the offensive game plan after handling only one touch in Week 11. This backfield belongs to rookie Jonah Coleman, and Denver has not exactly hidden that fact.
Combined with Harvey still being out, Badie should be activated and operate as the No. 2 behind Coleman against the Steelers, perhaps mixing in with recent practice squad callup Cody Schrader.
Badie's snaps will seem minuscule compared to Coleman's anticipated workload — especially with the forecast calling for some rain and possibly light snow — but he'll certainly see the field at Acrisure Stadium.
What happens next week ... is another story.

title: Broncos' J.K. Dobbins Drama Escalates With One-Game Suspension
full_text:
The Denver Broncos have suspended veteran running back J.K. Dobbins.
With a road trip to take on the Pittsburgh Steelers on Friday this week, head coach Sean Payton stepped up to the podium on Tuesday and made the announcement.
"I'm suspending J.K. Dobbins for this weekend's game [for] conduct detrimental," Payton said. "It's all I'm going to say about it. Coach's decision."
Payton made it clear that he would answer no follow-up questions on the Dobbins suspension. As for why this may have happened, all we can do is speculate.
As I wrote early on Tuesday , a few hours before this news dropped, the Broncos' words about Dobbins haven't matched their actions over the past month. Payton has repeatedly stated that Dobbins is "important" to the Broncos, as recently as Monday morning after the running back was given just one snap against the Las Vegas Raiders.
And yet, Dobbins's role within the offense has continued to dwindle since Jonah Coleman returned from injured reserve in Week 7. In that Week 7 game against the Arizona Cardinals, Dobbins received a career-low 14 snaps.
In Week 8 against the Kansas City Chiefs, Dobbins again received a career-low, with 13 snaps. That number fell even further against the Carolina Panthers in Week 9 to 11 snaps, and then just one, single, solitary snap in the Broncos' 38-24 win over the Raiders.
Meanwhile, as the Broncos have given Coleman more snaps and touches since his return from IR, he's made the most of them. The fourth-round rookie has rushed for 263 yards and five touchdowns over the past four games, including his 111-yard, three-touchdown tour de force on Sunday against the Raiders.
Coleman became the first Broncos rookie since Clinton Portis in 2002 to rush for 100-plus yards and three touchdowns in a game.
Knowing what I do about Dobbins, I can only imagine that he hasn't been happy with his diminished role. Beyond that, I won't speculate on what may be going on behind closed doors.
But given Dobbins's role as a locker room leader, suspending him is a big decision by Payton. I can only assume that it's for a valid reason, but we'll have to wait for further information on that as time unfolds.
The Broncos started Badie's clock to return from IR on Tuesday. He's spent the past four games on IR with a thumb injury, but he practiced in full on Tuesday.
If the Broncos activate Badie for Friday's game in Pittsburgh, he and Coleman will be the only available running backs on the 53-man roster. The Broncos also have Cody Schrader on the practice squad, but they've elevated him three times already this season, which means that if they do so again, they have to sign him to the active roster.
The Broncos will be able to activate Badie without cutting anyone this week due to Dobbins's suspension, but if they were to elevate Schrader, they'd have to sign him to the 53-man roster. Pittsburgh has a very physical defense that is ranked third against the run, so Payton is going to need to ensure his he's got enough horses in the backfield, just in case.

title: Sean Payton's Words About J.K. Dobbins Don't Match Broncos' Actions
full_text:
With their words, the Denver Broncos say that veteran running back J.K. Dobbins is important, but with their actions, it's a different message.
Amid the meteoric rise of rookie running back Jonah Coleman, Dobbins has not only been relegated to the bench, but he's also become the forgotten man. And yet, head coach Sean Payton continues to stick to his messaging about how important Dobbins is.
"J.K. is going to be super important for what we’re doing in this stretch," Payton said in his Monday morning Zoom presser.
Yeah, but Coach, Dobbins — your $8 million running back — saw just one snap, while Coleman had 62 snaps on his way to 111 rushing yards and three touchdowns on 24 carries.
"We certainly didn’t go in with the idea it was just going to be maybe that one dimensional, but that was the way that game unfolded," Payton said.
In each of the past four games since Coleman has returned from injured reserve, Dobbins has set a new career-low in snaps , going from 14 to 13 to 11, and against the Las Vegas Raiders on Sunday, he saw exactly one snap.
It's perfectly understandable that Payton would want to ride the hot hand, especially given how impactful Coleman has been since his return from IR, and how it's opened things up for Bo Nix and the entire offense.
But Payton has always preferred a split backfield, whether it was Reggie Bush and Pierre Thomas or Mark Ingram and Alvin Kamara in New Orleans, and we've seen that philosophy play out in the coach's first three years in Denver, first with Javonte Williams and Jaleel McLaughlin, then with Dobbins and RJ Harvey last season.
Even if it's just for the sake of preserving Coleman, you'd think that Denver would want to give Dobbins at least 15 snaps and a handful of touches. It makes me wonder whether Dobbins is as healthy as we're being told, and if he really is 100%, whether he's somehow landed in the doghouse.
"J.K. is healthy," Payton said on Monday.
Well, shoot, there goes that theory.
You might say, "They're just saving Dobbins for the playoffs." Maybe. But "saving" him for postseason play by almost completely keeping him from the field, as the guy who started the season as this team's RB1, would be unprecedented in Broncos canon.
Preserving his health, to some degree, likely is part of the explanation. But I still don't see it as the full explanation.
Whatever the reason, it's conspicuous how little involvement Dobbins has had since Week 7. Now, it's not just that Coleman has been great; let's not forget how bad Dobbins was through the first six weeks of the season.
Even in his one carry against the Raiders, Dobbins gained zero yards. He's sitting on a 3.3 yards-per-carry average right now, which would be a career low.
The Broncos' strength of schedule through the first half of the season, and the tier-one defenses they faced , explain some of Dobbins's struggles, but it can't account for it all. Last season, Dobbins rushed for 772 yards and four touchdowns (5.0 average) before suffering a Lisfranc (foot) injury in Week 10 that cost him the rest of the campaign.
It was the third major injury of Dobbins's NFL career, including a torn ACL and a torn Achilles. Since returning from the Lisfranc injury, he has looked slow and so overly patient that he appears indecisive in the backfield, and there's been no semblance of the burst we saw last year that allowed him to pick up five yards every time he touched the ball.
Perhaps it's the culmination of all these injuries — whatever it is, Dobbins hasn't looked the same this year, and it's a shame, given that Denver gave him a two-year, $16 million extension in the spring. We're now 12 weeks into the NFL season, and he's yet to 'miss' a game due to injury; at least, that's the case officially, but I have to wonder what's really going on behind closed doors.
So in that sense, Dobbins has held up his end of his summertime " pinky promise ," as he hasn't missed a game. But he may as well have been on IR for the past month, given how little usage and playing time the Broncos have given him.
Don't mistake what I'm writing as a denouncement of Coleman. I'm not advocating for Dobbins to be this team's RB1 — I'm simply observing how the Broncos' messaging has not matched their actions on the subject.
It's a great reminder that, in the NFL, what matters is what teams do, not what they say. Something is going on with Dobbins that goes beyond Coleman's emergence, but the Broncos are staying mum on the subject.
All will be known in due time, though. RJ Harvey is eligible to return from IR next week. Tyler Badie is eligible to return now, but the Broncos have to start being strategic about using their eight short-term IR designations, as they've already used four.
We'll see what Dobbins's usage looks like on Friday against the Pittsburgh Steelers , but it's likely going to look a lot like it has the past four weeks. If the Broncos return Harvey next week and immediately plug him into the rotation behind Coleman, it'll tell us everything we need to know, even if it stops short of explaining why Dobbins has been iced out.
About three hours after I published this article, Payton announced that Dobbins has been suspended for one game for "conduct detrimental." Payton would not elaborate on the conduct or suspension.
As I said, something is rotten in the state of Denmark.

title: Film Room: Jonah Coleman's Historic Day Tells a Bigger Story About the Broncos
full_text:
The Denver Broncos' offensive line flat-out dominated the Las Vegas Raiders en route to a 38-24 victory at Mile High . Jonah Coleman had a career day, finishing with 111 yards on 24 carries and three rushing touchdowns .
Coleman averaged 4.6 yards per carry, but his longest rush only went for 14 yards, and it came in the fourth quarter. Going back through the game logs, there were a bunch of plays for five to seven yards, and nearly everything went for a positive gain.
Coleman had a lot of room to operate, and he took advantage of it early and often.
Have a day, rookie. Let's dive into the tape.
Nice execution on the screen to open the 3rd drive. pic.twitter.com/0casjNNQ75
Denver made it clear that Coleman would be a prominent part of the offensive game plan on its first drive, giving him three touches to open the game. He didn’t see the ball on the short field-goal drive on their second possession, but he was on the field for most of the game after that.
To open the Broncos' third drive, Sean Payton dialed up a screen to Coleman on the first play. This was executed perfectly, and it popped for seven yards to start the drive on the right foot.
Watch how left guard Matt Peart, center Luke Wattenberg, and right guard Quinn Meinerz set up the wall of blockers to open a nice lane for Coleman to burst through. Right tackle Mike McGlinchey seals the backside defender, and Coleman does the rest.
Great vision from Coleman here. Wattenburg gets beat quick, but Coleman sees the cutback and gets to the 2nd level. Watch Meinerz climb on this. pic.twitter.com/3My4BQhusM
On the next play, Denver runs inside zone, and Coleman picks up seven yards and a first down. Watch his vision on this play to hit the cutback lane at the point of attack, then slash upfield and finish with power.
Wattenburg gets beaten badly on this play, and Coleman has to break this back against the grain to avoid a negative play.
Check out the work that Meinerz and Peart do against the linebackers at the second level to keep the lane open. McGlinchey also does a great job of washing J.J. Pegues (#92) down the line of scrimmage from his 3-tech alignment. This is great execution up front.
This play shouldn't have even happened. McGlinchey false started and brought Crosby up field. They let it go, though. Coleman for 9 on this one. pic.twitter.com/1aSrJ6Xg1f
This is a play that shouldn’t have even happened. McGlinchey gets away with a false start right before the snap, which actually worked out in the Broncos’ favor. His flinch drew Maxx Crosby upfield, opening a huge hole in the B-gap. The play was allowed to continue for some reason, and Coleman ripped off a nine-yard gain in the red zone.
Denver is running a draw on this play, and Wattenburg does a great job climbing the second level and picking off Quay Walker to seal the lane. Coleman hits this with authority while allowing Wattenberg time to get to the second level and clear more space.
This is an awesome showing of vision, patience, and lateral agility with a nasty cutback to finish the run. Denver would finish this drive with a Bo Nix touchdown pass to tight end Adam Trautman on a nifty red-zone design to open the second quarter.
Coleman's 1st TD of the game. Meinerz, Powers and Bolles blow this thing wide open. pic.twitter.com/jJREZmhqdM
On Denver’s next possession, the Broncos hit a flea-flicker to Marvin Mims Jr. to set the offense up inside the 1-yard line. Nix couldn’t sneak his way in on first down, so the Broncos asked Coleman to finish the job.
Denver runs power at the goal line, pulling Meinerz across the formation as a lead blocker. Denver rotated Powers in at left guard in the second quarter, and he and left tackle Garett Bolles dominated the point of attack on this play.
You can’t block it much better than this, opening up a nice lane for Coleman to plunge into the end zone and take a 17-point lead
Coleman's 2nd TD. Powers and Peart dominating on IZ. Coleman runs through Walker for 6. pic.twitter.com/gVHHUzxF0v
Denver’s offense struggled on its next four possessions, and the defense allowed several explosive plays to open the door for the Raiders to tie the game in the third quarter. Denver answered with a 10-play, 72-yard touchdown drive of its own, capped off by Coleman’s second rushing touchdown of the game.
Watch Meinerz and Peart dominate at the point of attack on this inside zone play. Meinerz drives his defender into the end zone, and Peart is serving pancakes to the backside defensive tackle.
Wattenberg loses to Walker at the second level, but it doesn’t matter. Coleman runs directly through his chest, determined to finish in the painted grass.
Denver ran pin and pull a lot down the stretch. Meinerz was the lead on it, and it was effective to say the least. pic.twitter.com/0c1bUNqEJ7
Coming off of a great defensive stop to force a turnover on downs, Denver went into four-minute mode and leaned into the run game.
The Broncos saw something on tape they knew they could exploit and spammed pin-and-pull run plays with Meinerz coming from right to left to seal off the edge. They ran this concept three times on this drive, with all three resulting in nice chunk gains.
This is the first one. Watch fullback Adam Prentice detonate Walker in the hole, with Meinerz sealing Nakobe Dean on the edge to open the lane. Courtland Sutton gets just enough of the cornerback, and Coleman hits it hard. Great execution up front, once again.
Watch Meinerz on this. He has nobody to block for 5 yards after he turns the corner. This was Coleman's longest rush of the day, and it's in the 4th quarter. pic.twitter.com/NZDkTW2b6l
A couple of plays later, the Broncos ran it again. This time, Meinerz has nobody to block when he turns the corner.
Tight end Nate Adkins comes in slice motion to pick off the linebacker while Trautman and Bolles double-team the defensive end on the pin-down block. Meinerz eventually lands on the safety five yards downfield, opening a cutback lane to the inside.
This is one of my favorite attributes of Coleman’s game. He gets skinny behind Trautman and Meinerz and slashes through the secondary, ripping off his longest rush of the day in a critical moment. His contact balance and power shine on this rep as well.
Coleman's 3rd TD. Pin and Pull. Jermod McCoy gets run over on this play. So does Nakobe Dean. pic.twitter.com/6Qx9Inkpcr
If it’s not broke, don’t fix it. Run it again. Make them stop you.
This one is all on Coleman, who runs through Jermod McCoy like a freight train for his third score of the night. Meinerz buries Dean at the second level, Trautman and Bolles win the double team, and Sutton inserts to pick up the safety, leaving Coleman and McCoy one-on-one on the edge.
Coleman’s career day should result in an AFC Offensive Player of the Week award. Putting three touchdowns on the board speaks for itself, but his consistency throughout the game was very noticeable.
Coleman is going to get the accolades for his performance, but this one is on the Broncos' offensive line. The unit was tremendous against the Raiders, opening up several lanes to get Coleman to the second level.
This was the most impressive outing for the Broncos' run game all season, and it’s a performance to build around.
There’s little doubt Coleman is this team's lead back. The Broncos need to keep feeding him the rock.

title: Broncos-Steelers Weather Forecast Could Present Big Challenges on Black Friday
full_text:
The Denver Broncos just notched their sixth straight win , but they won't get much rest between opponents.
The 8-2 Broncos will serve as the NFL's Black Friday guinea pigs, scheduled for a road trip to take on the 6-4 Pittsburgh Steelers this week. The Broncos have already had one short-week turnaround this season, defeating the Seattle Seahawks in overtime on Thursday Night Football back in Week 6.
This week's practice regimen will be similar to that of any Thursday night matchup, with the Broncos holding walkthrough-level practices on Tuesday and maybe Wednesday, too. Then it's Turkey Day, which will be a travel day for the Broncos, and it's on to Pittsburgh for a Black Friday AFC throwdown.
The Broncos' future is bright and sunny, but the weather in Pittsburgh will be far from it. As the Broncos travel east to battle the Steelers, let's take a look at the weather forecast for Friday's game.
It's only Monday, so the forecast could change, but it's likely to be a bit chilly and wet in Pittsburgh on Friday. That might not bode well for the Bo Nix and the Broncos' burgeoning passing game — which has improved by leaps and bounds over the past four games — but it plays directly into the hands of Jonah Coleman and this ground attack.
Coleman rushed for 111 yards and three touchdowns in Sunday's 38-24 victory over the Raiders, becoming the first Broncos rookie to finish north of the century mark with a trio of scores in a game since Clinton Portis in 2002 .
The rookie deserves a lot of credit for how he's sparked this offense, and certainly for his tough running against the Raiders , but Sean Payton's bye-week deep dive into the blocking up front and the subsequent change to the offensive line rotation also deserves some love.
Matt Peart started in place of Ben Powers at left guard, and while the two rotated in and out of the game throughout the day, it played a big role in the Broncos' rushing production. Beyond the left guard rotation, though, this offensive line, as a unit, blocked much, much better than it had for most of the season, and the same goes for the tight ends, including Evan Engram.
And with Nix's confidence restored, he no longer appears reluctant to run with the ball when the situation demands it. Coleman is built to carry the RB1 load, but this Steelers defense is no joke, so everyone will need to bring their lunch pails to work on Friday, and get ready to strap it on, especially given the weather.
We'll keep an eye on Friday's forecast in Pittsburgh, and update this article when there are meaningful changes. But if you're planning on traveling to be at this game, you might want to bring a rain coat.

title: Broncos Front Office Should Listen to What Ja'Quan McMillian Just Said
full_text:
Denver Broncos nickel cornerback Ja'Quan McMillian has a penchant for making big, game-changing plays look easy.
Late in the fourth quarter against the Las Vegas Raiders, McMillian used his instincts to read quarterback Fernando Mendoza, throw his arm out, and make a one-handed snag, which he returned to the house for the third pick-six of his young career.
That defensive touchdown slammed the door on any hope of a Raiders comeback. It also sent a message to the Broncos' front office about McMillian's looming free agency .
McMillian is playing on a one-year restricted free-agent tender that is paying him $5.8 million. He'll be an unrestricted free agent after this season, and we know the Broncos are planning for the future, even as the 2026 campaign marches on.
The Broncos signed Riley Moss to a four-year, $67 million extension last week, and multiple reports say the team also approached McMillian's agent during the bye, though the two sides were unable to come to an agreement. After Sunday's 38-24 win over the Raiders , McMillian was asked whether things stand with the Broncos and any extension talks.
“I’m not sure,’’ McMillian said, via The Denver Gazette 's Chris Tomasson . “I’m letting my agent handle that. Right now, I’m just focused on winning..."
BRONCOS PICK-6 🚨 LVvsDEN on CBS/Paramount+ Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/QYcLRnTPus
Rumors abound on what kind of money McMillian is asking for, but it's important to remember that he's a nickel cornerback, his takeaway production notwithstanding. The NFL's highest-paid nickel is Kyler Gordon of the Chicago Bears, who's making $13.3 million per year.
The Broncos could be trying to get McMillian re-signed on a deal closer to $10 million per year, but there are rumors that his reps turned down an offer for more. That intel is unverified, though, so take it with a grain of salt.
The expectation now is that Denver will revisit contract talks with McMillian after the season. Turning down any sizable offer from the Broncos is a bit of a gamble because he's healthy and playing well right now, but football is a violent and crazy sport that can produce wacky and tragic outcomes.
For example, Moss could have turned down the Broncos' offer of $16.75 million per year because he was projected to command north of $20 million annually on the open market. Now, we know staying in Denver was a big priority for Moss, so that played a part in his willingness to sign, but he likely also wanted to capitalize on the opportunity for financial security right now, because you never know what the future holds.
God forbid that anything should happen to McMillian. I'm simply pointing out the risk and highlighting how the feisty nickel is betting on himself. Since becoming a starter early in the 2023 season, he's never missed a game, and that's a big part of his value, too, as a pending free agent.
McMillian's dagger pick-six to ice Sunday's win over the Raiders will be an iconic memory that Broncos Country is unlikely to soon forget. The same can be said for his teammates, some of whom went to bat for him in the locker room after the game.
When asked whether the Broncos should extend McMillian, Pro Bowl cornerback Patrick Surtain II said, "Yes, indeed. They need to make that happen."
"He makes big-time plays, so hopefully we can get him [re-signed]," Surtain said of McMillian, via ESPN 's Jeff Legwold . "But he's going to be an expensive guy."
You could see how much McMillian's teammates love and appreciate his knack for the big play in the celebration that ensued after his pick-six.
"It just means they see the effort, the work that I put in," McMillian said of his teammates post-game. "Those guys mean so much to me. It's love."
Ja'Quan McMillian with the Pick-6 on Mendoza. His teammates run up and start making it rain 🤑💸 PAY THAT MAN! #BroncosCountry pic.twitter.com/ZNzvfJxxpb
The Broncos don't really need to see much more from McMillian to know how special he is. I just mentioned his availability on the health front, and he's been this team's most reliable ballhawk over the past two seasons, but really, dating back to his first year as a starter.
Plus, McMillian is physical in the box and relishes the opportunity to stick his nose in the muss and make a tackle. He finished second on the team with eight tackles against the Raiders, and his 10 career sacks already rank near the top of the Broncos' all-time books among cornerbacks, especially those with undrafted origins.
McMillian is a smart, instinctual player who does his homework, and plays hard every game.
"Very smart, always dialed in, the way he goes about his business. It's very exciting," Surtain said about McMillian. "That's how he makes his plays. Always right when we need it, in the clutch, he always comes through."
Although McMillian's reps and the Broncos are yet to agree to terms on an extension, he made it clear after the game that he wants to remain in Denver beyond 2026.
"I would want to stay here, of course; these are my guys," McMillian said via Legwold. "Been here for five years now; you build relationships. I'd want to be here."
The onus is now on Broncos GM George Paton to come back to the table with a reworked offer. But McMillian isn't Paton's only concern when it comes to pending free agents, with other deserving veterans like safety Brandon Jones and wideout/returner Marvin Mims Jr. playing in a contract year.
Speculation surrounding McMillian's unsigned status after this season will continue as the campaign marches on. The noise surrounding the topic at Broncos HQ is currently at a fever pitch, so it'll be interesting to see if any dominoes fall during this season.
McMillian is a closer — one of the NFL's best. And just like in Major League Baseball, closers tend to get the bag.

title: Lions Search for Defining Thanksgiving Win Of Campbell Era: A Look Back
full_text:
Detroit Lions head coach Dan Campbell is facing a big opportunity Thursday against the Chicago Bears.
Now in his sixth-year as the team's head coach, Campbell has a chance to notch arguably the biggest Thanksgiving win in the franchise's recent history. The Lions and Chicago Bears, both 8-2, are meeting Thursday with first-place on the line in the NFC North.
It hasn't been the smoothest of sailing for Campbell on the national holiday, as the Lions are 1-4 under him on Thanksgiving. However, he has an opportunity to exorcise some of the demons of Thanksgivings past if he can lead the team to a win on Tuesday.
Here's a look at Campbell's first five Thanksgiving games as head coach of the Lions and how it's shaped his tenure heading into a big showdown on Thursday.
In the first Thanksgiving game of the Campbell era, Detroit scored on its first offensive series. Jared Goff hit Josh Reynolds for a 39-yard touchdown, and the 0-9-1 Lions had the lead early in the game.
However, the game was not an offensive affair as there were a total of 10 punts between the two teams. Chicago had the lead by halftime thanks to 13 unanswered points, but the Lions rallied to reclaim the leading heading into the fourth thanks to a touchdown from Goff to T.J. Hockenson.
After a stop, the Lions got the ball back leading by a point early in the fourth. However, their drive was derailed by penalties on three straight plays, and as a result they punted the ball back to Chicago with 8:30 remaining. It was the last time they'd have possession.
Chicago went on a methodical march down the field, and had the ball inside Detroit's 20 at the two-minute warning. What ensued was an unfortunate turn of events. The Lions took a timeout after David Montgomery's 1-yard run that set up a third-and-9, then took another time out when the defense was misaligned.
The consecutive timeouts resulted in a five-yard delay of game penalty, and the Bears converted the ensuing third-and-four. Doing so allowed them to run the clock all the way out, as Cairo Santos connected on the game-winning 28-yard field goal as time expired.
The Lions entered their 2022 Thanksgiving game on a much different trajectory than the year prior, as they were winners of three-straight entering this game against Josh Allen and the Bills. The two teams traded punches early in the game, with Jamaal Williams and Amon-Ra St. Brown reaching the end zone for Detroit and the Bills countering with scores from Allen and Isiah McKenzie.
Tyler Bass knocked a 47-yard field goal attempt through the uprights before the half to give the Bills a 17-14 advantage. Goff was sacked in the end zone by Ed Oliver to boost the Bills' lead to five in the third, but Goff rallied to hit DJ Chark for a touchdown and D'Andre Swift added the two-point conversion to give the Lions a 22-19 lead.
As was the case in the previous year, chaos ensued in the fourth. After the Chark touchdown early in the quarter, the Bills retook the lead with a pass from Allen to Stefon Diggs, but a missed extra point kept the deficit at three for Detroit.
The Lions drove into Buffalo territory, and faced a third-and-1 with :32 remaining. Rather than run the ball, a deep pass was dialed up that ulitmately fell incomplete. This stopped the clock and allowed Buffalo to preserve all three of its timeouts.
Though Michael Badgley connected on the field goal to tie the game, the 23 seconds that remained were all Buffalo needed. Allen hit Diggs for 36 yards on first down, and runs from Allen on the next two plays set up Bass' game-winning field goal to deal Detroit another heartbreaking loss on Thanksgiving.
After the renaissance that the Lions finished the previous season on, they carried that momentum into an 8-2 start ahead of the Packers' game on Thanksgiving. They sat in first-place, while the Packers were a lowly 4-6 in Jordan Love's first full year as a starter.
However, the tone was set from the very first snap as Love connected with Christian Watson for a 53-yard gain. Green Bay would score first, and while the Lions would answer with a touchdown from Goff to Sam LaPorta, the wheels quickly came off for Detroit starting with a missed extra point.
Green Bay made it 14-6 on its ensuing drive, then Rashan Gary strip-sacked Goff on the next possession leading to a Jonathan Owens scoop-and-score to make it 20-6 before the end of the first quarter.
Goff would lose another fumble on the next series, and the Lions were down 23-6 going into the half. They would score and get the two-point conversion to get back within nine early in the third quarter, However, Detroit was doomed when Campbell dialed up a fake-punt on their own 23-yard line that was stuffed and led directly to a Packers' touchdown.
Detroit would be stopped on downs a total of three times and lost three fumbles, which created the ideal recipe for the Packers to come in and steal a win.
The 2024 season was a banner one for the Lions, even with all the injuries they had to endure. They entered this matchup with Chicago at 10-1, and rolled out to an early 16-0 lead after scoring on each of their first four drives.
Still, the game was not without its drama. Chicago was reinvigorated after the break thanks to the performance of then-rookie quarterback Caleb Williams. He hit Keenan Allen for a score, and after Detroit answered with a touchdown of its own he threw back-to-back scores to get Chicago within three points late in the game.
With a chance to salt the game away with just over five minutes remaining, the Lions went three-and-out to give the Bears one more shot. Needing just a field goal, the Bears got a big boost when Kindle Vildor was whistled for pass interference to put them in field goal range.
The Lions would ultimately get very fortunate, though, thanks to a twist of fate. Williams was sacked, and the Bears elected not to use a timeout which set up one final play where the passer threw an incomplete Hail Mary.
After escaping in overtime against the New York Giants, the Lions were looking to snap their streak of alternating wins and losses and gain ground in the NFC North division. However, it was not to be as the Packers once again came in handled business against Detroit on the holiday.
Green Bay took an early 10-0 lead, and had a 17-7 lead late in the first half before Jameson Williams hauled in a 22-yard touchdown pass from Jared Goff. Detroit got the ball to start the third quarter, but was stopped on downs just past midfield. The Packers wasted little time, as Jordan Love hit Christian Watson for a 51-yard touchdown to put them back up two scores.
Detroit struck back quickly with a touchdown from Goff to Isaac TeSlaa, but Green Bay once again had the answer. The deficit remained 10 points into the fourth quarter, and was stopped on downs inside Green Bay's 25-yard line with over 10 minutes to go.
The decision would be speculated upon later, as a field goal in that situation would've pulled the team within a score. Ultimately, Detroit would get there much later in the game as Jake Bates connected to get the Lions to within seven, but it came with under three minutes to go.
Detroit's defense had one last-ditch attempt to stay in the game, forcing Green Bay into a fourth-down from Detroit's 45-yard line. However, Love hit Dontayvion Wicks for 16 yards to effectively end the game and give Detroit another painstaking loss.

title: Odds Detroit Lions Beat Chicago Bears in Week 12
full_text:
The NFL schedule makers hit a home run with their matchup for the Detroit Lions this Thanksgiving. Detroit will battle with former offensive coordinator Ben Johnson and the 8-2 Chicago Bears in one of the most highly anticipated Turkey Day games in recent memory.
With a victory, the Lions would not only capture a “statement win” but also improve to 3-0 against their NFC North opponents in 2026. Additionally, a win would provide Dan Campbell's squad with a significant leg-up in the race for the division crown.
Detroit will be challenged every step of the way in the Week 12 clash. The Bears enter the holiday affair winners of five in a row, with both a top-10 offense (No. 8 in points per game) and a top-10 defense (No. 6 in points allowed/game). Plus, their defense received a major boost via the midseason trade for defensive tackle Jeffery Simmons.
Simmons, formerly of the Tennessee Titans, has already recorded nine sacks this season, and is coming off a three-sack performance in Week 11 against the New Orleans Saints. He's also generated 36 total pressures, and for his efforts, has earned Pro Football Focus’ fourth-highest pass-rush grade among 132 qualified interior defensive linemen (84.9).
The two-time Pro Bowler is the definition of a difference-making defensive tackle. Consequently, it wouldn't be surprising to see the 6-foot-4, 305-pounder end up with a couple of pressures and possibly even a sack Thursday.
Additional Lions NFL Insider Analysis: No Red Flags For Safety Kerby Joseph After 2026 Debut
Then, on offense, the Bears are led by 25-year-old signal-caller Caleb Williams. The former No. 1 overall pick might not have the most prolific passing numbers (10 touchdowns and 1,727 yards in seven games), but he's still very much a force to be reckoned with (both with his right arm and his legs).
For the season, he's completing a career-best 68.3 percent of his passes, and is throwing for a career-high 246.7 yards per game. And on top of that, he's posted a 68.9 QBR, the eighth-best mark among 30 qualified quarterbacks.
Plus, he's a constant threat to pick up a first down with his legs, with 12 first downs on the ground this season. And although he hasn't made much of an impact as a runner in recent weeks, he still has 156 rushing yards and a couple of rushing scores to his name.
Along with Williams, the Bears feature a pair of ultra talented wideouts : Luther Burden III and Rome Odunze. Burden leads all Chicago receivers in catches (51), reception yards (654) and receiving scores (four). Meanwhile, Odunze has also had a solid campaign, with 36 catches, 573 yards and a touchdown to his name.
Burden and Odunze will likely be a handful for the Lions' injury-plagued cornerbacks group, which could be without No. 1 CB D.J. Reed (hip) for a fourth consecutive game.
The Bears also possess a top-flight rushing attack, spearheaded by former Lions running back D'Andre Swift. Swift has compiled 627 yards and 10 touchdowns on 168 carries in 2026. And as a team, Chicago has amassed 1,424 yards on the ground, the third-most in the NFL through 11 weeks.
Additionally, if I were a betting man, I'd put my money on Johnson dialing up a trick play or two against his former team.
Simply, it will not be easy for Detroit to emerge victorious in this Week 12 affair. However, at this present juncture, I'll give the Lions a 52 percent chance to secure their seventh straight win .

title: Evaluating Lions Options to Replace Injured DT Skyler Gill-Howard
full_text:
The Detroit Lions got some unfortunate news on the injury front early this week, as rookie defensive lineman Skyler Gill-Howard will be out for the remainder of the season due to a knee injury.
Gill-Howard suffered the knee injury in the fourth quarter of Detroit's Week 11 win over the Tampa Bay Buccaneers, when he got rolled up on while blocking as an extra lineman in Detroit's jumbo goal-line package.
In his debut season, the sixth-round pick proved to be a pleasant surprise for Detroit's defense. After a strong preseason, Gill-Howard earned a significant role rushing the passer from the interior line and wound up with two sacks.
Now, Detroit must find a replacement for that role, which will be difficult given Gill-Howard's athleticism. Fortunately, they have another defensive tackle playing extremely well at this point in Alim McNeill.
Here are eight options for Detroit to consider when replacing Gill-Howard.
A former second-round pick of the Lions in 2021, the road for Onwuzurike up to this point has been a challenging one. He's missed two full seasons in his career, and returned to Detroit after his contract tolled on account of him not playing last season.
Detroit has stuck with him due to the versatility he has along the defensive line, and with Gill-Howard out Onwuzurike seems like the most natural internal option to replace the rookie. He's shown some pass-rush upside throughout his career when healthy, and had already gotten a bigger workload last week in the first game without Aidan Hutchinson.
A sixth-round draft pick of the Lions in 2024, Wingo has played a very small role over the last two seasons after appearing in 11 games as a rookie. He suffered a season-ending injury on Thanksgiving as a rookie, and ever since has been an afterthought in Detroit's defensive line rotation.
Wingo appeared in just two games last year, and has yet to be active for a game this year. His skill set is somewhat similar to Gill-Howard's in that he's more productive in pass-rush, and with one year remaining on his rookie deal this may be his final chance to prove himself in Detroit.
The Lions inked an undrafted free agent contract with Keanaaina this offseason, but the Cal product suffered an injury that resulted in him being waived with an injury settlement. He returned at the conclusion of that settlement, and has been on the practice squad ever since.
Because Keanaaina didn't play in the preseason, it remains uncertain what exactly he'd have to offer for Detroit. However, the team seems intrigued by his size and skill set. While he may not be a replacement for Gill-Howard's pass-rush ability , there is some upside to potentially having another rotational run-stuffer in the mix.
Taimani is another practice squad option for Detroit. He played parts of two seasons with the Lions' division rival Minnesota Vikings, totaling nine appearances over 2024 and 2025. Dan Campbell mentioned Taimani as another potential option to enter the rotation, and at the very least could be utilized as an elevation for roster depth.
The Lions had Stille in the organization up until recently, as the team released him from the practice squad last week. He was utilized as an elevation in the team's Week 1 game, as he played nine snaps against the New Orleans Saints.
With the nature of Gill-Howard's injury and general manager Brad Holmes' track record of prioritizing familiar players who fit the organization's system, Stille could be an addition that fits the mold. However, Stille has drawn some interest from around the league as he visited the Denver Broncos on Tuesday.
Loudermilk visited the Lions in the offseason, and just hit the free agent market again after being released from the New York Jets practice squad. Detroit seemed to have some interest in adding him before going with Jay Tufele, but Tufele was let go prior to training camp.
Because Loudermilk is now available, perhaps Detroit revisits the idea of adding him and looks to bring him in. He has a versatile skill set with the ability to play on the interior or slide out and play the big end, which fits Detroit's flexible scheme.
Loudermilk has appeared in 60 games in his career across stints with several teams, but hasn't played in a game this year across stints with the Jets and Minnesota Vikings.
Chris Smith (Miami Dolphins)
The Lions are very familiar with Smith, as he has played parts of four years with the organization. He was with the team's practice squad to start the year, but was released and landed in Miami.
Smith has appeared in five NFL games, but has been reliable depth for the organization over the years. Dan Campbell gave Smith a shoutout earlier in the season for his effort and work ethic, and he's ultra familiar with the scheme so he'd be a plug and play option.
Mazi Smith (Green Bay Packers)
A former first-round pick of the Dallas Cowboys, Smith's career hasn't panned out the way some thought it would. He's currently with the Packers' practice squad after beginning the year in Miami, where he played one game as an elevation.
Smith had a sack in each of his first two seasons with the Cowboys, but was traded to New York last year in the Quinnen Williams trade. When he's at his best, he can offer some of the pass-rush upside that Gill-Howard provided.
Holmes has also shown a willingness to take chances on players as reclamation projects, most recently with another former first-round pick in Payton Turner, and because of that he could see some buy-low value in Smith to see if the defender can unlock his potential for the stretch run.

title: Detroit Lions 2026 Thanksgiving Referee Presents Favorable Trend
full_text:
The officiating crew for the Detroit Lions' Thanksgiving matchup with the Chicago Bears has been revealed.
When the teams take the field Thursday to battle for first-place in the NFC North , the game will be officiated by Shawn Hochuli and his crew. It is Hochuli's first Lions game this season, while he has worked one Bears game already this year.
Hochuli may be a familiar name for some, as he has been a head referee since 2018, and his father Ed Hochuli was also a long-tenured NFL referee before retiring in 2018. In Shawn Hochuli's career, he has presided over 10 Lions games as a head referee. Detroit is 5-5 in those games.
Notable games Hochuli has worked in his career for the Lions include last year's Thursday Night Football win over the Dallas Cowboys, as well as the 2024 Monday Night Football win over the San Francisco 49ers.
With Hochuli as the official, the home teams have had a distinct advantage this year. The hosts are 7-2 in the nine games he's officiated this season, and there's a slight skew in penalty count as 66 have been called on visiting teams compared to 60 on home teams.
Overall, Hochuli's crew ranks tied-for-ninth in penalties called per game with 14, according to NFL Penalties. Hochuli's group has been fairly lenient, as they have yet to have a game with 20 flags thrown up to this point in the year.
Hochuli's busiest game this season was a Week 4 matchup between Baltimore and Tennessee, where the two teams combined for 18 flags.
He also has a history with the Bears, having already reffed the team's Week 3 Monday Night Football win over the Philadelphia Eagles led by veteran backup Case Keenum. He also reffed Chicago's Divisional Round loss to the Los Angeles Rams at Soldier Field last season.
Detroit enters Thursday's game unbeaten at home and looking for a seventh-straight win, while the Bears have won five in a row since slipping up against the Green Bay Packers. Both teams are 8-2, and the winner will take the top spot in the division heading into the final stretch run of the regular season.

title: Detroit Lions Owner Martha Firestone Ford Dies at 101
full_text:
Former Detroit Lions team principal owner and emeritus Martha Firestone Ford died Tuesday, November 24, at the age of 101.
Ford began holding majority control of the team beginning in 2014, as she was passed ownership of the team after the death of her husband William Clay Ford. She became an emeritus of the team beginning in 2020, when she turned control over to her daughter Sheila Ford Hamp.
The Lions have been owned by the Ford family since William Clay Ford purchased the team for $4.5 million in 1963. In the Ford family's time as owners, the Lions have never won a championship. They won four titles before the Super Bowl era began, but have never appeared in the big game.
In Martha Firestone Ford's tenure as the team's majority owner, the Lions amassed a 45-50-1 regular season record and were 0-2 in their appearances in the postseason. Since turning the team over to Hamp, the Lions have found some sustained success as the team hired the tandem of head coach Dan Campbell and general manager Brad Holmes.
Under their leadership, the Lions have won two NFC North titles over the past three seasons and made an NFC Championship appearance in 2023.
"For over 60 years, Mrs. Ford has been an owner of the Detroit Lions. In 1963, she and her husband, William Clay Ford, purchased full control of the team," read a press release from the Lions Tuesday. "Upon her husband's passing in 2014, she assumed sole control of the franchise. In 2020, she transitioned to emeritus status where she served until her passing.
"In her most recent role as Owner/Chair Emeritus, Mrs. Ford supported her four children – Principal Owner/Chair Sheila Ford Hamp, Owner/Vice Chair Martha Ford Morse, Owner/Vice Chair William Clay Ford Jr., and Owner/Vice Chair Elizabeth Ford Kontulis – as they assumed leadership responsibilities within the family franchise. Today the Ford family proudly carries forward the legacy established by Mr. and Mrs. Ford, preserving the values, love, and passion that have shaped a family tradition spanning multiple generations."
Martha Ford was an active member of the Detroit community, making numerous financial contributions and donations to local projects. Among them were improvements to Ford Field and Detroit Lions Inspire Change.
Additionally, Ford held significant leadership roles in organizations such as Merrill Palmer Skillman Institute, University Liggett School, Children's Home of Detroit and Edsel and Elanor Field House.
NFL commissioner Roger Goodell also commented on the passing of Ford Tuesday in a written statement .
"Martha was special. She cared so deeply about her family, the players, their fans, and the city of Detroit," Goodell's statement read. "She was committed to making the Lions—and the game of football—better. Martha and her husband, William Clay Ford, led the franchise with dignity and integrity. We will miss her kindness and sweet sense of humor. We extend our deepest condolences to her children, the entire Ford family, and the Lions’ organization.”

title: Detroit Lions Injury Updates: Reed, Wonnum, Mays, LaPorta, Clark
full_text:
The Detroit Lions conducted another walkthrough on Tuesday, two days before the team takes the field against the Chicago Bears for the annual Thanksgiving Day Classic.
Three players did not participate, including Ennis Rakestraw, Skyler Gill-Howard and DJ Wonnum.
Two players were upgraded, as safety Chuck Clark returned as a limited participant and tight end Sam LaPorta was a full participant.
Head coach Dan Campbell was asked about the status of several injured players prior to a pivotal contest against another 8-2 team.
DJ Reed, Clark, Rakestraw and Wonnum are likely all going to be game time decisions , according to the former NFL tight end.
When asked about Reed, Campbell expressed, “Yeah, he's improving. I mean, I thought he ran around pretty good yesterday. But I can't give a definitive answer on that just yet. Probably come down to,   could be game time decision.”
Veteran center Cade Mays was again placed on the injured reserve list, but there is an expectation he will returnn at some point this season.
“Yeah, we'd like to believe so. We just felt like it didn't feel good the next two games for sure, possibly three," said Campbel. "So, it just made sense because it's these two games and a short period of time. Whatever that is, you get two of them knocked out and it buys you the roster spot . But yeah, we feel like we'll get him back.”
Additional Detroit Lions NFL Insider Analysis: 5 Risers, 2 Fallers After Defeating Tampa Bay Buccaneers
With Mays unable to remain in the lineup, Juice Scruggs has filled in admirably. The appeal of the former Houston Texans lineman was his ability and experience to play at multiple different spots along the offensive line.
"I really can't say enough great things about Juice," Campell said. "He's just been a great addition for us. He's a pro. He's the same guy every day. He's very consistent. He doesn't ride the wave, the ups and downs. He's positive. He goes to work, makes corrections, plays snap to whistle, hustles, great teammate. He's everything. So, he was a guy that we just felt like when we were able to acquire him, he's really a utility lineman. He's got starts under his bel t at guard and center. So, we knew he had that capability.
"Once the injury happens to Cade (Mays), then it's about, 'Alright, well this is where, because he was bouncing back and forth. Alright, it's all about the center position.' And he's just steadily gotten better and better for us as we've gone," Campbell added further. "And you're right, we put a lot on him. We put a lot on him, certainly asked him to do a lot of jobs, but he just continues to get better, and he's made the right way. I mean, he fits us like a glove. He's a stud.”
