title: Detroit Lions Rookie DT Skyler Gill-Howard Lost For 2026 Season
full_text:
The hits keep on coming for the Detroit Lions defense, as another talented defender is lost for the remainder of the 2026 NFL season.
Head coach Dan Campbell explained to local reporters on Tuesday afternoon that rookie defensive lineman Skyler Gill-Howard has suffered a knee injury that will require surgery.
After a slow start to training camp, the sixth-round pick settled in and emerged as a key contributor in  Kelvin Sheppard's defense.
According to the former NFL tight end, Gill-Howard injured himself on Sione Vaki's rushing attempt against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers at Ford Field.
Along with Alim McNeill and Tyleik Williams, the Lions' defensive line has been a bright spot this season.
Taki Taimani and Aidan Keanaaina are currently on the practice squad, and the team could also look to Levi Onwuzurike or Tyler Lacy. Mekhi Wingo has been inactive for the past several weeks and could see some action on the field soon.
Detroit's defensive line has also lost defensive end Aidan Hutchinson for the season, as he tore his anterior cruciate ligament against the New England Patriots.
The former NFL tight end expressed earlier this week, when asked about not taking anything for granted during the build up to big games, that there is a fine line of not taking anything for granted but still pushing the roster to get better every week.
“I mean, I think you want to, as with anything, man, you don't ever want to take anything for granted. Even when times aren't going so good, you really need to embrace every moment of it, even the hard ones," said Campbell. "Because I think they shape you to be what you're going to be or where you're going to go or give you direction, and I think that's important. But like I mentioned, when you get in this where we're at right now and we feel like we're doing some good things , we're finding ways to win, you just don't want to let go of it.
"You don't want to squeeze it so hard that you break it in half either. So there is that fine line, man. Let's keep it what it is," Campbell added further. "Don't make more of it than needs to be, but at the same time we have got to continue to grow, get better and have enough urgency here to get our job done. So, it's exciting.”

title: 3 Detroit Lions Under the Most Pressure Against Bears
full_text:
The Detroit Lions have a massive game looming on Thursday against the Chicago Bears.
When they take the field for their annual Thanksgiving showdown, it will be with the opportunity to clinch first-place in the NFC North heading into the stretch run of the 2026 season. As a result, it's as high stakes of a game as Detroit has played on the holiday in recent memory.
Here are three players under the most pressure in the Lions' Thanksgiving matchup against the Chicago Bears.
Goff is looking for his second win as quarterback of the Lions on Thanksgiving. His lone win came two years ago against the Bears, and though he has had some struggles in the win-loss column, he has been fairly effective on the holiday over the years.
Over his first five seasons as the Lions' quarterback, Goff has totaled 1,202 passing yards, nine touchdowns and zero interceptions on Thanksgiving. However, he did lose three fumbles against the Green Bay Packers in 2023.
Against a Bears defense that will pose a tough test for Detroit's run game, the Lions may open up through the air and get Goff opportunities to pick apart the Bears' secondary. It won't be an easy task with a pass-rush that has been invigorated by the addition of Jeffery Simmons, but Goff is playing at a high level currently and has a chance to put himself in MVP talks if he delivers a solid performance against the Bears on Sunday.
On the other hand, if he doesn't play well it could result in the Lions missing an opportunity to put themselves in the driver's seat in the division. For a team looking to win it's third division title in four years, this would be a big missed opportunity if they come up short.
The Lions have turned to Scruggs once again as the starting center, as Cade Mays was placed on injured reserve for the second time this season. After being acquired as guard depth, Scruggs has started eight of the team's 10 games at center and has handled the role very effectively.
Scruggs currently ranks fifth among starting centers with a 75.4 overall offensive grade via Pro Football Focus, and ranks third with a 78.6 run-blocking grade. On Thursday, he'll have as tough of a test as he's had all season with this Bears defensive line.
Jeffery Simmons and Grady Jarrett are both pass-rush threats who get plenty of action on Chicago's interior defensive line, and Scruggs will be responsible not only with blocking them but also communicating protections to the rest of the offensive line.
As a result, Scruggs carries a massive role in whether or not the Lions will have success offensively against the Bears' defense.
McNeill has been the Lions' most consistent defensive lineman this season, and is playing like a potential All-Pro candidate at this point in the season. He ranks third among all interior linemen in pressures with 38, and is also third in sacks amongst defensive tackles with 6.5 behind Simmons and Dallas' Quinnen Williams.
Chicago poses a unique threat offensively with Caleb Williams leading the charge. Williams is a crafty passer, as he thrives playing out of system and routinely extends plays with his legs to make life difficult for defenses.
The season-ending injury to Aidan Hutchinson leaves a void, and while DJ Wonnum and Derrick Moore have been successful as of late, ultimately McNeill holds the key with his ability to get after the quarterback from the interior and chase down plays.

title: Lions Playoff Picture, Week 12: Battle for NFC North Lead Looms
full_text:
The Detroit Lions and Chicago Bears have both done their respective parts to make Thursday's Thanksgiving clash one of the biggest in recent memory.
Though the Lions have a history of struggling on the national holiday, they have an opportunity to right those wrongs in a battle that will decide who holds the lead in the NFC North to start the late-season stretch run.
Both Detroit and Chicago enter Sunday's game at 8-2, in a tie for first-place in the division. Detroit currently holds the advantage based on divisional record , as they're 2-0 while the Bears are 0-2 in NFC North games.
There's plenty of history between Chicago and Detroit, adding to the stakes of Thursday's game. The Bears are coached by former Lions offensive coordinator Ben Johnson, and the team features multiple former Lions such as running back D'Andre Swift and wide receiver Kalif Raymond.
As a result, the Thanksgiving matchup will be ultra consequential. While these two teams will meet again in Chicago in Week 17, winning this game will give one team the advantage when it comes to jockeying for standings advantages late in the year.
Additionally, both teams are one game back of the No. 1 seed in the NFC, so continuing to win will be important when it comes to a team controlling its own destiny late in the year.
The Minnesota Vikings lost to the San Francisco 49ers in Mexico City on Sunday, dropping them to 7-3. Detroit currently holds the head-to-head tiebreaker over the Vikings, while the Bears lost to them in Week 2.
All four of the NFC North teams currently sit above .500 on the year, with the last-place Packers holding a 6-4 record. This week is a big one across the division, as the Packers have a massive game of their own against the Los Angeles Rams.
Both teams will be coming off a bye week for Wednesday's game, which will be streamed on Netflix. Green Bay and Los Angeles are both 6-4, with Green Bay holding the three-way tiebreaker over the Rams and Seattle Seahawks.
The winner of Wednesday's game will have a massive advantage thanks to the head-to-head tiebreaker it would grant, while the loser will drop a game back of the logjam for the final playoff spot.
Minnesota, meanwhile, will have a matchup Sunday with the Atlanta Falcons. A loss could be detrimental to them, as it would drop them to 7-4 and even with whomever wins Wednesday's game. It's worth noting that they hold the head-to-head tiebreaker over Green Bay as they swept the two meetings they've had this year.

title: Packers-Rams Predictions: Who Will Win Showdown 32,200 Days in the Making?
full_text:
The Green Bay Packers have played only one Wednesday game in franchise history, a 24-22 win over the Chicago Cardinals in Buffalo in 1938. That was 32,200 days ago.
“Obviously, this is a unique thing. The NFL made up their own holiday,” linebacker Zaire Franklin said. “I’ll be looking forward to celebrating the new holiday, Thanksgiving Eve, with all you guys in LA. So, that’ll be pretty fun.”
It’s a huge game. Both teams are 6-4. The winner will remain in the lead for the final spot in the NFC playoffs. The loser will essentially be two games behind because of the tiebreaker.
“Man, there’s nothing worse than losing off the bye. Hate it,” Franklin said. “And I don’t like losing with a long plane ride. So, triple reasons to get the win.”
Even with their injury issues on offense , the Rams are 2.5-point favorites at FanDuel Sportsbook; the line had been 3. Who will earn the crucial victory? Here are our weekly game predictions.
The Rams were the overwhelming favorites to win this year’s Super Bowl before the season. They overhauled their defense by adding legendary edge rusher Myles Garrett and cornerbacks Trent McDuffie and Jaylen Watson. Enticed by their potential, legendary defensive tackle Aaron Donald came out of retirement.
Games are played on the field and not on paper. The Rams started 2-4, including a woeful home loss to the Cardinals. However, they’ve rounded into form with four consecutive wins. They’ve allowed just 28 points the last three games, with Garrett recording three sacks against the Commanders and Donald 1.5 sacks in the rematch against the Cardinals.
Last week, Packers quarterback Jordan Love was pummeled for eight sacks in about two-and-a-half quarters. If they couldn’t block the Vikings, how on earth are they going to block Garrett, Donald, Byron Young and Kobie Turner? They are the best four-man rush in the league.
It sounds like Mission Impossible, with the potential of Love getting the stuffing knocked out of him for a second consecutive week.
However, the Packers’ defense will get a major lift with the return of Micah Parsons. The question entering the season was whether the defense could survive the first four-or-so games of the season without Parsons. Well, it survived the first 10 games.
While the Packers are in relatively good health, the Rams will be limping into the game. Premier receiver Puka Nacua is on injured reserve with a knee injury and Davante Adams remains on IR with a hamstring injury. Plus, their starting left guard and starting center will be inactive. Added together, there is a real opportunity for Green Bay’s defense to feast.
On the other side of the ball, the Rams’ pass rush is going to create all sorts of problems, though the return of center Sean Rhyan and the potential starting debut of right guard Kevin Zeitler should help. They’ll have to be studs so the Packers can swing the pressure toward whoever has to deal with Garrett.
Regardless of who’s blocking, coach Matt LaFleur and quarterback Jordan Love had better have learned a lesson from last week. LaFleur needs to call some quick-hitting passes and Love needs to run those quick-hitting passes rather than sticking with his bombs-away mentality. McDuffie is having a sensational season but Watson is on injured reserve, so there should be some opportunities for receivers Christian Watson and Matthew Golden.
Ultimately, the bigger advantage is with Green Bay’s defense against Los Angeles’ beat-up offense. Parsons, Xavier McKinney and Evan Williams will make enough plays to give the Packers the victory necessary to propel them toward a run to the playoffs.
Who’s getting the W tomorrow? 🤔 pic.twitter.com/bUX4vDaSlY
Bill’s Prediction: Packers 20, Rams 17.
This is a tough matchup for Green Bay.
The Rams’ defense is excellent against the run, so the Packers’ putrid run game will have even less room to roam than usual.
The passing game is going to struggle with Myles Garrett and Aaron Donald breathing down Jordan Love’s neck for most of the night. Once the ball does go in the air, Trent McDuffie is one of the best cornerbacks in football. He could take away one of Green Bay’s top two passing options.
So, why take the Packers? The return of Micah Parsons should give the defense an emotional boost. That doesn’t even include what he could be on the field. Green Bay’s defense has been good without Parsons this year. With him back, if he is even close to his usual, dominant self, they have the ceiling to be one of the best defenses in football.
After suffering knee injuries in Week 15 of last season, Micah Parsons is expected to make his return vs Rams in Week 12 😤 pic.twitter.com/pVqnMsTxQJ
Couple that fact with the fact Matthew Stafford will be missing his top two receivers and two starters on the offensive line.
This game could come down to one game-changing turnover. If we’re calling our shot, we’ll bet on Parsons stripping Stafford to set up a game-winning drive for Love.
Jacob’s Prediction: Packers 21, Rams 17.

title: Three Fear Factors Why Rams Will Sack Packers in Pivotal Thanksgiving Eve Showdown
full_text:
GREEN BAY, Wis. – It’s not a must-win game but it’s pretty darned close.
The Green Bay Packers are 6-4 and clinging to the final playoff spot in the NFC. The Los Angeles Rams – the preseason Super Bowl favorites – are 6-4 and right on their heels. The winner of Wednesday’s made-up holiday showdown will not only have a one-game lead over the loser but also own the tiebreaker.
Here are three reasons why the Packers will lose to the Rams and see their playoff teetering on thin ice.
Games aren’t won on first down and they’re not decided between the 20s.
No, games are decided on third down and in the red zone. In all four areas, the Rams have enormous advantages.
When the Packers have the ball, they are 20th on third down (37.2 percent conversions) and 20th in the red zone (54.3 percent touchdowns). On defense, the Rams are second on third down (30.0 percent conversions) and fourth in the red zone (43.3 percent touchdowns).
“It’s a really sound defense, obviously,” Packers coach Matt LaFleur said when asked about the Rams in those areas. “They’ve got some creatures up front that are a problem. I think they do a great job in the back end. It’s well coordinated just in terms of challenging when they play man, and then when they’re playing their soft zones, of not getting beat deep and giving stuff over the top.
“I think all in all, I just don’t see many holes and there’s not many weaknesses to the defense. I think Chris Shula does an unbelievable job coordinating  that thing and putting those guys in position to be playmakers, and then they have playmakers.”
When the Packers are on defense, they are 22nd on third down (42.7 percent conversions) and 21st in the red zone (63.6 percent touchdowns). The Rams are ninth on third down (41.8 percent conversions) and seventh in the red zone (66.7 percent touchdowns).
To put a bow on it, in all four categories, the Packers are 20th or worse and the Rams are inside the top 10.
In what's essentially a must-win game, here are three reasons why the Packers will earn a critical victory over the Rams tonight. (Opposite side of this story coming shortly.) ⬇️ https://t.co/t25ekTvQDE
Obviously, the matchup will not be Packers running back Kaleb Johnson vs. Rams running back Kyren Williams. But the Rams have an elite rushing attack, meaning they can mitigate the Packers’ pass rush, and the Packers have a putrid rushing attack, meaning the Rams can attack Jordan Love with little fear.
Los Angeles enters the game ranked seventh in rushing yards per game (133.0) and per carry (4.62). It has an outside chance of having two 1,000-yard rushers with Williams (616 yards, 4.4 average and six touchdowns) and Blake Corum (547 yards, 5.3 average, five touchdowns). Both rank among the top 20 individuals in rushing yards.
Williams is the proven workhorse with three consecutive seasons of 1,100-plus rushing yards and double-digits touchdowns, but Corum is the hot hand as he comes off a 100-yard game at Arizona and is on a streak of four consecutive games with a touchdown.
“Yeah, you can’t tackle them,” defensive coordinator Jonathan Gannon said. “That’s what they’ve shown. They’ve got really good contact balance. They’re both very strong, they’ve got really good vision, they’ve got good patience with their run scheme. I think what goes unnoticed is how they make it go with the acceleration when they need the acceleration, the hesitation when they need the hesitation to let the blocks declare.
“I’ve got a high opinion of both of these guys. And they’re both weapons out of the backfield, so they can hurt you in the pass game, as well. I’m not screens; I’m talking out on routes as receivers. They’ve got really good players in a really good scheme and it’s another reason they put a lot of points on a lot of people.”
Aside from the one horrendous game against the Falcons, Green Bay’s run defense has been solid this season, though it has allowed the fourth-most rushing touchdowns (12) in the league.
The run offense is another story. The Packers are last in the league with 67.0 rushing yards per game and 3.06 yards per carry. Johnson has provided a bit of a spark but can he do enough against a Rams run defense that ranks 11th with 3.92 yards allowed per carry to give the offense necessary balance?
“We have that mindset every week to go out there and try to dominate,” Rams defensive tackle Aaron Donald told reporters this week. “We have to go out there and do it, starting with stopping the run. We have to be able to play the run well and get them in situations where they have to pass. If we do that, we feel like we can take advantage, but we have to earn that.”
The Packers are going to be in big trouble, and Jordan Love is going to be in a world of hurt, if it becomes a pass-every-play kind of game.
The Rams will be wearing throwback jerseys to the Fearsome Foursome era. These Rams have a fearsome pass rush.
In his first game back following a two-month layoff, outside linebacker Myles Garrett had three sacks. Defensive tackle Aaron Donald, who came out of retirement to chase a Super Bowl ring, had 1.5 sacks last week. Defensive tackle Kobie Turner, who had nine sacks as a rookie alongside Donald in 2023, eight in 2024 and seven in 2025, was activated from injured reserve this week. Outside linebacker Byron Young has 5.5 sacks this season after a career-high 12 last year.
Along with defensive tackle Braden Fiske, the Rams have five players who can get after the quarterback.
“The front. That’s what stands out to you,” Love said. “Obviously, Myles Garrett, Aaron Donald, they’ve got a lot of good guys up front. Especially when they’re in base, you get five one-on-one blocks. They’ve got some good players over there, so that definitely stands out.
“It’s something that we talk about it all week, it starts up front. We’ve got to handle business. We’ve got to be able to block the front, give me some time and in the run game, we’ve got to be able to get hands on people, create some lanes in the run game. But I think if you look at their team, the defensive front stands out.”
With the Browns, Garrett set an NFL record with 23 sacks last season and led the league with 33 tackles for losses, including a half-sack and four pressures against the Packers.
“There’s not too many guys with his size and speed,” coach Matt LaFleur said. “He’s got a great get-off. Obviously, his strength is as good as anybody. It’s a rare combo of size and speed.”
Green Bay allowed eight sacks last week against the Vikings. The challenge won’t be schematic this week; the Rams are only 18th in blitz rate. The challenge will be winning the individual matchups because they can’t double team everyone.
“They try to press and assert their will, and they’re looking for a game to break through that barrier, and we can’t allow that to be us,” Garrett said. “They have an exceptional quarterback in Jordan Love, who can push the ball downfield and make plays, which they’ve done pretty much all season to this point.
“We can’t allow them to be versatile with being able to [rush] on the ground and gain yards there but also push down the field with his arm. We’re going to have to make them one-dimensional and get after the passer.”

title: These Three Critical Factors Point to Packers Beating Rams
full_text:
GREEN BAY, Wis. – The Green Bay Packers and Los Angeles Rams are 6-4 and lead the chase for the seventh and final playoff spot in the NFC.
Which team will be thankful for a win and which will be crying into the cranberries?
Here are three reasons why the Packers will beat the Rams in their Thanksgiving Eve showdown at SoFi Stadium.
The Packers will be getting the biggest lift imaginable with the return of Micah Parsons. They did well to win six games without him, with Jonathan Gannon figuring out a way to field a defense that is second in takeaways and fourth in yards allowed per play.
“He's one of the ones, for sure,” nickel Javon Bullard said. “I think it's only going to make us better, man. With [No.] 1 on the field, we're a better team. We're a better defense. He's an unselfish player. He's a guy that really wants to win. He works his ass off, and you know he's going to make our team better.
“And, honestly, with him coming together, I think it's going to make us jell even more. He's going to up everybody else's game, you know? And we're going to up his game. I think that's what makes this defense special. I think we really care about one another. We want to see each other maximize our full potential.”
Team Pressure Rates Data: @FantasyPtsData pic.twitter.com/ly0w6yBx01
The Packers rank 11th in sack percentage and fourth in pressure percentage. Now, they are getting back one of the marquee players in the game.
“It's similar to me in that you can line me up pretty much anywhere and expect to win,” Rams star Myles Garrett told reporters. “He has success rushing inside the tackle, outside the tackle, over the guard and over the center. He's smaller. He moves well. He has great get-off. He has supreme instincts. He really is the full package.”
He will face a tough matchup against the Rams’ unsung tackle tandem of Alaric Jackson and Warren McClendon, who have allowed only two sacks apiece.
“Man, I would say I have no targets,” Parsons said on Monday. “The only thing I’m targeting in a sense of mindset is to win every week to try to uplift this season, change this season around, and do exactly what the Packers brought me here to do. That’s it. That’s my only target and that’s to make a run for the playoffs and make guys around me better.”
The Packers have been outscored 81-9 in the final 5 minutes of the 4th quarter and in OT since Micah Parsons tore his ACL (including playoffs) NFL-worst -72 pts diff https://t.co/JYprkeg7mW
Packers coach Matt LaFleur is 5-0 against his best friend and former boss, Rams coach Sean McVay. That includes Green Bay’s win in the 2020 playoffs.
The first four of those games were played at Lambeau Field. The fifth was at SoFi Stadium in 2024, with the Packers holding on for a 24-19 win as the Rams played without Puka Nacua and Cooper Kupp. (More on that in a moment.)
McVay is one of the best coaches in the league. And yet, for whatever reason, LaFleur has had his number.
“It’s a cool thing to have as many friends as we do from just us all growing up, pushing one another to be in leadership opportunities,” McVay said this week. “It's about the Packers versus the Rams, but I do have a lot of love for Matt.
“Our friendship goes way back. Before I met my wife and before they even had their kids, I'd go hang out with Bre [LaFleur] and Matt in Reston Town Center and I was like the third wheel of their relationship. I was like the little brother. I love Matt, love Bre, love their family. It'll be cool, but we're trying to kick each other's ass, I know that much. He's going to try to do the same thing. This is about the Rams versus the Packers and I'm excited for a good competitive game and, hopefully, we both stay healthy.”
As an important aside, LaFleur has gone against Aaron Donald three times. He had one sack, which represented the only tackle for loss in those games.
The Packers have worked their way through some key injuries this season, so they will have no pity for what the Rams are going through.
Just like the 2024 game, the Packers will be facing a Rams offense that will line up without its premier receivers. Puka Nacua and Davante Adams, who have combined for 100 receptions, are on injured reserve. So is Jordan Whittington, who had a career-high seven catches to pick up the slack for the Rams in the 2024 game.
On the perimeter, the leading receiver is Konata Mumpfield, who has 14 catches. Next is Tutu Atwell with eight.
If anyone can make it work, it’s quarterback Matthew Stafford. He’s got a fleet of quality tight ends, led by Tyler Higbee, who has 31 catches. Plus, he can lean on a stud running back tandem, led by Kyren Williams, who has 38 catches.
“I think we have a pretty good idea of who they want to be,” Packers coach Matt LaFleur said. “Sean, he’s as good as anybody in the business at what he does. They do a great job running the football. Obviously, when you’ve got an MVP quarterback, that presents its own set of challenges. Matthew Stafford’s as good as it gets. And they’ve got other players outside of Puka and Davante. I think the tight end group is as complete as you can find in the National Football League.”
Complicating things even further for the Rams, starting center Coleman Shelton and starting left guard Steve Avila will be inactive.
The ability to get pressure through traditional means will be huge. There is no blitz or disguise that Stafford hasn’t seen. Green Bay with Parsons must win up front against a Rams line that will start two backups.
“You still got to try, but you’re not tricking Matt. That’s for sure,” Packers defensive coordinator Jonathan Gannon said. “Playing vs. this guy a bunch, he’s as good as they are. Timing, accuracy, knows where to go with the ball. They do a really good job of finding space for him, and he can fit any throw into any window that you want.
“Was just watching a bunch of tape with the guys. You think no chance he can make that throw and he makes them, so big-time challenge. I got a high opinion of Matt, and I think he’s one of the best in the business. Then, obviously, Sean and their whole staff do a really good job with him.”
Stafford is aggressive with the ball. He’s thrown 10 interceptions this season – including one in four consecutive games. That could play into the hands of Green Bay’s playmaking secondary and deliver a game-changing play.

title: Packers-Rams Final Injury Report: One Interesting Questionable for Showdown
full_text:
GREEN BAY, Wis. – The Green Bay Packers listed eight players as questionable for Wednesday night’s game at the Los Angeles Rams.
One of those players jumps off the list.
No, not Micah Parsons , though he is questionable to make his season debut.
It’s running back Josh Jacobs.
Jacobs sustained a broken ring finger early in the blowout win at New England a couple weeks ago. He had surgery before last week’s game against the Vikings and did not play.
All week, Jacobs was limited participation at practice. All week, coach Matt LaFleur suggested Jacobs would not play.
“I’m not anticipating that, but we’ll see how he progresses, as well,” LaFleur said before Saturday’s practice. “He would definitely have to prove the function in order to play.”
On Sunday, LaFleur didn’t really change his tune.
“I would say so,” he said when asked if Jacobs was unlikely to play.
But LaFleur didn’t rule out Jacobs on his final injury report. He didn’t even list him as doubtful.
Without Jacobs for most of the New England game and the entire Minnesota game, Kaleb Johnson went from the doghouse to, well, not quite the penthouse but to the team’s No. 1 ball-carrier.
The Packers acquired Johnson, a third-round pick by the Steelers last year, from Pittsburgh in a trade during final roster cuts. Two fumbles in his first three games led to Johnson barely playing over the course of the next four weeks.
Due to injuries to Jacobs and Chris Brooks and ineffective play by MarShawn Lloyd and Pierre Strong, Johnson carried 24 times for 110 yards the last two weeks. He ranks among the NFL leaders in yards after contact per carry.
“I feel like I faced adversity throughout the whole time because I feel like in college everything was going good for me,” Johnson said this week. “I really haven’t faced adversity, and I felt like during that time it was just like when it happened, it was like ‘Oh, shit, here we go. Overcome this and see how I bounce back.’
“I feel like it was me just believing in God and just keeping going and just keep striving and keeping my head down and working. That was really it and being me. Got comfortable with the system and went out there and be Kaleb.”
Before departing for Los Angeles on Tuesday, Packers coach Matt LaFleur listed eight players as questionable. Along with Micah Parsons and Josh Jacobs, the others were linebacker Zaire Franklin (shin), receivers Bo Melton (thigh) and Skyy Moore (ankle), and offensive linemen Sean Rhyan (ankle), Kevin Zeitler (triceps) and Travis Glover (shoulder).
All eight of those players would have been limited participation had the Packers practiced on Tuesday.
The Packers could be rolling out their seventh starting line this season if Rhyan returns at center and Zeitler starts at right guard. Rhyan missed the last three games and Zeitler’s starting debut was derailed last week by a triceps injury.
The importance of continuity on the offensive line is “absolutely not” overblown, LaFleur said. They’re still searching for it this season.
“I think continuity is critical, especially when you’re talking about the offensive line, where you need five guys working as one,” he said on Monday. “I think that is a huge component in terms of your ability to go out there and have consistent success. And I also think the experience of that group up front plays a pivotal role in that, as well.”
Rhyan and Zeitler have experience. Rhyan has started 35 games the past two-and-a-half seasons and Zeitler has started 213 games in 15 seasons. Along with Laken Tomlinson, who figures to make his 170th career start, Green Bay’s potential interior trio could enter the game with 417 career starts.
Speaking of experience, Franklin – a defensive captain – is expected to be back in the lineup after missing the last four games.
“I genuinely believe everything happens for a reason,” Franklin said . “I had a close friend tell me that I came here to play 17; I just got to play 17 a different way. We missed four; that means we got to get the extra four. I’m just glad I’m back, ready to play.”
The Rams, as has been known all week, will attack the Packers without their two star receivers, with Puka Nacua (knee) and Davante Adams (hamstring) on injured reserve.
Complicating matters is they’ll also line up without two of their starting offensive linemen. Left guard Steve Avila (hamstring) and center Coleman Shelton (hamstring) were ruled out by coach Sean McVay. Neither player has allowed a sack this season.
Nacua and Adams have a combined 100 catches. No other receiver on the roster has more than Konata Mumpfield’s 14.
“The one thing is you feel for the players that don't get a chance to be out there that you have big visions for and are significant factors,” McVay told reporters on Monday. “What you don't want to do is minimize what a big deal it is to those other guys that are getting opportunities to be able to figure out what they do best? How do you accentuate their skill-sets? How do you instill a belief of confidence in their ability to go play as well as they can?
“Our job as coaches is to help these guys go shine with our decisions, with the spots that they're put in. Then let's go have the courage to cut it loose and have no regrets.”
Questionable: LB Zaire Franklin (shin), G Travis Glover (shoulder), RB Josh Jacobs (finger), LB WR Bo Melton (thigh), WR Skyy Moore (ankle), edge Micah Parsons (knee), C Sean Rhyan (ankle), G Kevin Zeitler (triceps).
No injury designation: G Aaron Banks (knee), CB Brandon Cisse (rib), Isaiah McDuffie (rib).
Out: LG Steve Avila (hamstring), TE Terrance Ferguson (ankle/hamstring), C Coleman Shelton (hamstring).
No injury designation: TE Davis Allen (oblique), LS Joe Cardona (ankle), S Kam Curl (toe), G Justin Dedich (hand), DT Aaron Donald (rest), OLB Myles Garrett (knee), TE Tyler Higbee (rest), LB Nate Landman (toe), CB Trent McDuffie (back), TE Colby Parkinson (ribs), QB Matthew Stafford (right elbow), DE Kobie Turner (groin), RB Kyren Williams (toe), OLB Byron Young (rest).

title: He’s Back! Five Areas Where Micah Parsons Can Lift Packers’ Defense to Next Level
full_text:
GREEN BAY, Wis. – Micah Parsons is officially back with the Green Bay Packers. Parsons was activated off injured reserve on Tuesday and is expected to make his season debut at the Los Angeles Rams on Wednesday.
Parsons will bolster one of the better defenses in the NFL. The Packers are a mediocre 16th in points allowed per game, though that is skewed a bit by the combined 69 points allowed in the two games against Minnesota, when Green Bay was guilty of six turnovers and gave up 12 sacks.
The better picture is the Packers have allowed 20-or-fewer points in six games this season, one off the league lead. They are fourth in yards allowed per play, fourth in yards allowed per passing play, second in interception percentage, fifth in opponent passer rating and 11th in sack percentage.
This is a really good defense that’s about to regain the services of one of the best players in the NFL.
“I would say I’m really, really confident,” Parsons said after Monday’s practice. “I’m my own biggest critic. You don’t put together multiple good seasons if you don’t set your bar really high.”
Early in the week, defensive coordinator Jonathan Gannon – with the caveat that it might be a “silly question” – was asked if there was any challenge to adding a player of Parsons’ talent and production.
“No, that’s a good question,” Gannon said. “Obviously, when you have very talented players, you want to highlight them and put them in good positions as much as we can to impact the game and, understanding a player of his caliber, people are going to play you different.”
Remember, the Packers went 0-5 following Parsons’ knee injury last season. They are 6-4 this season. So, they weathered the storm well enough to be in the thick of the playoff race, even if they’re not strong competitors to win the loaded NFC North.
Here’s where Parsons will make the biggest impact, beginning against the Rams.
The Packers are tied for seventh in the league with 29 sacks. It’s a rather astounding feat considering they were last in the league with only four sacks during the final five games of last season.
Defensive coordinator Jonathan Gannon has created pressure out of thin air. Lukas Van Ness is tied for 18th in the league with six sacks. The Packers desperately needed him to have a breakout season and he’s delivered.
Nobody else has really filled the void. Karl Brooks, Dani Dennis Sutton, Devonte Wyatt and Edgerrin Cooper are next with three sacks apiece. That’s tied for 68th in the league. Brooks had all three the last two games, Wyatt hasn’t lived up to his contract, Dennis-Sutton is a rookie backup and Cooper hasn’t played since Week 4.
Enter Parsons, who last season became the only player in NFL history to start his career with five consecutive seasons of 12-plus sacks. He’s probably not going to get a dozen sacks over the final seven games, but he will be an impact addition.
For a big chunk of the season, the pass rush has been dependent on Gannon creating it. Now, Gannon might not have to dig through his bag of tricks so heavily.
Most pressures over last 6 seasons Maxx Crosby            433 Myles Garrett           416 Micah Parsons        409* Josh Hines-Allen    396 Chris Jones               378 *Hasn’t played since Week 15 of last season, questionable for Wednesday’s game vs Rams pic.twitter.com/qimM91IavC
It’s not as if he’s seen a never-ending stream of double teams, but Lukas Van Ness has been the one player circled by opposing offensive coordinators.
Among the 75 edge rushers with at least 150 pass-rushing opportunities, Van Ness ranks ninth in pass-rush win rate and 11th in pass-rushing productivity, a PFF metric that combines sacks, hits and hurries per pass-rushing snap.
Van Ness has done a good job keeping the pass rush relevant without Parsons, but nobody would consider him a consistent, field-tilting pass rusher. Now with the return of Parsons, Van Ness should get better opportunities. That makes the return of Parsons almost a two-for-one addition. Parsons will make an impact and Van Ness will be better.
The Packers gave Devonte Wyatt a three-year contract extension worth $54.9 million this offseason. Wyatt has three sacks, which are as many as former teammate Colby Wooden has with the Saints. According to PFF, Wyatt has only nine pressures. Among defensive tackles, Wyatt is 68th in pressures and 66th in pass-rush win rate.
If that’s not enough, Packers safety Evan Williams has 13 pressures.
Maybe the attention paid to Parsons will help Wyatt get to the quarterback with greater frequency.
A great pass rush is a defensive back’s best friend.
Even without an elite pass rusher, the Packers enter Week 12 ranked second in the league with 20 takeaways. That’s one behind Tampa Bay’s team-leading total and at least five more than 25 teams. It is arguably the greatest strength on the team.
A great pass rush could set up a ballhawking secondary for more interceptions. The Packers are second in the league with 14, led by Xavier McKinney’s NFL-high six . Cornerbacks Keisean Nixon and Brandon Cisse have covered well for most of the season but have only one interception apiece.
And you can’t have a sack-strip without a sack. Parsons had two forced fumbles last season and 11 in his first five seasons.
“We’re hoping they get as many sacks as they want,” starting slot Javon Bullard said. “You know the ball’s coming out hot. We’re ready. And with those guys patrolling the back end and with the corners playing the way they’re playing right now, I think it presents itself with a lot more opportunities for us taking the ball away. We try and do that at a high level, so shit, man, they can do they do what they want up front, man. As long as they get into that quarterback, we good.”
Without question, takeaways have been a strength. What has not been a strength is the consistency of the offense, which ranks 14th in scoring. A big takeaway in a big game could help deliver the pivotal points.
Green Bay’s defense is across-the-board good except in two critical areas.
One is on third down, where the Packers are 22nd in the league and gave up three killer third-and-long conversions last week against Minnesota. The Rams on offense are ninth on third down, one of six top-12 opponents they’ll face to end the season. The second is in the red zone, where they are 21st. The Rams are seventh, one of five top-12 attacks they’ll face down the stretch.
Parsons’ ability to get after the passer – or free up others to get to the passer – could be the critical difference in big moments.
“Man, I just like how the guys extremely stepped up all across the front. I’m so proud of everyone between BC, Luke and Barryn and KB and D-Wy,” Parsons said of Brenton Cox, Van Ness, Barryn Sorrell and Wyatt.
“We’re just a part of the brotherhood. I know I don’t get to spend time with everyone, but I would say we’re a really close-knit group and we really care a lot about each other and we really want to see all of each other be great. So, the things that we accomplish isn’t a surprise. I just think we can go to another level.”

title: At 10-Year Anniversary of ‘Run the Table,’ Can the Packers Do It Again?
full_text:
Like Babe Ruth, Aaron Rodgers called his shot almost exactly 10 years ago today.
With the Green Bay Packers mired in a tailspin with four consecutive losses during the middle of the 2016 season, saddled with a disappointing 4-6 record and having just been blown out by the then-Washington Redskins 42-24, Rodgers made his claim.
“I feel like we can run the table,” Rodgers said at his locker on Nov. 23.
The comments were met with a general disbelief. The Packers had been terrible in each of their last two games. They had been blown away by the Tennessee Titans before getting blown up by Washington.
The Packers had six games left on their schedule. They likely needed to win all six to get into the playoffs.
Rodgers went on a tear. The Packers made Rodgers’ words prophetic. They won road games against Philadelphia, Chicago and Detroit. Ditto for home games against Houston, Minnesota and Seattle.
The result was an NFC North title and an improbable run to the NFC Championship Game, before a beaten-up roster was overwhelmed by the Falcons.
Fast forward to 2026. Can this year’s version of the Green Bay Packers run the table and finish the season 13-4?
The Case: For all the talk about the Packers’ injury situation, the Rams’ offense looks like that of a MASH unit compared to who they are supposed to have on the field. Puka Nacua and Davante Adams are going to spend Wednesday’s game on injured reserve. Terrance Ferguson, the Rams’ most explosive tight end, is on injured reserve, as well.
The Packers, meanwhile, will welcome Micah Parsons back to the lineup. Even if he’s not his usual dominant self, his presence makes everyone around him better. That’s true from the emotional boost he will provide along with the gameplan that Sean McVay must put together to account for him.
While this is a true road game, the likelihood is that SoFi Stadium will turn into Lambeau Field West, which could give the Packers an advantage at the biggest points of the game.
The Case: The Saints are 1-5 in conference play and 1-5 at home. They are likely ticketed for one of the top spots in April’s draft. The only reason they are in playoff contention is because they play in the dreadful NFC South.
Yes, they will be playing at home, but the Packers’ offense should play up on the Saints’ fast track. Tyler Shough vs. Jordan Love is a massive advantage at quarterback in favor of the Packers.
The Case: Josh Allen is the best quarterback in the NFL. That’s a reality the Packers’ defense will have to handle. Allen is a tough customer, no matter how good your defense.
In this game, however, the biggest mismatch could be Green Bay’s offense against Buffalo’s defense. In his first season as coordinator, Jim Leonhard’s unit ranks 19th in passing yards allowed per game and 21st in sack percentage.
Jordan Love, Christian Watson and Matthew Golden could be licking their chops.
Stopping Allen is no easy task, obviously, but the Packers have the defense to potentially keep him in check. He’s also prone to some mind-numbing turnovers. Allen has thrown five picks in his last four games. That could turn the tide in Green Bay’s favor.
The Case: Jeff Hafley may eventually build a winner in Miami, but the expectations in South Beach were clear this season.
Jon-Eric Sullivan said after they traded Jaylen Waddle to the Broncos that his team needed to get younger and cheaper. They’ve succeeded in that regard, but are now going through the growing pains required of having a younger team.
Malik Willis, who is on injured reserve with a groin injury but could be back in the lineup for this game, has not maintained the success in Miami that he enjoyed during his time in Green Bay. Miami’s offense is limited, especially with De’Von Achane on the sideline for the rest of the season.
Hafley’s defense could frustrate Jordan Love at times, but the Packers should be able to control this game with their defense.
The Case: Chicago’s defense has gotten better with the addition of defensive tackle Jeffery Simmons before the trade deadline. Simmons had three sacks against the Saints on Sunday and has been a true game wrecker since arriving in the Wind City.
Green Bay’s offense does match up well with Chicago’s deficiencies. Christian Watson and Matthew Golden lit up Chicago’s defense for more than 100 receiving yards apiece when the teams met in early October.
Of course, Simmons was not in the lineup that day. For all the fanfare about Caleb Williams’ ascension, he’s been fairly mediocre since returning from a hamstring injury. Williams threw four interceptions against Tampa Bay two weeks ago and struggled to generate offense in the rainy conditions against the Saints on Sunday.
He has thrown 10 touchdowns to six interceptions this season. He is very talented, but has not been consistently great.
The Case: C.J. Stroud in the cold has typically been a good recipe for opposing defenses. This will be a Monday night game in January for Stroud. Will the Texans be playing for anything? After a 0-4 start, they are out of the AFC South race. Having rebounded with four wins in their last six games, can they work their way back into the wild card chase, where they’re two games off the pace?
If they can’t, will they be overly motivated in wintery conditions as a dome team? The weather has not mattered as much for the Packers in recent years, but the Texans could be feeling the disappointment of an underwhelming season.
The Case: Jared Goff’s physical limitations could make for an interesting matchup for a January game at Lambeau Field.
These teams met earlier in the year, with the Lions coming away with a 20-17 victory at Ford Field. The Lions had Aidan Hutchinson and Jack Campbell that day. They also had the benefit of their offense playing on a fast track and against a defense without Micah Parsons.
Lambeau Field should be in full Frozen Tundra form by mid-January.
Can Green Bay beat a bad defense at home in a game in which they could be playing for their playoff lives? In the run-the-table-scenario we’re laying out, they could be playing for something as high as the second seed in the NFC playoffs.
The Packers would and should be highly motivated if it comes down to the final game of the year.

title: Packers’ Xavier McKinney on Being ‘Special Player’ Compared to Other NFL Safeties
full_text:
GREEN BAY, Wis. – Baltimore Ravens safety Kyle Hamilton is in his fifth season in the NFL. A first-team All-Pro in 2023 and 2025, he has six interceptions in his career.
Green Bay Packers safety Xavier McKinney has a league-leading six this season.
How? How has McKinney, who had eight interceptions when he was a first-team All-Pro in 2024, remained a premier ballhawk when his game-changing ability remains well known around the NFL?
“I think that’s just who I’ve always been,” McKinney told Packers On SI on Sunday. “Always been a guy that’s been able to be around the ball, to make plays on the ball, use my instincts, and ultimately be a playmaker. I think it’s a very unique thing to be able to do.
“Even the good safeties, sometimes you don’t see them get a lot of picks. But some guys are different and better in different areas. So, it’s not taking away from them as far as how good they are. But I think it does take a special player to be able to get his hands on the ball frequently every year, even when they are game planning for you. You know what I mean? So, it takes a special player. But I think just for me, man, I just continue to keep using my instincts and letting my ball awareness take over.”
Since signing with the Packers in free agency in 2024, McKinney has 16 interceptions – four more than any other player.
For McKinney, it’s the unmatchable combination of talent, intelligence and feel for the game that puts him in position to make plays and then make those plays.
“I think a part of that is just play recognition, play awareness, route awareness,” he said. “I think I’m very good with route awareness. I think a lot of times that’s where it stems from is being able to decipher routes. A lot of times, I’m not even looking at the routes, but I can feel routes.
“And then obviously reading a quarterback, I’ve been doing that for a long time. I think it’s a mind game. I consider it’s really me versus the quarterback. So, whoever can manipulate their eyes or however I can manipulate my body position, make it look like I’m going this way but I’m actually already in my mind going the other way. So just knowing different stuff and knowing the quarterback’s tendencies and what he likes to do.”
Packers defensive passing game coordinator Bobby Babich spends a lot of practice with the safeties. When Babich was with the Bills, Micah Hyde and Jordan Poyer had five interceptions apiece in 2021 en route to earning All-Pro honors. So, he knows a good safety when he sees one.
Before the 2020 draft, Babich said he had McKinney ranked No. 1 at the position. McKinney has proven Babich right. Since being drafted by the Giants early in the second round, he leads the NFL with 25 interceptions.
“I think some people come out of the womb with the ball finding them,” Babich said. “That is part of it, but the other part is the work he puts into it. I mean, God has gifted him with some incredible football acumen that’s just natural to him. But he works at it. He works at getting the ball – and there’s so much that goes into getting the ball – but he puts in the time.
“Football is extremely important to him, and he’s got his personal goals. So, he has tremendous ball skills, tremendous football awareness. He understands when the route develops what they’re trying to do to us and then assessing how to read quarterbacks. He works at it all. And I can’t say enough about how he’s putting himself in position to make plays. That’s what we talk about all the time. You have to make plays, but before you make plays, you have to put yourself in position to make plays.”
McKinney, a team captain who leads the secondary in the meeting room as well as the playing field, blossomed under former defensive coordinator Jeff Hafley and has continued his elite play under first-year defensive coordinator Jonathan Gannon.
“He really patrols that whole back end and then, obviously, you’ve seen when the ball goes his way, he has a chance to take it away,” Gannon said. “Six through 10 games, that’s a pretty high clip he’s taking it away. But the football character is what I’m so impressed with X about. He takes it on the chin when he’s wrong and he’s trying to always get better. He wears a ‘C’ for a reason.”
McKinney has an elite feel for the game. It was the case in 2024, when his streak of five consecutive games with an interception continued against Matthew Stafford and the Rams, and it’s the case again this year headed into Wednesday’s game at the Rams.
According to Sports Info Solutions, he has almost as many interceptions (six) as completions allowed (eight). It’s not as if he’s chasing plays; he has not been charged with allowing a touchdown since his final season with the Giants.
It’s almost like he has a sixth sense or he’s plugged into the quarterback-coach headset.
“I think it’s a study thing, but I think for me, man, I’m not going to lie, it’s a feel thing,” McKinney said. “I’m great at being able to anticipate things. Right when the ball is snapped, if he’s stemming a certain way, or if we’re in a certain part of the field of what he might run” are cues that lead him to the ball.
“A lot of times,” he continued, “I don’t need to look at the route. It’s like a feel thing. It’s kind of hard to explain. When you’re out there, it’s just like I can feel routes. It’s weird, but that’s how I always have been. I hate looking at routes. I hate looking at routes . Because when I look at routes, it slows me down. But when I’m able to just kind of feel the route, it’s a lot easier. I just can feel the routes a lot of the time. I’m not going to be right all the time. But I think for the most part I do a good job of being aware of knowing what’s coming.”

title: Packers’ Micah Parsons Has Heard the Noise And Offers Thoughtful Response
full_text:
GREEN BAY, Wis. – After a comeback more than 11 months in the making, Green Bay Packers superstar Micah Parsons was cleared to return to game action on Monday and will make his season debut on Wednesday against the Rams.
“Yeah, I would say I’m very eager,” Parsons said. “I think there’s been a lot of whitewash noise out there about my injury and my return to play and things about my injury and comparing it, and I just don’t get into those type of things. I just like to stay straightforward and worry about my own process because I know what type of player I am and I know what type of player I’m going to be when I come back.”
He didn’t add any specifics about that noise, though Parsons and Chiefs quarterback Micah Parsons suffered torn ACLs on Dec. 14 of last season. Mahomes was on the field for the start of training camp and has started every game. Parsons didn’t start practicing until three weeks ago and won’t make his season debut until Week 12.
Even Fox Sports’ Jay Glazer took note of Mahomes’ comeback juxtaposed to Parsons’ prolonged recovery.
The latest on Micah Parson's return to the Packers from @JayGlazer pic.twitter.com/IkHwlnUM6q
What Glazer inexplicably failed to mention was Parsons also suffered meniscus damage, which kept him off his feet for considerably longer than was the case for Mahomes and Packers tight end Tucker Kraft. They also play completely different positions. Mahomes needs to move, obviously, but not at the same level of frequency, explosiveness or violent change of direction as a pass rusher like Parsons.
Glazer was hardly the first person to compare the comebacks of Parsons and Mahomes. And Glazer’s larger point was how Mahomes had surgery shortly after the injury while Parsons waited, which is the norm.
Nonetheless, it’s added a bit more fuel to a fire that’s been smoldering, anyway, as weeks have turned into months for a player who is used to crushing every challenge that’s come his way. In a way, it created a mindset of appreciation and gratitude.
“During this ACL process and meniscus and things like that, you really see some stagnant days,” Parsons said. “Like where ‘Damn, I’m not getting better. I’m not really growing as much as I wanted to grow.’ And I went through seasons of hardship, seasons of test, and it challenged me to be a better person, a better man, and really own every day like its own special day.
“I’ve really embraced just being in the building, being around the guys, being around practice and just being present. Ignoring a lot of the outside world and really just dialed in on what’s really in front of me. There’s nothing right now in life that could really faze me, that could really get me out of a good mood, because I’m so rich in life.”
Parsons went on to talk about his “beautiful kids” and “beautiful family,” his teammates, mentors and everyone who has helped him along the way.
They’ve all set him up for this moment. When Parsons steps onto the field at SoFi Stadium, it will have been 346 days since his career changed at Denver.
Parsons knows what’s at stake. It’s a seven-game, make-or-break dash to the playoffs.
“I would say I’m very hungry,” he said. “I think that guys kind of joke on me because last year I just had all this energy and I was coming back with answers, and now I just take it all in. I’m just like whatever. Keisean’s like, ‘Man, I never seen you so calm and timid.’ It’s just because it’s like built up. ‘I don’t want to waste it on you, Keisean. I don’t want all my energy going toward you, arguing with you.
“I’m ready for the games. I think it’s just a lot of that, man. I’m really geeked up and they like, ‘Are you nervous?’ No, I’m just so focused, I’m so locked in on what’s ahead of me. I understand what this game Wednesday means to the organization and myself and what it means for playoffs. And if I can be out there, I want to be out there. I’m excited for any time, because we only got seven more games left, so I want to capitalize on all those if I can.”
Time is running short. The Packers are 6-4, which is a strong record considering how they went 0-5 without him last season. However, the NFC is loaded. The Packers are in last place in the division and clinging to the final spot in the playoff field .
With the addition of Parsons, anything is possible, “as long as we fix the mistakes and not beat ourselves,” he said.
“We’re in this conference where it’s like you have to play perfect. We don’t got the ability of basketball to lose by 40 one night and come win by 30 the next week. That’s not in our future. Every game has to be perfect and what you need is 53 guys that’s going to buy into being perfect.”
That sense of urgency is something Parsons has preached. He’s been an All-Pro. He’s set records. Now that he’s back, his focus is on “the big one” – aka the Super Bowl.
“That was my message to our D-line room. If you looking down at this, there’s seven games. So, that’s like 49 days and you just mark it down by the weeks, right, so that’s seven weeks. In hindsight, that’s such a small time in your life.
“What are you willing to give in that short time period to maximize what we have right here? Because the deadline’s over. There’s no more adding pieces. This is the best we’re going to get. To be honest with you, we’ve got some really good players and we’ve just got to really maximize our potential to do what we want to do.”

title: Packers-Rams Monday Injury Report: Micah Parsons’ Return Had Ties to Rams’ Doctor
full_text:
GREEN BAY, Wis. – When Green Bay Packers star Micah Parsons spoke to reporters on Monday following the final practice of the week before Wednesday’s game against the Los Angeles Rams, he was awaiting clearance to make his season debut following last year’s season-ending knee injury.
“I really don’t know yet,” Parsons said. “I’ve still got to talk to ElAttrache. I still got to get cleared from my surgical doctor, so we’ll see.”
Dr. Neal ElAttrache, a renowned, Los Angeles-based orthopedic surgeon whose specialties include ACL repair, was part of that decision.
He’s also the head physician for the Rams.
Following a Monday afternoon conference call that included Parsons, ElAttrache and the Packers’ medical staff, Parsons was deemed “100 percent ready” and will play in his first game since he suffered a torn ACL at Denver on Dec. 14.
#Packers star Micah Parsons has been cleared and is set for his season debut against the #Rams , sources say. After tearing his ACL and meniscus on Dec. 14, 2025, Parsons has checked every box. Now, he’s back. pic.twitter.com/etrfD2NOa1
“They care more about the mental and how important it is,” Parsons said. “Do you feel confident in your leg, your knee and everything that’s been going on, confident in your rehab and how you feel about that?
“But also they want to know how you’re playing. Are you playing timid, things like that? Obviously, you’ve got the results of the testing numbers, of the asymmetry, how equal your quads are, your hips, your calves, things like that. I think it’s about 30 percent the player, another 50 percent the team and another 20 percent the doctors.”
Following three weeks of practice, Parsons said he “for sure” felt confident in the knee.
“I would say I’m really, really confident,” he said. “I’m my own biggest critic. So, however I like to set the bar – if I feel like I’m not at that bar, that’s kind of how I feel. You don’t put together multiple good seasons if you don’t set your bar really high. It’s more just that I play confident, I’ve got a lot of great feedback from my teammates, but it’s just about the team and the doctors just giving me the OK. That’s just an extra boost of confidence right there.”
Parsons was listed as limited participation for a second consecutive day. Also for a second consecutive day, every player on the roster practiced.
That includes cornerback Brandon Cisse, who progressed from limited participation to full participation following last week’s rib injury. Along with the addition of guard Travis Glover, those were the only changes to the injury report.
The final injury report will be revealed on Tuesday, even though the practice week ended on Monday.
“I would say I feel like I’ve done everything I possibly could to put myself in position to potentially play on Wednesday, but for sure this season, and I’ll be looking forward to returning to the field,” Parsons said.
The conference call was the final box for Parsons to check following an injury sustained exactly 49 weeks and one day ago.
Now, all that awaits is the game. Parsons, though, didn’t think the game would be any different than practice. Parsons plays with a relentless mentality. He attacked his rehab and the return to the practice field in the same way.
“If you’re dominant, you’re dominant, regardless of the setting,” he said. “That’s like me saying we go to the west side bowling alley and you bring me over to the east side and I’m a better bowler because it’s the east side and not the west side.
“I look at it like that: Games are games. But practice is always going to be more challenging than games. Obviously, I think I’ve really pushed myself to feel some of them things. I went against our best. I didn’t shy from it. I knew what I had to feel and what I had to embrace to be ready to play. So, I don’t think I need that. I think whenever that time is, I'll be very dominant.”

title: Packers Monday Update From Practice: Perfect Week Includes Micah Parsons
full_text:
GREEN BAY, Wis. – Green Bay Packers coach Matt LaFleur continues to play it close to the vest regarding the progress and availability of Micah Parsons.
“He did well,” is all LaFleur would say on Monday about Parsons’ practice on Sunday, a full-pads session that served as the last big test standing between Parsons and his presumptive debut against the Los Angeles Rams on Wednesday night.
Asked if he was confident that Parsons would play, LaFleur before Monday’s practice said, “We’ve still got another day of practice, so we’ll see.”
For the third consecutive day, all 52 players on the roster participated in practice. While the Packers have been hit hard by injuries this season, the mini-bye has them in relatively good shape to face the Rams.
Not only did Parsons join his teammates for the start of practice inside the Don Hutson Center, but so did everybody else. Cornerback Brandon Cisse (rib), linebackers Zaire Franklin (shin) and Isaiah McDuffie (rib), receivers Bo Melton (thigh) and Skyy Moore (ankle), center Sean Rhyan (ankle), right guard Kevin Zeitler (triceps) and running back Josh Jacobs (finger) were limited participation at Sunday’s practice.
Will this be the week for Rhyan and Zeitler to join the starting offensive line? Rhyan missed the last three games with an ankle injury but returned to practice this week. Zeitler, who was signed after Week 3, would have made his starting debut last week if not for a triceps injury sustained at practice.
“They’ve done some nice things,” LaFleur said when asked about Rhyan and Franklin, the defensive captain who missed the last three games. “I wouldn’t stamp them that they’re 100 percent going to be in the lineup. Again, just like Micah and all these other guys, we’ll let them work today and then make a decision.”
Cisse dropped out of Sunday’s loss to the Vikings but is practicing with “no” limitations, LaFleur said.
One starter who probably will not play is Jacobs, who sustained a broken right ring finger early in the win at New England, had surgery and was inactive against Minnesota. He is practicing this week so he can remain sharp for a potential return next week.
Without Jacobs, the Packers for the second consecutive week will roll with Kaleb Johnson, Chris Brooks and MarShawn Lloyd as a three-man backfield. Johnson played only 14 snaps against the Vikings but carried the ball on 10.
Everybody is practicing again for the Packers. Josh Jacobs is not expected to play, LaFleur said, potentially leaving Kaleb Johnson atop the depth chart. pic.twitter.com/FdnB8XxF4O
That’s not sustainable going forward, though, because defenses will quickly figure out that No. 26 is going to get the ball if he’s on the field.
“That can be a huge tell, absolutely,” LaFleur said. “You spend a lot of time with these defensive guys, they’re trying to find any nugget they can, whether it’s certain tight ends in the game, certain backs. So, you absolutely have to be conscious of that.”
Micah Parsons suffered a torn ACL with meniscus damage at Denver on Dec. 14. So, his return to the field will be about 49 weeks after the injury.
The Rams know he’s playing.
“We’re expecting him to play,” Rams offensive coordinator Nate Scheelhaase told reporters on Sunday. “I think from the word out there, it seems like it’s his time to come back into the fold. I have a lot of respect for him. I feel like we saw him a couple times through joint practices against Dallas and stuff. I respect him as a player. He seems like an enjoyable dude to be around as a football player so I’m sure they’re excited to get him back. We have to be prepared for him.”
The Packers released running back Pierre Strong late last week to create a spot on the roster for Parsons.
The Packers are getting back one of their defensive stars. So are the Rams with defensive lineman Kobie Turner, who had a total of 24 sacks during his first three seasons. He had none this season before a groin injury sent him to injured reserve.
“He’s awesome,” Rams defensive coordinator Chris Shula told reporters. “I said, ‘He’s the best assistant D-line coach maybe we’ve ever had, but I’d much rather have him out on the field.’ He’s been awesome at the games. He’s been locked in in the meetings. You felt like he’s there. Obviously, he’s a great player and we want him out on the field. He’s a huge leader for us and just a big energy boost for us.”
This is as close to a football video as we get to shoot on Friday. Or Monday. Packers-Rams on Wednesday night. pic.twitter.com/3u2vsOZD2p
The Packers and Rams will reveal updated injury reports after Monday’s practice, the final practice of the week. So, for now, here are the injury reports from Sunday. While this is a Friday in the NFL world, the teams will not have to produce their final injury reports until Tuesday.

Full participation: G Aaron Banks (knee).

title: Texans, C.J. Stroud Among Biggest Winners of Steelers-Rodgers Drama
full_text:
The Pittsburgh Steelers made an eye-catching, and really, a stunning change to their offense heading into Week 12 of the NFL season.
After having Aaron Rodgers under center as their starting quarterback for the last 26 consecutive games, the Steelers have decided to bench the future Hall of Famer for Mason Rudolph for their upcoming game vs. the Denver Broncos, leaving Rodgers as an inactive on their gameday roster.
pic.twitter.com/F2qo4OawcY
The change in the Steelers' quarterback room is one that was largely unpredictable.
Rodgers was all but locked into his spot as Pittsburgh's QB1, despite their lackluster passing production across the first half of the season, and after their latest 16-19 loss to the Philadelphia Eagles, he might've finally played his last game in the NFL with no signs that Pittsburgh plans on turning to him moving forward.
However, as the Steelers have made a big change under center, there's a chance that the Texans and C.J. Stroud now come out of this decision as some of the biggest winners of all––and that's for more reasons than one.
One of the most important fallouts from this decision that connects with the Texans is the fact that Houston will be playing this same Steelers team in a little over a week come Week 13's Sunday Night Football matchup; a game that could have significant consequences for playoff seeding in the AFC.
The Texans have a history of taking care of Rodgers and the Steelers' offense as of their most recent matchup in the Wild Card Round of last postseason, where Houston claimed a dominant 30-6 victory on the road at Acrisure Stadium.
But for their matchup against the Steelers looming this season, they'll now be faced with the task of seeing Mason Rudolph, which could be a simpler–– or perhaps even tougher battle for the Texans to take on–– depending on how Rudolph looks as Pittsburgh's QB1 on Friday against Denver.
On top of the implications now in play for the Texans' Week 13 game, the AFC Wild Card race now has a bunch of backup-level quarterbacks competing alongside Houston that now tend to make their road to the postseason suddenly a bit more palatable.
Of the six teams that are reasonably within the hunt to make some noise in the postseason, only two of those teams have yet to make a significant change at the quarterback position: that's the Texans, who have C.J. Stroud playing at an MVP-level , and the Cleveland Browns with Deshaun Watson.
Current starting QBs of the six AFC teams I believe will fight for the last two playoff spots … • Browns: Deshaun Watson • Steelers: Mason Rudolph • Patriots: Tommy DeVito • Texans: CJ Stroud • Raiders: Fernando Mendoza • Ravens: Jacoby Brissett Advantage: Houston.
Having the edge at quarterback can be a much-welcomed lift for any NFL team on a given week, but that's especially so for those looking to make a run into the playoffs.
The top five teams sitting clearly above the Texans in the AFC standings each have an above-average to elite option at quarterback: the Buffalo Bills and Josh Allen, the Denver Broncos and Bo Nix, the Jacksonville Jaguars and Trevor Lawrence, the Cincinnati Bengals and Joe Burrow, and the Kansas City Chiefs and Patrick Mahomes.
The Texans and Stroud aren't far away from becoming that sixth or seventh team in the standings. With a few victories in a row over the next few weeks against winnable matchups like the Ravens and Steelers, along with the Philadelphia Eagles and Tennessee Titans, it might be just enough to give Houston the necessary lift in the Wild Card race .
And if that late-season run does come to form again for the Texans, that only helps Stroud and his case of cashing in an even bigger check once it comes time to negotiate a new contract extension later this offseason.
But making such a run happen all starts with the Texans taking care of business against the Ravens, then doing so once again against the Steelers the following week, which would then lift Houston to .500 for the first time this season.
With Pittsburgh's latest decision to turn away from a Hall of Fame quarterback like Rodgers until further notice, those chances of the Texans making that climb happen begin to look a whole lot better.

title: Predicting Texans' Final 7 Games as Playoff Hopes Remain Alive
full_text:
The Houston Texans are creeping closer and closer to being within range of a playoff spot in the AFC , as they sit at 4-6 with just seven games to go on the schedule, but ride into those upcoming matchups with some positive momentum on their side.
So how could those upcoming games for the Texans pan out? They've got three matchups at home and four on the road, and each of them are looking critical for their chances of clawing their way up the AFC ladder for a top-seven seed.
With that in mind, let's take a look at all seven matchups that are on the horizon for the Texans, predict how each could go, and see how their record pans out at the end.
The Ravens are on a six-game losing streak, are still without Lamar Jackson, and are taking the road against a Texans team with some momentum building up in their favor.
While the Ravens did play the Carolina Panthers close this past weekend, Houston's scoring attack combined with their improving defense should overwhelm them enough for the Texans to win back-to-back home games for the first time since 2025.
Prediction: Texans Win, 31-13
The Texans get a chance to face the Steelers in a primetime setting for the second time this calendar year on Sunday Night Football. And while Pittsburgh's defense could cause some distress for C.J. Stroud, it's hard to imagine their offense making much of a dent on the other end.
That's especially so after the Steelers just announced they were benching Aaron Rodgers in Week 12 for Mason Rudolph. This is a game the Texans have to take advantage of, and should, which would finally take them to .500 for the first time this year–– so long as they take care of Baltimore.
Prediction: Texans Win, 28-10
This is a sneaky game for the Texans that could quickly become a challenging one by the time we get to Week 14.
Washington is currently on a two-game win streak that could quickly turn to four with wins over the Arizona Cardinals and Tennessee Titans, and could lead to Jayden Daniels and Co. being a bit of a freight train to stop, especially on their home field.
However, the Texans would be a pretty tough force to stop at this point as well. They'd be on a three-game win streak, and if their defense is catching fire, Jayden Daniels and the Commanders’ offensive line might be overwhelmed enough for Houston to keep things rolling for a much-needed Week 14 win.
Prediction: Texans Win, 23-21
This is undoubtedly the toughest game left on the Texans' schedule; a rematch against a divisional opponent in which they already beat once this season. But it's even harder to beat a team twice in a season––and for a Super Bowl contender like Jacksonville, they could be best equipped to stop Houston on a hypothetical win streak.
Perhaps the Texans gut out a last-minute victory in their second game of the season against Jacksonville, as they did around this time last year. However, I've got Jacksonville and their improved roster from Week 6's meeting splitting their season series vs. Houston, and paving the way to an inevitable AFC South victory.
Prediction: Texans Lose, 17-16
This needs to be a game the Texans come out with a win in. The Eagles have sunken to the bottom of the NFC North, will likely be starting Joe Milton, and might just be gunning towards better draft positioning at this point in the year, rather than playing spoiler to Houston's playoff hopes.
The Eagles do lead the all-time series against the Texans 6-0. So maybe claiming a win here will be easier said than done. But their offense appears to have no chance of overcoming what could be a dangerous Houston defense at this point in the year, and could lead to a resounding road victory.
Prediction: Texans Win, 21-6
This is another challenge for the Texans that might be a bit too tough to overcome: a road test against a fiery offense in another playoff threat, the Packers, who could have their defense rolling for their best production of the season with Micah Parsons back in the lineup.
Maybe the Texans will be able to defy historical precedent in this game once again. Green Bay is 5-1 all-time against Houston. But it seems like it would have to take some real C.J. Stroud heroics or a star-studded Will Anderson to take down the Packers here. I'll have them coming up just short by less than a touchdown.
Prediction: Texans Lose, 23-17
This is the perfect moment for a cathartic win over a division rival they've already bested once this season. While the Titans will certainly be playing for pride in their final game of the year, Houston will be searching for any life that might be left for a playoff appearance and end the regular season off with a home victory.
The Texans have already dominated the Titans for a 20-plus point victory in October, and the same could be in store once Week 18 rolls around.
Prediction: Texans Win, 33-6
If each of these seven projections pans out, the Texans end up at 9-8. Not exactly eliminated from the postseason picture, but they'd certainly need some help in order to find their way to a seventh seed in the AFC.
The Texans would likely need the Steelers and the New England Patriots to lose three or four of their next seven games. Considering each of them has a backup-level quarterback set to start down the stretch, seeing such an outcome is far from impossible.
However, for the Texans to find the easiest route to the postseason, it relies on their ability to stack up as many wins as possible through their next seven games.
By the looks of it, a vast majority of those matchups appear to be winnable, but a loss in just one or two of those games makes the road quickly become a whole lot tougher.

title: Texans' Chances of Beating Ravens Look Strong Based on Week 12 Odds
full_text:
The Houston Texans put together their first home win in nearly 11 months during their Thursday Night Football matchup against the Indianapolis Colts .
And now as the Texans head into Week 12, it seems they're pretty strong favorites to come out with a second straight win against the Baltimore Ravens––at least based on initial betting odds.
The Texans enter the weekend as some of the heavier favorites to come out on top in their respective matchup, as Houston has started the week at -6.5 over the Ravens, per odds from FanDuel Sportsbook .
Despite the Texans' 4-6 record, it's actually the eighth game of the season that they stand out as the pregame favorites. Houston's 4-6 against the spread, and has hit the spread in four of their last six games.
The Ravens, however, have not been as kind against the spread.As Baltimore has fallen into a six-game losing streak, they've also failed to cover in five of their last six games.
They did narrowly cover at +2.5 in this past weekend's 33-35 loss to the Carolina Panthers, and in this one against Houston, they'll have a chance to do so once again as underdogs of just under a touchdown.
Odds refresh periodically and are subject to change.
If you or someone you know has a gambling problem and wants help, call 1-800-GAMBLER.
Just by the looks of this game on paper, the Texans are rolling into this game with all of the momentum on their side.
Houston's coming off a resounding Thursday night win over a division rival that's given them the benefit of a mini-bye , and a few days of extra rest over the Ravens.
The Texans will be at home, should be a bit healthier than they were this time last week, and have been performing better than Baltimore on both sides of the ball over the last few games.
As for the Ravens, they're on a six-game losing streak, have a combined point differential of -79 on that losing streak, and are still without their starting quarterback, Lamar Jackson. All momentum is leaning in the Texans' favor.
But, we have seen the Texans struggle in similar positions this season where it feels like all is going their way, just for them to fall flat on Sunday. Just look back to Week 7 against the New York Giants , or just a couple of weeks ago against the Cleveland Browns .
If the Texans can continue to produce as well as they have through the air behind MVP-level production from C.J. Stroud, the pass-rush can continue to produce, and the secondary keeps on trending upwards as it has been since the bye, it'll be tough for the Ravens to come out of Houston with a win.
It remains to be seen if the Texans will keep firing on all cylinders for a second straight week. But if they do, it'd certainly be another step in the right direction for their hopes of making a late run to a spot in the postseason.
