title: What Woody Marks' Return Means for Texans Run Game vs. Ravens
full_text:
The Houston Texans' run game is set to get a bit of a facelift in their upcoming matchup against the Baltimore Ravens.
According to an update from Texans head coach DeMeco Ryans, the team is "hopeful" that Marks will return to the lineup in Week 12 after missing Thursday night's game against the Indianapolis Colts.
Marks has been in concussion protocol since the Texans' Week 10 game against the Cleveland Browns, in which he left and didn't return in the middle of the third quarter. Once Sunday against the Ravens arrives, Marks will be two weeks removed from that injury and should be good to go for his return to the field.
But for the Texans' run game, it'll be the first time that both Marks and Montgomery will be working in tandem with one another for the first time since Week 5 against the Tennessee Titans.
What can we expect from Houston on the ground as they'll be back to 100%? And will the backfield split be any different than what we last saw from when each of Marks and Montgomery were healthy at the start of the season?
Now, since the first four weeks of the season when the Texans had a collective 0-4 record, their run game has looked a lot better in the moments that Woody Marks or David Montgomery has led the operation by themselves.
However, we can look back to those first four weeks at the Texans were fully healthy in the backfield to get a better picture of what to expect for their running back split when both of their top guys are healthy.
From Weeks 1 through 4, Montgomery was on the field for an average of 54% of the Texans' offensive snaps and saw 47 total carries. Marks was out there for around 45% of the snaps and came away with 28 total carries.
So Montgomery, when both guys are healthy, is typically leading the way over Marks by a slight margin in snaps, but also takes a bulk of the Texans' carries in the backfield, while Marks operates as a pass-blocker and a more potent weapon in the receiving game.
However, based on how Montgomery operated in the Texans' last game against the Colts, maybe there's a route to him seeing a bit more than that 55% snap share.
There's a case that Montgomery should get a bigger workload in the Texans' offense moving forward because of how solid he looked against the Colts . And that outcome certainly remains a possibility if Montgomery continues to carry his efficiency into the next game against the Ravens.
However, at least initially, the Texans feel more likely to roll with their previous setup in the backfield at a 55-45 split and roll with the hot hand on a weekly basis, rather than simply lean on Montgomery more right off the bat.
Marks has been a solid weapon in the Texans' offense when he's been given the opportunities. He's a quick, home run hitter on the ground, can work well as a pass-catcher, and is an underrated pass-blocker that is deserving of seeing the ball in his hands to make plays on a weekly basis.
Houston has entrusted him with over 15 touches a game in every week that Montgomery has been sidelined, and it's hard to imagine he's totally taken out of the game plan moving forward now that the position looks a little bit healthier.
The one back in the Texans' offense who feels most likely to be taken out of the game plan is their now-third-string runner, Emari Demercado , who has taken around 25% of the offensive snaps to Marks and Montgomery when the other has been sidelined, but now feels due to see that number reach closer to zero.
Demercado has been a serviceable backup when the Texans have had him on the field this season, but he was only meant to be a plug-and-play veteran who stepped up due to injury.
Now that Houston is healthy in the backfield, Demercado reverts back to their RB3, and only sees looks on the offense if either of Marks or Montgomery is forced out for more time. There's a chance he could find some snaps on special teams so he's not a complete non-factor on the Texans' roster, though.

title: Texans Fantasy Football Check: Buy, Sell or Hold These 7 Players
full_text:
The Houston Texans have about seven weeks to go before their fate is decided on whether or not they'll be able to climb out of their current hole for an eventual playoff appearance.
But for fantasy football managers, the playoffs are right around the corner. Trade deadlines are approaching, and now marks a pivotal point in the year where roster decisions and big moves can have major implications for how championships shake out over the next several weeks.
So in the spirit of those fantasy football leagues heating up, now is as good a time as ever to take a step back to look at the Texans' roster and evaluate which players you might want to add to your fantasy team, who you might want to sell, and others that might be best to hold onto if you have them.
Let's break down the buy, sell, or hold case for seven players on the Texans roster and see who you really want to invest in for the home stretch of the season.
C.J. Stroud is the quarterback you want to have in fantasy football right now. Not only has he exploded onto the scene as QB5 through the first 11 weeks of the season, but he's also been extremely consistent over the last several games as well.
The Texans' signal-caller has scored 20 points or more in six of his last seven games. Stroud's been accurate, making good decisions, and scoring touchdowns— which is most important for his fantasy production.
Hang onto Stroud if you've got him, and if you need a quarterback, go out and find the guy who's got him.
Montgomery's coming off one of his best games of the season against the Indianapolis Colts, where the Texans running back found his way to a season-high 26 carries for 107 rushing yards, but didn't find the end zone.
On one hand, the game was extremely encouraging to see from Montgomery after he's been both injured and ineffective through the first half of the year. But Montgomery only has three 100-yard games to his name since 2024. The production he showcased on Thursday night probably isn't sustainable for the rest of the season, especially once Woody Marks returns from his concussion.
If there's an opportunity to sell high on Montgomery, now would be the perfect time to do so. At best, he's a high-end flex option to rely on for the rest of the season. There might not be many more times this season that the Texans back claims over 15 PPR fantasy points in a single week.
Woody Marks was out of the Texans' lineup this past week due to a concussion, but he's trending for a return in Week 12 against the Baltimore Ravens as he'll have had two weeks to fully get out of concussion protocol.
But will Marks be able to be utilized as a reliable fantasy option? It's hard to say. Marks wasn't the most effective running back to plug into lineups over the past several weeks that Montgomery was out with a groin injury––and now, he's back in the mix. Marks' carries will only slim from the point they've been at.
He's probably not worth much in a trade right now, and he's got too much appeal even as a running back in a committee to be truly droppable. So keep him as a bench stash, hoping that his upside as a pass-catcher can allow him to be usable in the future.
Nico Collins has had better years of production over the last three seasons, but the Texans' No. 1 wideout has finally begun to catch his stride over the last two weeks.
Collins has scored 14 or more PPR fantasy points over the last three weeks, and has found his way to a touchdown in each of those. In Week 10 against the Cleveland Browns, Collins found his way to a staggering 16 targets , turning those into 24.4 points.
With his big-play ability and nose for the end zone, Collins is someone who could continue to rise over the second half of the season and settle in as a quality WR2, even with the talent around him in the Texans’ wide receiver room.
Tank Dell certainly got many excited for what the second half of the season could hold for him once he saw over 100 yards in a game for the first time since his injury back in Week 9 against the LA Chargers. But since that performance, Dell has remained pretty quiet.
He's seen a combined six receptions for 48 yards over the last two games he's played, and has scored less than 10 PPR fantasy points in each of those. He's not exactly the more reliable play to plug in at receiver in your lineup, but not exactly someone to give up on just yet.
The Texans love utilizing Dell as a potent weapon in their passing game when the opportunities are there, and those looks will only increase as he gets more and more time on the field. Right now, he's best valued as a WR4/5, but with a couple of good games, he could rise back to a WR3/high-upside flex play.
Last week against the Colts was the quietest we've seen from Hutchinson in a while. He saw just two receptions for the second game this season, which resulted in his second-lowest point total of the year.
But Hutchinson could still be a low-end flex play to rely on for the next few weeks. Hutchinson has still brought in a touchdown in three of his last four games, and he stays on the field a considerable amount–– logging over 75% of the offensive snaps across the last three games of the season.
If he's out on waivers, he's a worthwhile pickup to stash on your bench, and could be forced into your lineup in a pinch, considering he's a frequently utilized option in a high-volume passing offense.
Schultz has been a bit of a non-factor in the Texans' receiving game over the last three games. He hasn't seen more than two receptions since before Houston's bye in Week 8, and has caught one touchdown on the season.
While the Texans tight end started off his season with an encouraging Week 2 contest against the Cincinnati Bengals with 26 PPR fantasy points, he's probably best served to be on waivers at this point in the year, only to be picked up if you're in desperate need of a spot-start at the position.

title: Texans Have Good Reason to Repeat Key O-Line Change in Week 12
full_text:
The Houston Texans went into their Week 11 game against the Indianapolis Colts preparing to roll out a different look than usual on their offensive line.
The plan was: rather than roll out one primary tackle on the right side of their line, the Texans would instead rotate their right tackle duties between two players throughout the night–– that being Trent Brown and Braden Smith.
Things didn't exactly go according to plan, though. In less than 10 snaps for Brown, he would leave the game with a back injury that was unable to return from. That led to Braden Smith holding things down on the right side of the line for most of the night against the Colts.
And overall, Smith had a rather impressive performance. In the 59 total snaps he saw, he allowed just two pressures, zero sacks, caused zero penalties, and led to David Montgomery rushing for a season-high 107 yards.
It was about as good of a performance the Texans have seen at their right tackle position all season long. It was also Smith's first time really holding the fort down as Houston's primary starter on the right side of the line. His opportunity finally came, and he delivered.
So now, it begs the question: will the Texans simply continue with Smith as their starting right tackle moving forward, will they hand the keys back to Brown, or will they re-try their plan of rotating both if each is healthy?
Throughout the first half of the season, the Texans' starter on the right side, Trent Brown, has remained serviceable in his role. Pro Football Focus grades him as the 32nd best run-blocking tackle (66.6) among 72 eligible players, but 50th overall (63.2).
But there are some glaring flaws within Brown's fit: he's highly penalized, he's allowed 24 pressures on the season, and his ability to be consistently available is questionable, to say the least.
Smith, however, has finally returned from his prior injury issues, stepped as the Texans' starter, and was exactly what the team has been looking for ever since they signed him to a $20 million deal this offseason: a positive run blocker, an improvement in pass protection, and someone who helps limit Houston's excessive penalties .
Smith was signed this offseason with the idea that he would step up as the Texans' starting right tackle, and now, he's finally showcased a bit of the vision Houston had when they brought him in less than a year ago.
Now, it's on Houston to continue giving him opportunities to start and be a positive force in what's been an up-and-down offensive line unit over the last few seasons.
Texans head coach DeMeco Ryans spoke about Smith's performance in Thursday's game against the Colts, crediting his ability to be a physical force in the run game.
"In the game on Thursday, I thought Braden did a good job, going out, playing physically," Ryans said. "It seemed he was excited to play. I just liked the play style, and how he was finishing downfield in the running game. That was also a contributing factor to us running the ball as well as we did."
Perhaps it may depend on what the health of both Smith and Brown looks like heading into the week against the Baltimore Ravens before the Texans make an official decision on who starts.
But based on Thursday's performance, it might be increasingly hard to keep Smith out of the lineup if he can continue to play as well as he did.

title: Texans Week 12 Consensus Power Rankings: Houston Has Some Hope
full_text:
The Houston Texans are 4-6 with seven games to go on their schedule––and it's starting to look like there's a chance that this team could rattle off a similar win streak in the second half of the season as they did last year .
The offense is beginning to click both through the air and on the ground, and the defense has started to turn things around as of their latest performance against the Indianapolis Colts . With a win in their next two, maybe three games, Houston could be right where they want to be: a top-seven seed in the AFC.
And as the Texans have started to turn a corner , many are starting to give them a little bit of a boost in this week's edition of NFL power rankings.
Let's take a look at where the Texans stand in various power rankings heading into their Week 12 matchup against the Baltimore Ravens:
Sports Illustrated 's Conor Orr gives the Texans a slight boost into the middle of the pack––but still a far distance away from the top-five placement he gave them earlier in the year.
"If you loved the feature on the Texans’ vegetable score on Amazon Prime last week, read the story from where it came…all the way back in August."
NFL.com 's Nick Shook has the Texans squeak into the top 15, as their playoff hopes continue to stay alive thanks to their own win on Thursday night, paired with some help around the AFC.
"I can’t quit the Texans and neither can you! Houston dominated Indianapolis on Thursday night, moving to 4-6 and -- thanks to Pittsburgh’s upset loss to Philadelphia on Sunday -- preserving its playoff hopes. Those hopes can move closer to becoming reality if the Texans cantake down the Steelers two Sundays from now."
ESPN 's writers kept the Texans steady at their 16th spot, D.J. Bien-Aime was tasked to name Houston's most likely extension candidate to keep an eye on this offseason, and highlighted none other than C.J. Stroud.
"Through 10 games of Stroud's fourth season, he is up to 2,656 passing yards, 22 touchdowns and only four interceptions. He is on pace to throw for 4,515 passing yards and 37 touchdowns, both of which would be career highs. And his Total QBR (73) is fifth best in the NFL. Stroud has earned the payday he bet on himself for. Now, it comes down to whether the Texans are willing to pay whatever that price is. They're not expected to balk at Stroud's offers, but if they do, things could get interesting."
The Athletic 's Josh Kendall and Chad Graff still don't seem to trust the building hype surrounding the Texans, as they rank them right outside of the top 20, and just two spots higher than last week's ranking.
Houston had 167 yards on the ground Thursday, its highest total since Week 18 of the 2024 season. David Montgomery returned to the lineup after missing four games with a groin injury and had 107 yards, his best output as a Texan. “I think we can be really, really good (on offense),” Montgomery told reporters afterward. “It’s never too late to find your stride.”
CBS Sports ' Pete Prisco sees the vision for the Texans' potential run to the postseason, but doesn't envision much margin for error, either.
"After beating up the Colts, they are once again eyeing the last playoff spot. But they can't afford any more missteps the rest of the way."
FOX Sports ' Ralph Vacchiano tempers any high expectations around the Texans because of their win against the lowly Colts last week. But he does see the route for Houston to claw their way into postseason positioning.
"It’s hard to read too much into last Thursday’s rout of the Colts, since Indy has become unfathomably pathetic. But the Texans are a team that just doesn’t seem to want to go away. They are 4-2 since their season-crushing 0-4 start, and they’ve mostly been playing well. Their biggest problem is that they probably need to go 6-1 the rest of the way to have a shot at the playoffs. It’s not as crazy as you think, though. Their only games against teams with a winning record are at Pittsburgh, home versus the Jaguars, and at Green Bay. They’d have to win two of those three and not stumble against anyone else. It’s a lot to ask, but not impossible."

title: Handing Out Texans Midseason Awards for MVP, ROTY and More
full_text:
The Houston Texans are a little over halfway through their 2026 regular season, having gone through 10 of their 17 games on the schedule that's led to a 4-6 record, but a potential runway to make another surge up the standings with a run in the second half of the year.
And before the Texans get any further, now feels like a good time to take a step back from the season and look at just who around the roster has stood out more than most for one reason or another.
Who's been the Texans' team MVP? What about the best players on the offense and defense? Who's been Houston's most improved player?
I've got six midseason awards to hand out for the Texans. Let's sort through who's the most deserving of each, along with a runner-up for each award.
Not many would've predicted C.J. Stroud to come alive like he has through the first half of this season. But he's been on pace for a career-best year of production despite the Texans as a whole facing some turbulence.
If he keeps up at his current rate, he'll finish the year with over 4,500 passing yards and 37 passing touchdowns. He's helped turn the passing attack around to the closest thing we've seen to his rookie year production, and exceeded all expectations that the Texans could've had for him entering the year.
While Stroud has been putting together the best production of his NFL career so far, it hasn't exactly paired with a dominant season from the Texans' No. 1 pass-catcher, Nico Collins.
But while Collins might not be stuffing the stat sheet, there's little doubt he's continued to be Houston's best offensive weapon as he has been throughout the past three years.
He's on pace to break 1,000 yards for the fourth straight season, could wind up breaking his career-best total in touchdowns, and elevates the ceiling of this Texans offense anytime he's on the field.
Considering the guy is the current frontrunner to come away with this year's league-wide Defensive Player of the Year award, there's no question that Will Anderson is deserving of some credit here.
Anderson's been the engine behind the success of this Texans defensive line that has still remained atop the league for overall production, despite the turbulent first half of the season this unit has seen as a whole.
Anderson's still remained one of the NFL's best run defenders at his position, is leading the league in sacks at 11.5, is on pace to smash his sack total of 12.0 from last season, and that year led to an All-Pro First Team selection.
Runner-Up: Derek Stingley Jr.
The Texans' rookie class hasn't been the most impactful in their first season. Kayden McDonald has been mainly a rotational piece in Houston's defensive tackle group, and guys like Marlin Klein and Febechi Nwaiwu have only just started to see opportunities come their way.
But Keylan Rutledge has been a starter on the Texans' offensive line all season. He has struggled in pass protection, considering he's allowed 28 total pressures in the nine games he's played at left guard, but he has been a solid run blocker and has only room to continue growing moving forward.
Runner-Up: Kayden McDonald
Yes, Jaylin Noel did get placed on season-ending injured reserve due to a toe injury back in Week 8 before the Texans' bye. But there's no doubt that through the first half of Houston's season, Noel had made some of the most impressive improvements to his game from his rookie year.
Noel was leading all Texans receivers in yards per reception, had already bested his rookie season receiving yards total in seven games, and was a real explosive piece within Houston's passing attack that just started to catch his stride in the middle of the season.
Noel will have to wait until 2027 to build upon the positive start he had this season. However, there's certainly reason to feel encouraged about what the second-year wideout showed in the opportunities he had.
Is there any question about who deserves this one? After nearly two years of rehab from the devastating knee injury he suffered in December of 2024, Tank Dell finally made his return to the Texans lineup in Week 7 against the New York Giants.
And since then, Dell has actually found his way back into being a truly impactful and explosive piece of the Texans' passing game. He's averaging even more receiving yards per game from his 2024 season, and has seen four or more targets over his last three games of the season.

title: Texans Provide Updates on Danielle Hunter, Woody Marks Ahead of Week 12
full_text:
The Houston Texans went into their Thursday Night Football matchup against the Indianapolis Colts suffering from multiple key injuries to their lineup .
However, there were two key starters–– one on each side of the ball–– that stuck out a bit more than the others with their absence: that's lead running back Woody Marks, who was out with a concussion , and star defensive end Danielle Hunter, who missed a second straight game due to a hamstring injury.
The Texans still managed to take care of business without both of them, winning in dominant 26-3 fashion over the Colts this past week. But we know that this Houston roster can be even better when both of those guys are on the field.
And heading into the Texans' Week 12 matchup against the Baltimore Ravens, we now have a couple of new updates on what the status of each of those players looks like about a week away from kickoff.
Texans head coach DeMeco Ryans provided an update on both Hunter and Marks on Monday as the team arrived back at the facility, noting that Hunter was "still progressing," while Marks is "hopeful" to play on Sunday against the Ravens.
"Danielle [Hunter] is still progressing with a hamstring injury," Ryans said. "Woody [Marks] is trending in the right direction. We're hopeful to have him on this coming Sunday."
Based on Ryans' comments, Marks seems to have a more optimistic status to play for Week 12 than Hunter does.
Marks is recovering from a concussion that he suffered during the Texans' Week 10 game against the Cleveland Browns that left him to be sidelined on a short week against the Colts.
Given that Houston will be two weeks removed from that matchup against the Browns by Sunday, there's a good chance that Marks will have cleared concussion protocol by that point, and thus return to the lineup alongside David Montgomery .
As for Hunter, though, it seems that while he's still progressing from his hamstring injury suffered ahead of that Week 10 game against the Browns , the Texans aren't quite as hopeful that he'll be at 100% to play against the Ravens.
Hunter has not participated in a practice since November 12th due to a hamstring issue that he seemingly suffered in practice. He was listed as a limited participant that day and has been a DNP ever since.
Ryans addressed the balance between practicing hard and avoiding injuries during his Monday presser, expressing that while it's unfortunate, the nature of the game of football means players will inevitably get hurt in practice––such as in the case of guys like Hunter and Marvin Harrison Jr.
"It's football. Guys are going to get hurt. We have to practice. We can not practice, and guys can not get hurt. Or, you've got to practice, and, unfortunately, guys get hurt in practice," Ryans said.
As the Texans get this week's practice kicked off on Wednesday to prepare for their upcoming matchup against the Ravens, we'll get a better idea of where Marks and Hunter stand when it comes to recovering from their respective injuries. If either is able to be a full participant between now and Friday, they've got a good chance of suiting up.
However, there's no doubt that having each of them back in the lineup as soon as possible will be a big lift for the Texans to truly elevate to their ceiling on both sides of the ball.

title: Texans Seem to Have Big Plans Ahead for Rookie TE Marlin Klein
full_text:
The Houston Texans had a handful of standouts show up throughout their win on Thursday Night Football against the Indianapolis Colts .
One of those standouts happened to be none other than the Texans' rookie tight end Marlin Klein , who put together the best stat line yet of his first-year campaign.
Klein saw a season-high four targets that he converted on for four catches, 24 yards, and his first career touchdown in the third quarter thanks to a 13-yard pass in the red zone from C.J. Stroud.
The production from Klein is enough to offer real optimism in how his role could continue to expand as the Texans move deeper into the second half of the season. But things tend to look even more encouraging for his stock based on some recent comments from head coach DeMeco Ryans.
As the Texans came back from their mini-bye on Monday, Ryans spoke about what he's seen from Klein on film and during practice––explaining that Houston's rookie tight end has been "deliberate" in practice behind the scenes and is deserving of getting more reps in the offense.
"What I've seen from Marlin [Klein] is how deliberate he's been in practice. He's been working hard at practice. He's getting better behind the scenes, and he's deserving of the opportunity to get in there and get more reps," Ryans said.
"He really maximized his opportunity on the game the other night; making a couple of tough, contested catches. Also being able to be in sync with C.J. [Stroud] on the scramble drill, come back to the football, and get his first touchdown."
"So, just playing smart football. Really playing aggressive in the run game, staying after his matchup there, and he'll continue to get better with the more reps he gets. He's still a young player, young in the game. He'll thrive. He'll continue to improve. We'll give him more opportunities."
DeMeco Ryans on Texans rookie TE Marlin Klein: 🗣️ "He's been getting better behind the scenes, and he's deserving of the opportunity to get in there and get more reps." "He's still a young player... He'll thrive. He'll continue to improve. We'll give him more opportunities." pic.twitter.com/ObtmGMdUbb
Thursday's game against the Colts marked a long-awaited opportunity for Klein, as he saw his second game seeing over 20% of the Texans' offensive snaps, and managed to turn in his best performance of the season as Houston allowed him to run more routes and stand out as a run blocker.
Just last month, Klein found himself stuck down the Texans' depth chart as a healthy scratch for multiple games, leading to many questioning Houston's selection to even take the tight end in the second round of the draft, and why he wasn't getting more opportunities to perform in the offense.
And while it took some extended time before Klein was able to find an increased role in the offense, Week 11 proved that he was more than deserving of seeing more looks on that side of the ball moving forward.
He's got the ideal positional size standing at 6-foot-6, 250 pounds, has the potential to be a solid pass-catcher , and has strong qualities as a blocker that can help out in the run game based on his time at Michigan.
Klein has now seen over 20% of the Texans' offensive snaps in two of his last three games, and it's hard to imagine he'll be limited to any lesser amount of opportunities this coming weekend against the Baltimore Ravens now that he's finally begun to catch his stride.
If he continues to perform as he did against the Colts more moving forward, don't be shocked to see Klein ending the season as the Texans' TE2 on the depth chart, or even higher, depending on just how much he improves as diligently as he has through his rookie season.
