title: Chargers’ Jim Harbaugh Just Made the Best Case for His Own Firing Yet
full_text:
Exiting a rather embarrassing loss that sent them to 1-9, the Los Angeles Chargers don’t feel like a franchise that has any sense of direction yet when it comes to the fate of head coach Jim Harbaugh.
There’s a popular theory that Harbaugh’s contract will prevent the Chargers from moving on from him early. But that tends to overlook the fact the front office in Los Angeles has been willing to spend at times, whether it was actually paying up for Harbaugh, going to get Mike McDaniel or any other number of examples.
If the Chargers feel any hesitation on the Harbaugh topic though (hesitation would be ridiculous at 1-9, but hey), good news:
Harbaugh just made a pretty good case against his future employment during the latest loss.
It’s one thing to lose to the 3-8 New York Jets. The Chargers have looked like the worst team in football most weeks.
But it’s another to look completely lost in mid-November.
Alas, there was Harbaugh and his coaching staff on Sunday, seemingly in a position to really make a game of things in the fourth quarter.
Instead, inexplicable game management struck, as neatly summed up by Steven Haglund of the GAC Podcast:
The Chargers were down 10 points and really got down to the Jets 8 yard line with 4:33 left in the game and didn’t score until after the two minute warning today. After a 22 yard reception by Tre Harris gets them to that point: - Huddled, Herbert designed run at 3:50, loses 3…
One could almost accuse the Chargers of “tanking,” were it not for years of iffy game management by Harbaugh and his staff.
After the game, deja vu in the presser, too, with Harbaugh dropping his usual stuff. An example: "There's more work to be done, and we're going to work at it."
There were other examples, sure.
"We'll really look at the tape as it pertains offensively and see how we acquitted ourselves," Harbaugh said. "Some points of emphasis that got done, but if you don't win, everyone feels like there's more work to be done. Keep working at it."
And this is where it should dawn on onlookers that the Harbaugh way isn’t working. In the past, it was easier to overlook the in-game struggles and the cheesy one-liners because the locker room was bought in and winning (before the playoffs, anyway).
But now the message is lost. Bud Dupree’s tantrum aside, it sure feels like the Harbaugh message stopped working during last season’s playoff loss. Poor roster building and the injury bug haven’t helped things, but it’s pretty obvious it’s time for a refresh.
In fact, this is one of the better, more obvious examples of a franchise that needs an overhaul to the locker room by way of coaching staff change. And at this point, it’s almost worth wondering whether, if the Chargers front office won’t do it, Harbaugh himself might make it happen.

title: Chargers' Loss to Jets Raises Long-Term Concerns
full_text:
The Chargers lost yet another game, and it was quite embarrassing.
The Bolts took a 27-24 loss to the New York Jets, and it was not pretty at all. The offense looked decent compared to recent games, but the defense finally lost their touch .
The hope was to go up a winning streak, however that obviously didn't happen. In every game, there are players who perform better than others and that's just simply how it goes.
Hampton gave the Chargers a spark. He broke loose for a 36-yard run that helped set up a fourth-quarter scoring drive. That burst showed what the offense can look like when its ground game creates space.
Hampton did not score, but he found positive yardage and helped make the comeback possible. His production was a clear positive.
McConkey was the Chargers’ most important receiving threat near the goal line. He caught five passes for 37 yards, with two receptions going for touchdowns. Both scores came in the fourth quarter, keeping Los Angeles within striking distance. His yardage was modest, but finishing those drives mattered. When the Chargers needed a play, McConkey delivered twice. He was a bright spot in an offense that spent too much of the game searching for consistency.
Herbert found McConkey for two touchdowns and added a rushing score, helping keep the Chargers in the contest.
More troubling was the pressure. The Jets sacked him six times, disrupting drives and making it difficult to build momentum. Herbert avoided an interception, but Los Angeles cannot expect consistent results when its quarterback takes that many hits. He needed better protection and a stronger start.
The late scoring surge could not erase the earlier problems.
Johnston had too little impact when they needed more from its receivers. He caught one pass for nine yards on two targets and had one rushing attempt for a yard.
Those numbers did not give the offense much of a lift while the Chargers were trying to catch up. Johnston was not the only reason the passing game struggled, but the team needed another receiver to contribute alongside McConkey. His afternoon passed with barely a mark. The Chargers need more consistent production from him.
Njoku struggled to provide a spark.
The Chargers chased the game for long stretches, making each opportunity important. Njoku was not responsible for the defeat, but he offense needed more from its supporting cast to take pressure off McConkey. His limited production reflected a wider offensive problem: too many drives lacked an answer when the first option was covered.
Hampton’s running and McConkey’s touchdowns gave the Chargers something positive, but those moments could not cover the slow start or pressure allowed up front.
The Bolts scored 14 points in the fourth quarter, yet needed one more stop to complete the comeback. The Jets controlled the ball longer and finished with more total yards. A strong finish cannot substitute for a complete performance overall.
The Jets get their first win vs the Chargers in 15 years! 📺: FOX/FOX One pic.twitter.com/tRcyCpKAWg

title: The Morning-After Thunder: Chargers D Breaks, Herbert is Hurt, Draft Picture Narrows
full_text:
The Los Angeles Chargers were unable to follow up on their victorious effort from Week 10 when they faced off against the New York Jets on their home field this week. The Chargers, unfortunately, found a new way to lose this week with the defense seemingly shorthanded and exhausted.
The Chargers were missing multiple starters from their defense against the Jets, just days after they put forth a dominating effort against the Baltimore Ravens on Monday Night Football. The Jets' rush offense, between running backs Breece Hall and Braelon Allen, landed body blows and jabs on the Chargers defense at an exhausting pace. The same defense that held Derrick Henry to ten yards on ten carries just six days earlier, could not stop the Jets ground attack, even when the game was on the line.
The loss drops Los Angeles to 1-9 on the season and any miracle run of winning nine in a row for a shot at the playoffs has quickly been killed off. There are many potential reactions to this game from the Chargers perspective, let's run through several of them.
The Chargers may have dropped a game to the Jets but the victory may have cost New York a chance to draft a quarterback without having to use their draft war chest to trade up. The current draft order is relatively unchanged with the Titans still holding down the top spot followed by the Chargers and Dolphins.
The Chargers, having lost, now face the reality that they are likely picking in the top five in the draft in 2027. Head coach Jim Harbaugh finally acknowledged that the process now includes an eye to the future in his postgame press conference. The Chargers now have a more firm handle on a top-three pick in losing to the Jets with both the Jets and Colts having three wins. The game between the Chargers and Dolphins Christmas weekend will likely determine who gets the better draft pick.
The end of the game was baffling from a time management point of view for the Chargers and Jim Harbaugh. The Chargers went on their final scoring drive, taking possession with nearly ten minutes left in the game and took a slow, methodical approach down the field and finally scored with under two minutes left in the game. Where was the urgency?
The long drive essentially forced the defense into a one first down and the game is over type scenario and left no room for error. The Jets were able to close it out but there was an odd sense of lack of situational awareness from the team.
It is obviously too little, too late for the 2026 Chargers but they seem to have found an identity on the ground and sprinkled in with the passing game the offense looked ok. Having Ladd McConkey back on the field proved to be critical as he accounted for two touchdowns. The tight ends were involved in the attack and Tre' Harris made several grabs as well. It was at least functional and the original vision could be seen through the smoke.
The jump in scoring with McConkey back on the field underscores the need for additional weapons for the Chargers next offseason. Even if the Chargers miss out on drafting Ohio State wide receiver Jeremiah Smith, this class is fairly loaded at the wide receiver position.
The Chargers made several moves this offseason specifically for Mike McDaniel as he went to retool the offense and prepare for his system install. The first signing was grabbing Cole Strange from free agency to assume a starting guard role, he has now been benched mid-game and lost his starting job this week to veteran Kayode Awosika.
It was a fun note when it happened, but McDaniel actually made wanted posters for fullback Alec Ingold and running back Keaton Mitchell to ask general manager Joe Hortiz to go get them in free agency and Hortiz obliged. Ingold is almost certainly done for the year on IR and Mitchell has seen his snaps and role dramatically cut down.
It is hard to fault rookie wide receiver Brenen Thompson who, for what seems like a different soft issue injury every week, has been unable to get on the field. Thompson was specifically requested by McDaniel as a prospect to be drafted and again, Hortiz obliged. The bottom line is, the offense that McDaniel thought he was building, never took shape but has seemingly evolved more towards the Rams or 49ers offense, a move that should have been made long ago.
NFL analyst Warren Sharp rightly identified a major problem for the Chargers and their 2026 schedule back in the spring following the schedule release. The NFL gave the Chargers a devastating rest disadvantage this season and in hindsight, it sould have been taken more seriously at the time.
NFL 2026 Net Rest Edges net rest = total days of extra rest vs a team's opponent, summed over the course of the season (negative=bad) -24: LAC -23 -22 -21 -20 -19 -18 -17 -16 -15: PHI -14 -13: LV -12 -11 -10 -9: NYJ -8 -7: NO -6: IND, LAR, MIA, PIT -5 -4: CIN -3: BAL, JAX -2:… https://t.co/Yo03poZurv
The Chargers had a late-night travel schedule following a cross-country Monday Night Football matchup in Baltimore and did not arrive home in Los Angeles until just before four A.M Tuesday. The Chargers played a tough game on Monday, had a brutal turnaround and it looked like they were sluggish on the field. The same defensive line that dominated Baltimore got beaten up by the Jets offensive front.
The Chargers are getting a very clear picture of their roster, with so many bodies going down, the depth is stretched thin. Missing multiple starting defenders proved too costly for them but the offense is at least showing signs of life.
Los Angeles' reality may finally be setting in and now with Justin Herbert in the NFL's concussion protocol the season is that much more bleak. At least the Chargers seem well positioned for a top-three pick in April.

title: Chargers Players Rising, Falling After Week 11 Loss, Benched Starter and Breakouts
full_text:
Now that the Los Angeles Chargers are officially unable to capture a winning season with nine losses this year, this team needs to really start considering its future and moving on to next season. This process can start as soon as now, evaluating players who deserve more attention and players who do not.
So, after this 27-24 loss to the New York Jets, who is rising? Who is falling?
David Njoku finds himself back on the field for the second week in a row after suffering what looked to be a season-ending fibula injury . In a weak Chargers passing offense, Njoku was able to record two catches for 21 yards while being an effective run blocker for a heating-up Chargers run game.
Expect for Njoku to continue gaining snaps in this offense, as this coaching staff obviously prefers his abilities over the once exciting young TE, Oronde Gadsden II.
Travis Burke was not expected to immediately start and contribute for the Chargers, as he has done thus far this season. Even with this unexpected nature of playing time occurring, Burke has been quite solid in his starts thus far, especially as a run-blocker.
As a pass blocker, his warts against speed have been seen, but this week against the Jets highlighted it more than ever. David Bailey, a speed-first rusher, was able to get Burke multiple times, whether it was Burke giving up a sack or the offensive plays being stalled out due to pressure from the right side.
Ladd McConkey was finally able to see himself on the field for a full game, which feels like this is the first time since Week 1 he has been able to do so. In a passing game that lacked explosive plays and general volume, McConkey was able to make the most of his day, recording five catches for 37 yards and two touchdowns.
If you have McConkey in fantasy, it may be a safe bet to start considering him as a flex option in your lineup. If you are the Chargers, it is nice to see your WR1 finally on the field and producing as he is expected to, even after all the injuries.
Cole Strange, where do we even start? As what seems like a weekly inclusion as a faller on these lists, he finds himself on this list once again, hopefully for good. Strange was benched in favor of Kayode Awosika, yielding his playing time to be nearly zero this week.
Awosika did not play amazingly, but it was better than what we have seen from Strange all season long. Moreover, on a PAT attempt from Cameron Dicker late in the game, Strange was on the field as an extra blocker. On this play, Strange collected a 15-yard penalty. Even in a handful of snaps, Strange still finds a way to hurt this team.

title: 5 Keys to Victory: How Rams Can Gain an Edge in Playoff Race Against Packers
full_text:
The Los Angeles Rams will be looking to extend their four-game winning streak when they take on the Green Bay Packers on Thanksgiving Eve. With both teams fighting for a playoff spot in the NFC, the Rams have an opportunity to put themselves in a good position heading into December. While the Rams will be without some of their best offensive players, there is still a clear path to winning this game. Here are five keys to victory for the Rams against the Packers in Week 12.
The Packers are one of the most explosive offenses in the NFL, especially in the passing game. They have a 10.9 percent explosive pass rate, which ranks fourth. Conversely, the Rams have allowed an explosive pass play at a rate of seven percent. That’s the eighth-lowest rate in the league. The Packers have a boom-or-bust offense, and the Rams need to force them to work their way down the field. If the Rams allow the Packers to find their explosives, it could be a long day for the defense.
Without Puka Nacua, the Rams are going to have to lean on the run game again. Against the Cardinals, the Rams ran the ball 44 times. While the Rams may not run the ball 40+ times again, they do need to lean on Kyren Williams and Blake Corum. The Packers rank 27th in defensive rushing success rate and the Rams have the third-highest rushing success rate on offense. Last week, the Rams utilized Pony Personnel and threw the ball on all 17 plays. It wouldn’t be surprising to see the Rams build on that going forward and start to run out of Pony Personnel as well.
Jordan Love had an average time to throw of 2.33 seconds against the Minnesota Vikings in Week 10. It’s unlikely that the Rams will be able to generate that type of pressure, but they have generated quick pressure on 18.4 percent of opposing dropbacks this season, which is the fourth-highest rate in the NFL. The Rams need to pick their spots to blitz and get that type of pressure on Love and force him into mistakes and negative plays. Love has been the third-most-sacked quarterback this season.
The Packers have struggled at times in the red zone in 2026. They rank 20th in red zone offense with a touchdown rate of 54.3 percent. While the Packers are good at generating explosive plays, their inability to run the ball efficiently shows up in the red zone. This season, the Rams have the fourth-best red zone defense, allowing a touchdown at a 43.3 percent rate. The Rams haven’t allowed a touchdown in three of the last five games. The Packers will be the best offense that the Rams have played since allowing 37 points to the Buffalo Bills, but the defense has found its stride since then.
Matthew Stafford’s 10 interceptions this season are the fourth-most in the NFL, and he’s thrown an interception in four consecutive games. Stafford has thrown an interception in all but two games this season. The Rams can’t afford to have Stafford turn the ball over on Wednesday night against a Packers defense that has the second-most interceptions.Stafford threw an interception in six consecutive games in 2024. Prior to that stretch, he hadn’t thrown an interception in five consecutive games since 2014. The Rams just need Stafford to be efficient and not turn the ball over to win.

title: 3 Key Matchups That Will Decide Rams vs. Packers on Thanksgiving Eve
full_text:
The Los Angeles Rams will look to extend their four-game winning streak when they take on the Green Bay Packers on Thanksgiving Eve. With both teams fighting for a playoff spot in the NFC, there will be plenty at stake on Wednesday night. For the first time this season, Micah Parsons is set to play while Myles Garrett continues to work his way back. Here are three key matchups to watch when the Rams take on the Packers in Week 12.
Myles Garrett impressed in his return off of injured reserve for the Rams as he had three sacks two weeks ago against the Washington Commanders. However, Garrett was pretty quiet in Week 10 against the Arizona Cardinals as he continues to manage his knee injury. According to NFL Pro, Garrett has generated a quick pressure on nine percent of his pass-rush snaps through three games. That’s more than double the rate of any other player on the Rams. Jordan Morgan of the Packers has allowed quick pressure on 4.5 percent of his pass-blocking snaps, which is the sixth-highest rate among left tackles.
It will be interesting to see how much the Packers play Micah Parsons in his return from injury . Parsons has been out since last December with a torn ACL, and Wednesday will be his first game back. Given Parsons’ versatility, the Packers will likely move him around and try to get him matched up against Beaux Limmer or Justin Dedich on the interior. With that said, Parsons will primarily line up on the edge against Alaric Jackson. Jackson has allowed a 7.9 percent pressure rate this season, which is the eighth-lowest among left tackles. However, Parsons is a special player defensively and will provide a different type of challenge.
When Trent McDuffie has been healthy, he’s been one of the best cornerbacks in the NFL. McDuffie’s 0.51 yards per coverage snap ranks eighth. The Packers have the most explosive passing offense in the NFL, and Christian Watson is a big part of that. His average depth of catch of 13.3 yards ranks 10th. The Packers like to move Watson around and line him up out wide and in the slot. It wouldn’t be surprising to see the Rams have McDuffie follow Watson. The Rams are going to have to limit the Packers’ explosive plays, and having McDuffie on Watson will be their best chance.

title: Rams Have Let Confidence Turn Into Arrogance at Wide Receiver
full_text:
Despite the Los Angeles Rams having a major need at wide receiver, they have consistently shown confidence in the players they have on the roster. That hasn’t changed as they put Puka Nacua on injured reserve and are set to be without Davante Adams for at least a few more weeks.
When the Rams didn’t make a trade at the deadline, they stood pat with the idea that they would get players back. Since then, Nacua and Terrance Ferguson have each been placed on injured reserve and Adams' return timeline has been pushed back. Earlier this week, head coach Sean McVay was asked by The Athletic’s Nate Atkins if he felt it was the right decision to not pursue a wide receiver at the trade deadline.
“Based on last week, I'm excited about what those guys that did get opportunities did. Let's continue to see if we can grow and figure out what it looks like,” said McVay. “I don't want it to ever be misunderstood. I am confident in Tutu Atwell and Konata Mumpfield and Xavier Smith and C.J. Daniels, and Presley getting a chance to get back there and return kicks.”
With that said, there’s a difference between having confidence in the players the Rams have in the building and have developed and being arrogant about it. The Rams can publicly support and have confidence in their players. There’s nothing wrong with that.
However, Konata Mumpfield is a seventh-round pick in his second season. Tutu Atwell would have been cut from the Miami Dolphins had the Rams not traded for him. C.J. Daniels showed promise in training camp but is still just a sixth-round pick. Xavier Smith was cut by the Rams after Week 3 and didn’t make a roster elsewhere.
Asking those players to carry the passing game isn’t putting them or the offense in position to succeed. It’s obviously easy to criticize decisions in hindsight. At the same time, the needs at wide receiver have been evident since March.
Back in July, ESPN’s Mina Kimes previewed the NFC West and highlighted the concerns at wide receiver for the Rams.
“They have like 300 tight ends, but outside of Puka Nacua and Davante Adams, it’s a pretty thin receiving group,” said Kimes. “The way that Puka Nacua plays is absolutely unhinged at times. He’s such a wild man on the field…House of Cards is maybe too strong, but it could come crumbling down if one of those guys gets hurt and they just start to have issues at depth spots.”
The Rams needed a wide receiver in the draft and didn’t take one until the sixth round. They had several opportunities to sign veteran wide receivers.
While McVay can say things like, “You know the information that I had at the time,” and “This is the hand that we're dealt,” that’s not completely true. The Rams had information going into the season.
Nacua hasn’t played a full season healthy since his rookie year. Given his off-field situation, a suspension was always likely. It would have been safe to assume that in some way, shape, or form, Nacua was going to miss time.
Adams was 33 and coming off of a major hamstring injury from last season. Given his age and hamstring issues, it could be assumed that he might miss time again this season. That’s exactly what’s happened.
It’s impossible to predict injuries, but the Rams could have had contingency plans in place. Instead, they balked at every single opportunity to add at the position this season. There have been so many chances to add to the position and those have been ignored every step of the way. While the current options may be limited and not help immediately, this wasn't a problem that just popped up last week because Puka Nacua went on injured reserve.
The Rams didn’t add a wide receiver on Day 2 of the draft or sign a veteran. While they didn’t have a first-round pick to deal at the trade deadline, no wide receiver was traded for a first-round pick. In fact, the Kansas City Chiefs acquired Josh Downs for a fourth-round pick and a fifth-round pick.
Continuing to do nothing at wide receiver borders on arrogance and negligence from the front office. Matthew Stafford is 38 and nearing the end of his career. Aaron Donald came out of retirement with hopes to win another Super Bowl.
However, there is a seemingly complacent mindset within the front office despite the Rams being in the middle of the playoff hunt after winning four straight.They’ve done nothing, and the message has essentially been that despite sitting at 6-4, they are punting on the season. That message would be disappointing.
The Rams have earned the right to be confident in their ability to identify and develop talent. They’ve earned the right to scheme up an offense around players who fit in defined roles. Still, that doesn’t make them immune to criticism. For as good as they’ve been, Les Snead and McVay aren’t perfect. They’ve made mistakes and ignoring wide receiver this season is near the top of the list.
At some point, continuing to believe that they have enough at wide receiver despite mounting evidence to the contrary borders on arrogance. Konata Mumpfield is currently the most productive wide receiver on the roster and he has just 14 catches.
The Rams couldn’t control the injuries to Nacua and Adams, but they could control how prepared they were for those injuries. That’s where the front office failed, and it’s a failure that could ultimately define the 2026 season.

title: Rams Injury Report: Offensive Line Takes Major Hit Ahead of Micah Parsons’ Return
full_text:
The Los Angeles Rams will be without two starting offensive linemen Wednesday as they take on the Green Bay Packers on Thanksgiving Eve , who are expected to get Micah Parsons back in the lineup. Both Steve Avila and Coleman Shelton will be out with hamstring injuries.
While the Rams have mostly remained healthy on the offensive line, that has changed over the last few weeks. Avila has been managing a hamstring injury, forcing him to miss the game against the Arizona Cardinals. Shelton left during the game and is set to be out for the next 4-6 weeks.
With Avila and Shelton out, the Rams will have to make adjustments to the offensive line. Against the Cardinals, the Rams went with Bill Murray and Beaux Limmer on the interior. Limmer is expected to take over for Shelton at center, but it is unclear what the Rams will do at guard.
The Rams activated Justin Dedich off of injured reserve this week. However, he could be rusty after not playing all season. Murray stepped in well against the Cardinals and the Rams could go that route again. The Rams should have some confidence in Limmer as he stepped in for Jonah Jackson at center two years ago.
“I thought he came in and handled some of their fronts and pressures and structures really well. He gets to be around and learn from a guy like Coleman so I think that's rubbed off and he's done a nice job,” said quarterback Matthew Stafford. “He's a guy that takes a lot of pride in doing his job at a high level so that rubs off on everybody around him and we’re looking for more of the same.”
Sean McVay has done well to scheme around injuries this season, but that can be more difficult on the offensive line. With that said, the Rams had one of their best offensive performances without Avila and Shelton for a majority of the game.
However, the Packers will present a larger challenge as they are set to get Parsons back in the lineup for the first time in almost a year. Parsons tore his ACL last December and has been recovering ever since. The Packers are hoping Parsons can add to what is already a dangerous defensive front.Parsons is expected to play but is officially listed as questionable.
Also on the Packers, Zaire Franklin (shin), Josh Jacobs (finger), Bo Melton (thigh), Skyy Moore (ankle), Sean Rhyan (ankle), Kevin Zeitler (triceps), and Travis Glover (shoulder) are all questionable.
With the Rams and Packers both fighting for a playoff spot in the NFC , the timing of the injuries to Avila and Shelton certainly isn’t ideal. The Rams have done well to overcome injuries on offense over the past month, but how the interior of the offensive line holds up will be something to monitor.

title: Myles Garrett’s Knee Injury Remains a Concern as Rams Enter Critical Stretch
full_text:
During the offseason, the Los Angeles Rams traded for edge rusher Myles Garrett.After Garrett was placed on injured reserve with a knee injury following the Week 1 loss to the San Francisco 49ers, the Rams didn’t see him back on the field for two months. While Garrett impressed with three sacks in his return, it was a much different performance in Week 10.
That’s not to say that the Rams should expect three sacks from Garrett on a weekly basis. Even for Garrett, that would be unrealistic. However, he clearly wasn’t the same player that he was when he returned the week prior.
In Week 9 against the Commanders, Garrett had eight pressures and three sacks with a 93.3 defense grade via Pro Football Focus. Last week, Garrett had one pressure with zero sacks and a 46.9 defense grade. Garrett’s defense grade of 46.9 was his lowest output via PFF since Week 10 of his rookie season.
The lack of production wasn’t the only cause for concern. Garrett only played 17 snaps, which was somewhat understandable given the score. However, he only had a 7.7 percent pressure rate and pass-rush win rate against a team managing injuries on its offensive line. It should have been another game in which Garrett dominated.
It makes sense that the Rams would want to continue managing Garrett. With that said, Garrett has remained on the injury report since returning from his knee injury. Garrett has been limited in every practice that he’s participated in. It’s not unusual for the Rams to give veterans rest days  but Garrett has missed one practice each of the last three weeks.
If the Rams are going to make a push for the playoffs after their bye week, they need a dominant version of Myles Garrett. The Garrett that the Rams traded for might be enough to get them into the playoffs and lead them on a playoff run. However, it’s worth wondering if that’s a player that the Rams can expect on a week-to-week basis.
Following the game against the Commanders, Garrett noted that he still wasn’t 100 percent. “I can't go that far, but we're not 100,” said Garrett. “We're trying to make our way there and the bye week is coming at a perfect time for all of us.”
It’s possible that Garrett is still getting into game shape and gaining confidence in his knee. However, the drop in performance from one week to the next and Garrett’s continued presence on the injury report are mildly concerning. Without speculating too much, it’s fair to have some level of concern that his knee didn’t respond well after his return.
That’s a question only Garrett will be able to answer with his level of play on the field. When the Rams managed Todd Gurley’s knee in 2019, they couldn’t count on consistent production from week to week. They need to be able to rely on consistent production from Garrett given how much they gave up to acquire him and what’s at stake.
With Puka Nacua out for the season and several other players on offense dealing with injuries, the Rams are going to have to rely on their defense. The Rams are going to need to rely on Garrett to be their closer and the playmaker that they traded for. Coming out of the bye week, the Rams will play the Packers, Chiefs, and 49ers over the next three weeks. Those are the types of games that the Rams acquired Garrett to help them win.
The Rams need Garrett healthy down the stretch, and that doesn’t seem to be a certainty at this point. Coming out of the bye week, the hope is that Garrett got some much-needed time to recover and that his performance against the Cardinals was simply an outlier.
However, with the Rams entering arguably the most important stretch of their season, Garrett’s ability to consistently play at an elite level could ultimately determine how far this team goes. While the Rams have won four consecutive games, their margin for error remains slim. They’ve already spent much of the season without Garrett and can’t afford for his knee to limit his effectiveness over the final two months. They can’t afford for their biggest difference-maker on defense to be a diminished version of himself.

title: How to Watch Rams vs. Packers in Week 12 on Thanksgiving Eve (Start Time, Channel, What to Watch For)
full_text:
The Los Angeles Rams are set to take on the Green Bay Packers in Week 12 in a matchup with major NFC playoff implications . It’s the perfect way to start the NFL’s Thanksgiving slate in what is the first-ever game on Thanksgiving Eve. Both teams enter the game at 6-4 and tied for the final playoff spot. A win on Wednesday would give either team an important head-to-head tiebreaker as the season enters December.
The Rams are set to play their second game this season on Netflix. They also played in primetime on Netflix in Week 1 against the San Francisco 49ers, losing 27-7. Fans watching on Netflix will need an active subscription, but the game is included in all subscription plans. The game can also be watched locally on CBS LA.
Alan Eck is set to be Wednesday’s referee. Home teams are 5-3 with Eck as the referee this season. Eck’s last Rams game came last season against the Detroit Lions. The Rams are 2-0 with Eck as the referee, while the Packers are 0-2.
A big topic of conversation with the Rams and Packers set to play on Thanksgiving Eve is the shortened bye week. Instead of both teams getting 13 days between games, the Rams and Packers are getting nine. Despite the scheduling disadvantage, teams still have to adhere to rules in the CBA.
According to the CBA, players are required to get four consecutive days off during the bye week. With the Rams set to play next Thursday, the Rams took those four days off last week after their win against the Cardinals. Conversely, the Packers are set to take their four off days after the game against the Rams.
Sean McVay finally got a win over a LaFleur brother before the bye week, beating Mike LaFleur and the Arizona Cardinals. Prior to that win, McVay had been 0-6 against the LaFleur family. Of course, five of those losses have come at the hands of Matt LaFleur and the Green Bay Packers.
This is a matchup that Matt LaFleur has dominated. McVay and the Rams have lost by one score or less just twice in the five matchups, most recently losing 24-19 back in 2024. McVay got his first win against Nick Sirianni earlier this season and will hope to get his first over Matt LaFleur on Wednesday.
The Rams will wear their Fearsome Foursome throwback uniforms on Wednesday against the Packers for the first time this season. During the offseason, the Rams released two throwback-style uniforms, one of which paid tribute to the Fearsome Foursome.
Coincidentally, the Rams will be relying on their defense to win the game on Wednesday against the Packers. For the first time this season, the Rams will have Kobie Turner, Braden Fiske, Aaron Donald, Byron Young, and Myles Garrett on the field together.

title: Rams Perfect Free Agent WR Target Just Became Available
full_text:
The Los Angeles Rams have been in need of wide receiver depth for much of the season. With the season-ending injury to Puka Nacua and Davante Adams’ timeline getting pushed back, that is even more the case. After the San Francisco 49ers released wide receiver Brandon Aiyuk on Monday, it’s worth wondering if the Rams would look to sign the former all-pro.
It’s highly unlikely that the Rams would claim Aiyuk off waivers and take on his contract, but he is someone they could look into if he clears waivers. However, despite the Rams being in need of a wide receiver, they don’t appear to be in a hurry to add one
“We've talked about all those types of things. I would never rule out opportunities to upgrade, but like I said, I think the guys have done a really good job,” said head coach Sean McVay. “They did a great job last week and I'm excited to see them play well on Wednesday night.”
It seems like the Washington Commanders could be the favorite to sign Aiyuk. They were reportedly in conversations to trade for him prior to the season. Aiyuk and Jayen Daniels have also allegedly set aside their differences following some offseason drama.
Why should a team give Aiyuk another chance given the last two years? "I think they are going to get the best version of Brandon Aiyuk moving forward."--Drew Rosenhaus
Still, given the Rams’ wide receiver room, they would be smart to consider Aiyuk. It could end up working out similarly to the team signing Odell Beckham Jr. following his failed stint with the Cleveland Browns. Beckham signed a one-year contract with the Rams for the league minimum. Had Beckham not torn his ACL in the Super Bowl, it’s possible that the Rams would have re-signed him instead of signing Allen Robinson in free agency.
There is certainly some risk with Aiyuk. The short week also doesn’t help, with the Rams set to play the Green Bay Packers in two days. However, when Aiyuk was healthy, he was a borderline top-10 wide receiver. He had 1,300 yards and seven touchdowns in 2023. Until 2024, he had five or more touchdowns in each of his first four seasons.
Aiyuk’s ability to create separation and contribute as a blocker in the run game is part of what makes him an intriguing option. Those are two traits that McVay has consistently valued in his wide receivers. It’s possible that Aiyuk could step into Nacua’s role in the offense and fit into what the Rams want to do offensively.
The Rams currently have a very clear need at wide receiver with not many reinforcements coming. They are set to get Davante Adams back, but Nacua and Terrance Ferguson are both out for the season . Even still, it seems unrealistic to expect Adams to carry the Rams’ passing game at 33 years old and coming off of major hamstring surgery.
Outside of Adams, the Rams don’t have anybody that necessarily scares defenses. Konata Mumpfield has been inconsistent and inefficient throughout his career. Atwell has two drops on five targets over the last three weeks and CJ Daniels is still just a rookie.
Even if Aiyuk isn’t a personality fit for the Rams, they have nothing to lose at this point . The Rams are 6-4 and in the thick of a playoff hunt. If Aiyuk works out, he has the upside to help propel the Rams into the postseason. The Rams should want a wide receiver who is motivated to beat the 49ers.
In the case that Aiyuk isn’t the same player or isn’t a fit, the Rams can either cut him or just move on after the season. It’s fair for the Rams and other teams to be skeptical, but they have reached a point where it doesn’t hurt to make this type of move.
Some teams I've spoken are skeptical Brandon Aiyuk will walk right into a job. At least three unknown variables exist: Health, conditioning, motivation. On the flip side, buying low isn't the worst thing. He's only 28. And practice squads are tailored for fliers like this.
The Rams have balked at the idea of adding a wide receiver since the early spring outside of drafting Daniels in the sixth round. Given the current wide receiver situation, not looking into adding a player like Aiyuk is borderline negligence. However, given what McVay told the media on Monday, it seems like the Rams are fine with who they have in the building, for better or worse.
Signing Aiyuk may end up not working out, but the Rams can’t continue to do nothing as they sit at 6-4 and in the middle of a competitive playoff race. The Rams spent much of the yea r waiting for wide receivers to get healthy , only for those players to be lost for the remainder of the season. Aiyuk may not be the answer, but refusing to explore a potential upgrade would only reinforce the same questionable decision-making that put the Rams in this position in the first place.

title: Rams Face Major Questions About Future of Pass-Catchers Ahead of 2027 Offseason
full_text:
It’s no secret that the Los Angeles Rams mismanaged their pass-catchers going into the 2026 season. The Rams’ front office is very good, but they put a lot of faith in a player with off-field issues who hadn’t stayed healthy since his rookie year, a 33-year-old wide receiver coming off of a major hamstring injury, and a player with 11 career receptions.
There were a lot of reasons to be excited about the Rams’ pass catchers going into the season. Puka Nacua was one of the NFL’s best wide receivers and arguably should have won Offensive Player of the Year in 2025. Davante Adams led all wide receivers in touchdowns last season. With the Rams moving to more 13 personnel, there was also some upside with tight end Terrance Ferguson.
However, that doesn’t mean that the Rams shouldn’t have also had some contingency plans. It never made sense to ignore the wide receiver position until the sixth round of the draft. That’s not to say they should have taken a wide receiver over Ty Simpson. There were options later in the draft, as well as veteran options available in free agency
Additionally, the Rams had the ability to trade for a wide receiver. Instead, the Rams operated with the idea they would get players back healthy. Since then, Puka Nacua and Terrance Ferguson have both been placed on injured reserve and Davante Adams’ return timeline has been extended to Week 14 or 15 instead of Week 12 or 13.
Nacua’s decision to opt for season-ending knee surgery in combination with everything else surrounding the Rams’ pass catchers makes it one of the more interesting position groups in the 2027 offseason.
Not only will the Rams have to take a look in the mirror at how the position was handled, but they also need to establish a foundation for the future. There are several key decisions that the Rams will have to make.
To start, Puka Nacua, Davante Adams, Colby Parkinson, and Davis Allen are all free agents. Right now, the speculation seems to be that the Rams could tag Nacua or even trade him. Given Nacua’s injuries and off-field stuff, an extension seems risky.
Additionally, Tyler Higbee and Davante Adams will be 34. Higbee contemplated retirement last offseason and Adams likely won’t play for another team.
That leaves the Rams with Ferguson, who has 18 career receptions, and Max Klare at tight end. At wide receiver, the Rams would have Konata Mumpfield, Jordan Whittington, and CJ Daniels. That’s without mentioning that the Rams don’t have a first-round pick.eve Those names don’t provide a lot of reason for optimism.
Even if the Rams were to tag Nacua, it’s hard to imagine his contract situation not becoming a distraction, just as it has been this season. For the first time in four years, Nacua’s future with the team seems more uncertain than ever.
When healthy, Nacua is one of the best wide receivers in the NFL. He’s the type of franchise player teams should build around. However, the Rams are also in a position where moving on from Nacua would leave them without a starting-caliber wide receiver.
The Rams simply don’t have a foundation among their pass catchers past this season. They put all of their chips in on 2026 and it appears like the bottom may fall out in a way that it didn’t after they went all-in in 2021.
That’s not to have a negative outlook on the Rams’ future. It’s simply some of the challenges that the Rams’ front office is facing. The front office could navigate those challenges as it has navigated other obstacles in the past. Still, it will be something they’ll have to figure out this offseason. The Rams will either need to give Matthew Stafford a group that’s good enough to push for a Super Bowl or provide Ty Simpson with a group that won’t set him up to fail.
The Rams have managed to overcome difficult roster situations before, but that doesn't make the decisions ahead any less important. This is a front office that’s going to have its work cut out for it this offseason

title: Rams Lose Terrance Ferguson for Season as Injury Situation Continues to Spiral
full_text:
The Los Angeles Rams will be without tight end Terrance Ferguson for the remainder of the season . After the team previously expected to activate Ferguson off injured reserve regardless of whether he was ready, the Rams have opted not to activate him as he is still dealing with an ankle injury, according to ESPN’s Sarah Barshop.
Rams TE Terrance Ferguson is still dealing with an ankle and will not come off IR. He is done for the season.
Ferguson entered year two with high expectations as the team moved to more 13 personnel in the offense. While Ferguson is a tight end, he was seen as the third wide receiver in the offense. However, he was placed on injured reserve after Week 3 with an ankle injury. The Rams designated Ferguson to return after Week 8. In Ferguson’s first practice back, he injured his hamstring.
With Ferguson’s 21-day practice window nearing its close, the Rams were initially planning on activating him even if he wasn’t ready so that he was available for the stretch run. However, now the Rams are set to lose Ferguson for the year, and according to NFL rules, will also lose his return designation.
“The plan is to not shut him down,” said head coach Sean McVay on Friday. “You want to leave out hope to be able to give him an opportunity to return to play and come back and be a part of this thing.”
Ferguson’s season hasn’t gone as planned. He finished with seven receptions for 63 yards and a touchdown, with his best game coming in Week 2 against the New York Giants. In that win, Ferguson had six receptions for 54 yards and a touchdown. The Rams were hoping to make Ferguson a large part of the passing game , but that never truly came to fruition.
While Ferguson is only in his second season, it’s worth having a conversation about whether he is injury-prone. Ferguson missed some of training camp his rookie season with an injury, causing him to have a slow start to the year. An ankle injury put him on injured reserve this year before he injured his hamstring.
The Rams designed a lot of their offense around Ferguson and the tight end position this season. Ferguson’s been out since Week 3 and they haven’t used rookie Max Klare very often. Last year, the Rams were high on Ferguson coming out of the draft as players like Harold Fannin Jr. were taken later.
With Ferguson continuing to manage his ankle injury, the team opted for season-ending surgery. Ferguson is the second Rams pass catcher to undergo season-ending surgery in the last week. Last week, Puka Nacua opted for surgery on his MCL.
The Rams didn’t make a move at the trade deadline for a pass catcher with the idea that they were set to get players back. Since the trade deadline, Nacua and Ferguson have been ruled out for the year while Davante Adams’ return timeline has been extended. The complementary pass catch in the offense continues to be a position that the Rams’ front office has significantly mismanaged since the early spring.
Ferguson's season-ending injury adds to the growing list of players the Rams have lost this year. With Ferguson and Nacua now out for the season, it’s fair to wonder how much faith the front office and coaching staff have in salvaging this season or if they’re already looking ahead to 2027.
The Rams have shown they can adjust offensively, but with each additional injury, McVay is being asked to do more with less. With games against the Packers, Chiefs, and 49ers coming up, the Rams will need their offense to continue finding ways to produce without some of its most important pieces.

title: Rams vs. Packers Prediction: Major Playoff Implications in Thanksgiving Eve Showdown
full_text:
The Los Angeles Rams and Green Bay Packers are set to kick off the Week 12 Thanksgiving slate in the NFL’s first Thanksgiving Eve game. There will be major playoff implications as the Rams and Packers both sit at 6-4 and in a three-way tie for the NFC’s final playoff spot. A win for either side on Wednesday will give them an important tiebreaker and some momentum heading into December.
Over the past few years, the Rams and Packers have played important games late in the season, including a playoff game in 2020. Most of those matchups have been at Lambeau Field, and Sean McVay will be looking for his first career win over Matt LaFleur.
The Rams have been one of the more balanced offenses in the NFL during their four-game win streak. Without Puka Nacua for the remainder of the season , the Rams need to lean into that and continue featuring Kyren Williams and Blake Corum. This season, the Packers’ defense ranks 27th in defensive rushing success rate. However, the Packers have a top-10 pass defense and also rank in the top 10 against play-action. The Rams need to be able to stay ahead of the chains with the run game. This will also be Micah Parsons’ return after tearing his ACL.
Given the lack of options at wide receiver, it wouldn’t be surprising to see the Rams use a lot of 13 personnel in this game. The Packers rank 22nd in passing success rate out of their base personnel and Zaire Franklin ranks 55th out of 63 linebackers in coverage via Pro Football Focus. This could be a game where the Rams look to get Colby Parkinson and Tyler Higbee involved in the passing game.
There have been times this season in which Jordan Love has played at an MVP level. However, when teams have gotten pressure on Love and taken away the big plays, they’ve had success. Not every team is the Minnesota Vikings. However, the Vikings pressured Love 31 times and got eight sacks back in Week 10. The Rams are as healthy as they’ve been on the defensive line this season and could have some success.
Anthony Belton has struggled at times on the right side this season and Byron Young has 5.5 sacks. The Rams should be able to exploit some of the weaknesses on the Packers’ offensive line, and Belton could be one of them. If the Rams can get pressure on Jordan Love and get him moving left, they may be able to force some mistakes.
This is a must-win game for both teams. The NFC playoff race is going to be tight with three teams fighting for one playoff spot. Given that the Rams and Packers are two of those teams, this game has major implications when it comes to tiebreakers. The Rams will have an advantage playing at SoFi Stadium, but these are two similar teams that have both battled inconsistency. At the end of the day, the Rams should be able to lean on the run game and wear the Packers down in the second half. Prediction: Rams 24, Packers 21

title: Raiders Rookie, Sophomore Power Rankings: What Stands Out
full_text:
The Las Vegas Raiders entered the season planning to spark their rebuild by depending upon several of their young players to play pivotal roles this season. As the season has progressed, even more young players have been forced into action, as Las Vegas searches for the right mix of players.
“We have a roster of a lot of young guys, and it's our job as coaches to develop them and make sure they're a huge part of our future,"  Klint Kubiak said on Monday.
“The expectation is for these young guys to play and these young guys to contribute. Those guys definitely have stepped up really all season. Fernando [Mendoza] is making his second start, but we have a roster of a lot of young guys, and it's our job as coaches to develop them and make sure they're a huge part of our future."
After 11 games, Las Vegas is all in on its group of young contributors . Below are our power rankings for the Raiders' rookies and second-year players who impacted Week 11.
Mendoza played well in the first road start of his career. The pick-six was unfortunate, but several other things could have been done better by others around the rookie. Overall, the Raiders are likely not competitive in that game without Mendoza under center.
The rookie made several plays that simply would not have been made earlier in the season. Tough completions and timely runs have opened up the Raiders' offense. It will be interesting to see how Mendoza does over the final six games, especially if Las Vegas keeps running the ball well.
Jeanty finished Week 11 as the team's leading rusher and its leading receiver. He still leads all running backs in receiving yards this season. Once the Raiders improve the roster further, performances like that from Jeanty will lead to wins.
Regardless, outings like the one he had on Sunday are why Las Vegas' front office was comfortable using the No. 6 overall pick on the running back. Now, they need more games like that from Jeanty.
Las Vegas has needed Bech to step up for some time, but injuries kept the second-year player out for weeks. The Raiders' receivers have had their ups and downs this season, especially without Brock Bowers, but on Sunday, the unit stepped up, largely behind Bech's solid contribution.
Bech caught eight of his nine targets for 88 yards, leading Las Vegas' receivers in yards on Sunday. Kubiak explained the connection Bech has already formed with Mendoza in just two starts with the rookie quarterback.
“Well, I think a quarterback and receiver relationship builds when there's adverse times and the guys are making plays. So, those plays that Jack [Bech] made last night, those are things that he's done in practice with Fernando [Mendoza]. He has the trust of the quarterback,” Kubiak said.
Las Vegas' coaching staff to its time with McCoy, gradually bringing the rookie along as he recovered from a significant injury before entering the league. After shuffling through other young corners, the Raiders were forced to lean on McCoy more heavily in Week 11, and he responded well.
McCoy did dodge a major bullet that could have swung the game. However, even on that play, things worked as they should, as Las Vegas' pass rush helped force a throw that was just off target enough.
It has only been a few games, but the Raiders have run the ball better since Zuhn became a starter. He isn't the sole reason for the improvement, but he is the only change the Raiders have made along the starting lineup in recent weeks.
If Zuhn keeps developing, that would be huge for Las Vegas' offseason plans and their future. The Raiders' front office will likely thoroughly address the offensive line this summer. Zuhn's ascension could mean the Raiders need one less offensive guard.
Stukes remains a pivotal player in Las Vegas' defensive backfield. The rookie shows progress with each game and seems to make fewer mistakes by the week. The final six games will be critical for Stukes ahead of what will be an even more vital second offseason in the league.
Ezekiel is a former Sports Editor from the Western Herald and former Atlanta Falcons beat writer.

title: How Raiders' Week 11 Performance Confirmed Areas of Improvement
full_text:
The Las Vegas Raiders' Week 11 outing against the Denver Broncos will go down as a loss, but it featured many of the positives the Raiders hope will one day become mainstays of Klint Kubiak's tenure. The Raiders have lost three in a row, but gained valuable experience at the same time.
That experience has come with its bumps in the road, as the Raiders have struggled for weeks in several areas, on both sides of the ball. Yet, the past two losses have felt like building blocks for the future. Las Vegas is a rebuilding team facing many of the league's best teams in consecutive weeks.
The overall results have been about as expected, as Las Vegas' roster is still a work in progress. That unfinished product has given two of the league's more polished teams competitive games with a rookie quarterback.
Rookie quarterback Fernando Mendoza started his first career road game in Week 11. The Raiders' supporting cast stepped up. Las Vegas' ground game exploded for its best outing of the season and, technically, one of its best games on the ground in the past two seasons.
Las Vegas entered Week 11 with the second-fewest rushing yards in the league, but ran for 143 yards against the Broncos. It was the most rushing yards they have had in a game this season. It came against one of the best teams in the league, and without Brock Bowers on the field.
Las Vegas' Week 11 success on the ground was a surprise, to say the least. That success helped the Raiders' offense get going after weeks of struggles. Klint Kubiak shared his thoughts on Las Vegas' improved ground game.
"I just think over the season, as it's gone on, our guys are getting more familiar and comfortable with the scheme, and the more time on task that you have, you anticipate improvement, and it was a step in the right direction,” Kubiak said on Monday.
“Obviously, you get to shorter third downs. In the fourth quarter is when you normally get bigger runs. So, when you're able to run the ball in the fourth quarter, that has a big effect on the outcome of the game. It helps the defense. It helps the whole organization when you're running the football well."
Raiders running back Ashton Jeanty ran for 79 yards on 11 carries. Mike Washington added 42 yards on nine carries, and Mendoza added another 22 yards on the ground. Kubiak noted how the running backs' success, combined with the threat of Mendoza running the ball, helped open things up.
“I think plays like that are successful when there's the threat of the run. Then on third-and-two, when there's a threat of the run, that's when you can get the edge like that. Play fake or no play fake, early in the game when you're running the football, that's when those play actions and those keepers really come to life. But you got to be able to run the ball first," Kubiak said.
Las Vegas needs much more than one good game on the ground to confirm they have figured out their issues. However, for a team that has struggled to run the ball for as long as the Raiders have, Sunday's outing could be the turning point for the long-standing issue that has plagued Las Vegas.
Las Vegas finished with the fewest rushing yards in the league in two of the past three seasons. In the third of those three seasons, they finished with the third-fewest rushing yards in the league. Along with their issues at quarterback and elsewhere, finding a consistent ground game has been elusive.
Las Vegas has one of the toughest schedules in the league this season, but has made it through the hardest part of the schedule. The remaining six games give the Raiders a chance to make the most of the struggles they've had this season in an attempt to end the season on a high note.
The Raiders have a manageable final quarter of the season. The past two weeks have solidified that they are headed in the right direction . The next six weeks may give an idea of how soon they can realistically reach their destination.
Ezekiel is a former Sports Editor from the Western Herald and former Atlanta Falcons beat writer.

title: Raiders Snap Counts: Biggest Takeaways From Week 11 vs. Broncos
full_text:
The Las Vegas Raiders lost to the Denver Broncos on Sunday, 38-24, in another defeat to an opponent with a winning record. It was a game that featured the Raiders erasing a three-possession lead with a chance to tie the game, only to let it slip from their grasp late.
There were several notable developments for the Raiders on both sides of the ball as several players received more playing time due to injury or to play in an effort to find more improvement from key areas on the roster.
I looked over the snap counts from Sunday's game. Here are my biggest takeaways from my overview.
The top-15 prospect turned fourth-round selection was named the starter on Sunday opposite Eric Stokes, and frankly outperformed the Raiders' supposed No. 1 cornerback. Defensive coordinator Rob Leonard clearly trusted Stokes and McCoy to handle a majority of the defensive snaps—the first time we've seen this almost all season.
It was fascinating that Hezekiah Masses played just six snaps, and Darien Porter was relegated to special teams play, though it makes sense given how both have displayed inconsistencies for the last month or so.
This was also the first time we saw Klint Kubiak deploy a significant amount of 11 personnel in the absence of Brock Bowers, and the Raiders offense with quarterback Fernando Mendoza looked impressively efficient out of it. Bech played the most snaps of his career and was a trustworthy target for Mendoza, catching eight passes on nine targets for 88 yards and a touchdown.
Foley Fatukasi: 38 snaps (52%)
J.J. Pegues: 30 snaps (41%)
Chris Williams: 24 snaps (33%)
Thomas Booker IV: 22 snaps (30%)
Adam Butler: 18 snaps (25%)
Tim Keenan III: 9 snaps (12%)
Injuries to Butler, Pegues, and Keenan left the Raiders thin at defensive tackle . Fatukasi and Chris Williams saw significant playing time in situations they wouldn't normally be in, while Booker got snaps late in the contest. This group did a better job than I expected considering all that happened to this group throughout the game, and with the trade deadline having come and gone, this is likely going to be an area opponents will attack in the run game.

title: Hondo's Raiders Mailbag: Biggest Key to a Win in Cleveland
full_text:
The Las Vegas Raiders (4-7) are headed to the banks of Lake Erie to take on the Cleveland Browns (6-4) this weekend, and the Silver and Black have something to prove.
The Raider Nation sees their fandom as far more than just an NFL team; it's a way of life , and they will be there.
The game has been flexed by the NFL, meaning that while it was originally scheduled for an early kickoff, it will now be a Sunday night primetime game.
Each week via my social media, I ask Raider Nation to talk with me. On my X account on Tuesday, @HondoCarpenter, you all did what you do best: Respond.
Gotta take less sacks- this is on Mendoza and the protection. 11 in two games is way too many.
I can’t argue with this. Kirk Cousins took 11 sacks in two games, and Fernando Mendoza has now taken eight. I went over this in detail when I discussed the winners and losers, but what I can add here is that it is part of the learning curve for a rookie.
I believe in Fernando more than I ever have. The Raiders made the right move with the trade, but rookie and young players and coaches make mistakes.
Cleveland has a very good defense, and the last two teams did as well, and found multiple ways to get pressure. If Cleveland tries to repeat what others have done, Fernando can handle that; the concern is that if they show something different, it will be a learning curve.
Same things for me.  OL looks like it's beginning to gel and get some push.  Continued improvement in the run game.  And need to see Fernando slow down a little bit and set his feet. Patience is a virtue.  Patience is a virtue.
I agree that the performance against the Denver Broncos indicates the offensive line is gelling. While I have said it numerous times since last December, I say it again. The Klint Kubiak system is completely and totally predicated on the running game.
It is imperative for Klint Kubiak's mental health to get the running game going. The better it gets going, the more successful this team will be. I have a full appreciation for this coaching staff, and I expect the Raiders to continue their resurgence in the running game.
Pressure up the middle bye the defense better offense guard play
This is so accurate. We knew coming into the season that the Raiders' defensive line was anemic. I expect at least two new ones in the offseason, but the Raiders were down one starter going into the Denver game, and lost three more during the game.
Think about that: already the weakest position on the defense, and you lose four of your five DTs.
With that said, they aren’t going to be able to add players like they will in the offseason, but from a pride perspective, it's simple for this team. You may not be loaded at DT, but play for the name on the back of your jersey. Get the push. If the Raiders can do that this week, they will win the football game. If they can’t, they still might, but if they do, there is no might; they will.
The push by the defensive tackle position is the single biggest key for the Raiders' win.
I’ll stick to offense because the defense is a challenge right now. Less 3 and outs, continue to stack positive plays, even if just small gains. Cut back on penalties again. Just play a clean game and put points on the board.
This is such a practical response, and clearly you know what you are talking about. Three-and-outs are brutal because your defense gets no rest. The Raiders need those, even if they don’t score, to give a battered defense a rest. I have seen good teams lose games because of a plethora of three-and-outs, and their defense getting run down. This is critical.

title: What We Learned About the Raiders After Week 11 Loss
full_text:
The Las Vegas Raiders suffered their third consecutive loss on Sunday, falling to the Denver Broncos, 38-24.
Here is what we learned about the Silver and Black from their loss to their divisional rivals.
The stat sheet indicates that the rookie signal caller struggled mightily, completing 48.6% of his passes. However, Mendoza was operating with an undermanned receiving corps. In a hostile environment, without Brock Bowers and with a porous offensive line, Mendoza had everything working against him.
The No. 1 overall pick showed off his mobility and anticipation on intermediate passes. The result of the game and stat line don't accurately depict Mendoza's outing. Now, he showed his inexperience, forcing a pass into traffic on the final drive of the game, resulting in a pick-six and sealing the Raiders' fate. Nevertheless, Mendoza proved why he is the future franchise quarterback in Las Vegas.
Trading Kirk Cousins was absolutely the right move, as landing a third-round pick for an aging quarterback after signing him to a bargain contract is great business. However, it also signaled that the organization is moving towards 2027. Now, Las Vegas was unlikely to reach the postseason after losing to the San Francisco 49ers a few weeks ago. While giving Mendoza some on-field experience will be best for the long term, the short term suffered.
That's not to say that Mendoza is at fault, as his first two career starts were against the Seattle Seahawks and Broncos. Not to mention, the Raiders were likely to lose those games even if Cousins was still the starter. Las Vegas' season will come down to Week 13 against the Cleveland Browns. If the Raiders lose that game, their playoff hopes are effectively over.
Mendoza was already fighting an uphill battle facing two of the best defenses in the league. You then add poor protection and a receiver corps lacking a true go-to option with Bowers out. Ashton Jeanty led the team with five receptions for 90 yards and one touchdown. Jack Bech was also more than serviceable, catching eight passes for 88 yards and one touchdown.
Regardless, this wide receiver corps is nowhere near good enough to support a young quarterback. Also, Mendoza was under constant duress, pressured 17 times, hit 10 times, and sacked five times. With Mendoza on a rookie contract, the front office needs to aggressively pursue offensive linemen and wide receivers via free agency and the draft.

title: How Raiders' Youth Movement Is Finally in Full Effect
full_text:
It has not resulted in many wins yet, but the Las Vegas Raiders' grand plan is slowly starting to come together. After years of roster decay finally led to the Raiders' roster bottoming out in 2025, the Raiders' front office immediately got to work this offseason, gutting the coaching staff and roster.
The rebuild the Raiders embarked on has been thorough and is just getting started. As with most true rebuilds, Las Vegas is largely dependent upon a growing number of players who recently entered the league.
Klint Kubiak noted how much a part of the plan it always was to lean on the young players they have added to their roster over the past two seasons. Relying on so many inexperienced players has been problematic at times, but that is to be expected.
“Yes, the expectation is for these young guys to play and these young guys to contribute. And you're right, those guys definitely have stepped up really all season. Fernando [Mendoza] is making his second start, but we have a roster of a lot of young guys, and it's our job as coaches to develop them and make sure they're a huge part of our future," Kubiak said on Monday.
Development is why it was critical to get Mendoza on the field. All of the other young players Las Vegas' front office and coaching staff planned to lean on this season had already played significant minutes.
Mendoza was the only one who hadn't. As Mendoza's play has quickly improved, the team's confidence has increased. In just two games, Mendoza has directly or indirectly impacted nearly every other young contributor. Mendoza rounds things out for Las Vegas' group of young players.
The Raiders have leaned on first- and second-year players on both sides of the ball this season, especially in the defensive backfield. The unit has spent most of the season experiencing the highs and lows that come with being a young defensive back in the league.
Hezekiah Masses, Darien Porter, and Treydan Stukes have all played significant minutes this season. Rookie cornerback Jermod McCoy has played sparingly throughout the season, with his most extensive action coming on Sunday against the Broncos.
It was his best performance, as he showed physical progress after gradually recovering from an injury that sidelined him for his final collegiate season. McCoy's contribution and overall steady play helped Las Vegas' defensive backfield eliminate more big plays through the air than in previous weeks.
“That was just our decision as coaches, and I thought Jermod [McCoy] did some good things yesterday. Obviously, he had a high snap count. There's plenty of things he's got to continue to improve on, but I like where he's headed, his trajectory,” Kubiak said.
“It doesn't mean that we're down on Zeke [Hezekiah Masses]. Doesn't mean we're down on DP [Darien Porter]. We got a room full of really solid players. But yesterday, we wanted to get a bigger look at Jermod."
The Raiders added five defensive backs to the roster this season via free agency and the draft. Most of them were rookies. After years of turnover in their defensive backfield, Las Vegas' decision to load their roster with rookies and then get them on the field early appears to be paying dividends.
The decision is paying off elsewhere. Kubiak's coaching staff has prided itself on development since arriving during the offseason. After 11 games, that development appears to be working.
Along with Mendoza and McCoy, rookie offensive lineman Trey Zuhn has also begun making himself a valuable addition to the starting lineup. Zuhn was recently named the team's starting right guard and has gradually gotten better since.
Zuhn has been the primary change along the offensive line in recent weeks. In Week 11, Las Vegas produced its best rushing game of the season, practically doubling its season per-game average. Kubiak explained how important the team's Week 11 success on the ground will be moving forward.
“I just think over the season, as it's gone on, our guys are getting more familiar and comfortable with the scheme, and the more time on task that you have, you anticipate improvement, and it was a step in the right direction," Kubiak said.
Ezekiel is a former Sports Editor from the Western Herald and former Atlanta Falcons beat writer.

title: Why Raiders Are Closing in on Paramount 2026 Victory
full_text:
For the last two weeks, the Las Vegas Raiders have inched closer to a major win.
They're a 4-7 team, all but out of the playoff hunt at this point of the season, given the state of the AFC and the AFC West. Yet, their 21-13 loss to the Seattle Seahawks and 38-24 defeat to the Denver Broncos on Sunday suggested the organization had taken a small step forward with each game.
Yet as the Raiders continue to lose games, the margin gets smaller and smaller. The roster is getting better in the final several weeks of the regular season, which could lead to a significant upset before or after the Week 13 bye.
"Jared, why do you think an upset is coming? That's crazy talk."
Well, I'm no genie in a bottle, but I can see with my eyes when a team is taking a step forward. The Raiders are doing just that as their defense continues to show signs of growth on all three levels while their offense evolves with rookie quarterback Fernando Mendoza .
What gives me a sense of a future upset is head coach Klint Kubiak and his staff sticking with what they have and trusting in their development within the offensive and defensive systems to become a better football team. I would say in the last two weeks, Las Vegas has been playing solid defense that is giving its offense an opportunity to produce.
Also, the more opportunities for the offense, the more learning and growth Mendoza can have under center for Kubiak and the Raiders.
This is all part of an evaluation process in a rebuilding year, and so far, the team has exceeded expectations. This team is better than it was a year ago, with more talent at key positions, while using the last two draft classes to build its foundation.
Las Vegas's first opportunity for an upset bid is Sunday night against the Cleveland Browns, who have far exceeded expectations and are in the thick of the playoff race as the AFC North's second-place team.
Both teams match up evenly from my early glance at both rosters, and if the Raiders get a similar performance from their defense and Mendoza, this could be a big win on primetime. Cleveland is a tough place to play when the Browns are playing well, and it will likely be a harsh environment in late November.
Hurting the Browns' playoff chances would be a signature win for Kubiak's team. It is a culture-building victory that could set the tone for the rest of the season and years to come. They're close, and they know it; time to find out if it happens on Sunday.
