title: Vikings Verdict: Judging Brian Flores, Justin Jefferson & More Overreactions Ahead of Week 12
full_text:
The Vikings won by 20 in Green Bay in Week 10, then got demolished by 25 points on Sunday Night Football. So, will the real Minnesota Vikings please stand up?
There's plenty of reason to think the Vikings are still on track for a Super Bowl run, and just as many think the wheels are starting to come off. Has Brian Flores been solved? Is Justin Jefferson washed up? Let's get into these overreactions and more ahead of Week 12.
The 49ers offense got whatever they wanted against the Vikings on Sunday night, racking up 35 points against a team that allowed just 14 per game. The big question, of course, is: do teams now have the blueprint to beat the Vikings, or are the Niners simply a level ahead of the rest of the league?
Brock Purdy dissected the Vikings' disguises with ease, quickly finding gaps behind the ferocious pass rush on his way to 255 yards and three touchdowns. So far, the MVP candidate has been the anomaly this season. Teams know the pressure is coming against Minnesota; that's no secret. The real challenge, and one that nobody had been able to crack, is to know where it's coming from and then make the correct read in about a second and a half.
We'll chalk this up to an incredibly well-coached and talented team in San Francisco rather than Flores getting exposed. It'd be fairly surprising if Atlanta's Michael Penix achieved the same success next week.
This hardly deserves addressing, but there's been a lot of chatter about the Vikings star receiver losing a step after another week without 100 yards . It's now been almost a year since Jefferson eclipsed triple digits, and the flashy plays haven't really been there either.
But to think that Jefferson is anything but one of the league's premier receivers is utter nonsense. His numbers haven't been there, sure, and it may be his first season without reaching the 1,000-yard benchmark, but the Vikings also rank 27th in pass attempts per game. Not to mention, the quarterbacks throwing those pass attempts up until last week are now on the bench for a reason.
Kirk Cousins has targeted Jefferson 22 times over his two games, and Jefferson has rewarded him with 16 catches for 160 yards. As they rekindle their connection, things will only get better. The second half of 2026 will see some vintage Jetta games.
The Vikings are averaging just four yards per carry this season, which sits at 22nd in the NFL, but here's the thing: it's completely unsurprising.
Obviously, not every position on the field can be full of superstars, but the Vikings had plenty of opportunity to address running back in the draft or at the trade deadline. Clearly, the offensive line hasn't held up its end of the bargain either, and the losses of Donovan Jackson and Josh Oliver certainly hurt, but Jordan Mason hasn't had the breakout some expected.
He's sub-four average, and a single rush over 20 yards (in Week 1) hasn't moved the needle. Meanwhile, Aaron Jones Sr. has been fine , especially for a 31-year-old, but he's also in the midst of his worst statistical season as a pro. If the Vikings can't find ways to carve out more room on the ground, the play-action game will dry up as well.

title: Vikings Have a Chance to Correct Their Myles Price Mistake in Week 12
full_text:
Sunday night's loss to the 49ers didn't exactly fill Vikings fans with much optimism . Sure, there's still plenty of the season left, and securing an NFC North title is still a legitimate possibility, but it's also clear the Vikings need to make several changes to erase lingering doubts plaguing the fan base.
One questionable decision the Vikings made in Week 11 was opting not to use wide receiver Myles Price as much as they should have. After a personal-best four catches and 49 receiving yards , while making his first career touchdown reception against the Packers in Week 10, Price was targeted only twice for as many catches and 26 yards in the loss to San Francisco.
Sure, Price was busy with special teams duties (four kick returns for 94 yards, one punt return for 19), but that doesn't explain why he was only used for 11 offensive snaps.
After all, he played 33 plays while also returning three kicks the week before, so that can't be an excuse—especially when the Vikings were also without WR2 Jordan Addison against the 49ers. Instead, they targeted perennial disappointment Jauan Jennings six times, while Tai Felton saw an unfathomable 12 targets.
Considering how Jennings and Felton combined for 62 receiving yards on nine catches, it's safe to say the Vikings made the wrong decision. Fortunately, they have a chance to right those wrongs against the Falcons in Week 12.
On Monday (h/t ESPN 's Kevin Seifert), head coach Kevin O'Connell told reporters that he felt "encouraged" by Addison's ongoing recovery from thumb surgery , and that the Vikings "don't necessarily expect to have him this week."
Kevin O'Connell on Jordan Addison (thumb surgery): "Encouraged about where Jordan's at. Don't necessarily expect to have him this week but he's progressing really well for having just gotten that thing fixed."
Even though Addison hasn't been ruled out yet, it sounds like the Vikings are content with a patient approach. Although his presence is important, the former 2023 first-rounder won't be much help to the Purple and Gold down the stretch if he's dealing with physical limitations—especially given how important his hand is to, well, his job.
Assuming that Addison doesn't suit up against the Falcons, who allow the second-most passing yards (239.1) and fifth-most completions (23.2) per game, the Vikings have good reason to give Price a proper do-over.
After all, Jennings and Felton have been inconsistent at best and frustrating at worst throughout the 2026 season. Jeshaun Jones hasn't done much outside of his 32-yard reception in Week 5, while Justin Jefferson continues to look more human each passing week and is currently on pace for the first sub-1,000-yard season in his seven-year career.
Price can't wake up the Vikings' passing attack on his own, but involving him more could light a fire under his fellow WRs. The Texas Tech/Indiana product already showed chemistry with quarterback Kirk Cousins when the duo connected on a 38-yard TD score in Week 10's blowout win over Green Bay.
COUSINS TO MYLES PRICE FOR A TD ON 3RD AND 23 MINvsGB on FOX/FOX One Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/jSQvCluTla
His 70.3 receiving grade also trailed only Jefferson (73.0) as far as Vikings pass-catchers were concerned in that game, per Pro Football Focus .
With how banged up and inconsistent the WR room has been this season, the Vikings have nothing to lose, and potentially everything to gain, by expanding Price's role. If he can't ball out against the Falcons' vulnerable secondary, that's okay, and they can revert to peppering Jennings and Felton with targets in December and beyond.
But if turning back to Price works? Suddenly, the Vikings' offense has a new layer, and Cousins has another talented weapon to take advantage of. The intrigue of that path alone should be enough to force O'Connell's hand, leaving it to time to tell whether he'll do the right thing this weekend.

title: Harmon’s Vikings Longship Week 11: 4 Pressing Thoughts After Reality Check From 49ers
full_text:
The Vikings loaded their ships and sailed south this week for a battle between NFC powerhouses in Mexico City. With Kirk Cousins back under center and Brian Flores’s defense fresh off an incredible eight-sack performance, Minnesota appeared ready for the moment, even with Jordan Addison and Isaiah Rodgers sidelined.
Instead, Vikings fans got a sobering 35-10 reminder that this team is far from championship-ready at the moment.
Now, the 7-3 Vikings must reestablish their identity over their next seven games, even though they still appear destined for the playoffs. How they approach the next month and a half will determine just how far their journey can go.
It was clear early on that the Vikings were facing their toughest opponent yet, as the 49ers marched downfield with precision to score an opening-drive touchdown via the first of two Brock Purdy-George Kittle scoring connections. The Vikings would attempt to get on the board shortly after, but Will Reichard missed his third kick of the season, all coming from 50+ yards out. They would eventually get on the board with a TD run by Aaron Jones late in the first.
Showtyme for 6 😤 📺: @SNFonNBC pic.twitter.com/j6iLyPqq2Z
After a 7-7 end to the first quarter, any semblance of a close game was thrown out the window. Minnesota would put up only three more points on the night via a Reichard field goal in the second. San Francisco would tack on 28 additional points, 21 of which came in the second quarter alone. The most brutal moment of the night? An 18-yard Cousins pick-six to Ji'Ayir Brown that gave San Francisco a 28-10 halftime lead.
The 49ers would go on to add one more touchdown thanks to Christian McCaffrey in the fourth, but the result of the game seemed long decided by then. Minnesota’s defense was simply unprepared for the task, in a game that was a far cry from what we’ve seen them do all season. Safety play by Josh Metellus, Theo Jackson, and Harrison Smith was a major factor, as all three gave up key gains at different points. If other teams want to attack the Flores’s defense, they certainly now have their targets.
Minnesota’s offense was able to move the ball for the most part, with the passing game showing occasional promise . Ultimately, Cousins’s interception and an uncharacteristic fumble by Justin Jefferson killed two key drives and ended any hope of keeping up with San Fran’s elite offense.
A couple more looks at the Justin Jefferson fumble where he should've kept running to the pylon. You can see KOC's reaction on the sideline angle. pic.twitter.com/yGtNEjHbnC
As I’ve stated before, O’Connell is a very good head coach. His 50-28 record proves that, for the most part, he consistently leads his team to victory, even in less-than-ideal circumstances. That said, the Vikings’ consistent failures in their biggest games continue to raise serious red flags about the fifth-year head coach. The Vikings followed an emotional Week 10 win in Green Bay with an embarrassing performance on the biggest stage of the week, a result that’s becoming all too familiar.
Their incredible win against the Bills in 2022 was followed by a 40-3 home loss to the Cowboys. Their statement win against the Packers in Week 17 of 2024 was followed by an inexcusable showing in Detroit, with the No. 1 seed on the line. I could go on, but I think you can see the pattern.
Outside of last week’s 30-point output against the Packers, the Vikings have scored 15, six, and 10 points in games against the Lions, Bills, and 49ers, respectively, over the last month. Simply put, O’Connell and the Vikings need to step up against the league's better teams , or he may end year five still searching for a single playoff win.
Here’s the good news: the 2026 Vikings are still a playoff team barring a collapse of historical levels. The worry now is whether they can consistently keep up with the best opponents the NFC has to offer.
For those who like to view their glass as half full... The #Vikings still have the highest chance to win the NFC North after Sunday's loss, and the second-highest chance to win the Super Bowl in the NFC (Per @TheAthletic ) pic.twitter.com/fF46YBKcYF
Minnesota’s schedule gets much simpler in the coming weeks, with consecutive home games against the Falcons and Panthers before a Thursday night game against a Patriots team missing their starting QB. Going 3-0 in these games will be key before a Dec. 20 Sunday night battle at home against the Lions. Luckily, Detroit will host Chicago on Thanksgiving, so one team will be taking a hit in the divisional standings this week.
The Vikings return to the friendly confines of U.S. Bank Stadium next week as Kirk Cousins makes his 2026 home debut against his former Falcons team. Ironically, Cousins played for the Falcons the last time he played in Minnesota in 2024. Minnesota will be heavily favored in this one, but ignoring the Falcons may be risky. Two of their three wins have come against the Packers and 49ers, proving they are capable of beating anyone on any given day.
This is the perfect “get right” opportunity for the Vikings, but they cannot afford to ignore a Falcons team that has already managed to play spoiler.

title: 21 Things Wrong With Vikings After Blowout Loss to 49ers Serves as a Wake-Up Call
full_text:
Sunday night's loss stung, but it came against the best team in the NFC, and the Vikings' season is far from over.  Still, even though the future remains bright, there are plenty of things that could use some attention.
Without being overly dramatic, here are the 21 things still plaguing the Vikings heading into Week 12.
Put the Vikings in a 3:25 slot against the AFC South every game, and the NFL will be looking at its first-ever 17-0 team. Instead, Minnesota has been assigned to 18 primetime games in head coach Kevin O'Connell's tenure, and he's now gone 6-12 after last night's loss to San Francisco. At some point, the "can't win big games" narrative just becomes the reality.
If the Vikings' defense has a weak spot, it's safety, where the back end has been burned constantly throughout the season. Minnesota rosters six safeties, so it's a bit hard to believe that the deepest position is actually their weakest, but Joshua Metellus is the worst-graded safety in the NFL by Pro Football Focus, and Harrison isn't far behind at 96th out of 100.
Passing on a running back near the top of the draft, and then again at the trade deadline, has continued to plague the Vikings. Both Aaron Jones Sr. and Jordan Mason are having their worst statistical seasons ever (no, really), and there's just no juice in the backfield. Kirk Cousins' back is going to be sore for months.
The 49ers were the first team to really dominate the Vikings' defense this season. So are Kyle Shanahan and Brock Purdy the perfect duo to beat Flores, or is their success repeatable?
The undrafted free agent gets a pass here, but the other Vikings starters up front have been mostly disappointing this year. The Vikings have one of the highest sack percentages (8.28%, 26th) in the NFL, and it's not like the ground game has been blossoming either.
Jennings had his one shot at a breakout against his former team with Jordan Addison out, but was a non-factor with just three catches for 20 yards. It's probably safe to say now that this signing just didn't work out.
The Vikings haven't needed to rely heavily on their rookies yet, but when that time comes, it's tough to see any of them ready for a starting role just yet. Caleb Banks and Jake Golday were both taken on as projects, so they may get a slight pass, but Domonique Orange and Max Bredeson should've been further along by now.
T.J. Hockenson is the Vikings' second-leading pass catcher this season, and he's also missed two games. Gavin Bartholomew and Ben Yurosek still have some bright futures, but already down Josh Oliver, the Vikings may need to worry if Hockenson continues to get nicked up.
Price continues to make plays (when he gets the ball) and had a nice 22-yard catch against the Niners just a week after his 38-yard score in Green Bay.
COUSINS TO MYLES PRICE FOR A TD ON 3RD AND 23 MINvsGB on FOX/FOX One Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/jSQvCluTla
And yet, Tai Felton saw 12 targets on Sunday compared to Price's two, and it certainly feels like those numbers should be swapped if anything.
Stop the bubble screens. Stop the second-and-long runs. As problematic as execution on offense has been for Minnesota, Kevin O'Connell isn't without fault either. KOC should still remain as the playcaller, but some self-reflection needs to happen, too.
The Vikings are 7-3 and still boast a 93% chance to make the playoffs, yet they play like a team desperate to scrape and claw their way towards a postseason berth. The vibes have been weird all year for this team, but at the end of the day, a measly 4-3 record down the stretch still gets them in.
The Vikings went 1-3 in November this year and 0-4 last year. It's a good thing they are 9-0 in December over the last two seasons.
Oh yeah, the team is cursed. Always has been, but can't forget that in any calculations.
Will Reichard's leg accounts for 46% of all scoring this year, and even since Cousins's return, that number is still 45%. The Vikings have got to find the end zone more, plain and simple.
The Vikings haven't been losing many fumbles with just four, but they've also had some lucky bounces after coughing up the rock 10 times this season. Those four turnovers could have easily been seven or eight had the ball been kicked in another direction a few times.
The Vikings are 31st in third-quarter scoring with just two points per game. Not sure what the fix is—if there is one—but clearly the halftime adjustments aren't resonating.
Due to the trade, Cousins won't have a bye week. That may not be an issue, but he's also 38 years old and getting tossed to the ground every other dropback. Minnesota might limp into the playoffs—literally.
The Vikings are 29th in yards after the catch, and whether that's due to personnel or playcalling, it hasn't been good enough. Perhaps getting Price more involved can fix these woes?
The Vikings have just 14 total broken tackles across the board this season. For reference, the league-leading Steelers have 52.
Playing in the best conference in the league certainly isn't doing the Vikings any favors in 2026. 7-3 is a better record than 23 other teams, and yet here they sit, third in their own division.
If the bid for a Super Bowl falls short in 2026, next year looks even more ominous for a run. Half of the starting defense will be free agents; there's still no long-term solution at quarterback, and Flores may get a head coaching job elsewhere. That's a lot of hypotheticals, but there's no question that significant challenges remain in 2027.

title: Patriots Offense Gets Major Boost with Return of Injured WR
full_text:
FOXBORO — The New England Patriots continue to get healthier as they try to scrape together a push to the playoffs.
Wide receiver Romeo Doubs , who's missed the last four games with a shoulder injury, returned to practice this week. That begins his 21-day window to be activated off of injured reserve and onto the 53-man roster.
Doubs signed a massive free agent contract with the Patriots in the offseason . Since then, he hasn't really put together a consistent string of games in his first season with New England. In 6 games, he's caught 14 passes for 261 yards and three touchdowns — two of them coming against the Buffalo Bills in Week 4.
Against the New York Jets two weeks later, Doubs injured his shoulder as he came down with a 42-yard touchdown less than five minutes into the game. He'd be placed on IR the following week, and has recently been spotted more in the locker room when reporters were present.
Doubs might not added to the 53-man roster this week, considering his later return to the practice field. But seeing him run at practice is a better sign for a Patriots wide receiver room that's been banged up for quite a while.
A.J. Brown continues to be absent from practice as he works his way through an ankle, hamstring and knee injury. Without Brown/Doubs in the room , the Patriots have had to rely on Mack Hollins (who's also dealt with injuries this season), DeMario Douglas, Kyle Williams and Efton Chism III to catch passes.
This year when healthy, Doubs has added some deep threat to the Patriots passing attack, especially down the sideline. Sometimes, he hasn't been able to haul in the pass, but the ability to stretch the field is something this offense needs to utilize.
Getting Doubs back into the fold this week will also help ease in Tommy DeVito, who's set to make his first start as a Patriots quarterback . Adding as many talented players around the Patriots' backup-turned-starter this week against the Los Angeles Chargers will help a team that's looking to snap a two-game skid.
"A lot of energy. I think a lot of work in there with those guys," Mike Vrabel said Tuesday about DeVito's connection with the receivers. "We talked about it at training camp with that group. I think he's taken advantage of his opportunities."
Should the Patriots activate Doubs to the 53-man roster this week, they'd need to make room with a corresponding transaction. They could also add offensive guard Alijah Vera-Tucker to the roster, who also returned to practice after a four-game absence.

title: Tommy DeVito Feels Good Heading into First Patriots Start
full_text:
FOXBORO — Tommy DeVito hasn't started an NFL game since 2024 , and he's excited to return to that spot. After Drake Maye's injury that's left his status for this season up in the air, the New England Patriots are turning to DeVito this week against the Los Angeles Chargers.
DeVito says that it's been a good week so far as he adjusts to his new role with the Patriots .
"(It's) gone well. Yesterday was a little less than today, but felt good to be out there with the guys," DeVito told reporters after Tuesday's practice. "A lot of energy, a lot of flying around. It felt good."
On paper, it's a heartbreaking turn of events for the Patriots — who have to throw the face of their franchise to the side. Maye, despite his struggles all season, was the north star on a team looking to get back to the Super Bowl conversations. Now, they'll have to hand the keys over to DeVito for the foreseeable future.
The team declined to add an external quarterback this week to plug the gap a la Daniel Jones or Jimmy Garoppolo , so DeVito has earned the Patriots' faith and confidence. He said that feels good for him to rely on this week in practice.
"It's been awesome. Everybody's embraced me. Even from the first snap and the first play that I was in there last week, it's always been the same message over and over again from the guys," he said. "They have full trust in me, and that's what I've tried to earn throughout OTAs, training camp, preseason and up until now. And that's every day I come in. I work, I try to put my best foot forward, do everything I can to earn their trust. Because when we're on the field, that's all it's about."
Sitting at 5-5, the Patriots have the opportunity to make things interesting in a weaker AFC. DeVito will be tasked to conduct an offense that really hasn't looked like it's clicking. A.J. Brown and Romeo Doubs continue to deal with injuries, so it will be a lot of Mack Hollins, DeMario Douglas, Kyle Williams and Efton Chism III out wide.
Lucky for DeVito, those were the guys he was throwing to all summer .
"A lot of the guys that are in there right now are guys that I've had reps with during training camp, and I think that's huge," DeVito said. "I mean, not just for timing and any of that, it's more about the comfortability in the huddle and guys knowing how I talk, how I operate in the huddle, what my cadence sounds like and then just building off that. So, I mean, the receivers, the running backs, everybody, I've had a ton of reps with them.
"The new thing was really just the O-line, just getting used to the cadence and building and going from there. But no, I feel good with that group."
During New England's bye week, while some players stayed home, DeVito was in the facility working out and getting a jumpstart on the Week 12 matchup. He feels "energized" when he walks into the building, and that's the type of energy the Patriots need right about now.
"So for me, it's being able to be ready because I've waited for this moment," DeVito said. "I’ll enjoy this moment. I’ll embrace it, no matter what it is - good, bad, ugly, whatever the situation is."

title: Hunter Henry Has Plenty of Confidence in Patriots Teammate This Week
full_text:
FOXBORO — Hunter Henry has spent his time with the New England Patriots catching passes from plenty of starting quarterbacks. Mac Jones, Brian Hoyer, Bailey Zappe, Jacoby Brissett, Drake Maye.
This week against the Los Angeles Chargers, it will be time to add Tommy DeVito's to the list. The Patriots will be turning to the 28-year-old this week as their starting quarterback after Maye's fractured fibula suffered two weeks ago .
For Henry, he remains confident in DeVito's ability to help a Patriots offense that's looking to break out of a two-game losing streak.
"Obviously, he hasn't been out there a ton with us, so that is obviously a new thing of stepping into (the starting offense)," Henry told Patriots On SI at his locker before Tuesday's practice. "But I think already, he's stepped into that role and had a lot of command, just in the short time we've been with him."
Henry has been a valuable piece of this offense in 2026, catching 34 passes and racking up 383 yards and a pair of touchdowns. But that was coming from Maye, the young superstar who helped lead the Patriots to the Super Bowl less than a year ago.
Now he'll have to try to replicate that success with a quarterback who hasn't started a game since 2024.
Lucky for the veteran tight end, he's been able to get some reps in with DeVito this year. During training camp, the Patriots had a plan in place to get Henry additional snaps in practice. So Henry, who was voted a captain this season once again, took part in the first-team offense before switching over and getting into the second-string offensive huddle.
He's seen how DeVito operates the huddle and commands the offense on the field, and is sure that it will translate to his first New England start on Sunday .
"I spend a lot of time with the quarterbacks in general. Tommy's a great dude, man. He's still young and growing in this league, and he has a big opportunity ahead of him. I think he's just continuing to get better," Henry said.
"I've banked some reps with Tommy, and just looking forward to kind of building that as we go, man. I know he'll be ready to go."
Henry was part of a DeVito start in the past, where the New York Giants beat the Patriots 10-7 back in 2023. DeVito threw for 191 yards and one touchdown in a game where the Patriots offense really, really struggled. Henry didn't remember much about that game other than his side struggling, but did look back on that game and used it to prove that DeVito knows what he's doing.
"He's done this in the past," he said. "Obviously, he's played in this league and played in some big games and won games in this league. (He) knows what it takes, so having guys stepping up in that aspect is always good."
The Patriots really like DeVito, as evidenced by his two-year contract extension he received in the offseason to jump from QB3 to QB2.
DeVito might not offer the same excitement that a Maye-led offense does, but the Patriots need their backup to step up and help carry them to a win.
"I'm excited to kind of see that continue to expand," Henry said of DeVito's leadership. "I think he definitely has that in him. It'll be good."

title: 9 Former Patriots Advance in Pro Football Hall of Fame Voting, including Rob Gronkowski
full_text:
The Pro Football Hall of Fame has announced the 52 players who have advanced to the next round of voting for its 2027 class. The group includes nine former New England Patriots, three of which have already been inducted into team's own Hall of Fame.
Tight end Rob Gronkowski, defensive tackle Vince Wilfork and safety Rodney Harrison are the inductees into The Hall at Patriot Place who now seek to be enshrined in Canton, Ohio. Guard Logan Mankins, linebacker James Harrison, running back Fred Taylor, plus wide receivers Reggie Wayne, Torry Holt and Antonio Brown round out the group of former New England players who could receiver their gold jacket next year.
Here's a look at each of their resumes in New England:
Although his playing career ended with the Tampa Bay Buccanneers, Gronkowski's rise to stardom came in New England. The 2026 first-ballot Patriots Hall of Fame inductee has the most receiving touchdowns in franchise history (79) and the second-most receiving yards (7,861).
Plus, he won four Super Bowls (three in New England) and tallied the same amount of First-Team All-Pro nods.
Wilfork, a 2022 Patriots Hall of Fame inductee, spent the first decade of his playing days in New England before rounding out his career with the Houston Texans. With the Patriots, he won a pair of Super Bowls and five total All-Pro nods.
The 2004 first-round pick has also been named to the Patriots All-2000s and All-2010s team.
Since retiring in 2009, Harrison has been a multi-time Pro Football Hall of Fame snub. The two-time Super Bowl champion spent the first half of his career with the San Diego Chargers before joining New England.
Harrison is a member of both the Chargers' and Patriots' respective Hall of Fames.
A multi-time Patriots Hall of Fame nominee, Mankins has been a victim of New England's surge of dynasty players becoming eligible for a red jacket. The six-time All-Pro spent most of his career with the Patriots prior to being dealt to the Tampa Bay Buccaneers.
Although he never won a Super Bowl in New England, Mankins was named to the team's All-2000s and All-2010s teams.
Harrison begins the group of players substanially more renowned for their accomplishments prior to joining New England. The former NFL Defensive Player of the Year spent the majority of his career with the Pittsburgh Steelers, before joining the Patriots in December of his final NFL season.
The former undrafted free agent is a two-time Super Bowl champion and multi-time First-Team All-Pro.
Although he appeared in just 13 games as a Patriot, Taylor's accomplishments beforehand could make him Canton-bound. The former Jacksonville Jaguar had seven seasons where he rushed for over 1,000 yards, and totalled nearly 11,700 on his career.
Taylor is also a member of the Pride of the Jaguars, Jacksonville's ring of honor.
Although Wayne never suited up for the Patriots in a regular season game, he still cracks the list after spending a week and a half in New England in 2015.
With the Indianapolis Colts, Wayne earned a Super Bowl ring, three All-Pro nods and led the NFL in receiving yards in 2007. Plus, he is a member of the Colts Ring of Honor.
Although he spent a season with the Jacksonville Jaguars prior to joining New England, Holt is most well-known for his decade spent with the St. Louis Rams. The three-team All-Pro led the NFL in receiving yards twice and in receptions once.
Holt also won Super Bowl XXXIV while with the Rams.
If Brown were to get into the Pro Football Hall of Fame, it certainly would not be due to his contributions in New England. The pass catcher played just one game in red, white and blue, after spending most of his career with the Pittsburgh Steelers and spending an offseason with the Oakland Raiders. He then wrapped up his career with the Buccaneers.
While the four-time First-team All-Pro has the resume to punch his bid into Canton, his off-field could hinder his case.

title: Week 12 Rooting Guide for Patriots Fans: Which AFC Teams You Need to Lose
full_text:
Currently ranked eighth in the AFC and holding a 5-5 record, the New England Patriots need a lot to happen in the next seven weeks in order to make the playoffs.
Their chances of playing postseason football aren't just r eliant on the team winning games without their franchise quarterback , but also depend on other teams in the mix losing games.
The Patriots are one of the best teams when facing other AFC opponents, which gives them an advantage over head-to-head victories and common opponent tie breakers. Beating teams like the Raiders and Steelers gives the Pats a huge advantage if they were to tie their record with any of the other teams 'in the hunt' for a Wild Card spot.
🏈AFC Week 11 Playoff Picture🏈 Will your team make the playoffs? pic.twitter.com/BHuLSkZTAw
Looking at Week 12's slate of games , Patriots fans will be joining forces with the following fanbases in order to increase the likelihood of a second straight playoff birth for the Pats.
This matchup can have varied impacts on the Patriots. For starters, the Bills are the most immediate divisional threat to the Pats, but have a pretty large lead over New England for the AFC East title.
However, if Buffalo drops their Thanksgiving night game to the Chiefs, and the Patriots pull off a miracle the following week at home against the Bills, there is slight hope for an AFC East title in New England, despite the loss of Drake Maye.
Buffalo will also enter the hardest part of their schedule, facing the likes of Green Bay, Chicago, and Denver after their divisional match against the Pats in Week 13.
Although, rooting for a Wild Card spot would mean rooting for the Bills. Kansas City losing would be more ideal for the Patriots, who head on the road in Week 15 to play the Chiefs. If Denver ends up winning the AFC West, the Chiefs would compete with New England for a Wild Card spot.
Once again, having to root for an AFC playoff team is never fun, but the Broncos taking down the Steelers would be monumental for the Patriots, who hold a tie breaker over Pittsburgh.
The Steelers are second in the AFC North, to the Bengals (7-3), but a loss in Week 13 would create a larger gap between the two teams and catapult the Patriots ahead of the Steelers in the standings (if the Pats beat the Chargers).
Like Kansas City, Denver may wind up as a Wild Card team, depending on who wins the AFC West. And New England will face the Broncos in a big Week 17 game at home which could have massive playoff ramifications.
For now, New England will hope the Steelers lose, which gives them a path right into the playoff picture with a win on Sunday.
This game is conflciting for the Patriots, as both teams sit just behind New England in the current AFC standings.
However, Baltimore will play four of their last five games against divisional opponents, which doesn't help their case for a playoff bid. Additionally, the Ravens are on their fourth starting quarterback of the season in Jacoby Brissett and aren't looking like a legitmate threat to anyone.
The Texans, on the other hand, have underperformed this season and have the potential to compete with playoff teams in the AFC. Their remaining schedule is difficult, having to play the Jaguars, Steelers, and Packers, but this Texans team poses one of the biggest threats to a Patriots playoff birth, and can jump New England in the standings with a win and a Patriots loss on Sunday.
Sunday Night Football this week features two teams in the playoff bubble hoping to outlast one another and make it to the post-season.
While the Raiders are another team inching up on the Patriots, New England holds a tie breaker over Las Vegas from their Week 5 win. Already with seven losses, the Raiders are seeking a first victory for rookie first-round pick Fernando Mendoza.
The Browns, who have exceeded expectations this season, currently hold the seven seed and are one game ahead of the Patriots. A loss on Sunday night, paired with a New England victory, would put the Patriots right into the playoff picture.

title: Patriots Offense Rallying Around QB Drake Maye After Injury
full_text:
FOXBORO — After New England Patriots quarterback Drake Maye suffered a potentially season-ending injury last week, the signal caller's teammates have quickly rallied around him.
Last Sunday against the Detroit Lions, the 24-year-old went down at the end of the game's first drive. He did not return, and was later diagnosed with a fractured fibula. That diagnosis is one that fellow quarterback Behren Morton knows all too well.
"I know it's gonna be a course," the rookie said on Monday. "I actually dealt with a similar injury last year with my fibula, and it's not fun. But, Drake's a tough dude, and he's gonna bring so much positive energy to this team, and he's gonna keep being himself."
Morton explained he suffered a hairline fracture to his fibula last year with the Texas Tech Red Raiders, which he played through. Although Maye's injury seems to be to a more significant degree, Morton says the team captain has remained the same old version of himself.
"I just saw him earlier today, he was in great spirits," Morton said. "He's the same Drake. He's upbeat, it's a deal, it happened, I hate it for him, but Drake's a great guy, he's gonna bounce back no problem"
Until Maye is back, the Patriots aim to pick up some steam for him. New England currently sits at a 5-5 record and is one spot out of the playoffs.
"Drake's a team captain on this team for a reason," Morton said. "So, we're gonna rally around Drake still, and Drake's gonna be in the facility every day. And so, he's still one of our main leaders, and we're gonna lean around him, for sure."
Morton's sentiment was shared by Patriots right tackle Morgan Moses , who praised Maye as a player, leader and person.
"Obviously, he's one of our core leaders," Moses mentioned. "So, you never wanna lose a guy like that, and what he brings to the table as a teammate, and just as a brother. You never wanna lose that guy, but we know his head's up. He's rooting for us, and he's doing everything he can do to help us."
Meanwhile, New England left tackle Will Campbell, whose tight-knit friendship with Maye has been well-documented, is confident in the gunslinger's ability to fight back from his injury.
"Yeah, I think he's very upbeat, very positive," Campbell said. "I know he's gonna work his tail off to get back whenever he can and we'll see what happens."

title: Patriots Get 'Talented' Offensive Veteran Back at Practice
full_text:
FOXBORO — The New England Patriots have been really injured this season en route to a 5-5 record. But ahead of their Week 12 matchup with the Los Angeles Chargers, they could be getting a really big piece of their puzzle back on the field.
Offensive guard Alijah Vera-Tucker , who missed the last weeks on injured reserve with a hamstring injury, was present during the Patriots' conditioning practice on Monday. Him returning begins the 21-day clock for Vera-Tucker to return to the active roster.
"I think AVT’s got a chance to be out there," head coach Mike Vrabel said prior to practice, signaling that the team was set to get him back in the fold.
"He’s (a) extremely talented player," offensive tackle Will Campbell said in the locker room . "I know everybody in our room loves him. He’s played a lot of good football in this league, and he’s played really well so far this year when he’s been in. I love playing next to him. I know Jared (Wilson) does, too. We’ll see what happens. It’ll be huge."
Vera-Tucker got hurt against the New York Jets in Week 6 and since then, the Patriots have really struggled to stay on the field at both guard spots. After already losing Mike Onwenu to a broken ankle, the Patriots have seen Greg Van Roten, Ben Brown and Walter Rouse get banged up.
Brown didn't make the trip to Munich, Germany in Week 11 because of a knee injury, but also returned to practice on Monday — "Ben Brown may do a little bit more. But yeah, we'll see what today looks like and then start on the Chargers," Vrabel said.
Without Vera-Tucker on the field, the Patriots have shuffled between Brown and Rouse at left guard. Getting AVT back is a good sign for his chances to suit up against the Chargers on Sunday, but it's not a forgone conclusion that he'll play.
The Patriots would need to clear up a spot for him on the 53-man roster if they activate him this week, and if it's not this week, they'll have until Dec. 3 to promote him. If they don't, his season will be over.
The Patriots started the season with eight return designations from IR. They've already used six of them, issuing them to A.J. Brown, Mack Hollins, Reggie Gilliam, Greg Van Roten, Marcus Bryant and now Vera-Tucker. They could end up using another this week with Romeo Doubs, who's eligible to be activated.
Doubs has dealt with a shoulder injury that he suffered in the same game as Vera-Tucker's injury. He was spotted in the locker room during media availability in cleats, but wasn't present during practice — something that didn't come as a surprise.
"I think Romeo, maybe later in the week, but it’s a bit too soon to tell right now," Vrabel said prior to practice.
Along with Doubs' absence, the Patriots were without Drake Maye, A.J. Brown , Carlton Davis and Craig Woodson during the stretching portion of the practice. They'll be back for practice on Tuesday and Wednesday before getting an off day for the Thanksgiving holiday.

title: Patriots QBs in Make or Break Scenario in Week 12
full_text:
Despite repeated affirmations from New England Patriots coach Mike Vrabel that "Tommy (DeVito)'s our starter," there is still plenty of discussion around who will be the Patriots short-term solution at quarterback.
On Monday, Vrabel shared the chances of adding another quarterback to the roster.
"We've talked about it," Vrabel said. "I don't think that's something that will happen today."
While on WEEI's The Greg Hill Show, he added that "We'll see. I don't know that's something we necessarily think. We have guys that have been with us, understand what we're doing, and how we want to try to do it."
The second-year coach of the Patriots also confirmed that DeVito would be making his first start as a Patriot on Sunday.
Despite not starting an NFL game in nearly two years, there are high expectations for the fourth-year former undrafted free agent.
DeVito is tasked with facing a one-win Los Angeles Chargers team in his first start with New England. The Patriots, sitting at 5-5, are still in contention for a playoff berth as they continue the back half of their season.
New England is expected to get back guard Alijah Vera-Tucker and potentially wide receiver Romeo Doubs this week from injured reserve, which would further increase the Patriots' chances of winning. Additionally, the Chargers may be without starting quarterback Justin Herbert, as he enters concussion protocol this week.
If DeVito can operate the offense at an efficient level with sufficient talent around him, he'll prove to the organization that he can keep the Pats afloat while Drake Maye recovers from a fractured fibula.
But losing to the Chargers wouldn't be ideal for DeVito, who's in his second season in New England. An embarrassing loss to the Chargers not only drops the Pats to a losing record, but puts them further out of reach from the playoffs.
With Maye's injury expected to sideline him through the month of December , New England is hoping to make a push into January and play postseason football.
If DeVito doesn't have a sound game against the Chargers, especially when coming off extended rest, then his job could further be in jeopardy.
For now, it seems like the Patriots will stick with DeVito and rookie Behren Morton as the only two quarterbacks on the roster. But if they have to find a replacement for their current plan, it's unlikely they'll trust a seventh-round rookie to push the team to the playoffs.
Some have floated the idea of signing Jimmy Garoppolo, who is not currently with an NFL team. There are also plenty of other experienced quarterbacks that are free agents or currently on NFL practice squads.
However, a big name starter was just made available to the entire NFL, as the Colts moved on from Daniel Jones.
Jones, who was replaced by DeVito in New York a couple seasons ago, is likely to clear waivers on Monday as team's won't want to take on his $38 million salary in 2027.
This would make the former first-round pick a free agent and eligible to sign with any team. Over the weekend, it was reported that Jones would take his time before signing with a team, hoping to land somewhere that is in need of a quarterback and has playoff aspriations.
The Patriots probably fit that criteria better than any other team in football for Jones. And since the veteran quarterback wants to wait before signing, he might as well wait to see how his former backup quarterback performs on Sunday against the Chargers before making a decision.

title: Patriots HC Mike Vrabel has Simple Message for Team
full_text:
FOXBORO — Following the injury of starting quarterback Drake Maye , New England Patriots head coach Mike Vrabel has a simple message for his team: Play better.
New England has dropped its past two games by a combined 43 points to the Green Bay Packers and Detroit Lions. The loss against Detroit also included the loss of Maye, who suffered a reported fractured fibula which is expected to sideline him for the majority of the season.
More about the possibility, but hardly a certainty, that Drake Maye could return toward the end of the season if New England is in playoff contention, via @MikeReiss and me: https://t.co/zHzlXU6967
Despite speculation on whether the Patriots could sign a new signal caller, they are expected to move forward with Tommy DeVito in place of Maye.
"Tommy's our starter," Vrabel put bluntly. "And again, we're excited about that. Good preseason and Tommy's improved. I know that going into the last game, I think that being thrown in there, and had some good plays, had some things that he can improve on, and little things."
With Maye out for the foreseeable future, and New England on the outside looking into the playoff picture, the Patriots' outlook for the remainder of the year may seem bleak. In response, Vrabel has a simple message for his team.
"Play better," Vrabel said on Monday. "And again, I think that we have a lot of confidence in Tommy. And I think just doing the little things better. You know, not hurting ourselves with negative plays. And making sure that we stay balanced. Offensively, take care of the football."
DeVito and the offense is not the sole group which needs to play better, however. The Patriots have lost a trio of games this season by at least three possessions due to inconsistencies throughout all three phases.
"Defensively, you know, limiting the X plays and finding ways to create turnovers," he added. "And then I think that we've been close on special teams ... trying to get Marcus going there, that was such a weapon for us and has been a weapon in the past. And then making sure that we stay — the ability to cover kickoffs and not have the one that, you know, gets out to the (45-yard line)."
New England's team-wide issues stem from far before Maye's injury. The Patriots have a -10 turnover differential this season , tied for second-worst in the NFL. Flipping that script remains a top priority.
"And those are the things that we have to continue to do no matter who's playing quarterback," Vrabel said. "Those are things that are going to be important. Protecting inside out, not letting pressure into the middle of the pocket that disrupts the timing of the play. You know, all the same things, no matter who the quarterback is."

title: Mike Vrabel Confirms Patriots' QB Plans Heading into Week 12
full_text:
FOXBORO — The New England Patriots, one day into their Week 12 prep against the Los Angeles Chargers, have landed on their starting quarterback .
Tommy DeVito, the team's second-string quarterback who stepped up to replace the injured Drake Maye two weeks ago, will be the starter. Seventh-round rookie Behren Morton will be his immediate backup — "Tommy's our starter," head coach Mike Vrabel said Monday.
After losing Maye to a fractured fibula, an injury that could knock him out for the remainder of the season, the eyes of New England turned to DeVito, who hasn't started a game since coming over in the summer of 2025. This week, he'll make his first Patriots start and continue the progression that he's been making this season.
"We're excited about that," Vrabel said of DeVito, who inked a two-year extension this offseason to stay with the Patriots. "Tommy's improved. I know that going into the last game, I think that being thrown in there and (he) had some good plays, had some things that he can improve on and little things."
It wasn't an inspiring outing for DeVito in Munich two weeks ago , where he went 12-for-24 for 81 yards, a touchdown and an interception.
Now with two full weeks to operate and prepare as the starting quarterback, there's a shot that DeVito improves on his play from Munich. He's earned the confidence of his coaching staff as well.
"I think that was probably the biggest thing is just saying, hey, getting back into game action, how do you work in the pocket?" Vrabel said. "These are things that he's gotten so much better on when he got here. So starting with those things and managing the offense and being able to get us in and out of the huddle and the right plays, and just get into a flow and a tempo.
"And I think that some of the things that we saw in training camp, a lot of those guys that he'll be out there throwing to (are) some of those guys that he worked with in training camp. So I think that there's some carryover there."
As for Daniel Jones, the plan isn't to add the recently-released veteran ... at least for right now. Jones was released by the Indianapolis Colts last week after a string of really bad performances and the Patriots were reportedly in the mix for a team that could be interested in his services.
The Patriots could find production in having a third quarterback on the roster in practice, though Vrabel mentioned how it's not the most important thing.
"We'll look at everything, but again, I don't think that that's something that's going to happen here in the next few days," he said.
Without Maye on the practice field, this week will also be a larger dose of snaps for Morton — who moves from QB3 to QB2. The Texas Tech rookie, who was drafted with the 234rd overall pick this spring, has been the Patriots' emergency third quarterback in the first 10 games of the season.
Now Morton can get a chance to run the show team offense himself in practice, something he was sharing with DeVito up to this point.
"I think that this is also a great opportunity for Behren to improve to where those reps that him and Tommy may have been splitting, or Tommy taking the majority of those, I think that this is a great opportunity for Behren to improve in that regard of running the show team," Vrabel said.
Morton has a big arm, something he showed off during the preseason snaps he received. In the Patriots' second game last summer, he chucked a game-winning touchdown to rookie Nick DeGennaro to knock off the Philadelphia Eagles in the final seconds. He has talent to be serviceable in DeVito's old role as the top backup, but things could get hairy if he ends up having to play.
For now, the Patriots will have all three of their quarterbacks on the active roster as the team weighs the options of potentially moving Maye to injured reserve.
"He's on the active roster, so you know, that's where he is today," Vrabel said. "I think those things are obviously fluid, but want to try to give him every opportunity that we can to be back at some point in time. I don't know when that will be, I'm not sure, but also try to manage the roster and do what we need to do to try to win each week."

title: Saints Stock Report: A Dynamic Receiving Duo and an Emerging Defensive Star
full_text:
The New Orleans Saints fell to 3-7 following Sunday's 21-13 loss to the Chicago Bears , as offensive inconsistencies and costly mistakes continue to plague Kellen Moore 's team.
However, despite the team's recurring struggles, a handful of players continue to stand out and give New Orleans reasons to be optimistic moving forward. That may not ultimately determine whether the Saints avoid a full rebuild, but it's still important to recognize the key pieces already in place if the team decides to blow it up and start over.
Here's whose stock is rising following Sunday's loss in Chicago.
While there weren't many positives, Chris Olave and Devaughn Vel e did not have many negatives, if any.
Olave continues to add another strong performance to an already impressive season, catching nine passes on 15 targets for 102 yards, recording his latest 100-yard performance despite facing one of the NFL's better defenses.
The former first-round pick remains the Saints' most dependable offensive weapon and one of the few players consistently producing regardless of the team's struggles.
Vele was equally impressive, catching all seven of his targets for 76 yards, providing Tyler Shough with another reliable option in the passing game as his 6-foot-5 frame makes him a mismatch.
While neither reached the end zone, both receivers repeatedly found ways to get open and move the chains despite Chicago's aggressive defensive approach.
With Olave continuing to establish himself as a legitimate No. 1 receiver and Vele developing into a dependable complementary weapon, New Orleans has two important pieces to build around offensively.
Unfortunately, their production wasn't enough to overcome the team's other shortcomings.
Despite the New Orleans Saints' 21-13 defeat against the Chicago Bears on Sunday, second-year linebacker Danny Stutsman emerged as a major bright spot.
Starting the game, the former Oklahoma standout led the team with nine tackles (including three solo stops) and snagged his first career NFL interception.
Stutsman's marquee moment occurred in the second quarter when he picked off a tipped pass from Caleb Williams at the Chicago 47-yard line. This turnover provided New Orleans a chance to narrow the Bears' 16-7 advantage, though the offense could not capitalize after kicker Charlie Smyth pushed a 47-yard field goal attempt wide.
Additionally, Stutsman played a key role in containing Chicago's ground game, holding their running backs to just 102 yards on 27 carries (a 3.8-yard average).

title: Tom Brady to Saints QB Tyler Shough: 'You Gotta Just Pull the Trigger'
full_text:
The New Orleans Saints dropped to 3-7 and remained in last place in the NFC South following Sunday's 21-13 loss to the Chicago Bears , with rookie quarterback Tyler Shough drawing criticism from seven-time Super Bowl champion Tom Brady for his decision-making.
Shough completed 25 of 42 passes for 222 yards, one touchdown and one interception, while taking six sacks. Although he showed flashes of potential, his hesitation in the pocket and inability to consistently push the ball downfield contributed to another frustrating offensive performance .
During FOX's broadcast on Sunday, Brady scrutinized the rookie's decision-making on a third-quarter play where Shough held the ball despite operating behind one of his cleanest pockets of the game.
Instead of delivering the ball on schedule, Shough hesitated before scrambling out of bounds for minimal gain.
"Got to come out of his hands in less than two and a half seconds, so you're not gonna get more open with that concept as the play goes on," Brady said .
"So that's just one of those ones with him that I see sometimes. Dude, you gotta just pull the trigger, put the play-action fake, pull it out. Again, he's a second-year player, and then just rip the ball to the perimeter, which is how the play is designed."
Tyler Shough scrambles for 1 yard and Tom Brady has some constructive criticism. “Dude you’ve gotta pull the trigger.” pic.twitter.com/DUbnazk7Ar
Brady's analysis highlighted an ongoing problem for Shough: his hesitation in the pocket continues to hamper New Orleans' offensive output.
Over the past three contests, Shough has taken 14 sacks—a stat that underscores both pass-protection failures by the offensive line and the quarterback's habit of holding the ball too long.
A critical second-quarter turnover proved costly when Shough was intercepted by Dillon Thieneman . That mistake gave Chicago strong momentum as they scored on the ensuing drive to go up 16-0.
While Shough played a role in the Saints' lone touchdown via a pass from Alvin Kamara , New Orleans produced a mere six points across their remaining eight drives and failed to reach the end zone again.
Despite throwing a touchdown pass in four straight games, Shough has also given up three interceptions during this four-game span.
Looking ahead to their upcoming game against the Cincinnati Bengals , the Saints need Shough to act on Brady's advice: releasing the ball more quickly and cutting down on the mistakes that repeatedly stall New Orleans' offensive drives.

title: The Good, Bad and Ugly: Saints, Kellen Moore's Offense Hits Another Low Against Bears
full_text:
The New Orleans Saints continue to find new ways to lose football games and just be a complete embarrassment to the sport, and Sunday's 21-13 defeat against the Chicago Bears at Soldier Field was another frustrating example.
Despite a competitive defensive performance and a late comeback attempt, the Saints (3-7) couldn't overcome their offensive mistakes, questionable execution and inability to capitalize on scoring opportunities.
New Orleans finished with 307 total yards, compared to Chicago's 311, but those numbers hardly tell the entire story. Two early turnovers, six sacks allowed and another afternoon of offensive inconsistency ultimately proved too much to overcome.
For head coach Kellen Moore , the loss raises familiar questions about the direction of his offense and whether the Saints are making meaningful progress in his second season.
Here is the good, bad and ugly from New Orleans' latest defeat.
While there weren't many positives, Olave and Vele did not have many negatives, if any.
Olave continues to add another strong performance to an already impressive season, catching nine passes on 15 targets for 102 yards, recording his latest 100-yard performance despite facing one of the NFL's better defenses.
The former first-round pick remains the Saints' most dependable offensive weapon and one of the few players consistently producing regardless of the team's struggles.
Vele was equally impressive, catching all seven of his targets for 76 yards, providing Tyler Shough with another reliable option in the passing game as his 6-foot-5 frame makes him a mismatch.
While neither reached the end zone, both receivers repeatedly found ways to get open and move the chains despite Chicago's aggressive defensive approach.
With Olave continuing to establish himself as a legitimate No. 1 receiver and Vele developing into a dependable complementary weapon, New Orleans has two important pieces to build around offensively.
Unfortunately, their production wasn't enough to overcome the team's other shortcomings.
While he is one of several bright spots on a dreadful team to watch for many New Orleanians, Shough's performance was a mixed bag, but his mistakes ultimately outweighed the positives.
The second-year quarterback completed 25 of 42 passes for 222 yards, one touchdown and one interception while taking six sacks.
Although he had a few highlights such as his 30-yard scramble and connecting with Alvin Kamara for New Orleans' lone touchdown, Shough struggled to consistently move the offense.
His second-quarter interception to Dillon Thieneman enabled Caleb Williams ' 15-yard touchdown pass to Colston Loveland , building a 16-0 Chicago lead. Shough relied primarily on short passes rather than pushing downfield.
Though Chicago's defense constantly pressured him behind weak offensive line protection, Shough's decision-making and key turnover still marred his performance. After their second-quarter touchdown, the Saints managed only six points, failing to score a touchdown on their final eight drives.
The Saints' offensive line was a disaster against Chicago, allowing six sacks for 35 lost yards, including three by Jeffery Simmons .
The worst moment came in the fourth quarter when Montez Sweat sacked Shough in the end zone for a safety, extending Chicago's lead to 21-10.
Injuries, particularly Erik McCoy 's absence, haven't helped, but the constant protection breakdowns remain unacceptable considering how much New Orleans has invested in its offensive line.
Unfortunately, the problems didn't stop there.
New Orleans committed two first-half turnovers, both leading to Chicago touchdowns. Special teams also struggled, with Charlie Smyth missing a 47-yard field goal and sending two kickoffs out of bounds, while Ryan Wright recorded three touchbacks.
Defensively, the Saints had two potential sacks erased by penalties and allowed a third-and-17 conversion.
Even when the defense forced turnovers, the offense couldn't capitalize, failing to score off either takeaway.
Despite being outgained by just four yards (311-307), New Orleans managed only 13 points and one touchdown.
That can’t happen under any circumstance with the game as close as it was.
What makes the loss even more frustrating is that the Saints had opportunities to win. They trailed 16-10 at halftime and held Chicago to just five second-half points, yet repeatedly squandered chances to take control.
While the Saints have a myriad of issues due to bad personnel and injuries, at some point it has to fall on Kellen Moore as he was hired to fix the offense.
However, it’s Groundhog Day for the Saints as the offense keeps stinking up the joint as they have now lost five one-score games this season, highlighting its inability to execute when it matters most.
The Saints aren't losing solely because of a talent disadvantage. They're losing because of turnovers, penalties, poor execution and an inability to capitalize on opportunities.
Now 3-7 with three straight losses, New Orleans has run out of excuses and nobody sees them winning their next two against the Cincinnati Bengals and the Green Bay Packers . I'm not saying they have zero shot at winning, but does anyone think this coaching staff can scheme up a winning game plan?

title: Kellen Moore Addresses Saints' Offensive Struggles After Bears Loss
full_text:
The New Orleans Saints had their opportunities to pull off an upset against one of the NFC's top teams Nov. 22, but the same offensive problems that have plagued them throughout the season proved costly once again.
After the Saints ' 21-13 loss to the Chicago Bears at Soldier Field, head coach Kellen Moore expressed frustration with his team's inability to capitalize on scoring chances, protect the football and execute in critical moments.
New Orleans fell to 3-7 after its offense committed two turnovers, and an injury-riddled offensive line gave up 6 sacks while repeatedly failing to finish drives, despite a defense that kept the game within reach.
The offensive struggles have become an increasingly concerning trend under Moore , particularly the team's inability to start fast. The Saints average just 0.9 points in the first quarter through 10 games, putting them in difficult situations before their offense can establish consistency.
Moore also addressed the team's ongoing ball-security problems, questionable fourth-down decisions, quarterback Tyler Shough 's performance and substitution issues that contributed to wasted timeouts and kept rookie wide receiver Jordyn Tyson off the field for an extended stretch.
"That's the NFL, and that's the frustration with it," Moore said. "I thought we battled. ... We just weren't able to make enough plays to win this football game."
The Saints will look to end their three-game losing streak when they travel to face the Cincinnati Bengals on Sunday, Nov. 29.
Q: The Saints are averaging just 0.9 points per game in the first quarter. Have you tried everything to fix the slow starts?
Moore: "Obviously, it's as frustrating as anything. Again, we're not starting fast. I think we basically had one possession, and we stalled out. We drove it again and then stalled out once we got into plus territory.
"I feel like that's been too common in our opening drives. That's the challenging thing. It's not three-and-outs. It's just being able to finish a drive off."
Q: The offense had several possessions in Bears territory but struggled to capitalize. What's the biggest issue?
Moore: "Again, it's about sustaining drives and giving ourselves the chance to get the points at the end.
"We did have the one turnover on downs where we tried to get the touchdown instead of settling for the field goal. Then we just had some chances that we weren't able to take advantage of."
Q: How frustrating is it knowing the Bears weren't particularly explosive offensively and that a few plays could have changed the outcome?
Moore: "That's the NFL, and that's the frustration with it. I thought we battled. It's a really good offense. For our guys to create a couple turnovers was big, to create some short fields there.
"I thought there was some really good play there. We just weren't able to make enough plays to win this football game."
Q: The Saints have lost 23 fumbles since last season, the most in the NFL. Why has protecting the football remained such a persistent problem?
Moore: "Obviously, the disappointing part of it is just the fundamentals of protecting the football.
"The one that happened today was a catch-tuck, and they beat us to it before we could secure the football. They did a better job than us on that down. Obviously, we had the one interception after our own first down."
Q: What did you make of Tyler Shough's performance overall?
Moore: "I think he battled. Obviously, there are going to be things that we're going to have to look at, correct and improve as an offense. Ultimately, 13 points isn't enough to beat these guys."
Q: Do you think Shough has taken a step backward, and has the constant shuffling along the offensive line affected his decision-making?
Moore: "I think ultimately, collectively, we all want to play better football and coach better football. We have to do this thing together.
"Again, Tyler's battling. He gave us an opportunity to get back into that. He got us back down for a field goal opportunity for Charlie to kick that, and then we're down to one possession.
"That game wasn't without opportunities to make some plays. We just didn't get it done."
Q: What happened on Shough's interception?
Moore: "I'll have to look at it again more closely. Obviously, the safety came off. In the scramble phase, we've got to keep running our routes and give ourselves an opportunity so that guy doesn't have a chance to peel back.
"I did not see, based on where I was, where the location of the ball ended up. Obviously, a frustrating one for all of us."
Q: Did Shough need to get rid of the football quicker on the safety?
Moore: "We should be helping the right tackle on that play, and obviously, we just didn't execute it. The edge rusher had the angle."
Q: Was there supposed to be someone helping the right tackle with a chip block?
Moore: "There should be a chipper there, yes."
Q: Was that a missed assignment?
Moore: "No. Jordyn ran the route and didn't do the initial protection element of it. Chip, then run your route."
Q: What did you think about Shough's decision-making on the safety?
Moore: "Obviously, I don't think he's anticipating the edge rusher to be there that quickly. I felt like we'd have some presence there to be able to work through the progression.
"I think if we give ourselves just a touch more time, he's going to have a completion over the ball."
Q: Why did Tyson go approximately 12 consecutive snaps without playing? Was that related to his workload?
Moore: "Just the sequencing of those personnel groups. Again, I've got to do a better job of getting him in there on a few more of those occasions.
"We stayed on the ball a few times and tried to keep certain personnel groups on defense so we could execute some plays. That kind of kept Jordyn off on a few occasions."
Q: Was his absence related to the missed chip block or some form of punishment?
Moore: "No. We had a couple substitutions where we had Bryce and Barry in there for specific plays.
"Once we get into tempo, sometimes we're keeping those guys on the field so we don't allow them to substitute and get to some of their packages."
Q: Were those substitutions predetermined or based on the flow of the game?
Moore: "A lot of it's predetermined."
Q: What went well on Travis Etienne's 46-yard run?
Moore: "Obviously, I'll have to review it from a film perspective. I think being able to capture the edge was an important part, and him being able to get to the edge and make a play was important for us. We needed something like that."
Q: Why wasn't Etienne more involved during the first two offensive possessions?
Moore: "Just the flow of the sequencing there. Again, trying to get completions early based on the hashes and the direction in which we wanted to attack them.
"We probably didn't have as many run opportunities those first two drives, but I think he got in there the rest of the way."
Q: Did you consider kicking a field goal instead of going for it on fourth down late in the game?
Moore: "Yes. We obviously discussed it very briefly. Ultimately, we were going to need a touchdown. We felt like we were down there. It's third-and-two, fourth-and-two. We had an opportunity to get the touchdown at some point.
"It's also an 11-point game at that point, so you're going to have to have a two-point conversion as well. We felt like trying to score there and gather as much information as we could was important."
Q: Did analytics influence that decision?
Q: There appeared to be several issues with offensive substitutions. What happened?
Moore: "There were just some receiver substitutions. I've obviously got to do a better job of making sure we have cleaner communication there. We had to use a couple timeouts."
Q: How frustrating was it to lose timeouts because of a failed challenge and substitution problems?
Moore: "It puts you in a goofy spot at the end of the game because you're not going to have all the timeouts at the end.
"Obviously, we had some situations we've got to do better…

title: Saints Can't Get Out of Their Own Way in Disappointing Loss to Bears
full_text:
The New Orleans Saints ' offensive struggles and inability to protect the football proved costly once again Sunday afternoon.
Despite a strong defensive effort and a late comeback attempt, the Saints couldn't overcome two early turnovers, six sacks and missed scoring opportunities in a frustrating 21-13 loss to the Chicago Bears at Soldier Field.
The loss marks three straight for New Orleans and drops the Saints to 3-7, while Chicago improved to 8-2 with its fifth straight win.
The Saints finished with 307 total yards compared to Chicago's 311, but failed to score a touchdown on their final eight possessions, showcasing the Saints' inability to capitalize on the opportunities given to them, a criticism that head coach Kellen Moore has faced all season.
After a slow start by both teams, things deteriorated for New Orleans. Its second-quarter run game faltered when running back CJ Donaldson fumbled, giving Chicago excellent field position. That allowed the Bears to strike as Caleb Williams with a 3-yard touchdown pass to D'Andre Swift , extending the Bears' lead to 10-0.
Chicago got the ball back after quarterback Tyler Shough threw an interception to rookie safety Dillon Thieneman , and Williams connected with tight end Colston Loveland for a 15-yard strike to give the Bears a commanding 16-0 advantage.
New Orleans did finally show signs of life late in the first half.
Running back Travis Etienne Jr. broke free for a 46-yard run, setting up Shough's 1-yard touchdown pass to Alvin Kamara on fourth-and-goal to cut the deficit to nine.
The Saints defense then got another chance when linebacker Danny Stutsman intercepted Williams after a deflected pass. However, New Orleans’ special teams woes returned midway through the quarter as kicker Charlie Smyth missed a 47-yard field goal.
However, Smyth redeemed himself with a 56-yard field goal as time expired in the first half, cutting Chicago's lead to 16-10.
New Orleans couldn't build on that momentum.
The Bears extended their lead to 19-10 on Santos' third-quarter field goal before their defensive front took control and bullied the Saints' injury-depleted offensive line.
Chicago recorded six sacks, including three from defensive tackle Jeffery Simmons . Montez Sweat delivered one of the game's biggest plays in the fourth quarter, sacking Shough in the end zone for a safety that extended the Bears' advantage to 21-10.
The Saints had another opportunity after Julian Blackmon recovered a Swift fumble, but their ensuing possession stalled on fourth down at Chicago's 10-yard line.
Shough finished 25 of 42 for 222 yards, one touchdown and one interception. Chris Olave led New Orleans with nine receptions for 102 yards, while Devaughn Vele added seven catches for 76 yards.
Smyth connected on a 51-yard field goal with 1:10 remaining, but Chicago recovered the ensuing onside kick to seal the victory.
New Orleans now turns its attention to next Sunday's road matchup against the Cincinnati Bengals , looking to avoid another disappointing result in a season rapidly slipping away.

title: Three Keys to Victory: Can the Saints Upset the Bears?
full_text:
The New Orleans Saints face an uphill battle Sunday when they travel to Soldier Field to take on the Chicago Bears in a matchup between two teams heading in opposite directions.
Coming off another disappointing loss to the Carolina Panthers , the Saints (3-6) are looking to bounce back against a Chicago team (7-2) that has emerged as one of the NFC's top contenders.
However, pulling off an upset won't be easy for head coach Kellen Moore 's squad, especially against a Bears offense averaging nearly 27 points per game and a defense that ranks among the league's best .
For New Orleans to have any chance of leaving Chicago with a victory, it must eliminate the costly mistakes that have plagued it throughout the season while finding a way to slow down Caleb Williams and the Bears' explosive offense.
Here are three keys to victory for the Saints against the Bears.
This is a major necessity for the Saints.
New Orleans has 17 turnovers (tied for 27th in the NFL) and a minus-8 differential (29th). As great as Tyler Shough has been for the Saints, his seven interceptions and four lost fumbles have repeatedly put the Saints in tough spots.
Chicago also has 17 turnovers, including four interceptions from Williams against Tampa Bay. This gives the Saints defense an opportunity, with just nine takeaways (tied for 24th) and none in three games. Forcing turnovers can lead to great opportunities to put points on the board.
However, forcing turnovers requires the offense to capitalize, something New Orleans has struggled with all season.
The Saints have only scored nine first-quarter points through nine games (literally a point per quarter) and have gone scoreless in seven opening quarters. That will not work against a Chicago team averaging nearly 27 points per game. Moore's offense needs faster starts, fewer penalties, and touchdowns instead of field goals.
Do that, and the Saints’ chances of pulling off an upset get a little higher.
The Saints' defense faces a daunting task in slowing down one of the league's most potent offensive units.
Chicago's offense features top-tier production across the board: seventh in scoring (26.8 points per game), seventh in total yards (383.0 per game), and fourth on the ground (142.0 rushing yards per game).
Behind Caleb Williams, who has powered the Bears to four straight wins since returning from a hamstring injury, Chicago has put up 27 points or more in every game of that streak.
Given New Orleans' vulnerability against the pass, keeping Williams from finding a rhythm in the pocket is critical.
The Saints currently rank near the bottom of the league defensively—21st against the pass (231.0 yards per game allowed) and 29th overall (360.8 total yards per game allowed).
Defensive coordinator Brandon Staley needs to dial up pressure to disrupt Williams while keeping him contained inside the pocket to limit playmaking on the run.
Much of that pressure must come from edge rushers Carl Granderson and Chase Young , who have logged a combined 16.5 sacks on the season.
However, pressuring Williams is only part of the equation.
The Saints must also slow down a rushing attack that averages 142 yards per game, fourth-best in the NFL.
Running back D'Andre Swift leads Chicago with 576 rushing yards and 10 touchdowns, while Kyle Monangai averages 5.4 yards per carry with 324 yards and three touchdowns.
That does not bode well for a team ranked 27th in run defense, allowing nearly 130 rushing yards per game.
New Orleans has shown improvement against the run over its past two games, holding Cleveland to 95 yards and Carolina to 97.
Linebacker Kaden Elliss will be particularly important after recording 26 tackles and two sacks over those two contests.
If the Saints can limit Chicago's rushing attack and force Williams into obvious passing situations, they'll have a better opportunity to generate pressure and create turnovers.
Allowing the Bears to establish their running game would make an already difficult matchup even more challenging.
