title: Saints vs. Bears: Staff Picks and Score Predictions for Sunday
full_text:
The New Orleans Saints (3-6) face another difficult challenge Sunday when they travel to Soldier Field to take on the Chicago Bears (7-2).
Coming off a disappointing loss to the Carolina Panthers , the Saints continue to struggle with offensive consistency and finishing games under head coach Kellen Moore.
Those problems could prove costly against a well-rounded Chicago team that boasts one of the NFL's most productive offenses and a top-10 defense.
Can the Saints pull off an unlikely upset, or will their struggles continue against one of the NFC's top contenders?
Here's how our staff predicts Sunday's matchup will unfold.
This is a game that doesn’t favor the Saints.
The Bears are by far the best team the Saints have faced since the Detroit Lions , who beat New Orleans in overtime. They have one of the league’s best offenses , led by quarterback Caleb Williams , and one of the league's most balanced teams.
Defensively, the Bears have a top-10 defense.
Chicago boasts a top-10 defense, ranking eighth in scoring (20.4 PPG) and seventh in total defense (310.9 YPG). Their strength lies against the run, allowing 91.1 yards per game (seventh-fewest), while placing 15th against the pass (219.8 YPG).
Crucially, the Bears lead the NFL in third-down defense (22.8% conversion rate allowed) and rank 12th in red-zone touchdown efficiency (53.8%). They maintain consistent pass pressure with 26 sacks (ninth) and seven interceptions (tied for 11th).
Also, this will be the first cold-weather game for the Saints as the temperature will be in the 50s throughout the game.
I don’t think the Saints will pull off the upset, but what I do know is that the Saints have played better on the road as both of their wins came on the road against the Baltimore Ravens and New York Giants . I do think its defense will do enough to make this game tight before Chicago pulls away near the end.
This is a Saints team that seems to be searching, searching for an identity, a consistent offense, people on the same page.
The New Orleans offense sputters and coughs more than my old 1969 VW Beetle. No matter what I would do to that little air-cooled engine, it never could quite get started, and when it did, it usually took a few minutes of driving before it would get going smoothly. Once it was warmed up, that little thing was a joy to drive. Unfortunately, it took a while to even get to that point.
The Saints O reminds me of that Beetle.
They can't seem to get going in the beginning. Once they get warmed up and going, they are fun to watch. Until then, it's almost torturous to be a part of.
Eventually, I had to get rid of that little car. Keeping the valves aligned properly on that rapidly expanding air-cooled engine proved to be one of those "I'll be doing this forever" kind of projects, so I just gave up and moved on.
The New Orleans offense is at that point, in my opinion. A squad that cannot consistently move the ball, stopping and starting itself with poor run blocking, or wide receivers and a quarterback who aren't on the same page, or play calling that comes across as vanilla as can be (think runs in the middle).
Now, Brandon Staley's group is another story, another car if you will. They remind me of a Tesla. The Saints defense can really get going with the first acceleration, but fade at the end.
A battery-powered Tesla is a lot like that. They can fly right out the gate and tear the street up, but don't expect that to last, as those batteries won't go 300-plus miles (no matter what they say) like a gas-power engine will, losing energy much sooner than their gas counterparts.
This Saints defense has produced through the first three quarters, especially for the last few games. Although getting turnovers has been a notable absence for this group, it has played well, up until the final quarter. To wit, the Panthers' game.
I say all that to say this: you cannot do any of what the offense and defense has been doing against a quality team. The Panthers, Browns, and Steelers were not quality teams. This Bears team is.
It will take a complete game, start to finish, for this Saints team to have a chance to beat Chicago. The local boys haven't done that all year long.

full_text:
The New Orleans Saints (3-6) face one of their toughest defensive tests of the season Sunday when they travel to Soldier Field to take on the Chicago Bears (7-2).
In his second season as Chicago's head coach, Ben Johnson has established one of the NFL's most productive and balanced offenses, ranking seventh in scoring and total offense and fourth in rushing offense.
Between quarterback Caleb Williams ' playmaking ability, a talented backfield tandem featuring D'Andre Swift and Kyle Monangai , and an emerging star in wide receiver Luther Burden III, the Bears have no shortage of offensive weapons.
Considering New Orleans' offensive struggles, Brandon Staley 's defense will have little margin for error if the Saints hope to pull off an upset.
Here is a statistical breakdown of Chicago's offense and three players the Saints must account for Sunday.
Through Week 10 of the 2026 NFL season; NFL rankings in parentheses.
QB Caleb Williams (1,546 passing yards, eight touchdowns, five interceptions)
RB D'Andre Swift (576 rushing yards, 10 touchdowns)
RB Kyle Monanagai: 60 carries for 324 yards (5.4 yards per carry) and three touchdowns
WR Luther Burden III: 644 receiving yards, four touchdowns
WR Rome Odunze: 32 catches for 328 yards and a touchdown

Despite missing three games earlier in the season with a hamstring injury, Williams has completed 68.7% of his passes for 1,546 yards, eight touchdowns and five interceptions in six games. He has also rushed for 145 yards and two touchdowns.
The former No. 1 overall pick's arm talent, mobility and ability to extend plays outside the pocket present a significant challenge for New Orleans.
While Chase Young, Carl Granderson and the Saints' defensive front must consistently generate pressure, maintaining disciplined rush lanes to contain Williams will be just as important to keep Williams from escaping the pocket and creating explosive plays downfield.
Swift serves as one of Chicago's primary offensive engines, driving both the ground attack and contributing significantly through the air.
Through Week 10, Swift has rushed for 576 yards and 10 touchdowns on 155 carries, alongside 24 receptions for 162 yards. Despite averaging 3.7 yards per carry, his high-volume scoring efficiency makes him critical to Chicago's offensive consistency.
Paired with Kyle Monangai, Swift forms a versatile backfield rotation designed to control game tempo and keep down-and-distance manageable.
To stay competitive, the Saints defense must disrupt this backfield early and prevent Chicago from establishing a sustained rushing rhythm.
In his second NFL season, the former Missouri standout has established himself as Chicago's top receiving threat, securing 49 catches for 644 yards (13.1 yards per reception) and four touchdowns.
Clearing concussion protocol on Tuesday, Burden delivers a major boost to the Bears' receiving group ahead of Sunday's game. His downfield separation, run-after-catch dynamic, and adaptability in Johnson's offensive system present a tough defensive assignment.
With cornerback Martin Emerson Jr . dealing with a concussion and the Saints releasing safety Justin Reid this week , New Orleans' secondary will face a considerable test against Burden and Chicago's talented receiving corps.

title: Giants Refuse to Overlook Depleted Colts: 4 Storylines to Watch This Week
full_text:
On paper, the upcoming matchup between the New York Giants and the Indianapolis Colts suggests this week should be a cakewalk for the Giants.
The Colts have unloaded several key players, including guard Quenton Nelson, receivers Josh Downs and Keenan Allen and defensive lineman DeForest Buckner. They have also moved on from quarterback Daniel Jones and plan to start Anthony Richardson Sr. this week.
But that's not how the Giants are viewing the matchup.
"We know we're going to get the Colts' best this Sunday. They're not going to go out there and not play hard," said right tackle Jermaine Eluemunor.
"They're going to play as hard as they possibly can, especially with the gravity of the game for us, but then also, we're in first place. I'm sure they're saying in their locker room, 'Let's go out there and beat the first-place team of the NFC East and see what we can do.' We're going to take that, go in there and play as hard as we can."
And, of course, hope that they come out with a victory.
Now for this week's storylines.
Once again, a key starter has been claimed by the injury bug. This time it's cornerback Greg Newsome II. He suffered a high ankle sprain in Sunday's win over the Jaguars and had TightRope surgery to speed his recovery. He will miss at least four weeks.
The Giants have been relatively lucky with the next man up keeping the team afloat:
The Giants have been relatively lucky when it comes to the next man up keeping the team above water.
Jameis Winton stepped in for Jaxson Dart at cornerback, Kayvon Thibodeaux has stepped into a bigger role at outside linebacker following the ACL injury suffered by Brian Burns, Micah McFadden has been mostly solid after the team lost inside linebacker Tremaine Edmunds, and Dawaune Smoot and Trace Ford have both done well to fill the voids left by Roy Robertson-Harris and Chauncey Golston on the defensive line.
Paulson Adebo is set to fill Newsome's spot. Adebo played well on Sunday after Newsome's early exit, and the hope is that he can rise to the challenge.
The Giants are tied with the Green Bay Packers for second in the league with 18 fumbles, one fewer than the Los Angeles Chargers. Running back Cam Skattebo has five of them. That ties him for seventh among all offensive players and for first among running backs, alongside Colts running back Jonathan Taylor.
A big part of the problem appears to be that Skattebo seeks contact. That's all well and good, but in some situations a running back is better off avoiding contact that puts the ball in harm's way.
It would be surprising for the Giants to repeat the "quasi-benching" of Skattebo they handed him in Week 6 against the Saints. Still, this carelessness with the ball in traffic can't continue.
You could argue that Dominic Zvada's missed 32-yard field goal was actually good, and to our eyes it looked that way. But that's irrelevant.
What is relevant is that Zvada needs to get back to his early-season form, when his kicks were stress-free no matter which hash they came from.
The Giants' offense was meant to be powered by its running game, but that hasn't always been the case.
New York ranks 24th in the league at 3.8 yards per rushing attempt. When it comes to closing out games in the fourth quarter, the Giants average only 3.4 yards per attempt, which ranks 23rd.
They are also tied for third in the league with two fourth-quarter fumbles, one of which was lost. Their 13 rushing first downs in the fourth quarter tie them for 26th in the league.
In short, those aren't glowing numbers. They may help explain why the Giants have just a plus-6 point differential in the fourth quarter, and why head coach John Harbaugh is believed to want to add to the running back room at some point.

title: Giants' Abdul Carter Named NFC Defensive Player of the Week After Dominating Jaguars
full_text:
New York Giants linebacker Abdul Carter entered Week 11 of the 2026 NFL season on a mission.
The No. 3 overall pick in the 2025 NFL Draft knew the odds were stacked against Big Blue in its quest to topple the AFC South-leading Jacksonville Jaguars in their nationally televised showdown at MetLife Stadium.
Fortunately for Giants Nation, the 23-year-old delivered his best performance of the season, helping the club to a 23-18 victory over Jacksonville last Sunday in East Rutherford. He finished the game with four total tackles, two sacks, two tackles for loss, five quarterback hits and 12 pressures, the second-most by any player in a game this season.
For his efforts, Carter has been named the NFC Defensive Player of the Week for Week 11. It's the first time he has earned the honor in his career.
You already know 🔥 pic.twitter.com/JJQNJoVU2Z
Carter noticed that national pundits overwhelmingly picked the Jaguars to hand New York its fourth loss of the season. He treated the matchup as a chance to earn respect and to prove how good the Giants' defense is.
"Yeah, we heard everybody pretty much counted us out, that we pretty much had no chance, that we couldn't stick with their offense," Carter said from his postgame podium. "But we took that as disrespect, and we came out with a chip on our shoulder."
Despite a statistically slow start to the season, Carter has remained one of the Giants' most important defenders. Under defensive coordinator Dennard Wilson, the club has adopted a pass-rush style built on blitz pressure.
Since team captain Brian Burns suffered a season-ending ACL injury, the unit has been much more effective with schemed pressures. Carter, along with fellow linebackers Kayvon Thibodeaux and first-year phenom Arvell Reese , has helped champion that cause.
Still, the 2025 All-Rookie linebacker knew the Giants' defensive success in Week 11 depended as much on stopping the run as on making life uncomfortable for Jaguars quarterback Trevor Lawrence. The Giants held Jacksonville's rushing attack to just 77 yards, and seven of those came from Lawrence himself.
"Yeah, I think they had 70 rushing in total," Carter recalled. "Like I always say, if they can't run, they can't win. That's what we did today."
In his 10 starts this season, Carter has compiled 26 total tackles (five for loss), 13 quarterback hits, four sacks and one forced fumble, combining speed and power in a unique but effective way.
His athleticism and instincts routinely let him be a consistent, disruptive force against opposing quarterbacks, which only increases his value to New York's defense.
He also becomes the third member of Big Blue's defense to win the award this season. The Penn State product joins Reese (Week 9) and cornerback Deonte Banks (Week 4).
The last time New York had at least three Defensive Player of the Week winners in a season was in 2016. That year, safety Landon Collins (twice), defensive end Jason Pierre-Paul and cornerback Dominique Rodgers-Cromartie won the award, per Giants.com.
The Giants have also produced two NFC Players of the Month. Safety Jevón Holland was named the conference's top defensive player for September, and receiver Malik Nabers took home the offensive honor for October.
Reese continues to draw consideration for NFC Rookie of the Year and has been voted Pepsi Rookie of the Week twice this season.
As the Giants move into Week 12, coach John Harbaugh understands that their toughest tests may still lie ahead. Their victory over the favored Jaguars still shows that Big Blue deserves to be mentioned among the NFL's top-tier teams.
If any doubt remains, expect Carter to keep New York playing at its highest level.

title: Giants Refuse to Overlook Struggling Colts in Would-Be 'Revenge Bowl'
full_text:
Just think: Sunday's game between the New York Giants and Indianapolis Colts could very well have been the "Revenge Bowl" had the Colts traded running back Jonathan Taylor to the Giants and retained former Giants quarterback Daniel Jones.
As we know by now, neither happened, which for some might take a little of the luster off a game in which the Giants are heavily favored despite being the road team.
But that doesn't make the game any less important for Big Blue in its quest to keep more than just a little elbow room between itself and the rest of the NFC East.
"I think you go into every week trying to win the game," Giants right tackle Jermaine Eluemunor said when asked whether talk of this being a "must-win" game has infiltrated the locker room.
"No game is different than last week. You don't treat the Colts any differently than you would treat the Jags. You don't treat the Colts any differently than you would treat the Niners, or the Vikings, or the Bears. Every game in the NFL is hard to win."
In some ways, the Colts should be a gimme game for the 6-3-1 Giants, who are playing some of their best ball in years under new head coach John Harbaugh.
Indianapolis stands at 3-8 and, from the outside looking in, is a rudderless ship after firing general manager Chris Ballard and trading away guard Quenton Nelson, receivers Josh Downs and Keenan Allen, and defensive lineman DeForest Buckner.
But this is the NFL, a league where anything and everything goes. And that's one of the messages Harbaugh is undoubtedly reinforcing this week.
"I think that the notion of games you're supposed to win versus games you're supposed to lose, or teams are supposed to blow you out. I think that's just blown out of proportion, because at the end of the day, you're going against guys that are trying to put food on their table just like us, and they want to win," Eluemunor said.
"I've been in that position before where the season is not going as good as you want it to go. You have a losing record. You don't really have (anything) to look forward to postseason, but you're still going to go out there and play your tail off and try to win the game, because that's how much it means to you."
So will the Colts surprise the Giants on their home field, or is this just a case of players like Eluemunor saying the right things to avoid giving anyone bulletin-board material?
Despite their lead in the NFC East, the Giants can't afford to look past anyone, and how they handle this week will be another measure of their growth and maturation under Harbaugh.

title: Giants Back on the Rise in MMQB Power Rankings After Jaguars Upset
full_text:
For the entire week leading up to their matchup with the Jacksonville Jaguars at MetLife Stadium, all the New York Giants heard was how little chance they had of hanging around with, let alone defeating, one of the best-assembled rosters in the NFL.
Of course, most of those opinions had grown louder after their fourth-quarter collapse against the Commanders the week before, when they had numerous chances off timely turnovers to shut the door on their rival's rally but fell short.
What sets the John Harbaugh version of the Giants apart is their attitude: they don't let one game's result dictate what happens next. They felt disrespected by all the negative chatter and emphatically quieted it with a 23-18 win over the Jaguars, putting them back in firm control of the NFC East.
Big Blue's latest showing, which improved the team to 6-3-1, was enough for SI senior writer Conor Orr to move them up two spots to No. 13 in his newest MMQB NFL power rankings ahead of Week 12.
Orr is hardly the only writer back to spreading good vibes about the Giants after their statement win against an elite foe. Still, given how the rest of the weekend's results unfolded, it might be too early to start planning a rare postseason game in East Rutherford.
Sunday's win moved the Giants closer to sealing their first playoff berth in four seasons and their first division crown since 2011.
Very few Giants fans would trade the start New York has put together under Harbaugh, which includes answering serious doubts in games against the Dallas Cowboys, the Houston Texans and, most recently, the previously red-hot Jaguars.
All the talk heading into Sunday was that the Giants had to steal at least one of their next four games against playoff-caliber opponents from both conferences to stack enough wins and leave no room for the Cowboys or Commanders to catch them down the stretch.
They did that by beating Jacksonville, which renewed confidence in their chances in upcoming games against the 49ers, Seahawks and Lions. However, the win only partially made up for the utter mishap of falling to Washington and losing the all-important head-to-head tiebreaker.
The Giants avoided losing more ground this past week, but it was also a good week for their division rivals. The Cowboys dropped 51 points on the lowly Titans, and the Commanders eked out another last-second win over the Bengals on Monday night.
Many Giants fans might be focused on the schedule battle between their team and Dallas, but the bigger concern should be the Commanders. Washington sits in third place at 4-5-1 but has the easiest four-game stretch of the three, with matchups against the Cardinals, Titans, Texans and Falcons, all of whom are below .500.
If the Commanders keep winning, the NFC East could turn into a three-team race. That isn't the ideal scenario for the Giants, who have the league's eighth-toughest remaining schedule , the hardest of the three contenders.
As they move on from the Jaguars win and prepare for a road game against the Indianapolis Colts, Harbaugh and his players have never needed a short memory more.
Their ultimate quest is far from over. They've rebounded twice from unfathomable losses, but things could change quickly in the coming weeks if they leave the door open and don't stay focused on playing their best football one game at a time.

title: Is the Third Time the Charm for Eli Manning's Hall of Fame Case?
full_text:
Is the third time the charm? The Eli Manning Hall of Fame debate is picking back up, as the New York Giants legend is one of 52 players to advance to the next stage of the voting process.
The selection committee will trim that list to 25 semifinalists when it next casts its ballots, and Manning will likely be part of that exclusive group. But will he get a gold jacket in 2027?
The two-time Super Bowl MVP was denied entry into Canton in each of his first two years of eligibility. Now he'll have to contend with newcomers Ben Roethlisberger, Rob Gronkowski, Adrian Peterson, Richard Sherman and Antonio Brown. The competition is stiff.
Manning's chances are still murky, but a bust will eventually be made for No. 10. He threw two of the most iconic passes in NFL history, helping the Giants defeat the dynastic New England Patriots in Super Bowls XLII and XLVI.
Yes, his regular-season numbers are rather pedestrian, with a 60.3% completion rate and 244 interceptions. But he cleared 4,000 passing yards seven times and threw 27 or more touchdown passes five times. He was also an iron man, logging 210 consecutive starts before his controversial benching in 2017.
Still, Manning's most vocal Hall of Fame supporters will emphasize his playoff heroics. The No. 1 overall pick in the 2004 NFL Draft, whom the late Ernie Accorsi acquired in a trade with the then-San Diego Chargers, raised his game when it mattered most.
Manning is best remembered for the magic trick he pulled off in Super Bowl XLII, escaping a sack and launching the ball to David Tyree, who pinned it against his helmet. But his most impressive achievement came four years later.
He was fantastic in the 2011 postseason, throwing for 1,219 yards and nine touchdowns with just one interception across an unforgettable four-game run. Manning then willed the Giants past Tom Brady, Bill Belichick and the Patriots once more, perfectly placing a 38-yard pass along the sideline to Mario Manningham.
The historical importance of those moments, combined with his entire body of work, will be enough to earn him enshrinement. It just may not happen next year. Manning has kept his composure throughout the process, taking his rejections in stride , and he has plenty to keep himself busy.
It would be fitting if he got the call this time around, though. Manning's induction into the Pro Football Hall of Fame in the same year as a potential Giants resurgence would be poetic.
We'll see just how much the voters appreciate a good story.

title: From Healthy Scratch to Starter: Paulson Adebo Says He Was Ready All Along
full_text:
After losing his starting job this summer and then suffering an injury that landed him on short-term IR, New York Giants cornerback Paulson Adebo knew his time would come this season.
That time is now, as head coach John Harbaugh and the rest of the team are counting on Adebo to step in as a starter after the high ankle sprain suffered by Greg Newsome II, which will require surgery and keep Newsome sidelined for multiple weeks.
Adebo, for his part, is ready. In fact, he's been ready all along.
"I know what type of player I am. I know what I can do on the field. I know what type of person I am," Adebo told reporters during a video call on Tuesday when asked if he's learned anything new about himself based on the experiences he's gone through.
"I don't think it's anything new necessarily that I've learned about myself, but certainly just staying prepared and ready to go when you're called upon."
Adebo, currently the holder of the highest cap hit on the Giants' roster, has given Harbaugh and defensive coordinator Dennard Wilson enough reason to keep faith in him should an opportunity arise for him to play a larger role on the Giants' defense.
After returning from IR, Adebo started the Giants' Week 7 win over the Houston Texans with Newsome sidelined by a concussion. He finished the game with two tackles and a tackle for loss.
The following week against the Philadelphia Eagles, Adebo was limited to special teams. Then against the Washington Commanders, he was a healthy scratch, something he chalked up to the team needing more volume in other spots on the roster.
He was back in uniform for the Jacksonville game, and it was a good thing, as Newsome went down early in the first quarter. Adebo stepped in and earned a game ball after posting a career-high four passes defensed in the Giants' 23-18 win.
For Adebo, it was never about having a bruised ego as much as it was about being ready for whatever was asked of him, which is why he continued preparing as though he were going to start.
"You just do it," he said about pushing through the disappointment. "If you're the third guy, you're one play away from going in every single game, so you owe it to yourself, and you owe it to your teammates to be prepared."

title: Giants' Abdul Carter's Most Dangerous Trait Puts Him in Rare Company
full_text:
New York Giants offensive tackle Jermaine Eluemunor has been around for 10 seasons now and has gone up against some of the league's best edge rushers.
As far as Eluemunor is concerned, one guy making his way into the discussion about the league's best edge rushers is his young teammate, Abdul Carter, who Eluemunor says has a special trait that not many of the league's edge defenders offer.
"It's that get-off," Eluemunor said Tuesday on a video call with reporters when asked what sets Carter apart.
"There's a lot of guys in the NFL that are really talented but don't have that get-off, just anticipating the snap count, but then also being able to have that get-off.
"And because there's a lot of guys that jump the snap count, but they don't have that first explosiveness step that he has — that explosive step that he has is really rare in this league."
“Only a few guys have it—(Packers OLB) Micah Parsons, (Rams edge) Myles (Garrett), and (Texans OLB) Will Anderson —and those are three of the best in the NFL."
That explosive first step has certainly served Carter, the second-year outside linebacker out of Penn State, well. Before the Week 11 game against the Jacksonville Jaguars, 17 of Carter's 28 quarterback pressures were generated in under 2.5 seconds.
That 60.7% rate was the highest share of quick pressures among edge rushers with at least 25 pressures, according to NFL+.
In the Week 11 win, Carter turned in an astonishing 12 pressures, the second-most by a player in a game this season.
He also recorded two of the team's three sacks (doubling his season sack total and registering the first multi-sack game of his career), along with two tackles for loss and five hits on the quarterback among his 12 pressures.
Currently, Carter is tied with Miami's Chop Robinson for second with 23 quick pressures (under 2.5 seconds), one quick pressure shy of league leader Nik Bonitto of the Broncos.
The scary thing about Carter, who aspires to, in his words, "be the best in the world," is that he's just getting started.
"He can anticipate the snap count, but then he also has that explosiveness to help with that," Eluemunor said. "Then also his mindset — he thinks he's the best and he's gonna start playing like that."
When he does, good luck to whoever is assigned to slow him down.

title: Greg Newsome II Facing Surgery, Lengthy Absence for Giants Secondary
full_text:
The New York Giants ’ seventh-ranked defense just suffered another significant blow to one of its key players.
Cornerback Greg Newsome II, who signed a three-year, $46 million contract extension coming out of the team’s bye week, suffered what head coach John Harbaugh described as a “serious high ankle” sprain that “is going to be one of those lengthy high ankles” that will keep the starting cornerback out for “multiple weeks.”
That timeline now looks like it will sideline Newsome for most, if not all, of the rest of the regular season. NFL insider Jordan Schultz reported that Newsome will undergo tightrope surgery this week to address the high ankle sprain he suffered in the first quarter of the team’s 23-18 win over the Jacksonville Jaguars on Sunday.
Schultz added that Newsome will be out approximately four to six weeks, which, if things go well, could mean he’s back for the postseason if the Giants, who currently sit atop the NFC East, qualify.
It’s a significant blow for the Giants’ defensive secondary, which has been a major surprise given how well it has played.
The Giants’ pass defense is currently ranked fifth in the league, allowing 193.4 yards through the air per game, and it’s ranked second in average passing yards per play allowed (5.81).
Newsome has certainly been a big part of that success. He has five pass breakups and one interception in coverage and has not allowed a touchdown yet this season.
Per PFF, he has the second-best coverage grade among the team’s cornerbacks (71.2) behind Deonte Banks, and the NFL’s best coverage rating (41.8).
With Newsome sidelined, Paulson Adebo, who lost his starting job this summer in the battle with Newsome and Banks, will step in as the starter. Stepping in for Newsome early in Sunday’s game, Adebo posted a career-high four pass breakups in the win over the Jaguars.
“He’s got to be ready,” Harbaugh said of Adebo last week. “I told him, ‘In my mind, you’re a starter in this league. And when you started here, you’ve done really well. And you’re going to have to start again.’ So when that time comes, he’s in a good place.”
To increase their depth at the position, the Giants are also expected to open the 21-day practice window this week for cornerback Korie Black, who has been on IR since the start of this season.

title: Giants vs. Colts Week 12 Odds: New York Opens as Road Favorite
full_text:
New York Giants head coach John Harbaugh deserves a lot of praise for how he has handled his first season with the franchise. If one thing stands out in particular, it's how he rallies his players to respond to ugly losses and turn them into statement victories.
That is what happened once again on Sunday, when the Giants rebounded from a collapse against the Commanders in Week 10 to defensively throttle the Jacksonville Jaguars, 23-18, in arguably their most impressive win of the campaign.
Now at 6-3-1, the Giants have created a little extra space in the NFC East standings and finally earned some serious respect from the oddsmakers in Vegas. Ahead of Week 12, FanDuel Sportsbook has opened the Giants as 6.5-point road favorites for their trip to face the Indianapolis Colts.
That opening line is the largest road spread oddsmakers have given the Giants this season, and it's the second time in three weeks they've been favored. The team continues to fight to preserve its lead in the division race and prove it can compete with some of the teams it could face if it makes the postseason dance.
Really, this week's matchup offers the Giants a chance to finally be viewed as the top dog, while the Colts, at 3-8, have seen their season go in the opposite direction, with an inevitable rebuild looming in the offseason.
Given the paths both franchises have taken, the Giants carry a lot of pressure to win this game if they want to maintain their pace and keep the outside world's faith that they are a playoff-caliber team.
If one player on the Indianapolis roster could still stand in the way, it's Colts running back Jonathan Taylor, who was one of the biggest subjects of trade talk ahead of the November 10 deadline.
Harbaugh was among the most aggressive pursuers of the All-Pro ball carrier, as he wanted to land a true bellcow back to upgrade a Giants ground game that was struggling to produce.
The Giants' offer, which reportedly included a second-round pick and a fifth-round pick, wasn't enough to convince the Colts to move on from arguably their best player, whom they viewed as a centerpiece of their future.
With a bevy of key players either traded away or released, the four-time 1,000-yard rusher has the chance to spoil the Giants' visit to Indianapolis and prove the franchise that drafted him made the right choice in turning down their offer.
No one can blame the Giants for not throwing even more draft capital at the Colts, especially after they already sacrificed their 2027 fifth-round choice to the Minnesota Vikings to land quarterback J.J. McCarthy and turn their season around after losing Jaxson Dart in Week 2.
Even with the postseason in sight, it would have been tough to mortgage their future for a player who, despite his talents, might not have been around for more than a couple of years in a league where nothing is guaranteed.
That said, it might sting more for Harbaugh and company if Taylor wrecks their plans to cruise to a victory over the struggling Colts and puts them back in a precarious position in the NFC East standings.

title: Giants Offense Report Card: J.J. McCarthy Gets the Win as Offense Stays Streaky vs. Jaguars
full_text:
Streaky. That's the best way to sum up the New York Giants ' offense in the 23-18 win over the Jacksonville Jaguars.
Points were definitely left on the field, including on the second drive of the game, which went for a whopping minus-four yards after a defensive interception set the Giants up in Jaguars territory. New York settled for a field goal (made from the right hash!) to cap that drive.
Then in the second half, the offense had seven total drives, and three of them went for negative yardage, including the last of the third quarter and the first of the fourth. Four of those seven drives were four plays or fewer, which suggested the defense was getting gassed toward the end, when the Jaguars scored 12 points to bring the score much closer than it needed to be.
That said, there was the usual amount of good and bad from the offense this week. Let's jump into the evaluations.
This week wasn't one of McCarthy's best throwing games, but it was definitely a step or two in the right direction in learning how to lead an offense to victory against a difficult defense, once again without a running game.
If McCarthy had hit on just one of the deep balls to open receivers, this game would look entirely different.
That he overthrew every deep ball (except one) should tell him and his coaches that his deep ball needs work. He certainly has the arm strength, but the loft seems off. It's a work in progress.
His one good deep ball went to Malachi Fields and drew a 37-yard pass-interference call. McCarthy gets zero credit for those yards on the stat sheet, but that throw set up the team's first touchdown.
Early on, McCarthy looked like a rookie against the max blitz and took the game's lone sack on one of these.
One can blame these early struggles on being a young quarterback, but many veteran quarterbacks struggle with rushers in their face and having to speed up the internal clock under duress. It's not easy.
Fortunately, the Jaguars stopped sending the house, and the offense settled down. Though McCarthy didn't have great passing numbers overall (18-of-38 for 173 yards and one touchdown), he committed zero turnovers, unlike his counterpart, who threw for more than 300 yards and two interceptions.
McCarthy was the better quarterback out there even if he missed a bunch of throws.
Another big part of the win was McCarthy's scrambles. The four times he broke the pocket, he outran the defense for first downs. His seven runs for 33 yards included three kneel-downs. He also had a 29-yard scramble that was called back for a penalty.
With all the good and the not-so-good, McCarthy's biggest play was running down the fumble returner and finishing off the tackle himself. The defense held, and McCarthy's hustle and competitiveness shone through on this important tackle.
Though McCarthy did have a couple of big-time throws, a 35-yard dart to Isaiah Likely and an 8-yard TD throw to Malik Nabers, nothing was more clutch than the 19-yard layered throw to Fields with 3:02 left that got a much-needed first down.
This play set up his struggling offense to run out the clock, which it did. Kudos to McCarthy for gutting out this win against a very tough opponent.
Winston contributed with several tush-push snaps, including a 1-yard touchdown run. On one of these alignments, the coaches backed off and called a pass instead, and it should have been a touchdown.
The coaches schemed Likely wide open, and Winston hit him right in the hands, but the formerly sure-handed tight end dropped it. Thus, Winston finished the day with three carries for five yards and 0-for-1 through the air.
Skattebo once again struggled to find running room, but the blocking wasn't the only problem. A running back needs to make a defender miss occasionally; Skattebo doesn't. A running back needs to outrun a linebacker in space; Skattebo cannot do this.
He is a battering ram who can force missed tackles while he seeks contact. The problem with seeking contact is that defenses have become very adept at punching out the ball.
Since Skattebo is always finding contact, he's often getting punched in the back. That's what happened this week when Skattebo's third-quarter fumble nearly turned a comfortable lead into a close game and gave the Jaguars hope.
Later, the coaches finally found two runs that gave Skattebo a running start between the tackles, which he turned into 5 and 6 yards and the game-ending first down.
Skattebo otherwise played a positive game, with stellar blitz pickups and three catches for 14 yards out of the backfield. However, if you're not going to make any big plays out there, you'd better not be making any big plays for the opposition either.
The veteran played roughly 12 to 15 rotation snaps, and his two touches produced 10 yards.
Singletary remains very reliable and will play this role the rest of this season, but this team needs to get a whole lot more dynamic in the running back room if it wants to compete with the big boys.
The saga of the team's WR1 continues, with plenty of pluses and a couple of negatives.
He had another drop when a short sideline completion was overturned on replay after he lazily let the ball move when he went to the ground untouched.
Fortunately for Nabers, the coaches called his number on the very next play, on the same sideline comeback route, which he caught for 11 yards and a first down.
He followed that up with a pretty route in the end zone to score the team's second touchdown, an 8-yarder that gave the Giants a 17-6 lead.
When the offense couldn't get a running game going, it went to the short pass route, running Nabers into those hitches for short but positive gains.
He finished with seven catches for 55 yards (7.9 per catch), but only one long gain of 11 yards.
We didn't like Jameis Winston having to calm down a visibly upset Nabers on the sideline, or Nabers failing to run down the fumble returner, peeling away and giving up when the play was still very much in doubt.
That was a bad look, leaving his quarterback to make the tackle without hustling into the play.
The rookie came up big on a couple more plays, as he seems to do every week. His first-quarter contested fly pattern drew a 37-yard pass-interference penalty, and Fields still almost came down with the ball in the end zone.
Regardless, the play set up the offense's first score. Fields then came through with a huge, late-game 19-yard deep middle catch between the linebacker and safety levels. His route was perfect, and his hands were as reliable as ever.
Fields' positive blocking included a resounding block on the tush-push finish and several in-space blocks during those J.J. McCarthy scrambles.
Fields finished with two catches for 25 yards on the day as he continues to be a receiver you cannot go to sleep on.
The frustrations for this poor veteran receiver continue unabated, as week after week he is the victim of some of the worst misses by whoever is playing quarterback, despite getting himself open quite often.
He had three balls sail over his head when he got himself open deep. On his best route of the day, he burst wide open into a deep out area after a series of breathtaking moves, but McCarthy threw the ball too soon from a clean pocket, and it fell to the turf well out of Mooney's reach.
A penalty called back Mooney's lone 7-yard catch. On the stat sheet, an incomplete deep middle seemed attached to every mention of Mooney's name. He finished with zero catches on five targets.
The receiver caught his first ball of the 2026 season, a 4-yard hitch on a second-half 3rd-and-4. Though Hyatt bobbled the catch before reeling in the short throw, he got the benefit of the doubt on the first-down mark.
Also of note, despite his limited snaps, Hyatt had a deep hitch-and-go route that was well-defended, but to his credit, he went up and fought for the ball.
This is a significant development, as making an effort has never been a Hyatt specialty. Perhaps things are changing.
Getting a surprise second-half…

title: Jets Have Good Reason to Make Geno Smith Re-Signing a Priority
full_text:
Through the course of the last two years, the New York Jets have done a good job of retaining talent when needed, and letting aging players walk.
In the case of quarterback Geno Smith, though, the Jets should really consider altering their strategy.
At 36 years old, Smith is the kind of veteran the team has historically let walk in free agency after a stellar year. In New York's mindset, it's better to let an aging player walk instead of giving a contract extension to them.
Smith is a separate case. Not only because he is playing well above expectations this season, but because of what he could represent for the future.
Under his current deal, Smith makes just $3.3 million for the Jets. That makes his 2026 season one of the best bargains in the NFL this year.
Smith has completed 68 percent of his passes for over 2,400 yards, 15 touchdowns and just three interceptions. He is projected to throw for over 3,700 yards, 23 touchdowns and just five interceptions. That would be considered one of the best years for a quarterback in team history.
"I'm glad he's with us. I really am," Jets head coach Aaron Glenn said. "I've said this from the very beginning: I don't think that he came into this season trying to prove anything to anybody, I think he just wanted to prove to himself that he could be one of the top quarterbacks in this league, and I think he's still trying to do that."
Despite Smith's on-field success, the team has yet to win games at a convincing clip under his leadership. At 3-8, New York is set for their 11th straight losing season and 16th year without a playoff berth.
If the Jets are going to extend Smith after this season, the asking price will be far greater than just $3 million. It would be a safe bet to assume he would expect starter money that includes somewhere north of $20 million.
That would fit the Jets' cap situation. They will walk into the 2027 offseason with over $80 million in cap space. But should they retain an aging player just because he had a good year? New York was proven right to let Nick Folk and John Simpson walk in free agency last year and found more productive alternatives. They could argue the same for the quarterback position.
Of course, there are different circumstances the Jets will need to consider.
It's safe to assume the Jets will be drafting a quarterback with one of their three first-round picks this year. Throwing an unproven on the field before they are ready, though, would be a disaster for the organization. They must allow the young quarterback to sit behind a proven veteran to learn from.
That's where Smith comes in.
New York wouldn't just be spending money on a Smith extension to be the starter next year. They would be asking him to mentor his replacement at some point later in the season. It's a fundamental difference between replacing a kicker or offensive lineman.
Sure, the Jets could let Smith walk in free agency and sign a different veteran for less like Jacoby Brissett or other bridge quarterbacks. But Smith is objectively better than any bridge that will be on the open market.
All this shows is that the team must get an extension done with Smith; not just to be competitive in 2027, but so they can have someone help the incoming rookie for the first time in decades.

title: 3 Over the Hill Jets Veterans Who Clearly Need Rookie Replacements in 2027
full_text:
Like the Kevin meme from "The Office," the New York Jets should be thinking one thing above all else:
It's nice to finally win one.
New York defeated the Los Angeles Chargers to snap a five-game losing skid and a stretch of eight losses in their last nine games. At 3-8, there's still little hope the Jets will figure out a way to save their season. But there are still positives to look at after a win like that.
At the same time, some uncomfortable conversations should come up as well. New York's aging veterans struggled despite the win. And if those struggles continue, the Jets should look to replace three of them this coming offseason.
Let's get to that list now.
We've highlighted Davis' play over the last few weeks as something the team needs to address eventually . If he has a good performance, we will happily give him flowers for it.
That said, Sunday's game vs. the Chargers was another mediocre showing for the 37-year-old linebacker. Davis was graded the Jets' fifth-worst player, per Pro Football Focus, and remains the third-worst linebacker in the sport by that very metric. He missed tackles and struggled against the run, as he has all season.
The Jets will need to address their linebacker room this offseason. They can't play Jamien Sherwood and Davis together next year. Sherwood has been fine to an extent, but Davis has reached the point of being nearly unplayable.
And if nothing gets fixed, the NFL Draft may be the best place to find his replacement.
It may seem unfair for me to call for the Jets to replace a starting defensive tackle who recorded a sack on Sunday. After all, Harrison Phillips got to the quarterback for one of the team's six total tallies on the day.
That said, his claim to fame isn't rushing the passer. It's stopping the run. And Phillips has struggled in that regard.
New York gave up 158 yards on the ground in the Week 11 win and over five yards per carry. The defense is ranked third-worst in the league at stopping the run. Things won't be getting any better either. The Jets need to address their interior defensive line, and replacing Phillips will need to be done.
Stephens has been a serviceable starter in his second season with the Jets. That said, he gave up a touchdown early in the fourth quarter. While Ladd McConkey is the Chargers' best receiving threat, you cannot have a starting corner get beat as much as Stephens has been this season.
New York could add a cornerback in free agency, but they could look to the draft to address the position again. D'Angelo Ponds was a second-round pick at the position this spring, but New York has trained him to play inside.
If the Jets want a bigger corner, the draft will have prospects to target. And any of them may be better suited to replace Stephens.

title: David Bailey Is Proving He's Much More Than an Elite Pass Rusher for Jets
full_text:
There will be no need to discuss who will be New York Jets' team MVP this season. That award has been won by one of the most productive rookies we have ever seen.
David Bailey's performance this season has been transcendent—worthy of a player who was taken with the second overall pick in the 2026 draft. The edge rusher has 9.5 sacks and six forced fumbles—a first in league history for a rookie in his first 10 games.
"We expect that from him," Jets head coach Aaron Glenn said after the team's win over the Los Angeles Chargers. "I think he’s close to 10 sacks right now. The thing that’s really sticking out to me is the fact that he’s doing everything he can to get the ball back to the offense."
Bailey continues to make his mark on the Jets in his first season. But it's his improvement across his total game that is helping him exceed expectations at this point as well.
When the Jets made the decision to draft Bailey over linebacker Arvell Reese, they did so knowing Bailey was a more productive pass rusher. That has shown up in droves this season, and on Sunday, the Texas Tech product recorded another two sacks in the team's 27-24 win.
The six forced fumbles this season, though, are a wrinkle to his game that shows he's more interested in helping the team win than personal glory.
His impact in run defense has improved greatly as well.
Bailey is not a finished product when defending the run. The Jets knew that going into this season. But his play has improved. He currently ranks fourth in run stops with 20, which highlights his high motor to chase down runners. The tape also shows he is setting the edge a lot better and attacking blockers physically.
And as a teammate, Bailey's impact continues to be felt far beyond anything he's done on the field.
"I love him, bro,” Jets receiver Garrett Wilson said. “Every time I watch him make a play, I get so happy and excited because he’s a guy who doesn’t really get excited or happy for himself. He’s a baller, and I can’t wait to watch him keep growing."
The Jets know what Bailey can do as a pass rusher. He's currently five sacks away from the rookie sack record, and four forced fumbles away from the single-season record. What they've seen in his run defense and his high motor leads them to believe he can be even better than he already is.
And for a player that is seemingly on his way to winning the Defensive Rookie of the Year award, Bailey is set to be one of the top players on the Jets' roster for years to come.
"He still has a way to go, he really does, and I think he would tell you that, too," Glenn said. "I just look forward to him on a weekly basis of how he continues to progress and get better."

title: Jets Tanking Conversations are Missing the Bigger Picture After Divisive Week 11 Win
full_text:
Depending on who you talk to, the New York Jets' Week 11 victory was either a step in the right direction or the worst thing that has ever happened in the history of mankind. There's no in-between.
That, of course, comes with a team that has failed to record a winning season in their last 10 years, and has missed the playoffs in the last 16. Fans want to see change, but they want change to occur in a way that they think is beneficial for the future of the organization—not just for 2026.
But was their 27-24 win over the Los Angeles Chargers really that detrimental to their future?
In reality, most of the fanbase's anger is coming too early in the process. And it's making everything confusing for others who just want to see the team improve.
To the displeasure of some in their fanbase, the Jets were never going to purposely lose the final seven games of the season. They have simply too much talent and are loyal to their head coach to the point where they wanted to succeed for him.
What many angry fans forget to realize, though, is that the Jets don't need to tank in order to get a top pick in the upcoming draft. New York owns the Indianapolis Colts' first-round pick which is currently slated for fourth overall. The more the Colts lose (as expected), the better chance the Jets have of getting their future face of the franchise at quarterback.
Their own pick can be helpful in that regard, but it's not the be-all-end-all of the team's draft strategy. They can win as many games as possible and still come away with a top pick.
"I don't think anybody in this business is here to lose," Jets head coach Aaron Glenn said last week. "I don't think anybody in this business can stomach just going out there and trying to lose; that's just not the way that we're built... regardless of the record."
The idea that the Jets need to lose out in order to get their future franchise quarterback is also a flawed argument. In 2024, the New England Patriots and Washington Commanders missed out on the top overall pick, but managed to take quarterbacks that have gone further in the season than Caleb Williams has. The upcoming 2027 draft class is set to be deeper at the position as well.
New York could end up taking CJ Carr or Darian Mensah with the fourth pick and surround him with talent. This puts them in start contrast to, say, the Miami Dolphins.
The Jets are right on schedule to take a quarterback in the 2027 draft , and they don't need to tank to do it.
Glenn's current record as head coach of the Jets is 6-22. What the majority of fans are most concerned with, watching the team win, is that the more the organization is victorious down the stretch, the more likely it is that Glenn returns for a third season on the job.
We've been clear that seven wins for Glenn seem like the barometer for owner Woody Johnson to keep his current coach. That means New York would have to win four of their final six games. Here's the remaining list of opponents, in no particular order:
New York is talented enough to win four of these contests and perhaps more if the Bills, Patriots, and other contenders are without key starters.
But that isn't a guarantee either.
New York has two of its victories this season against one-win opponents. They have failed to show the ability to beat teams that are perceived to be better than them. Why would one win on Sunday and three wins this season be enough to save the coach's job?
In reality, there's no guarantee the Jets are going to keep Glenn after a three-point win over a one-win Chargers roster. Anyone saying otherwise is lying. There are a lot more games to determine before any decision gets made.
It would be best for Jets fans to let the process play out—and then wait to see where the team stands going into January, compared to worrying about a future decision over a month away.

title: Will McDonald IV’s Long-Term Jets Outlook Remains a Huge Question Mark After Week 11
full_text:
The Jets finally got into the win column Sunday, beating the one-win Chargers 27-24 at SoFi Stadium to snap their five-game losing streak. While New York’s dominance and efficiency on offense helped power the team to victory, the pass rush also played a key role.
The unit, led by second overall pick David Bailey and third-year defensive tackle Jowon Briggs , consistently kept Los Angeles quarterback Justin Herbert under duress, recording 17 pressures, eight quarterback hits, and six sacks.
It was a true team effort, as nine Jets defenders recorded at least one pressure. Surprisingly, edge rusher Will McDonald IV was one of the few who didn’t record a single pressure. Not only was the four-year veteran unable to generate pressure, but he also failed to make any impact in New York’s victory, finishing without recording a single tackle.
It’s become increasingly difficult to justify McDonald’s place in the Jets’ edge rush rotation. Despite New York picking up his 2027 option, McDonald entered this season in a make-or-break year after failing to establish himself as more than a rotational pass rusher during his first three seasons.
With his workload shrinking and production declining, it’s becoming increasingly unlikely that the former 2023 first-round selection will earn a long-term contract with Gang Green.
Through Week 11’s Sunday slate, the Jets are currently tied for seventh in sacks with 29, already surpassing last year’s total of 26. However, New York’s success has largely been driven by Bailey, who’s contributed 9.5 of the team’s 29 sacks.
The rookie from Texas Tech has quickly established himself as a legitimate franchise cornerstone, effectively taking McDonald’s role as the team’s top pass rusher. McDonald had led New York in sacks over the past two seasons, combining for 18.5 sacks across 32 games.
This season, he’s struggled to provide the complementary production New York needs from him, registering just four sacks and 22 pressures in 177 pass-rush snaps. Additionally, McDonald has shown minimal progress as a run defender.
Although he’s posted the second-highest run-defense grade of his career this season (61.3, per Pro Football Focus ), that doesn’t mean he’s become a reliable contributor against the run. In fact, McDonald has struggled to maintain that level recently, earning a run-defense grade below 60 in each of his last three games.
With McDonald struggling to make an impact in either phase, the team has opted to give Kingsley Enagbare and Joseph Ossai larger roles, especially in passing-down situations. This ultimately led to McDonald requesting two weeks ago.
With head coach Aaron Glenn and the team swiftly shutting down the idea of a trade, McDonald stayed put, and his playing time has slightly increased over the last two games. However, that doesn’t necessarily mean the Jets view him as a long-term piece of their defense.
Rather, keeping McDonald may have had more to do with ownership’s desire to give Glenn the best possible chance to succeed. By preserving the team’s already thin edge rush depth, the Jets can avoid further weakening an area that has already struggled to generate consistent production. Trading him would have left New York with fewer reliable options opposite Bailey, making an already floundering edge rush group more vulnerable.
Despite this, if McDonald wants to earn a lucrative payday, he must take advantage of his opportunities in the next seven games. He needs to show he can be a consistent contributor against both the pass and the run if he wants to receive a long-term extension.
Otherwise, the Jets could look to upgrade the position in the offseason rather than commit to McDonald’s projected $14.5 million cap hit in 2027, per Spotrac.

title: 3 Eye-Catching Box Score Stats From Jets' 27-24 Win vs. Chargers
full_text:
It's not exactly a win that will change the course of the organization.
But the performance put forth by the New York Jets on Sunday in their 27-24 win over the Los Angeles Chargers came at an important time for both their roster and coaching staff. New York ended a five-game skid and moved to 3-8.
Many numbers and stats were attributed to New York's victory. But three, in particular, stood out. Let's get to them now.
That was Geno Smith's QBR from Sunday's game. Smith went 17-for-21 passing with three touchdown passes. New York ran the ball more than they threw it, and for good reason - they dominated the line of scrimmage to the tune of 4.5 yards per carry and over 150 total rushing yards.
Smith has been incredibly efficient this season, though, to the point where New York must think long and hard about giving him an extension this offseason.
For reference, QBR is measured from 0-100. A 90.7 is considered the elite of the elite. It shows how well a team's quarterback is playing.
Smith's completion percentage of 68% is currently second in team history through their first 11 games. His 102.7 passer rating is the best, while he's thrown the fewest interceptions during that same stretch.
New York should be thrilled with Smith's performance all season. Sunday's game was the kind of efficient performance the team will want to see over the final six games as well.
The Jets had a lot of fun with the number six on Sunday. Their defense registered six sacks against Justin Herbert in their win. David Bailey led the way with two sacks, bringing him to 9.5 in his first 10 games.
But six also means something else.
New York has six games left this season. The Jets' coaching staff and roster must prove that head coach Aaron Glenn deserves a third season. At 3-8, the Jets can't lose out and keep their head coach. They will need to get as close to sweeping their final stretch of games as they can in order to keep Glenn around.
The number six was successful for New York's defensive line. But it also comes with a warning - there isn't much time for Glenn to show he deserves more years on the job.
There were a lot of zeros in New York's victory on Sunday. There were zero punts, zero turnovers, zero failed fourth-down attempts, and zero missed field goals. It's the first time the team has accomplished that string of zeros in franchise history.
We've already talked about the team's efficiency, but it's important to understand how rare Sunday's performance was. Their performance was the 6th-best for any team in a game this season, based on EPA per drive. It was also the second game this season in which they did not punt, tying the Dallas Cowboys for the most such games in NFL history.
It's a shame these numbers have come in the middle of a 3-8 season, but it's clear the offense is working with the talent on the roster. With more success, there will be some interesting decisions the team has to make moving forward.

title: Aaron Glenn's Biggest Decision He Got Right vs. Chargers (And What It Means as Week 12 Begins)
full_text:
At long last, the Jets are finally back in the win column after snapping a five-game losing streak in Sunday's 27-24 victory over the Chargers.
In a game that only featured 12 combined drives and turned out to be the shortest game of the NFL season, this was a well-played game from both sides, but particularly from a Jets team that only committed four penalties for 18 yards, converted 9-of-11 third-down attempts, and went 3-of-4 in the red zone.
Even more impressive, the Jets were victorious despite being down two of their wideouts (Omar Cooper Jr., Isaiah Williams). A lot of that had to do with the dominant play up front from the defensive line and rookie David Bailey , who added two more sacks during what is already shaping up to be a historic season.
Aside from the final drive of the game when the Jets ran the clock out, they scored on each of their five possessions before that and were as efficient as we have seen all season. A lot of that success stemmed from head coach Aaron Glenn's decision to move offensive coordinator Frank Reich from the booth to the field.
It gave the Jets a more balanced approach and helped them wear down the Chargers by possessing the ball for more than 32 minutes.
Sure, Glenn is still just 6-22 in Gotham, and his outlook is not going to immediately change after one win against a bottom-dwelling team like the Chargers. At the same time, this is a team that has been too conservative and has struggled to keep pace throughout an entire game. On Sunday, the efficiency was at an all-time high, and the Jets never trailed at one point.
With all that in mind, here is the biggest decision Glenn got right in Sunday's win over the Chargers.
Coming into this game, the Jets had the league's worst red-zone efficiency and had gone nine straight quarters without scoring a touchdown. After having to settle for a field goal on the opening drive and stretching that drought to 10 quarters, the Jets finally punched it in for six when quarterback Geno Smith found running back Breece Hall for a seven-yard TD (h/t NFL) early in the second quarter.
Geno to Breece Hall for a Jets TD! NYJvsLAC on FOX/FOX One Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/00cok49kom
The Jets were particularly strong at sustaining drives and moving the ball effectively, running at least 11 plays on three of their drives and picking up one first down after another.
From Smith (17-of-21, 176 yards, three TDs, zero interceptions) and wide receiver Sterling Shepard's big game after being called up from the practice squad (two catches, 24 yards, two TDs) to the two-headed approach on the ground from Breece Hall (20 carries, 86 yards) and Braelon Allen (16 carries, 75 yards), Reich did a much better job distributing the ball and maintaining some balance offensively.
While a lot of the credit should also go to the offensive line and the impressive job they did setting the tone up front, having Reich on the field and in closer communication with his players had a positive impact on this offense and is something Glenn may stick with going forward.
"I've always said that I'm going to do whatever it takes for us to improve and win games," Glenn said, per Sports Illustrated 's Nick Faria. "I'm not afraid of trying things. I thought it would be a good idea, so who knows? He had a chance to speak with the guys and I thought it was good for us."
This was the most efficient outing from a Jets offense since 2004, so it would probably be in Glenn's best interest to keep Reich on the field going forward, even if Sunday's breakout came against a 1-9 team. Granted, the defense's inability to lock this game up and the fact that it surrendered a pair of fourth-quarter TDs still speaks to the deficiencies that continue to plague it, not to mention the poor run defense that gave up 158 yards and a TD.
Glenn and defensive coordinator Brian Duker still have some work to do there, but the HC's decision to get Reich up close and personal with his offense, in addition to his adaptability in elevating Shepard from the practice squad and rewarding a veteran in a depleted WR room, should not be overlooked.
A lot of fans have made it clear they want the Jets to tank down the stretch to secure the best draft pick possible, but that was far from the case in Sunday's win. Whether you agree with that approach or not, it is clear there was no intention of doing that against the Chargers as the Jets head into a second consecutive road game and face the Dolphins in a rematch from Week 7.
It was the third time Shepard has been called up from the practice squad this season, so the Jets need to decide if they want to keep him around on their 53-man roster moving forward. One game or not, he showed up in the red zone and provided a much-needed spark in an area that has been a constant struggle this season.
Two TDs for Sterling Shepard! NYJvsLAC on FOX/FOX One Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/1unKNT1rMh
With another winnable game on deck against a Dolphins team that only won 28-25 earlier this season at MetLife Stadium, it would make sense for Glenn to stick with Reich on the sidelines and try to take some positive momentum into the looming Week 13 bye. Glenn's job is likely no safer than it was coming in, but this team clearly has a lot of fight left in it and must continue finding a competitive balance to ensure it can finish out drives.
This is still just a 3-8 team, but Glenn realized the offense needed a change and put his trust in Reich to make some positive gains on the field. If anything, the Jets now have a solid blueprint to carry into the rest of the season, even if it may not be the most popular approach among the fan base and has little say in Glenn's future in Gotham.

title: Jets Rookie & Sophomore Power Rankings Week 12: David Bailey's Rise Can't Be Ignored
full_text:
Breaking news: the Jets have won a football game. New York snapped its five-game losing streak Sunday, beating the Chargers 27-24 at SoFi Stadium.
While the win doesn’t change the fact that the Jets will miss the playoffs for the 16th consecutive season and that head coach Aaron Glenn is still on the hot seat , it does give the team a much-needed morale boost. Although it’s not a victory worth bragging about, considering Los Angeles is 1-9 on the season, wins are hard to come by in the NFL, and New York will take one wherever it can get it.
The Jets got valuable contributions from several of their young players, including rookie edge rusher David Bailey, who continues to make life miserable for opposing tackles. With that said, let’s take a look at where the rookies and sophomores rank heading into the team’s Week 12 showdown against the Dolphins.
Note: Anez Cooper is currently excluded from the list, as he is on injured reserve.
VJ Payne made his second NFL appearance against the Chargers on Sunday.
Since coming off injured reserve, the former Kansas State Wildcat has stepped into Andre Cisco’s role on the special teams, recording one total tackle across 12 snaps. While Payne has carved out a role on special teams, he’s yet to play a defensive snap.
However, we should expect to see him get an opportunity on defense at some point this season. Whether it’s due to an injury to the safeties room or once New York is eliminated from playoff contention.
The Jets have gotten minimal production from their depth receivers this season. But with Omar Cooper Jr. and Isaiah Williams sidelined, and New York dressing just five receivers, the team needed someone other than Garrett Wilson or Adonai Mitchell to step up.
Sterling Shepard answered the call . The ex-Giant played a crucial role in the Jets’ win, hauling in two receptions for 24 yards and two touchdowns. That’s the kind of impact New York hoped Arian Smith would provide when it invested a fourth-round pick in him in 2025.
However, Smith has recorded just seven receptions for 52 yards across 18 games. With the Jets likely to bolster their receiving depth in the offseason, the former Georgia Bulldog must show significant progression if he’s to remain with the team in 2027.
It’s been an extremely underwhelming season for Kiko Mauigoa, but that’s through no fault of his own. He’s dealt with multiple injuries this season and has been on the injured reserve since Week 6.
In the three games Mauigoa has played, he’s exclusively seen the field on special teams. While he hasn’t taken any defensive snaps yet, we should expect the Jets to give him reps in the coming weeks.
With New York’s playoff hopes all but gone and Demario Davis continuing to regress significantly, the Jets should turn to Mauigoa to see what he can provide during the final stretch of the season.
Earlier in the week, there was a chance Cade Klubnik would make his first career start with Geno Smith dealing with an ankle injury. The former Clemson Tiger showed some flashes in relief for Smith, completing 11 of his 20 passes for 137 yards and an interception.
However, Smith was intent on playing, and it showed, as the 14-year veteran completed 17 of his 21 passes for 176 yards and three touchdowns.
Geno Smith finds Sterling Shepard for the touchdown! 📺: FOX/FOX One pic.twitter.com/Lmhp9QYTOu
At 3-8, New York will need a miracle to make the playoffs. But with Glenn on the hot seat and needing wins to save his job, he’ll keep starting Smith. This doesn’t necessarily rule out Klubnik getting a start later this season. However, ownership clearly wants Glenn to succeed, and Smith puts them in the best position to win.
With Cisco pulled from the lineup and ultimately traded two weeks ago, the Jets elevated Malachi Moore to the team’s backup safety.
In 45 defensive snaps across two games, the former 2025 fourth-round selection failed to show improvement in coverage, surrendering two catches for 64 yards and a touchdown. Additionally, Moore committed a pass interference penalty that led to a touchdown four plays later.
As a result, Moore’s workload was reduced against the Chargers, as he played just 10 snaps while recording two total tackles. While Moore should continue to receive reps in a limited role, he’ll have to prove he deserves it.
With Payne entering the fold, New York could turn to him if Payne’s coverage woes persist.
With Jarvis Brownlee Jr. inactive and the Jets cutting Moore’s snaps, D’Angelo Ponds finally received more playing time. The former Indiana Hoosier played a season-high 35 defensive snaps, logging four total tackles and allowing just one reception for three yards.
While Ponds wasn’t lights-out, his performance was encouraging considering some of his previous struggles in past games. He’s shown promise as a tackler, but he’ll need to improve in coverage moving forward.
However, we can’t be too critical of Pond's performance this season. He’s playing a position that he lined up at just 28 times in college, so there’s going to be bumps in the road as he goes through these growing pains. Regardless, fans should expect to see significant progression from Ponds during the final seven games.
New York has an arsenal of playmakers. But with so many mouths to feed, not everyone is going to have big games. One day someone can have two touchdowns, and the next, have just one reception.
After leading the Jets in receptions last season, Mason Taylor’s usage has taken a hit. Through nine games, the former LSU Tiger has hauled in just 24 receptions (31 targets) for 192 yards and two touchdowns.
While Taylor had a great game a few weeks back against the Dolphins, recording five catches for 62 yards and two touchdowns, he’s been used as a complementary piece over the past few games. Against the Chargers, Taylor logged just two receptions for 25 yards, but his contributions were still enough to help New York win.
While it would be nice for offensive coordinator Frank Reich to utilize him more in the red zone, Taylor has been a solid, all-around tight end, and he’ll remain the team’s TE1.
Every time Kenyon Sadiq has the ball in his hands, it’s easy to see why New York used its 16th overall selection on him. He’s got high-end athleticism and incredible playmaking ability for a player of his position.
The problem is, Reich has struggled to find ways to get the ball in his hands. Through 11 games, the former Oregon Duck has hauled in just 25 catches on 33 targets for 268 yards and one touchdown.
He’s been targeted more than four times once, and has five games where he’s recorded either zero or one reception. So far, what’s worked for Sadiq is screen passes and underneath routes on play-actions. We saw that Sunday against the Chargers, where he recorded three receptions for 30 yards.
While Sadiq will have to work at creating separation, there’s no reason for Reich to stop calling screen plays or end-arounds moving forward.
After recording just four total tackles across his first three games, Darrell Jackson Jr. has emerged as an integral part of the Jets’ interior line rotation. Over the past few weeks, the former Florida State Seminole has stepped into a starting role amid injuries to David Onyemata and T’Vondre Sweat, providing steady contributions.
In the Jets' win over the Chargers, Jackson recorded four total tackles, two pressures, and half-a-sack. Although New York surrendered 158 rushing yards, Jackson’s presence in the interior played a key role in some of the team’s stops. On the second defensive drive alone, he recorded a run stuff and pressured Justin Herbert, helping force Los Angeles to punt.
Through 11 games, Jackson has registered 35 total tackles, seven pressures, and 1.5 sacks. While his impact doesn’t always show on the stat sheet, he’s given the Jets some meaningful production and a reason to believe he'll develop into a key rotational player for years to come.
In the NFL, there’s no hiding from injuries. Sometimes a team is fortunate…

title: 3 Sneaky QB Prospects Jets Could Target in the 2027 NFL Draft Despite 1st-Round Temptation
full_text:
The Jets would be foolish to not take a quarterback with at least one of their three first-round picks in the 2027 NFL Draft. When you get a chance to bring in an impactful playmaker at the position, you can't overlook it. That's especially true after Week 11's win over Los Angeles ,  as New York is projected to have the fourth, fifth and 15th overall picks in the opening round, per Tankathon .
Still, it doesn't mean there aren't quarterbacks after the first round who aren't enticing to general manager Darren Mougey & Co.
It's hard to determine exactly where many of the current crop of quarterbacks will fall, since many are underclassmen who could simply return to college. That said, the Jets are in a rare situation to have enough talent on offense to entice any young QB to come out. They'll have three first-round picks in April, and while they could use one on a quarterback, they have a plethora of needs to address across the roster .
There are plenty of sneaky signal-callers who could help the Jets beyond just the first round—including these three.
Sellers is going to be the most intriguing quarterback prospect from this draft if he ends up declaring. The South Carolina star has completed 62% of his passes for over 2,100 yards and 17 touchdown passes. His 6'3", 230-lb. frame also helps with his 600 yards rushing this season.
He is far from a finished product, and he will be a raw project coming out. That said, there will be many teams willing to take a flier on a raw comparison to Cam Newton if it means Sellers can become anywhere close to the former league MVP.
If the Jets are looking for a sneaky playmaker after round one, Sellers could be the high-ceiling/low-floor gamble to go after.
Remember him? Sorsby was potentially going to come out of the Supplemental Draft after being barred from playing college football due to a betting scandal while he was playing with the Cincinnati Bearcats.
On the field, Sorsby was an easy pick by many as a first-round player. Now it's hard to see him get anywhere near that, since he hasn't played on a competitive team in a full year. He has the athleticism and arm talent to be a player teams look for after the first round, especially if he lights it up at the NFL Scouting Combine.
Maiava has been a very solid starter for the USC Trojans over the last two seasons. This year, the senior signal-caller has completed over 66% of his passes, thrown for 2,800 yards and 21 touchdowns. He's not the kind of athlete Sellers is, but with plenty of playing experience as a starter, he could be the kind of rookie with starting experience many NFL teams look to target.
For the Jets, things may not have worked out with the last two USC quarterbacks , but Maiava could be an exception given their current talent under center.
