title: Dishing Out 5 Jets Awards After Gang Green Outlasts Lowly Chargers in L.A.
full_text:
Maybe that was what the Jets were supposed to look like all season.
New York traveled across the country and beat a one-win Los Angeles Chargers team by a score of 27-24 . The Jets' offense dominated throughout the day, while their defense held off Los Angeles just enough to pull off their third win of the year.
There are plenty of awards to hand out after the Jets' first Victory Monday in over a month . So let's get to those now.
New York's offensive performance on Sunday was historic. The Jets put up the sixth-best performance for any team in a game this season, based on EPA per drive. They didn't punt in their best performance in 20 years.
Part of it was due to the team running the football at a high clip. It also came down to Geno Smith orchestrating the offense perfectly. He went 17-for-21 passing and threw three touchdowns. Whenever a big play needed to be made, he made it.
Geno Smith finds Sterling Shepard for the touchdown! 📺: FOX/FOX One pic.twitter.com/Lmhp9QYTOu
And New York's offense felt the success.
"We did a really good job of being balanced, scoring in the red zone," Glenn said. "Getting pressure players the ball so those guys can make plays. I thought we orchestrated the drives the way we wanted. That was good to see."
Some fans will be upset that the Jets won on Sunday, but it was also a feel-good kind of day for Sterling Shepard . Here's a player who suffered two major injuries in his career, battled hard, and bounced around several practice squads, only to catch two touchdowns in Sunday's win.
" The Energizer bunny. That's who he is ," Glenn said. "He has so much juice, and he loves playing the game. He really does. I'm glad we have him."
New York got key production from Garrett Wilson, Breece Hall, and their usual cast of characters, but seeing a wily veteran make plays when the Jets needed it most is always nice to see for the organization and for Shepard now at 33 years old.
Few edge rushers in NFL history have been as impactful as David Bailey has been for the Jets this season. On Sunday, he recorded two more sacks and a forced fumble in the win. The numbers have now boosted to 9.5 sacks and six forced fumbles, and he is just the sixth player in league history with almost a sack per game in his first 10 games.
2 sacks today, 9.5 this season for David Bailey 😤 NYJvsLAC on FOX/FOX One Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/CPQkr1Mrc3
Other defensive rookies have played well. Arvell Reese is dominating with the Giants. But the Rookie of the Year award should be wrapped up in Bailey's favor. Not only is he the Jets' lone bright spot on defense this season, but he's also nearing the rookie sack record set by Javon Kearse nearly 30 years ago.
Bailey is the kind of transcendent star that many had hoped he would be.
David Onyemata has started practicing with the Jets after a near-season-long IR stint. T'Vondre Sweat is eligible to come off IR going into next week's game against the Miami Dolphins. It remains unclear whether the Jets will have one or both players going into Week 12.
But in Week 11, it was clear the organization desperately misses both players.
New York's run defense has been bad over the last two months. The Jets are currently third-worst in the league. Part of that is due to the team not having the defensive tackles needed to stop the run in the modern league. Both Sweat's and Onyemata's injuries have hurt in major ways.
On Sunday, the Jets gave up 158 yards on the ground and over five yards per carry. They were very fortunate they were able to hang on to their win due to their inability to stop the run. Things have only gotten worse.
But things could certainly change once Sweat and Onyemata return.
If the season ended today, the Jets would own the fourth, fifth, and 15th overall picks in the upcoming draft. That's a pretty good haul for any team looking to improve its roster.
That said, Sunday's win was a major hit for those who were hoping the Jets could come away with the top overall pick. Now, the team sits at three wins—two more than the Dolphins, Titans, and Chargers. The Jets already have wins over the Titans and Chargers this season, so the tiebreaker would go to both teams over New York for a higher pick.
New York's hopes of getting the top pick all but evaporated with the loss. That doesn't necessarily mean that the Jets are doomed going into the 2027 draft—they should be able to land a good quarterback prospect and a top defender .
It just means they won't have a true "pick of the litter" type.

title: Jeremiah Trotter Jr. Quickly Complicating Eagles' Offseason Outlook
full_text:
PHILADELPHIA — Jeremiah Trotter Jr. is making the most of his opportunity, and the Eagles' defense is the better for it.
With star Mike linebacker Zack Baun on injured reserve, the third-year pro stepped into the green-dot role and delivered a performance that felt like more than just a solid fill-in.
Against the Steelers this past Sunday, Trotter finished with 13 tackles (nine solo) while playing every defensive snap in Philadelphia’s 19-16 win. He set the tone early, knifing through to drop Jaylen Warren for no gain on a fourth-and-1 from midfield on Pittsburgh’s opening possession.
It was the kind of play that wakes a stadium and announces who is leading the defense.
That stop wasn’t blind luck. Trotter, the son of franchise legend Jeremiah Trotter Sr., has shown the football IQ and natural instincts that are his birthright. The gifts have allowed him to play faster than his measurable tools. The younger Trotter is decisive going downhill against the run and has looked increasingly comfortable in space.
The physicality has always been here, even if the size (6-foot, 225 pounds) and pure athleticism didn’t scream “prototype” coming out of Clemson.
Every time Trotter has been on the field this season, he has looked like a starting-caliber NFL linebacker. The emotion that fuels it is intentional.
“You can’t really play without emotion,” Trotter said at his locker on Tuesday. “That emotion inside of me comes out when I’m out there on the football field.”
Teammates have noticed the on-field intensity that can surprise people who only see the quieter version of Trotter off it.
That job description now includes a short-week turnaround against the Cowboys on Thanksgiving. Preparation has shifted heavily to the mental side while the body recovers.
“It takes a lot of mental reps,” Trotter said of the short week. “Our coaches are trying to make sure that we’re getting our bodies back fresh for this upcoming game coming so fast. So it’s gonna be a lot on the mental side as far as film work, studying the game plan that we have in, and making sure that we’re getting that aspect of the game so we’re ready to play and our bodies are getting ready, too.”
The Thanksgiving Day holiday itself adds another layer. Trotter played on Turkey Day in high school at St. Joe’s Prep, but this will be his first time in the NFL.
“Thanksgiving, we always think of that like a football holiday as well,” he said. “Sitting there watching football, watching whatever team’s playing with your family and everything. It’s gonna be an awesome experience for me.”
Trotter views Dallas and its explosive offense as a clear test.
“They got guys everywhere, a very strong offensive line,” the legacy said. “Dak [Prescott's] leading them very well, operating the offense. They got guys on the outside, too—dynamic receivers from CeeDee [Lamb] and [KaVontae] Turpin and [George] Pickens. They got a lot of talented players, so it’s gonna be a great challenge for us come Thursday.”
From the earlier meeting this season, a 38-21 Cowboys drubbing at Lincoln Financial Field on Oct. 26, the priority is straightforward:
“It’s gonna just be stopping the run. They did a really good job and were effective against us in the run game,” said Trotter. “So we gotta start off there, stopping the run, and then it’s gonna come down to trying to get after the quarterback, stopping their guys on the outside, their weapons that they have.”
The conversation around Trotter is eerily similar to two recent linebackers with the Eagles: T.J. Edwards and Nakobe Dean. Like Trotter, those players weren’t the best athletes but excelled with their instincts, football IQ and physicality.
Trotter is now traveling the same path. He will start at least the next three games while Baun recovers from his back injury, and potentially longer depending on how it progresses. That extended runway is valuable.
The fan base has noticed. “Ever since I got here, Philadelphia has really given me a lot of support,” Trotter said. “Always showing love to me when I’m out there playing and doing what I have to do to help out the team win, and I really appreciate that.”
The offseason picture at ILB is already interesting. Trotter has one more year left on his contract. Baun is an All-Pro entering his age-30 season. Jihaad Campbell, the 2025 first-round pick, has rare physical traits for the position and flashed in his return from injury on Sunday.
Assuming Baun returns healthy, the Eagles will have legitimate depth and not enough snaps for everyone. For at least one more year, they can pair the veteran with Campbell while deciding how Trotter fits. They could also explore a move at the position. Either way, Sunday made the case that Trotter belongs on the field.
“He's playing good, defensive coordinator Vic Fangio said . “Trot's a smart player, he's an instinctive player, but that only takes you so far. You've got to play good and he is, and he's done a nice job for us. Trotter Sr. should be proud of him.”

title: Eagles' Eli Stowers Use Is Creating More Questions Than Answers
full_text:
PHILADELPHIA—In a season of head-scratching personnel decisions, such as keeping four quarterbacks, trading a Pro Bowl center, and pedaling a defensive tackle that you had just given a three-year, $78 million contract extension to eight months ago, the decision to keep five tight ends on the roster stands above them all.
Simply put, it makes no sense, especially with a second-round development pick that is Eli Stowers, who is in Year 3 of learning how to play tight end after being a quarterback his entire life.
My quest to find out why began in the days leading up to the game against the Steelers.
It started with a question to head coach Nick Sirianni about it, specifically about how the offense can implement Stowers when you have four others: Dallas Goedert, Johnny Mundy, Grant Calcaterra, and Zach Ertz. And each of them has an expiring contract.
"He's getting some vital opportunities to play on special teams as well. I think I've said this to you guys before: Guys that play on special teams and do a good job earn more and more reps through the trust that they build there," said Sirianni about the 54th player taken overall last spring.
"That's the ultimate portion of football where they have to block in space, tackle, and block destruct. As an offensive guy having to do that, that shows a lot about a guy, and I think he's doing a nice job there. I like how he's developing, and we'll see how that continues to progress.”
The progress is evidently slow. Stowers didn’t play a single offensive snap against the Steelers. He did get 20 special teams snaps. It’s something, anyway. It’s not like the other tight ends were getting many offensive snaps, either.
As expected, the veteran got 47 (89 percent). Mundt had eight, Ertz six, and Calcaterra, like Stowers, got a goose egg. Also, like Stowers, Calcaterra got 20 special teams snaps while Mundt got 14.
The even weirder part about it is that they inserted offensive lineman John Ojukwu in a jumbo package set. Not a tight end. Do they not trust them to block? Certainly, they could have done better than Ojukwu in his one snap—and his only snap this season—when a Steelers defender flew right by him and sacked Joe Milton. Couldn’t they?
So, my quest to find out about the tight ends continued. The day after Sirianni talked, Sean Mannion held court, specifically asking how he could find a role for Stowers with four other tight ends clogging his path.
“I know one thing that is a total point of emphasis with this organization is player development,” said the offensive coordinator. “Even with Eli, his snaps throughout the season, each and every day he's out there on the practice field, we are totally focused on his development.
“I think as the season goes on, each week presents a different opportunity for different players on our roster, but our focus is completely on winning and doing the best thing we can for the Eagles to go out there and win the game. Eli's progressing nicely. We've got a deep group in the tight end room. Those roles will be always week to week in terms of what gives the Eagles the best chance to win.”
The Eagles put Ertz at the locker next to Stowers when the veteran tight end signed with the team’s practice squad on Oct. 10, wanting Ertz to be available for any questions or advice he could offer to a player 13 years younger than him.
So, how’s that going he was asked last week?
“He works his butt off,” said Ertz. “He wants to be really good. He understands that it's, it's a long journey, and I tell him all the time, you just gotta get better on day to day. That's what this whole league is about, is trying to be better today than you were yesterday.
“But the physical tools are so impressive. The work ethic is so impressive. His humility is so impressive. He's a guy that was a second-round pick for a reason, and to be able to just wanna learn and be a sponge each and every day, it's awesome to work with him.”
A role may yet come over the final seven games, but the Eagles should do themselves a favor and find out what he can do in a game, not just in practice or on special teams. Either way, they’re likely going to have to draft another TE this spring, but it would be nice to know more about what they already have.

title: Breaking Down Eagles' Injury Report Ahead of Cowboys Clash on Thanksgiving
full_text:
The Eagles will travel to AT&T Stadium to face off against the Dallas Cowboys in Week 12. It is the first time Philadelphia is playing on Thanksgiving Day since 2015. Overall, the Birds boast a 6-1 record on the holiday, including a pair of victories over the Cowboys (a 27-0 win in 1989 and 33-10 win in 2014).
Health remains crucial in the NFL. The Eagles will need to be in tip-top shape to keep up with Dallas' high-powered offense. Philadelphia utilized walkthroughs on Monday and Tuesday, so its injury report remains an estimate. Let's dive into who is banged up and who is ready to roll for Thursday's clash.
Tuesday’s Injury Report #PHIvsDAL pic.twitter.com/eGhrGMSYGj
Cornerback Jonathan Jones played well in an expanded role against the Steelers, tallying five tackles and three pass breakups in 35 defensive snaps. The veteran left late with a foot injury and was seen in a walking boot after the game. Back-to-back DNPs suggest Philly will be without Jones on Thursday.
Expect Riq Woolen to return to a starting role if Jones cannot suit up. Woolen was benched mid-game versus Pittsburgh due to a few frustrating missed tackles. The Eagles' secondary will have to be firing on all cylinders facing Dallas' elite wide receiver duo of CeeDee Lamb and George Pickens.
Arnold Ebiketie is nursing an oblique injury. The defensive end was not present for either Monday's or Tuesday's walkthrough. An upgrade to limited participation on Wednesday is vital for him to have any chance of playing. Expect A.J. Epenesa to join the pass-rushing rotation if Ebiketie is ruled out.
It's encouraging to see cornerback Quinyon Mitchell upgraded from DNP to LP on Tuesday. The All-Pro talent suffered a hamstring injury in Week 11, though he was seen on the stationary bike in the locker room after the win. Defensive coordinator Vic Fangio expressed optimism about Mitchell's status.
Eagles DC Vic Fangio on Quinyon Mitchell: “I think he’ll be fine.” After Nick Sirianni’s comments yesterday and now this, it looks like Mitchell will be good to go. pic.twitter.com/sOGqGIqVwn
Linebacker Smael Mondon's ankle injury kept him from playing against the Steelers. The good news is that an upgrade to limited participation means he is trending in the right direction. His status will be one to watch. The Eagles signed Chance Campbell to the active roster on Tuesday for depth at LB.
Will Shipley has been a limited participant on back-to-back days. The running back returned from a foot injury in Week 11, handling kick return duties and posting nine yards on four carries. That same injury, as well as an illness, continues to bother him. Wednesday's report will provide final clarity.
Philadelphia would turn to Jaydon Blue as Barkley's running mate if Shipley can't give it a go, as Tank Bigsby remains on injured reserve with a core muscle injury. Blue could use a bounce-back outing after he gifted Pittsburgh a possession by fumbling the opening kickoff of the second half.
Offensive coordinator Sean Mannion should have two of his top offensive weapons at his disposal against the Cowboys. Running back Saquon Barkley (neck/illness) and tight end Dallas Goedert (shin) were full participants on Tuesday. The duo accounted for 113 of Philly's 214 offensive yards in Week 11.

title: 3 Aging Eagles Veterans Who Clearly Need Rookie Replacements in 2027
full_text:
The Eagles boosted morale with a 19-16 win over the Steelers in Week 11. That said, it didn't change the fact that Philadelphia remains at the bottom of the NFC East. It's a disappointing result that should light a fire under general manager Howie Roseman as he tries to retool the roster for 2027.
Retooling covers several strategies, including cutting bait with aging players in hopes that youth can add a spark. Veterans bring important leadership and experience to the table, yet can also hold a team back from addressing clear needs. The last thing Philly wants is to be held back from improving.
Here are three aging Eagles veterans who need rookie replacements in 2027.
The nostalgia factor was turned up to the max when Philly signed tight end Zach Ertz in September. The three-time Pro Bowler has logged 582 catches as an Eagle, which trails only wide receiver Harold Carmichael for the most in franchise history (589). It's a record to monitor over the final seven games.
Nostalgia is unfortunately all Ertz has had going for him. The 36-year-old has failed to make an impact on offense, tallying 22 yards on three receptions (eight targets) in four games. Ertz was on the field for just six of the 53 offensive snaps in Week 11. It was his first game action since Week 5.
Not only is Ertz struggling as a receiver; he has whiffed on run blocks as well. The record should not be something that earns him snaps over rookie tight end Eli Stowers moving forward. Stowers is the sole Philly tight end under contract in 2027, so adding depth through the NFL draft will be crucial.
The Eagles have had to turn to veteran cornerback Jonathan Jones to play meaningful snaps on defense twice this season. Cornerback Quinyon Mitchell exited Philly's Week 4 contest early with a knee injury, and cornerback Riq Woolen was benched mid-game in Week 11 due to missed tackles.
The move paid off against the Steelers. Jones finished with the third-highest Pro Football Focus grade among defensive players (81.5). He gave up five receptions for 54 yards on 10 targets. Take note that Jones left late with a foot injury. It remains to be seen if he'll be healthy in time for Week 12's Thanksgiving showdown against the rival Cowboys.
Monday’s Injury Report #PHIvsDAL pic.twitter.com/TZVZ0UfQz3
Jones is 33 years old and is playing on a one-year deal. While he could be someone to lean on down the stretch, he should not be an option beyond 2026. Drafting Mitchell in the first round of the 2024 NFL Draft transformed Philadelphia's secondary. Roseman has an opportunity to make a similar move in April.
Let's circle back to the tight end position. Johnny Mundt was signed last offseason to be a gritty veteran blocker on an offense that excels when the ground game is working. It hasn't gone to plan. The Eagles are a bottom-five offense in rushing yards per game (88.8) and yards per carry (3.7).
Of course, there's more blame to go around. Mundt sports the third-lowest PFF grade among 75 qualified NFL tight ends this campaign (49.6), though. That is not someone who should be averaging 23 snaps per game and out-snapping a developing pro like Stowers at this point in the year.
Mundt joins Ertz, Dallas Goedert, and Grant Calcaterra as Philly tight ends who will enter free agency next offseason. The position is in need of an overhaul. Receiving tight ends gain draft hype, meaning there are always blocking tight ends available in the later rounds.
Roseman has a chance to double dip.

title: 3 Eagles Who Helped Their Uncertain Futures in Week 11's Win vs. Steelers
full_text:
The Eagles snapped a seven-game losing streak with their win over the Steelers on Sunday. Several unheralded players stepped up for the Eagles in the way, and some may have helped themselves out in the process.
Here's a look at three Eagles who may have helped their uncertain futures with the franchise in the win over the Steelers.
Quarterback Joe Milton got his second career start against the Steelers on Sunday, and while he didn't blow anyone away with his play, he led the Eagles to a win and flashed some potential in the process. He made some nice throws down the field over the course of the contest, including a great throw down the sideline on the move in the first quarter.
Heck of a throw on the run from Joe Milton PITvsPHI on CBS/Paramount+ Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/DWwabguGPB
He also iced the game for the Eagles with a clutch, tight-window throw to DeVonta Smith in the final minute(s) to snap Philly's seven-game losing streak.
On 3rd & 6, DeVonta Smith comes up clutch. PITvsPHI on CBS/Paramount+ Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/kx0HtT2tQs
Plus, Milton showed off his cannon with a bomb to Smith that was a couple of feet away from being an epic highlight for both players.
Joe Milton just threw the most perfect incomplete pass pic.twitter.com/jmYlsnZFzc
After the game, Smith gave props to Milton's arm strength. "I didn’t think I could get overthrown," the veteran QB said. "And he did it."
Again, Milton was far from perfect in the game. He completed just 52% of his passes and didn't toss any touchdowns, but he provided enough intrigue for the Eagles to continue to evaluate him as a future backup option.
Safety Marcus Epps turned in his best performance of the season against the Steelers on Sunday. Watching the game, it felt like Epps was all over the field, and the stat sheet backs up the eye test in this scenario. He was second on the team in solo tackles with eight, including one tackle for a loss.
Marcus Epps having a nice game.
Epps will be a free agent over the offseason, and while the Eagles absolutely still need to address the safety spot via the draft and/or free agency, bringing back Epps for some relatively cheap depth at the position might be something that the team considers, especially if he can continue to play as he did against Pittsburgh for the rest of the season.
Epps wasn't the only veteran member of Philadelphia's secondary who had a productive performance against the Steelers. Cornerback Jonathan Jones did also. He tallied five total tackles (two solo tackles) in the game, and he also led the Eagles with three passes defended.
At 33, Jones clearly isn't a long-term answer or option for the Eagles at the cornerback position opposite Quinyon Mitchell, but like Epps, he could be a guy the Birds look to bring back in free agency over the offseason as an inexpensive depth piece.
Unfortunately, Jones suffered an apparent foot injury late in the game, and he was seen in a walking boot afterward. So his status for Philadelphia moving forward this season is in question.

title: McMullen: Eagles' Offense Stopped Repeating a Major Mistake to Secure Week 11's Win
full_text:
PHILADELPHIA, P.A. — There was no white flag, no press-conference mea culpa, no formal burial of the Shanahan/McVay cosplay . But on Sunday against the Steelers, the Eagles essentially pulled the plug on the under-center experiment that has defined (and sabotaged) their offense all year.
They lined up in shotgun or pistol on a season-high 84% of snaps in Week 11's 19-16 win that snapped a seven-game losing streak and gave them their first victory in two months. The bye-week self-scout finally forced the issue: the “under center, play-action, wide zone” stuff that looked sophisticated on a whiteboard was killing them in real life.
A short week and a Thanksgiving trip to Dallas will tell us whether this is an actual course correction or just a one-game concession to a Pittsburgh defense that was prepared to feast on the most predictable tell in the league. Either way, the original plan looks more tortured by the day.
The offense still wasn’t good—214 total yards is nothing to hang a banner for—but the explosives came back, the quarterback looked like he belonged, and the entire operation stopped fighting its own personnel. Joe Milton thrived in the gun.
The now-sidelined Jalen Hurts, who became a star when the Philadelphia offense played to his strengths, never clicked when he was asked to turn his back to the defense and execute the Shanahan blueprint. That disconnect was obvious in the spring. It only became undeniable after the damage was done in a season where the playoff hopes, once a constant in the Nick Sirianni era, remain in hospice at 3-7.
“That [bye] week has been so critical for us over these past six years,” Sirianni said, still unbeaten after the bye (6-0). “... That work that happens in our process as coaches… dig and grind to try to repeat the things that you think you’re doing well and maybe ditch some of the other stuff.”
Someone has to answer for why “the other stuff” was allowed to stick around so long. Even casual observers could see the Eagles didn’t have the personnel to run a true under-center, play-action offense.
Defenses treated the snap under center as a neon “blitz me” sign. The quarterbacks (Hurts, Andy Dalton, Tanner McKee, and Milton ) looked uncomfortable. The protection broke down. The run game stalled. Through a 2-7 start, the offense still went under center 28% of the time.
Sunday started the same way: Milton sacked, Saquon Barkley dumped for a loss on the first two under-center snaps. Then the staff largely abandoned the concept. Milton was in the gun 94.6% of the remaining snaps.
“I think we’re able to hang on our blocks a little longer, and keeping the linebackers honest,” Jordan Mailata said. “They get trigger-happy and they just want to blitz every time… having them in gun kind of just holds them there just for a little second for us to get our double teams up.”
Heck of a throw on the run from Joe Milton PITvsPHI on CBS/Paramount+ Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/DWwabguGPB
Nothing was magically fixed. Success rate remained ugly. The offense still had stretches where it looked lost. But playing to the strengths of the people actually on the field—instead of forcing a scheme that never fit— produced a win .
That used to be a Sirianni hallmark. Why it was abandoned is the question the 2026 season autopsy has to answer.

title: Eagles Can't Ignore Budding Joe Milton-DeVonta Smith Chemistry Despite Missed Week 11 Connection
full_text:
PHILADELPHIA, P.A. — It was inches away from being the play of a game the Eagles would eventually win over the Steelers , 19-16 on Sunday. But Joe Milton threw it just out of reach of a wide-open DeVonta Smith deep down the middle of the field.
It would have been a 68-yard touchdown and would've pushed the Eagles' lead to 20-6 early in the third quarter.
The ball traveled at least 60 yards in the air. "Mr. Rocket"—Milton’s preferred nickname, so much so that he wore a diamond-studded necklace of a rocket around his neck —indeed has a rocket arm.
“I feel I couldn't be overthrown, but he did it,” Smith laughed.
There’s a sense that Smith and Milton will connect at some point on a deep throw over these final seven games. Maybe as soon as the Thanksgiving Day game against the rival Cowboys.
Maybe it’s as simple as Milton remembering his routine, which is to say his daughter’s name before he throws a pass like that. The QB says her name—Maleia—before launching a pass.
“It helps me relax,” said Milton about saying his daughter’s name. “I didn’t at that time. Other than that, I mean those moments; it just takes reps. It takes times where the pocket can be bad, or the pocket can be good at practice.
"Just being able to see the guys and knowing that he is winning reps, and to just give a little air to it. I saw it, and I just got real excited because before that play I just told him we’re gonna go home. It’s time to go home. It’s time to go score. When I’ve got the look that I wanted, I just got overly excited. But yeah, you just got to hit those, and especially in those moments.”
Milton and Smith connected when the Eagles needed them to. The third-and-six throw that delivered seven yards and a game-sealing first down with just over a minute to play certainly mattered. It was a gusty call and was executed well.
GAME OVER!!! Joe Milton to DeVonta Smith for the first down! #FlyEaglesFly win 19-16! pic.twitter.com/GfTzzhV8Oe
“Smitty obviously did a good job of running the route, catching the ball, and Joe delivered it right there,” said head coach Nick Sirianni. “We would end up giving the ball back, I don't know, with a minute left, and that's plenty of time to go to get a field goal. So, we wanted to end it with the ball in our hands.”
Added Smith: “The coaches trusted me. I knew they trusted me. I didn't know what the play call was gonna be, but I figured they were gonna put it in my hands.”
Two options were available on the play, but Milton knew right away which one he was using. After the long, overthrown pass, the QB told Smith to keep running his routes hard, and he’d be coming back to him.
“All I know is what came through the helmet, and I just knew that play was going to be the only play on this earth that mattered at the time,” Milton said. “If it was a pass play, which it was, just get a completion. It has to be in bounds just so we don’t stop the clock, obviously. When I looked to my left, I saw my guy … I went to the guy that we all know was going to catch the ball for sure.”

title: Kracz: 5 Biggest Reasons Why Eagles Finally Ended Their Losing Streak in Week 11
full_text:
PHILADELPHIA, P.A.  — The locker room music was back, thump, thumping from somewhere. So were the smiles, ear to ear, and the players’ playfulness with each other. This is what winning feels like inside the Eagles’ locker room . It had been more than two months since they experienced this.
It’s nowhere near time to make Super Bowl reservations, especially after the Giants reached six wins on Sunday, to the Eagles’ three, and maybe a win angered draftniks hoping the Eagles could get a top-five pick, but Sunday’s 19-16 win over the Steelers might silence the ‘Fire Sirianni’ crowd. Probably not, but at the very least, it ended a seven-game losing streak that began after their last win on Sept. 20.
“Definitely a good feeling to get that (losing streak) off your shoulders,” kicker Jake Elliott said. “It's something you can build on. Every week we get to a point where we feel really confident about winning a football game, and I think this is a testament to two long weeks of work and looking at ourselves in the mirror and figuring some things out. It's fun to see that come to fruition.”
There are many reasons the Eagles knocked off their cross-state rival. Here are my top five:
Elliott had attempted just eight field goals all year and missed only one. He was 4-for-4 on Sunday, making both attempts beyond 50 yards. He is 4-for-4 on 50-plus field goals this season. He had been just 5-for-13 from that distance over the last two seasons combined.
Both his 50-plus yarders against the Steelers increased the Eagles’ lead to two possessions and came in the third and fourth quarters.
Jake Elliott splits the uprights on a 55-yard field goal. PITvsPHI on CBS/Paramount+ Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/7ZASF9vxzz
“Haven't had a whole lot of chances this year, so it's always nice to be able to get a few early and kind of get into the rhythm of the game,” Elliott said. “Kind of helps it flow and just knowing what the wind's doing out there. I’m just happy to have a game like that. It feels like it’s been a while since we’ve had a bunch of attempts in a game.”
Playing his third straight game as a starting linebacker, Trotter was superb , making 13 tackles. In his three starts, he has 34 tackles, with three for loss. More starts are coming after Zack Baun was placed on injured reserve on Saturday.
“It's definitely a big opportunity,” he said. “My role has changed, and it’s increased, and I'm just trying to make sure I do my job and do my job out of the 11 guys out there and do what I gotta do to help the team win.”
Trotter played a part, but many others did, too. Pittsburgh's Jaylen Warren was averaging nearly six yards per run this season, but had 28 yards on nine carries. As a team, the Steelers averaged 116.1 yards rushing per game. They had 73 rushing yards on Sunday, and it’s never good when your soon-to-be 43-year-old quarterback, Aaron Rodgers, leads the way with 29 yards on the ground.
“Going into the game, (defensive coordinator) Vic (Fangio) told us to have them (in rushing yards) under less than... what was it?” Jihaad Campbell said, turning to Jonathan Greenard in the locker next to him.
Greenard replied, “I think under 75.”
Campbell, who had seven tackles, responded: “Whatever. It was really about having that mental toughness, that strength, whatever the circumstances were.”
Did T.J. Watt play? The rookie right tackle prevented one of the game’s all-time great sack artists from taking over the game and breathing on Joe Milton. Bell did get called for a hold when he dragged Watt to the ground, but that was better than Watt teeing off on the Eagles’ QB.
The offense still wasn’t much—the Eagles were outgained 255-214 and lost the time of possession by 11 minutes. Still, the Eagles' head coach once again found magic during the bye week, and Sirianni is now 6-0 coming out of a week off.
Some of the things that looked better: more shotgun formations, communication up front, and the offense got to the line quicker.

title: 3 Good, 2 Bad Box Score Surprises After Eagles' Victory vs. Steelers
full_text:
A third-down connection between quarterback Joe Milton and wide receiver DeVonta Smith sealed the deal. The Eagles' losing streak is over. Philadelphia snapped a seven-game skid with a 19-16 win over Pittsburgh in Week 11.
The Steelers are now 0-5 all-time in clashes at Lincoln Financial Field.
Of course, there were peaks and valleys on Sunday. Several Eagles stepped up in front of the home crowd, while a few others fell short of expectations.
Let's dive into the good and the bad box score surprises.
Talk about taking advantage of an opportunity. Linebacker Jeremiah Trotter Jr. has taken on an every-down role lately, as Zack Baun and Jihaad Campbell deal with injuries. Trotter logged a team-high 13 tackles (nine solo) against Pittsburgh. It was his third straight game with double-digit tackles.
It's worth pointing out that it was also Trotter's second straight game with at least two stuffs (tackles at or behind the line of scrimmage). The Clemson product's ferocity in run defense kept the Steelers in long third-down situations. Trotter should remain a leader on defense with Baun on injured reserve.
Philly fans waited with bated breath every time running back Saquon Barkley limped off the field in the three weeks prior to the bye. Week 11 was a different experience. Barkley looked explosive and handled a heavy workload. Backup running back Will Shipley's only carries came in the fourth quarter.
SAQUON HOUSE CALL! pic.twitter.com/e009d6X5H5
Barkley recorded 75 yards and one touchdown on 17 carries (4.4 yards per carry). It was his highest yardage total since Week 3. The veteran's 38-yard sprint to the end zone in the first quarter gave the Eagles their largest lead of the season at 13-0. It was an excellent effort that Philly needs to build on.
The Eagles were not feeling the absence of defensive tackle Jordan Davis in Week 11. That's partly because of Byron Young's performance. The 26-year-old made his presence felt with four tackles and two sacks. It was a major leap forward, considering Young entered with 2.5 sacks in 32 career games.
That's 2️⃣ for BY pic.twitter.com/V6HpQd7KuM
Young never quit during his reps, which helped him get quarterback Aaron Rodgers on the ground. He played 22 of the 71 defensive snaps (31%). Expect that mark to rise with Davis in Jacksonville. More timely sacks down the stretch will be crucial to Young's chances of getting re-signed next offseason.
Makai Lemon was drafted to be a reliable slot option in a wide receiver room filled with deep threats. There have been highlights during his rookie campaign, but his showing in Week 11 was not one of them. Lemon hauled in one of three targets for three yards. Two throws went right through his hands.
Lemon has posted five drops in his last four games. It's a surprising trend, considering he was praised for his sure-handedness at USC. That development cannot continue if the Eagles want to boost their offensive numbers . A matchup against the dismal Dallas defense on Thanksgiving gives Lemon a shot to bounce back.
Milton's first NFL win was far from perfect. He frustrated fans when he stared at his own fumble and overthrew Smith on a deep ball. The most concerning part of Milton's outing was his negligible impact on the ground. Someone with his mobility shouldn't finish with seven yards on five carries.
Milton struggled to escape the pocket, and when he did, a Pittsburgh defender quickly tracked him down. That was a very different result than his 64 rushing yards on nine carries against the Giants. Figuring out how to utilize Milton's legs should be a priority ahead of a duel with the Cowboys.

title: Eagles Week 11 Stock Market: Biggest Takeaways After Sunday's Win Over the Steelers
full_text:
PHILADELPHIA, P.A. — The Eagles finally ended the misery.
After seven consecutive losses, Philadelphia ground out a 19-16 win over Pittsburgh on Sunday at Lincoln Financial Field, snapping the skid and improving to 3-7 with their first victory since Sept. 20.⁠
Joe Milton got his first career win in his second start , going 11-for-21 for 141 yards. Saquon Barkley provided the early spark with a 38-yard touchdown run that helped build a 13-0 first-quarter lead. From there, it was mostly survival mode—the offense managed just over 214 yards total—but Jake Elliott was automatic with four field goals, including bombs from 53 and 55 yards, and the defense sacked Aaron Rodgers five times while keeping Pittsburgh in check most of the afternoon.⁠
Rodgers hit practice-squad call-up Max Hurleman for a late touchdown to cut it to 19-16, but Milton connected with DeVonta Smith on third-and-6 to run out the clock in the waning second.
The Steelers remain winless in Philadelphia since 1965.
It wasn’t pretty, but after two months of nothing, it felt like something. Here's the Week 11 Eagles stock market report: the Bulls and the Bears.
The Steelers arrived having not won in Philadelphia since 1965. That's six-plus decades, but only 11 games between the Keystone State intraconference foes. Whether it's the cheesesteaks or the Schuylkill River, Pittsburgh just can't win in this interstate rivalry, even with the Eagles entering the game on a seven-game skid.
Milton's numbers were pedestrian but his arm strength wasn't.
"Rocket Joe" was really humming in this one, eating up Makai Lemon with a Nolan Ryan fastball and overthrowing DeVonta Smith on a deep shot that traveled about 60 yards in the air. If Milton can ever figure out how to pitch , so to speak, look out. His out patterns are works of art when the accuracy is there, and he won the game with a third-down strike to Smith in the biggest moment.
The Eagles played their first game since trading nose tackle Jordan Davis to Jacksonville. Byron Young and Gabe Hall combined for three sacks, and the run defense didn't suffer at all, with Jeremiah Trotter Jr. showing off his instincts at middle linebacker and Jihaad Campbell playing well in his return.
What a play by Jeremiah Trotter Jr. for the fourth down stop PITvsPHI on CBS/Paramount+ Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/hrkAdRnrzv
Add in Ty Robinson, and the Eagles' makeshift plan at nose and shade was successful.
Both Braden Mann and Jake Elliott were big parts of the win.
Mann unleashed a 70-yard bomb that was placed to pin the returner on the sideline with near perfection. In four opportunities, Mann finished with a 59.3 gross average, with two punts placed inside the 20. Elliott was responsible for 13 of the Eagles' 19 points, hitting all four field goals and two 50-plus kicks.
The offense generated some explosive plays, including the 38-yard touchdown run by Barkley, and Milton throws of 38 yards and 29 yards to Dallas Goedert and Darius Cooper, respectively. Overall, though, the moribund Steelers offense still outgained the Eagles by a 251 to 214 margin.
Philadelphia's structured offense remains a work in progress, to be kind.
The Eagles' two longest and fastest cornerbacks struggled. Riq Woolen was benched at one point after having some tackling issues, while Kelee Ringo could not track a Rodgers touchdown throw to Max Hurleman that kept Pittsburgh alive late in the fourth quarter.
Eagles defensive line coach Clint Hurtt got into a bit of a dust-up with strength and conditioning coach Fernando Noriega on the sidelines. It was quickly settled, but it shows how frustration can boil over during significant struggles.

title: Aaron Rodgers Calls Out Mike McCarthy, Reveals Shocking Stories of HC
full_text:
Aaron Rodgers offered full insight into Mike McCarthy's tenure with the Pittsburgh Steelers after being benched ahead of the team's Week 12 game against the Denver Broncos.
During an appearance on "The Pat McAfee Show" , Rodgers stated that McCarthy came into a quarterbacks meeting late last Wednesday on November 18 before the Steelers' Week 11 game against the Philadelphia Eagles and then started snoring several minutes later.
Rodgers added that McCarthy missed multiple meetings and one of Pittsburgh's walkthroughs in the lead-up to the Eagles game, which the Steelers ultimately dropped by a score of 19-16 at Lincoln Financial Field.
The 42-year-old quarterback added that at halftime, McCarthy broke down the huddle with a "1,2,3, Packers!" chant.
“I think the nail of the coffin was at halftime, offense on one side defense on the other side," Rodgers said. "Without even a heads up, he says ‘1, 2, 3, Packers!’
Rodgers didn't hold anything back when talking about McCarthy and the general feel around the building since the latter has taken over as the Steelers' head coach after replacing Mike Tomlin in January.
It remains to be seen how the rest of this saga plays out, but Rodgers made his feelings and opinions crystal-clear.
Rodgers, of course, has a long history with McCarthy, as the quarterback and head coach were together from 2006 to 2018 with the Green Bay Packers.
While the pair did win Super Bowl LXV over the Steelers in 2010, their relationship wasn't exactly smooth despite Green Bay's success with the pair in place.
In fact, Rodgers stated that McCarthy believes he got him fired back in 2018 and told a staff member that he still doesn't forgive him for doing so. He also made it clear that the "ship has definitely sailed" in terms of returning to Pittsburgh at this point.
From stating that he learned that he would be inactive against the Broncos from Pat Freiermuth and not McCarthy to admitting that he has joked around with general manager Omar Khan about McCarthy falling asleep, Rodgers painted a picture of what feels like a broken operation.
Rodgers also insinuated that McCarthy didn't feel like he needed to get to know and talk to some of the Steelers' defensive players more than he already had, which is quite the departure from how Mike Tomlin approached the job and is overall an easy way to break apart a locker room.
There's multiple sides to every story, and McCarthy has yet to give his perspective, but things look pretty bleak as of right now all while Pittsburgh is still in an AFC Wild Card spot at 6-4.
Jack is a New Jersey native who graduated from the University of Pittsburgh as a Media & Professional Communications major in 2024 who is now covering the Pittsburgh Steelers and New York Yankees for On SI.

title: Steelers Players Not Happy About Aaron Rodgers Benching
full_text:
The Pittsburgh Steelers' decision to bench Aaron Rodgers and name Mason Rudolph their starting quarterback ahead of Week 12's showdown with the Denver Broncos came as a surprise to everyone.
It doesn't appear as though the Steelers' pivot from Rodgers to Rudolph was well-received within the locker room either. As reported by The Athletic's Mike DeFabo and confirmed by sources to Steelers On SI, head coach Mike McCarthy officially spoke with the team regarding their resolution on that front during a scheduled 8 a.m. team meeting on the morning of November 25.
It didn't seem to resonate well , with DeFabo noting that it sounds like it was "not a popular decision" in the locker room. Steelers on SI's Noah Strackbein reported that Rodgers was not at the facility for that meeting either.
Aaron Rodgers was not at the team facility this morning for the #Steelers 8am meeting, sources confirm
A spark is necessary for Pittsburgh's offense after posting a combined 477 yards of total offense in back-to-back losses to the Cincinnati Bengals and Philadelphia Eagles following its Week 9 bye.
With that being said, however, the timing and way in which the Steelers have gone about making the change to Rudolph and breaking the news that Rodgers was being benched almost seemed rushed, disjointed and like it came together quickly.
NFL Network's Mike Garafolo noted that the team went from "adamantly standing by Aaron Rodgers and tweaking the play-calling process in hope of providing a spark to turning to Mason Rudolph for said spark in a matter of hours," while the Pittsburgh Post-Gazette's Gerry Dulac reported that the situation had been "brewing for a while" before reaching a point of no return once he was benched.
Regardless, it still feels like there's more to the story behind the scenes that led to this decision being reached.
Rodgers was largely a shell of his former self for the Steelers this season, but that doesn't make the news any less jarring for both him and the rest of the team.
Given how well-liked he is in the locker room and the fact that he's an NFL legend, Pittsburgh turning its back on him is going to have reverberating effects.
Rudolph is an experienced veteran and should be able to steer the ship in Mike McCarthy 's offense, though it wouldn't come as a surprise if the coaching staff has a hard time getting the team to fully buy in over the final seven weeks of the regular season despite being 6-4 and in the final Wild Card spot in the AFC.

title: Could Drew Allar, Will Howard Start for Steelers This Season?
full_text:
The Pittsburgh Steelers' decision to bench Aaron Rodgers less than 72 hours before kicking off their Week 12 game against the Denver Broncos was nothing less than a total surprise.
Despite having a 60.9 percent completion rate that ranks as the 10th-worst among qualified passers to go with the third-worst EPA of any quarterback at -66.2 (per Next Gen Stats ), there was no real reason to believe the Steelers would move off of Rodgers as their starter and turn to Mason Rudolph.
The fallout from Pittsburgh's stunning resolution has yet to fully play out. With the 42-year-old in his final season, however, it feels like his relationship with the organization may now be completely severed, even if the team internally believes that it could still revisit their decision (as noted by NFL insider Jordan Schultz ).
If the Rudolph experiment doesn't work out for the Steelers and Rodgers is essentially out of the picture one way or another, is it possible either Will Howard or Drew Allar could supplant the former at some point this season?
If Rodgers sticks around on the Steelers' 53-man roster instead of leaving the team either by being released or retiring and thus is available to step back in for Rudolph if things go awry, neither Howard or Allar stands much of a chance to make their regular season debuts in 2026.
Should Rodgers and Pittsburgh part ways or the 42-year-old simply just be inactive for the remainder of the campaign, though, than a real conversation could be had about one of the franchise's young signal callers potentially earning a shot to prove themselves down the stretch.
At 6-4 and in possession of the final Wild Card spot in the AFC for the time being, head coach Mike McCarthy is likely going to stick with Rudolph for as long as he can.
The 31-year-old is a high-floor backup with 19 career starts under his belt who can manage a game and has seemingly impressed Pittsburgh's first-year coaching staff at every turn.
Rudolph is far more experienced and steady at this stage of his career than Howard and Allar are, and McCarthy probably believes he gives the Steelers their best shot at remaining competitive and in the playoff hunt moving forward.
At the same time, the decision to go with Rudolph might have to do with the fact that the team is in a short week before facing Denver and doesn't want to play Howard or Allar under those circumstances.
There's a very realistic scenario where Rudolph falters, though, as he's thrown just 56 passes since returning to Pittsburgh on a two-year deal worth $7.5 million ahead of the 2025 season and doesn't offer any real upside.
Should the wheels fall completely off over the next handful of weeks with Rudolph at the helm as the Steelers face the Broncos (Week 12), Houston Texans (Week 13), Jacksonville Jaguars (Week 14) and Baltimore Ravens (Week 15), that's when another quarterback change could come and either Howard or Allar are named the starter.
Allar is quite easily the higher-upside option between himself and Howard. The third-round rookie out of Penn State has a rocket of an arm and has made strides since entering the NFL, namely in terms of his footwork and throwing mechanics.
He showed off his potential during the preseason too, throwing for 351 yards and two touchdowns on  54 attempts, but 2026 was always supposed to be somewhat of a redshirt year for Allar.
He still has a ways to go in his development, and while he's more exciting of a player than Howard, the latter is the safer option at this juncture.
A 2025 sixth-round pick, Howard is simply further along than Allar in their respective progressions at the NFL level. He had a rougher go of it in the preseason, throwing three interceptions, though he's more polished mechanically and has picked up more experience dating back to college than Allar has.
Allar is a safer bet to be the Steelers' starter in 2027, but Howard is likely in better shape to do so in 2026.
Jack is a New Jersey native who graduated from the University of Pittsburgh as a Media & Professional Communications major in 2024 who is now covering the Pittsburgh Steelers and New York Yankees for On SI.

title: Steelers' Mike McCarthy Finally Proves Whose Team It Is
full_text:
PITTSBURGH -- The Pittsburgh Steelers are in a difficult place after dropping back-to-back losses. Is their season over?
Depending on how you view the Steelers' most recent games, you may draw the conclusion that this team has been exposed for what they are - a not very good one. Alternatively, you might have viewed the past two weeks as a brief misstep on the path to the postseason.
The truth is, both arguments are right. The Steelers are 6-4 heading into their Week 12 contest, leaving them still in the postseason race. Still, they are far from a Super Bowl contender given their current performance. It's now up to the Steelers to adjust and take the correct road moving forward, which makes head coach Mike McCarthy's decision to start quarterback Mason Rudolph against the Denver Broncos especially interesting.
The move might not restore the team's season, but McCarthy just made it abundantly clear who is running the ship in Pittsburgh.
pic.twitter.com/F2qo4OawcY
Benching a future Hall of Fame quarterback is a terrifying decision. You have to contend with the ramifications of this change and weigh your options. There's no clean way forward as the Steelers try to claw out of their recent two-game losing skid.
But McCarthy had to do something. He's had to stand in front of the media for 12 weeks, trying to justify and rationalize why this passing game has been so miserable despite an offseason filled with promises of change.
All the while, the outward appearance has been that this team is run by, and built to appease, Aaron Rodgers. The team didn't go out and trade for a talented wide receiver ahead of the NFL Trade Deadline, and that was chalked up to no one being a good fit with Rodgers. They've already elevated players like Brandon Johnson and Brandon Smith multiple times due to their "connection" with Rodgers, only to produce nothing when called upon. They signed free agent Marquez Valdes-Scantling to the practice squad.
Those were all seen as moves to appease Rodgers, and it led them nowhere successful.
McCarthy drew a red line after another disappointing performance, and it's clear that he is taking control.
It might have come out in a late-night news dump, which was convenient timing, but the change happened nonetheless. McCarthy pivoted away from the quarterback he won a Super Bowl with. He benched the quarterback, who returned for one final go, in order to reunite with McCarthy.
That might not be a universally revered move, and it might not solve the offense's issues, but it's exactly what the head coach needed to do.
This could very well be the end of the road for Aaron Rodgers. Not only is Rodgers out of the starting lineup in Week 12, the team's announcement specified that he will be inactive against the Broncos. That means second-year QB Will Howard will backup Rudolph, while rookie Drew Allar will serve as the emergency third quarterback, giving him a first chance to wear full pads and uniform on game day.
That specification about Rodgers is telling. The Steelers didn't declare that he was injured or announce some sort of team-imposed discipline.
Without a clear explanation from Rodgers or the organization, we are left to speculate on the reason why and where this leaves the 42-year-old QB moving forward.
One option could be to release the future Hall of Famer, if things are reaching that bad of a situation. That could lead to Rodgers retiring a bit earlier than expected, or maybe joining another playoff-hopeful squad. Another, less severe option, is to sit Rodgers for a week and then reconsider the quarterback plan for Week 13 and the rest of the regular season.
Either way, the Steelers won't have Rodgers in uniform in Week 12. As they try to get back in the win column, the player who we all thought was running this team is riding the pine, while the head coach has finally taken control of the organization.
Jacob is a featured writer covering the Pittsburgh Steelers for Steelers On SI and the NHL for Breakaway On SI. He also co-hosts the All Steelers Talk podcast. Previous work covering the NHL for Inside the Penguins and The Hockey News.

title: Steelers Bench Aaron Rodgers, Name Mason Rudolph Starting QB
full_text:
The Pittsburgh Steelers dropped some major news ahead of their Week 12 game against the Denver Broncos .
In an announcement posted by the Steelers on X from senior director of communications Burt Lauten, the team stated that starting quarterback Aaron Rodgers will not be active vs. Denver while Mason Rudolph will take over in his place.
"The Pittsburgh Steelers have named Mason Rudolph the starting quarterback for the game this Friday against the Denver Broncos," the team said .
"Aaron Rodgers will be inactive for the game on Friday."
pic.twitter.com/F2qo4OawcY
The Ringer's Tom Pelissero reported that sources told him that "this was a coach's decision" while also noting that the 42-year-old may have played the final snaps of his Hall of Fame career.
Over 10 starts for Pittsburgh this season after re-signing with the franchise in May, Rodgers has thrown for 2,241 yards, 16 touchdowns and six interceptions.
The Steelers' offense has really struggled since returning from their Week 9 bye, however, dropping back-to-back games to the Cincinnati Bengals and Philadelphia Eagles in the process.
There hadn't been any prior indication that Pittsburgh was considering such a massive change at quarterback in the middle of a playoff push, but they've now done so by turning to Rudolph and benching Rodgers in what he's declared will be his final season before retirement.
When Mike Tomlin stepped down after 19 years as the Steelers' head coach back in January, it sure felt like that closed the door on any chance of Rodgers returning to the franchise.
Once Pittsburgh hired Mike McCarthy as Tomlin's replacement, however, those circumstances changed in an instant.
McCarthy had served as Rodgers' head coach with the Green Bay Packers from 2006 to 2018, and the pair won Super Bowl XLV together over Pittsburgh in 2010.
Once there was an opportunity for Rodgers to reunite with McCarthy, a second go at it with the Steelers became the clear answer for the 42-year-old in terms of his destination for the 2026 campaign.
He eventually signed a one-year deal worth a base value of $22.5 million, and the hope was that he'd help Pittsburgh once again contend for the playoffs.
While the team currently holds claim to the final Wild Card spot in the AFC with a 6-4 record while Rodgers has been at the helm, he's pretty clearly a shell of his former self. His 60.9 percent completion rate is the 10th-worst among 32 qualified passers, and his -66.2 EPA ranks as the third-worst under that same criteria (per Next Gen Stats ).
Rodgers had only completed just 11 of his 52 passing attempts that went for 20-plus yards (per SumerSports ), and his lack of mobility at this stage of his career hampered him significantly when it came to evading pressure in the pocket.
McCarthy told reporters during his weekly press conference that "Aaron Rodgers is our quarterback" and thus left little doubt about his status as the starter.
Now, however, Rudolph has been called upon to spark the Steelers' offense after the unit recorded a combined 477 yards over its last two games while Rodgers will be sidelined.
NFL insider Jordan Schultz reported that Pittsburgh "intends to revisit" its decision to bench Rodgers, though going back on that choice and potentially turning back to him if things don't work out with Rudolph would be far easier said than done.
Never say never, but the organization's resolution in this situation feels like it may have drawn a finite line in the sand.
The complete fallout remains to be seen. For now, Rodgers is set to be inactive and has been completely stripped of his duties for the Steelers while Rudolph gets the starting nod as Will Howard likely steps into the backup role and Drew Allar potentially moves up to No. 3 on the depth chart.

title: Steelers Injury News: Good and Bad News Before Broncos Game
full_text:
The Pittsburgh Steelers ' first injury report ahead of a Black Friday matinee against the Denver Broncos in Week 12 featured both positive and negative news.
EDGE rusher Nick Herbig (hip/ribs) was a limited participant after missing each practice leading up to the Steelers' Week 11 game against the Philadelphia Eagles, which he was ultimately inactive for.
On the flip side, wide receiver Ben Skowronek (calf) was a non-participant.
He had previously missed three-straight contests through Pittsburgh's Week 9 bye with his calf injury before returning in Week 10. It appears that it remains an ongoing issue for Skowronek, however.
Elsewhere on the injury report, wide receiver Michael Pittman Jr. (foot) and offensive lineman Gennings Dunker (knee) were full participants in the middle of their 21-day practice windows while remaining on the reserve/injured list.
Additionally, Alex Highsmith (ankle) did not participate, and it seems as though he'll likely be out vs. Denver after head coach Mike McCarthy stated that it's "going to be tough for him to make it this week" in his press conference on November 23.
While Highsmith didn't play for long against Philadelphia, it seems like he and Herbig are heading towards essentially swapping statuses essentially against the Broncos.
Herbig, as previously mentioned, did not play vs. the Eagles while Highsmith was active and logged two sacks before going down with his ankle injury in the first quarter and not returning.
Now, Herbig is making progress towards a return to the field. It's no guarantee that he'll end up playing against a Denver team that's 8-2 and on a six-game win streak, but at least he's moving in the right direction in his rehab.
Highsmith doesn't appear to have much of a shot at suiting up, as McCarthy noted, though his game designation won't be set until later in the week on November 26 once the final injury report is put out.
Even if Herbig does play, he probably won't be 100 percent from a health perspective, meaning the Steelers will need T.J. Watt and Jack Sawyer to step up.
Just when it looked like Pittsburgh might have a fully healthy wide receiver room for the first time since Week 4, Skowronek's availability vs. Denver may now be up in the air.
Pittman Jr. appears as though he'll return from IR in time to play against the Broncos, which is huge news for a Steelers offense that's been reeling since returning from their bye week.
With Roman Wilson having been activated ahead of the Eagles game, Pittsburgh should have its top four receivers active in Week 12 with him, Pittman Jr. (if he is in fact back in action), Germie Bernard and DK Metcalf after the latter was not suspended following his ejection vs. Philadelphia.
If Skowronek isn't active against Denver, that would be more of a loss for the Steelers' special teams unit rather than their offense considering he's logged just 66 offensive snaps this season (per Pro Football Focus ).

title: Steelers Re-Sign Veteran WR to Practice Squad
full_text:
PITTSBURGH -- The Pittsburgh Steelers brought a familiar face back to the organization after recently releasing him.
As the Steelers prepare for a shortened week for their Week 12 opponent, the Denver Broncos, wide receiver Brandon Smith was back on the practice field. The Steelers released him from the active roster ahead of their Week 11 contest against the Philadelphia Eagles, but the team announced they re-signed him to the practice squad.
Smith played in five games with the Steelers this season, totaling four receptions for 39 yards. He was elevated three times from the practice squad before the Steelers signed him to the active roster.
We have signed WR Brandon Smith to the Practice Squad. @BordasLaw https://t.co/wG6JyhDyjQ
After the Steelers released him, Smith had the chance to join any other NFL franchise that wanted to sign him. Instead, he signs back with the Pittsburgh practice squad, and that comes with a bit of context moving forward.
Since he has already been elevated three times from the practice squad, the Steelers cannot elevate him without signing him again to the active roster.
Moving forward, that means Smith is not going to be the first receiver who gets the nod. Over the next few weeks, that honor will likely go to Max Hurleman , who recorded 61 receiving yards in his NFL debut.
But if injuries mount once again, Smith will be an option for this team.
Smith is in his third NFL season, and his experience in the league and with Steelers quarterback Aaron Rodgers made him an easy choice to bring back to the practice squad. Smith began his NFL career with the New York Jets in 2024, the final season Rodgers played with the Jets. The two got to know each other briefly during that preseason and training camp, and they reunited in Pittsburgh last season. In total, he's played in eight NFL games, with all of his recorded statistics coming as a member of the Steelers.
Smith impressed during the 2025 preseason as well, which earned him a practice squad spot and a Reserves/Futures contract with the Steelers for the 2026 season.
Once again, he was a standout player during this past training camp and preseason, and it earned him the right to be an early call-up for the Steelers. While he hasn't been able to put up eye-popping numbers, Smith has earned the trust of the quarterback and coaching staff. In a pinch, it's a very reasonable expectation to believe Smith could get signed to the active roster again before the 2026 season comes to an end.
Jacob is a featured writer covering the Pittsburgh Steelers for Steelers On SI and the NHL for Breakaway On SI. He also co-hosts the All Steelers Talk podcast. Previous work covering the NHL for Inside the Penguins and The Hockey News.

title: Steelers Named a Team to Watch for Brandon Aiyuk
full_text:
After not acquiring any wide receivers at the trade deadline, one NFL insider believes the Pittsburgh Steelers could potentially check in on free agent Brandon Aiyuk .
On his self-titled podcast with Ty Schmit of 'The Pat McAfee Show", ESPN's Adam Schefter stated that it would make sense for the Steelers to register interest in Aiyuk, who was recently released by the San Francisco 49ers.
"How many times have we heard the Pittsburgh Steelers connected to wide receivers the last couple years, including for Brandon Aiyuk?" Schefter said . "If the guy that you considered trading for at one point now were a free agent, would it not make sense that the Pittsburgh Steelers would check in?"
It's safe to say the Steelers dodged a bullet after their pursuit of Aiyuk via trade in the summer of 2024 fell flat.
Instead, Aiyuk inked a four-year, $120 million extension with San Francisco before proceeding to play in just seven more games for the franchise.
He tore his MCL and ACL in Week 7 vs. the Kansas City Chiefs in 2024 and did not play at all in 2025.
The 49ers later voided the guaranteed money in his deal for the 2026 season back in November 2025 (per ESPN's Nick Wagoner ) because Aiyuk was not meeting the requirements of his contract.
San Francisco also placed him on the reserve/left squad list last December, and Aiyuk's social media activity drew attention for all the wrong reasons, too.
From posting a video of himself chanting "Go Commanders!" despite being under contract with the 49ers to having a warrant for his arrest issued after posting a video of himself speeding past Levi's Stadium, Aiyuk became a major headache for San Francisco.
That saga finally came to an end with his release after he was reinstated by the NFL on November 9, and Pittsburgh does profile as a logical landing spot for his services.
Whether or not it makes sense for the Steelers to seriously pursue him, though, is a whole different question.
While Roman Wilson (finger) returned from the reserve/injured list in Week 11 vs. the Philadelphia Eagles, while it appears Michael Pittman Jr. (foot) will be activated in time to face the Denver Broncos on Black Friday in Week 12, the Steelers could still use wide receiver help.
DK Metcalf has struggled mightily for Pittsburgh, as he's on pace for a career-low 738 yards and has a catch rate of 48 percent over 75 targets on the season.
While he will not be suspended following his ejection against the Eagles after committing two unsportsmanlike conduct penalties, Metcalf has been a massive net negative for the Steelers. It doesn't help that he still has three seasons left on a four-year, $132 million contract, either.
With some of those issues the organization is currently dealing with in regards to Metcalf, it's worth wondering if they'd be willing to take on all of the risks Aiyuk poses given his recent off-field history.
The 28-year-old also hasn't played in two years after his major knee injury. He has a history of playing at a star level, as he recorded a combined 2,357 yards between the 2022 and 2023 campaigns, but he's a long way removed from those years at this point.
As a possible practice squad addition to start out, adding a player with as high of a ceiling as Aiyuk could help Pittsburgh's offense kick back into gear.
There might be too many hurdles to clear for the Steelers, however, and signing Aiyuk is something the organization may avoid as a result.
Jack is a New Jersey native who graduated from the University of Pittsburgh as a Media & Professional Communications major in 2024 who is now covering the Pittsburgh Steelers and New York Yankees for On SI.

title: Big Ben, Antonio Brown, Four Other Steelers Advance in Hall of Fame Voting
full_text:
PITTSBURGH -- Six former members of the Pittsburgh Steelers organization, as well as a current coach, have moved forward in the Pro Football Hall of Fame voting process.
The Steelers are a perennial presence in football's greatest honor, with 32 legends of the franchise enshrined in the Hall of Fame, and next year's class could increase that number to 33.
The Steelers PR Department shared that six former players, quarterback Ben Roethlisberger, wide receivers Antonio Brown and Hines Ward, center Maurkice Pouncey, linebacker James Harrison and defensive lineman L.C. Greenwood, and current offensive line assistant coach Jahri Evans, have all advanced in the recently revised process for electing the 2027 Hall of Fame class.
The Steelers' all-time leading passer is now one step closer to earning his gold jacket. A two-time Super Bowl winner finished his career with 64,088 passing yards and 418 touchdown passes. He currently ranks seventh in NFL history in career passing yards and ninth in career touchdown passes.
Since his retirement, the Steelers have been lost in the desert. The franchise hasn't found a suitable starting quarterback to take his place.
One of the most curious cases the Pro Football Hall of Fame must deliberate on is the case of Antonio Brown. One of the most prolific, productive and polarizing wide receivers in NFL history, will the HOF give more credence to the on-field production or his off-field issues? Depending on which way they go, it could delay his inevitable enshrinement in the Hall of Fame.
One of the players most overdue for Hall of Fame enshrinement is L.C. Greenwood. One of the key members of the famous Steel Curtain defense in the 1970s, he remains one of the biggest snubs, especially as so many members of that unit have been rightfully honored.
The same could be said for Hines Ward. A four-time Pro Bowler and a Super Bowl MVP, Ward is the Steelers' all-time receptions, receiving yards and receiving touchdown leader. He was the heartbeat of two Super Bowl-winning teams, and racked up over 12,000 receiving yards in his career while being one of the best run-blocking receivers in NFL history.
The Steelers had one of the most unique pass rushers in NFL history when James Harrison was on their defense. According to the Steelers' PR Department, he is the "only player in NFL history to win multiple Super Bowls, earn NFL Defensive Player of the Year Award and register 80.0+ sacks and 30+ forced fumbles."
Jacob is a featured writer covering the Pittsburgh Steelers for Steelers On SI and the NHL for Breakaway On SI. He also co-hosts the All Steelers Talk podcast. Previous work covering the NHL for Inside the Penguins and The Hockey News.

title: Will Gennings Dunker Ever Start for Steelers This Season?
full_text:
With Mason McCormick potentially out for at least the remainder of the regular season due to an ankle injury he suffered in Week 10 against the Cincinnati Bengals, left guard has now become somewhat of a problem area for the Pittsburgh Steelers.
Spencer Anderson , who opened the year as the Steelers' starting right guard before being replaced by Brock Hoffman in Week 3, stepped in as McCormick's replacement in Week 11 vs. the Philadelphia Eagles.
In a disappointing 19-16 loss to its Keystone State foes that had previously been in the midst of a seven-game losing streak, however, Anderson didn't look up to par at left guard and gave up a sack to go with three total pressures (per Pro Football Focus ).
If Pittsburgh looks to make a change at left guard in the near future in hopes of preventing the wheels from completely falling off, rookie third-round pick Gennings Dunker is among the top options to step in for Anderson.
Considering he still hasn't been activated from the reserve/injured list with an MCL sprain he suffered ahead of Week 3, however, is there a real chance Dunker earns an opportunity to play at all for the Steelers in 2026?
While the 23-year-old started at tackle during his collegiate career at Iowa, moving to guard once he arrived to the NFL was always the most sensible path.
While Dunker is a mauler and has the requisite power and strength to move defenders in the run game, his lack of athleticism and technique as a pass protector made it to where he wasn't likely to stick as a viable option at tackle right off the bat.
Those concerns in pass protection popped up for Dunker during training camp with the Steelers. While his stay in Latrobe this past summer wasn't smooth in that department, though, he did show some promising signs of growth once the preseason arrived by giving up only two pressures and zero sacks over 55 pass-blocking reps ( per PFF ).
He was never viewed as much of a factor in Pittsburgh's position battle at right guard between Anderson and Hoffman, but the expectation was never that he'd enter the regular season as the starter there either.
While Dunker's progression did take a hit once he suffered his MCL sprain, his 21-day practice window was opened last week after McCormick went down.
He's a tantalizing candidate to play at left guard to finish out the campaign, though head coach Mike McCarthy made it clear that he still has a ways to go as a pass protector.
"I think the biggest thing, if you go back to camp, early when we got back, really felt physically, [Dunker] obviously is what you are looking for. His run game is probably where it needs to be, but if he's like most guys coming out of college, he needs to really continue to work on the pass [protection]," McCarthy said during his weekly press conference .
Just based on McCarthy's comments, it feels rather evident that the Steelers believe Dunker has plenty of room ahead of him for growth in pass protection.
It's hard to make up for lost time, especially as a rookie. It's not totally out of the question that Dunker will be called upon when/if he's activated from IR, though expecting him to supplant Anderson at left guard feels unwise at the moment despite the latter's struggles.
Though it's far too early to get a clear read on what direction Pittsburgh might take its roster next offseason, it sure feels like Dunker's going to have at least a solid chance of winning the starting job at right guard.
He's the only option at the position who is currently on the team's 53-man roster and also under contract for the 2027 season. The Steelers will surely look to bring in competition for Dunker, whether that be via the 2027 NFL Draft, re-signing one of Anderson or Hoffman or perhaps an outside free agent, but he has to be viewed as a favorite to fill that role as of right now.
The key for Dunker is improving in pass protection, as McCarthy noted. If he can do that and grow into more of a force as a run blocker, he might just be a long-term solution on the interior of Pittsburgh's offensive line.
Jack is a New Jersey native who graduated from the University of Pittsburgh as a Media & Professional Communications major in 2024 who is now covering the Pittsburgh Steelers and New York Yankees for On SI.

title: Seahawks Land 'Legitimate Red-Zone Weapon' in New 2027 NFL Mock Draft
full_text:
As was the case in 2025, the Seattle Seahawks aerial attack is overly dependent on Jaxon Smith-Njigba. The reigning NFL Offensive Player of the Year is having a remarkable season with 79 receptions for 1,207 yards and 10 touchdowns. Those numbers would make for a great season, but JSN has seven games to add to those totals.
To highlight how much he’s leaned upon, the second-most receiving yards on the team belong to Cooper Kupp, who has just 272 yards. A.J. Barner follows with 229 yards, then it’s Rashid Shaheed who has 17 receptions for 171 yards and has yet to score a receiving touchdown.
It seems clear that the $51 million bet on Shaheed has not paid off, which is why NFL Draft On SI’s Justin Melo has the Seahawks looking for help at receiver in his latest 2027 NFL mock draft.
With their top selection in Melo’s mock, the Seahawks wind up with Indiana wide receiver Nick Marsh . Melo says Marsh is not only someone who can pick up yards after the catch, but he also called him a “legitimate red-zone weapon.”
"The Seattle Seahawks offense is made up of Jaxon Smith-Njigba and friends. Cooper Kupp is aging, and Rashid Shaheed is disappointing on his bloated contract. Nick Marsh is the best run-after-catch threat in this wide receiver class, and he's a legitimate red-zone weapon, too," Melo wrote.
Marsh began his career at Michigan State where he had 100 receptions for 1,311 yards and nine touchdowns in two years. He transferred to Indiana this offseason and has taken his game to a new level.
In 11 games, Marsh has 44 receptions for 791 yards and nine touchdowns. He’s proven to be a big-play wideout as well, averaging 18.0 yards per reception for the Hoosiers.
Adding Marsh would give Seattle an instant upgrade at the WR2 position. It would also bring up an interesting conversation regarding Shaheed.
While he signed a three-year extension this offseason, there is an out in his contract in 2027 ( according to Spotrac ). If Seattle exercised that, they would be left with $16 million in dead cap space, but they would avoid another $11.75 million in guaranteed money.
Unless they truly value Shaheed as a returner, that could be the path they choose to take.
