title: How the Seahawks' Defense Plays Better vs. 49ers in Week 12
full_text:
From now until the end of the season, the Seattle Seahawks (6-4) can’t afford any more mistakes as they push for the playoffs. The Seahawks are coming out of the bye week and into their next toughest game of the season. Seattle is set to go on the road to take on their NFC Divisional rivals, the San Francisco 49ers (9-1).
The 49ers are coming off a 35-10  win over the Minnesota Vikings this past Sunday Night Football. It was a game where the Vikings showed their defense isn’t as dominant as many experts previously believed. The Seahawks’ Dark Side Defense could have an opportunity to take down the 49ers’ offense in Week 12 after learning from the Vikings’ mistakes.
​The Vikings' defense was only able to account for four quarterback hits and one sack against the 49ers' offensive line. These aren't great numbers considering the Vikings like to send constant blitzes. The Vikings are one of the most blitz-heavy teams in the league at 67.4%. The next closest team is the Tampa Bay Buccaneers at 37.2%.
Minnesota gave up certain coverages on the field in favor of a quick pressure, but quarterback Brock Purdy and the players watched a lot of film to understand what spots would be less covered.
​The Seahawks are just in the middle of the league in blitzing percentages at 26%. Seattle is just second in the league in pressure percentage (30.2%), just below Minnesota at 34.4%, but the Seahawks don’t have to send constant blitzes . Four players for Seattle have, at least, three sacks this season and three have more than 10 quarterback hits.
They possess solid pass rushers from the interior defensive line, the edge and from the linebacker/defensive back zone. The main goal is to pressure Purdy constantly, but ensure the defense doesn’t give up spacing and allow easy first downs.
​The 49ers have one of the most dynamic offenses in the league at the start of the season. They have since traded for veteran wide receiver Kennan Allen from the Indianapolis Colts during the NFL Trade Deadline. The Seahawks now have to prepare to cover Allen, wide receiver Mike Evans, wide receiver Deebo Samuel, tight end George Kittle and running back Christian McCaffrey. Evans caught seven receptions for 113 yards and a touchdown in Week 5 against the Seahawks.
​This is a game where the Dark Side Defense has to remain vigilant and play strong contested coverages. Second-year nickelback Nick Emmanwori could be the key asset for the Seahawks as they could switch coverage schemes on him to ultimately confuse the 49ers’ offense.
The Seahawks also possess reliable corners in Devon Witherspoon, Josh Jobe (who is looking to redeem himself from Week 5) and Nehemiah Pritchett. They possess a potential All-Pro in safety Julian Love and an underrated starter in Ty Okada.

title: 3 Seahawk Role Players Who Could Have Big Stretch Runs
full_text:
If the Seattle Seahawks are to make it to the dance this season , we’re going to need big-time production from our top players. I think we all understand that. But who are the lesser-known pieces who could tip the scales? Some players that didn’t do much over the first ten games that now need to put up something more? Let’s take a look at three candidates.
I don’t think this edge group is built to survive with only three useful players, even with the occasional help from Leonard Williams and Nick Emmanwori . DeMarcus Lawrence, and even Uchenna Nwosu, aren’t meant to play a ton of snaps at this point in their careers. In order to bridge the gap, Dante Fowler Jr must take the field and do something for this team.
Of course, it’s not necessarily up to him if he can take the field. Mike Macdonald hasn’t been giving him a lot of opportunities. I have to believe that, at some point, there will be a commitment to at least getting him 16-20 snaps a game, for the sake of our starters not getting overloaded. And he’ll need to do something with those snaps for this to work.
It’s a little questionable if AJ Barner qualifies as a role player given how much he plays. But despite his constant presence on the field, he’s currently on pace to have less than 400 receiving yards, and he’s got one receiving touchdown after ten games. He’s been a capable blocker, but the numbers suggest he’s far from any sort of star player.
We know he’s capable of much more than that. Last year, on a team with Jaxon Smith-Njigba that was near the bottom of the league in passing attempts, Barner had over 50 catches for 500 yards. Many thought he’d take a step forward in 2026. If he wants to take that step forward belatedly, it would go a long way in balancing out this offense a little bit.
I’m double-dipping on secondary pass catchers because it feels critical that we start getting a little more out of these receiving options. And in the case of Shaheed , who got his meaty contract extension in the offseason, it seems especially critical. The offense needs more big plays, and Shaheed is a big play threat. Find him and get it to him.
But there’s a layer beyond even that. Shaheed has yet to bust any big plays on kick or punt returns this year. To be clear, I don’t blame him at all for this. The fault clearly lies with the blocking team, who have been unable to set the table for Shaheed at all this season. But if and when things turn around, it’ll be Shaheed with the ball in his hands, getting the credit.

title: NFC Playoff Picture: Seahawks Face Huge Stakes in Week 12 vs. 49ers
full_text:
The Seattle Seahawks still find themselves on the outside looking in on the NFC playoff picture after the bye week.
The team saw its chances of making it to the postseason dwindle to 44 percent, but they are still very much in control of their own destiny. A win against the San Francisco 49ers in Week 12 will increase their chances of making it to the postseason, but they still have a lot of work to do. Here's a look at how the playoff standings look going into Week 12.
1. San Francisco 49ers (9-1) — NFC West Leader 2. Detroit Lions (8-2) — NFC North Leader 3. New York Giants (6-3-1) — NFC East Leader 4. Carolina Panthers (5-5) — NFC South Leader 5. Chicago Bears (8-2) — Wild Card 1 6. Minnesota Vikings (7-3) — Wild Card 2 7. Green Bay Packers (6-4) — Wild Card 3 -------------------------------------------------- In the Hunt: 8. Seattle Seahawks (6-4) 9. Los Angeles Rams (6-4) 10. Dallas Cowboys (5-6) 11. Washington Commanders (4-5-1) 12. Tampa Bay Buccaneers (3-7) 13. Atlanta Falcons (3-7) 14. New Orleans Saints (3-7) 15. Philadelphia Eagles (3-7) 16. Arizona Cardinals (3-8)
There are several ways the NFC standings can change after the holiday week. In tonight's special Wednesday Night Football game between the Green Bay Packers and Los Angeles Rams, the tie between the two squads will be broken.
If the Packers lose, it opens the door for the Seahawks to climb back into that final wild card spot.
If they were to beat the San Francisco 49ers, who are in first place with a 9-1 record, and the Niners lose, it gives the Lions and Bears a chance to tie for first place depending on who wins the game between the two teams to start off Thanksgiving Day.
If the Seahawks were to lose to the 49ers while the Packers beat the Rams, it would put Seattle one game back of the final wild card spot.
Considering that they don't play the Packers at any point between now and the end of the season, it is actually in their best interest for the Rams to win . Seattle and Los Angeles will face off twice in the final three weeks of the season, including Christmas Day at Lumen Field.
No matter what happens, this week should be extremely transformative in how the rest of the season shakes out, so the Seahawks should do their best to be on the right side of this week's result.
Kickoff between the Seahawks and 49ers is scheduled for Sunday at 1:25 p.m. PT inside Levi's Stadium in Santa Clara. Fans can watch the game on FOX or stream it on the FOX One app.

title: Why the Seahawks Should Sign Brandon Aiyuk (And Why They Shouldn't)
full_text:
The Seattle Seahawks and the rest of the National Football League are reacting to the news of former first-round pick Brandon Aiyuk being released by the San Francisco 49ers.
Aiyuk was once a very talented receiver, notching over 1,000 yards and over 700 yards in each of his first four seasons, including 1,342 in 2023. Since then, his career has gone downhill. In 2024, he signed a 4-year, $120 million extension with the 49ers , but tore his ACL and MCL after just 7 games with the team.
In 2025, his relationship grew sour with the organization. Even though he was healthy from his knee injuries, the organization voided his guaranteed money for not showing up to the facility. The dilemma carried into the 2026 season, right up until earlier this month, when he was reinstated by the league. Two weeks later, the Niners opted to release him. Now he's a free agent and can sign anywhere, including the Seahawks.
The Seahawks have a need to add a wide receiver, especially considering the rumored trade interest for the position ahead of the deadline. Aiyuk is someone who won't cost the Seahawks much, and he also has a connection to Seattle's coaching staff.
"Despite Seattle's flip-flopping between quarterbacks Sam Darnold and Drew Lock because of injuries, Smith-Njigba leads the league with a whopping 1,207 receiving yards and 10 touchdowns. He's on pace to set a new single-season receiving record and has accounted for over half of the Seahawks' receiving yards this year," Bleacher Report contributor Kristopher Knox wrote.
"Unfortunately, the Seahawks lack reliable depth behind Smith-Njigba. Cooper Kupp is the team's No. 2 receiver with just 272 yards. It's worth seeing if Ayiuk can boost the overall group, as he'd be a natural fit for the offense. Coordinator Brian Fleury spent seven seasons on San Francisco's staff before joining Seattle in 2025."
There is also very little risk in signing Aiyuk to even just the practice squad. At worst, it doesn't work out, and the Seahawks can cut ties pretty quickly, considering they have been open to giving players a second chance after questionable pasts with cornerback Terrion Arnold signing with the team ahead of him being arrested for alleged battery and kidnapping charges.
Simply put, it's a move that won't hurt the Seahawks, so they might as well try.
Aiyuk is a walking red flag who hasn't played in an NFL game in over two years. His last NFL appearance came on October 20, 2024, when he had two catches for 23 yards against the Kansas City Chiefs. His last touchdown was during the NFC Championship against the Detroit Lions in January 2024.
The Seahawks don't need Aiyuk to be the player that he once was, but the possibility of that player coming in if they sign him is what is appealing. However, the Seahawks can't count on contributions from nearly three years ago as a reason to sign someone in 2026. Seattle has to focus on the future, and it doesn't seem likely that Aiyuk would be a major contributor during the 2026 season.
While the idea of signing Aiyuk is trendy and flashy, especially for the Seahawks as they play the Niners this week , it isn't a concept that makes much sense in theory.
The Seahawks can improve their wide receiver room from within and don't need someone like Aiyuk coming in to shake things up. The Seahawks have a strong locker room culture, and it's hard to see how Aiyuk fits in that. Ultimately, there are pros to signing Aiyuk, but the cons outweigh them. The Seahawks should not consider this idea until maybe the offseason, when circumstances may change.

title: Sam Darnold Injury Update Has Seahawks Keeping 49ers in the Dark
full_text:
The Seattle Seahawks are putting an end to their bye week and getting back to work as they prepare for their biggest matchup of the season to date against the San Francisco 49ers.
The Seahawks are in the middle of a playoff push , but a win against the Niners would go a long way to helping them achieve their goals. The team hopes to get quarterback Sam Darnold back on the field this week after he missed the last two games due to quad and rib injuries. Seahawks head coach Mike Macdonald gave some insight into Darnold's health but did not confirm whether he would be able to play against the Niners.
"He was able to train a little bit here, do some rehab here, he also was able to get away. He's optimistic, but I think with today's practice cadence and speed of today, it's probably wise to wait to make any declarations until we get through Wednesday's practice," Macdonald said of Darnold's bye week via the team's website.
Before the Seahawks went on their bye, there was reason to believe Darnold would be able to return against the 49ers. Macdonald committed to Darnold being the team's starting quarterback, even after Drew Lock led the team to victory in the previous two games.
Lock was also dealing with an oblique injury leading up to the previous game against the Las Vegas Raiders, but he also appears to have gotten healthier during the bye week.
"I'd say the bye week was really helpful for Drew," Macdonald said via the team's website. "A really well-deserved chance for him to feel better, and that's going to help us moving forward. I think that's the case for several of our guys as well."
As long as he doesn't have any setbacks, it appears Darnold is going to start for the Seahawks against the Niners. He has been confirmed as the team's starter when he's healthy, and if he continues to progress in practice, the Seahawks should make him available.
The Seahawks might be trying to keep that under wraps for now, but revealing this information now before the Niners get into the meat of the practice week is counterproductive. Now, the Niners must prepare for both quarterbacks, which should give a slight advantage to the Seahawks in a very important game.

title: Seahawks Legacy Grows as 7 Former Players Advance in Hall of Fame Consideration
full_text:
The Seattle Seahawks are celebrating after seven of their former players moved forward in the Hall of Fame Selection Committee's voting process.
Seahawks Ring of Honor Member Shaun Alexander, Super Bowl XLVIII champions Marshawn Lynch , Richard Sherman and Earl Thomas III, and running backs Ricky Watters and Adrian Peterson along with defensive tackle Kevin Williams are moving forward in the process in hopes of being enshrined in August 2027.
Shaun Alexander is a regular fixture on the Hall of Fame ballot, largely due to his time with the Seahawks from 2000 to 2007. For five consecutive years, he ran for over 1,000 yards and was the 2005 league MVP with 1,880 rushing yards and 27 touchdowns as he led the Seahawks to Super Bowl XL.
Unfortunately for the Seahawks, they fell short in that matchup, and Alexander's career began to tumble downhill after that. Injuries compromised him in 2006 and 2007, and he closed out his career with the Washington Redskins in 2008, appearing in four games and notching just 24 rushing yards.
Marshawn Lynch ranks 30th all-time in rushing yards, with 10,413. In seven years with the Seahawks, he ran for 6,381 yards and 58 touchdowns, cementing his status as one of the greatest players in franchise history. He ran for at least 11 touchdowns in four consecutive seasons from 2011-14, and he was arguably the best running back in the league during that span.
Lynch is in his third year of eligibility, but there is reason to believe he is getting closer and closer to Canton.
Adrian Peterson is in his first year of eligibility and would be going into the Hall of Fame as a member of the Minnesota Vikings.
He appeared in just one game with the Seahawks during his career: his final matchup in 2021, a Week 13 game against the San Francisco 49ers. He ran for 16 yards and a touchdown, the last of his career, which made him the fifth-best running back in NFL history in terms of rushing yards.
Sherman played seven seasons with the Seahawks, making it to the Pro Bowl in four of those years, from 2013 to 2016. He notched 37 interceptions throughout his career, 32 of which were with the Seahawks. His eight interceptions in 2013 led the league as he helped the Seahawks win Super Bowl XLVIII.
Sherman continues to be a contributor to the game as an analyst for Thursday Night Football, further putting his stamp on the sport. It's his first year of eligibility, so it will be intriguing to see how far he goes in the process.
Thomas spent nine out of his 10 seasons in the league with the Seahawks, making it to the Pro Bowl six times throughout his career. He was arguably the best safety in football from 2011 to 2015, making the All-Pro team four times in that span.
To be that dominant at a position over several years warrants some consideration for the Hall of Fame. He hasn't made it in his first two chances for eligibility, but there's hope that the third time is the charm.
Watters capped off an 11-year career with four seasons in the Pacific Northwest. He ran for over 1,000 yards seven times in his career, including three times in Seattle in 1998, 1999 and 2000.
In his final NFL season in 2001, Watters suffered an injury that cut his season short after playing in just five games. He finished his career with 10,643 rushing yards, which ranks 25th all time.
Williams spent the majority of his career with the Minnesota Vikings from 2003 to 2013. He made six Pro Bowls during his 11 years in Minnesota and is viewed as one of the greatest players in Vikings franchise history.
Towards the end of his career, Williams signed with the Seahawks shortly after they won Super Bowl XLVIII. He joined the Legion of Boom defense and was on pace to win another Super Bowl, but they lost to the New England Patriots. Williams recorded three tackles during the game.

title: Who is Chase Lundt? Seahawks Sign New OL Ahead of 49ers Game
full_text:
The Seattle Seahawks are making a change to the roster ahead of their Week 12 contest against the San Francisco 49ers.
According to NFL insider Tom Pelissero, the team is signing Chase Lundt off of the Buffalo Bills practice squad. In a corresponding move, the team is waving rookie cornerback Avery Smith.
The Seahawks are signing OT Chase Lundt off the Bills practice squad, per source. To make room, Seattle is waiving CB Avery Smith.
Lundt, 26, is in his second NFL season after being selected as a sixth-round pick by the Bills in the 2025 NFL Draft out of UConn.
Lundt played in two games with the Bills during his rookie season but ended the year on injured reserve due to a knee injury. He was in training camp with the Bills, hoping to make their 53-man roster, but ultimately missed out. The Bills signed him to the practice squad, where he has been all season long.
During the preseason, Lundt picked up a fine of $5,868 for unsportsmanlike conduct in the fourth quarter against the Cleveland Browns. Since then, he hasn't had much of an impact on the field.
This is a strange move for the Seahawks because they have already signed veteran tackle Bobby Hart to the 53-man roster. Hart filled in for Charles Cross in the team's Week 10 matchup against the Las Vegas Raiders, but it looks like the team might need more reinforcements at the tackle spot. Lundt will likely serve as the team's backup tackle, and they could utilize him if the injuries continue to pile up.
The Seahawks opted to waive cornerback Avery Smith to make room for Lundt on the roster. Smith was acquired in a trade with the Los Angeles Chargers for a 2027 sixth-round pick, just before the 53-man roster deadline after training camp. Smith has appeared exclusively on special teams for the Seahawks, playing in 56 snaps across six games.
The Seahawks had high hopes for Smith going into the season, trading a draft pick for him, even though he went undrafted out of Toledo. It ultimately never panned out for him in Seattle.
There's a chance he could return to the practice squad at some point, but other teams, including the Chargers, could give him a look on the 53-man roster. He could get some playing time between now and the end of the year.

title: Biggest Concerns for Seahawks After 49ers' Dominating Week 11 Win
full_text:
The Seattle Seahawks (6-4) took the week off to rest up and build on the momentum from the two-game winning streak. The Seahawks are set to take on the best team in the league once again, this time against the San Francisco 49ers (9-1) on the road in Week 12. Seattle has a lot of ground to make up to get back into the playoff standings and a shot at the NFC West Divisional title.
​The 49ers are coming off a 35-10 home win on Sunday Night Football to the Minnesota Vikings, who came in with one of the league’s top defenses. Seattle looks to get revenge for its 32-29 Week 5 home loss to the 49ers in a game where the running game was non-existent and the Seahawks turned the ball over four times . There is hope for the Seahawks to pull off the upset, but there are some immediate concerns hovering over them heading into this game.
​In Week 5 against the Seahawks, 49ers quarterback Brock Purdy and wide receiver MIke Evan had a breakout performance. Evans caught 113 yards and a touchdown on seven receptions in the Week 5 matchup. The next highest pass-catcher was tight end George Kittle for 24 yards on five receptions. It was easily one of the worst games of cornerback Josh Jobe as a Seahawk , as he allowed seven receptions on eight targets for 112 yards and a touchdown.
​Both Purdy and Evans are coming off another explosive performance on Sunday versus the Vikings. There is a good chance they can do it again to the Seahawks in Week 12. The Seahawks need to take Evans seriously and lock him down with the help of a zone linebacker or a safety. ​
​The last time these two teams faced each other, the Seahawks’ run game was hanging on by a thread. The Seahawks had to turn to veteran and power back Emanuel Wilson, who lacks the explosiveness and the vision to be a reliable back. Wilson rushed for 61 yards on 20 carries and a touchdown to average 3.1 yards per carry. He hasn’t played since veteran Zach Charbonnet and rookie Jadarian Price returned from IR.
​Both Wilson and George Holani haven’t been the running backs the Seahawks needed. Both players fumbled, but Holani lost the ball in the end zone with 13 seconds left until halftime. Charbonnet and Price should give the Seahawks above peewee-level football and competent backs against a 49ers’ defensive line that was strong at stopping the run until Sunday night.
​The Seahawks are going into the week with some serious concerns with their injuries . The first good news is that defensive tackle Leonard Williams, quarterback Sam Darnold and left tackle Charles Cross were all practicing. Left guard Quenton Nelson and right tackle Abraham Lucas remain out until they recover. The Seahawks have to be cautious about Darnold’s quad and rib injury that limited him in the Week 8 dominating loss to the Chicago Bears.

title: Why the Seahawks Are Rooting for the Rams Against the Packers
full_text:
It’s never fun to root for a division rival in sports. I don’t particularly look forward to it either. But if our primary interest is to root for outcomes favorable to the Seattle Seahawks, and our ultimate desire is to make the playoffs , then the way forward is clear.
On a special edition of Wednesday Night Football, the Seahawks benefit from the Los Angeles Rams beating the Green Bay Packers. And here’s why.
For reasons we’ve already discussed here, the Seahawks are not really in play to win the division at this point. The only way forward is a wild card berth . Furthermore, while you always have to be prepared for unexpected things to happen, it seems very likely that this is going to come down to a three-way battle for one spot between the Seahawks, Packers, and Rams.
I just can’t foresee any scenario where the Chicago Bears, Minnesota Vikings, and Detroit Lions fall out. So, despite the trappings of being a division rival, at the moment the Packers are just as big of a foe for the Seahawks as the Rams. Both teams are 6-4, same as the Seahawks, so there’s no argument to be made from that angle either. We need something more.
Not to suggest that the Packers have everything clicking on all cylinders right now, but the Rams are in dire straits right now. Puka Nacua , Terrance Ferguson, Jaylen Watson, and Poona Ford are out for the season, Davante Adams is still on the mend, they’ve got interior offensive line problems, and they’re not playing especially well even when injuries are discounted.
Furthermore, the Rams have a remaining schedule that includes the Kansas City Chiefs and San Francisco 49ers. Even the Dallas Cowboys and Tampa Bay Buccaneers are not gimmes. More on that in a second, but the Packers still have games against the New Orleans Saints and Miami Dolphins. They have other tough games, but I know which schedule I’d rather have.
You’ll notice that I didn’t mention who the Rams play in their other two remaining games after tomorrow. Well, those two games are against the Seahawks, meaning Seattle has a lot of power over the Rams salvaging their season. Beat them twice, and it’s very unlikely there’ll be anything to worry about. Even if they somehow manage to win every other game.
The Seahawks don’t play the Packers, so they have no real ability to influence their playoff push. You’re stuck hoping that the Buffalo Bills, Chicago Bears, Detroit Lions, and (maybe) the Houston Texans can do you a few solids. Better to have Green Bay get hamstrung here. If the Seahawks can’t handle the Rams themselves later, then they don’t deserve it anyway.

title: Brock Purdy Misses First Week 12 Practice With New Injury
full_text:
The San Francisco 49ers held out five players in their first Week 12 practice against the Seattle Seahawks, including Brock Purdy.
At his press conference today, Kyle Shanahan revealed that Purdy is nursing an ankle sprain. He suffered the injury in the second quarter against the Minnesota Vikings.
Shanahan was asked if he thinks Purdy can participate in practice later this week, to which he responded, "We'll see." He also said it's possible Purdy misses the game against Seattle.
The bright side is that Purdy is considered day-to-day. He's not dealing with a high ankle sprain, which is encouraging news. His absence on Wednesday is to keep him from aggravating it.
If Purdy can't go, Mac Jones will start in his place against Seattle. The 49ers were kept afloat last year thanks to Jones. He's a perfect fit in the 49ers' offense.
It's for times like this that justify why the 49ers didn't trade Jones, or why they held such a high price on him for anyone who wanted to acquire him.
The 49ers would've been forced to go with Kurtis Rourke. They stand no chance of beating the Seahawks, or any team, for that matter, with Rourke at the helm.
However, the Seahawks are an opponent the 49ers need Purdy to beat. Purdy's ability to keep plays alive, his in-rhythm passing, and his rapport with Mike Evans are crucial.
I wouldn't be confident the 49ers can beat the Seahawks, who are coming off a Bye Week, with Jones, as solid as he is. Purdy will need to be active for Friday's practice to keep his availability alive.
As for the other four 49ers that missed practice: Dre Greenlaw (neck), Siran Neal  (knee/foot), Evans (Achilles), and Jordan Watkins (groin).
Greenlaw was inactive against the Vikings with a neck injury despite getting in a limited practice before game day. He's in a volatile situation, but Shanahan said the 49ers aren't concerned about his longevity this season.
They will certainly want him back for Seattle, especially since he didn't finish the game in Week 5. His tone-setting physicality is needed for this matchup.
As for Evans, his absence is a moot point. This is part of the load management for him, and rightfully so. They need to keep his Achilles as fresh as can be for game days.
All eyes will be on Purdy throughout the week.

title: Former 49ers WR Brandon Aiyuk Signs With a New Team
full_text:
After only a day as a free agent, former San Francisco 49ers wide receiver Brandon Aiyuk has found a new home.
Aiyuk is signing with the Washington Commanders to their practice squad, per ESPN's Adam Schefter . This was always bound to happen from the moment he cleared waivers on Tuesday.
He conducted himself on social media in the Summer as if he were already signed to them. Although there was a stretch when it seemed he would never join the Commanders.
Aiyuk and Jayden Daniels had gotten into a back-and-forth on social media, but they reportedly reconciled. The Commanders signing him proves that.
Otherwise, if there had still been a conflict, the Commanders would never have signed Aiyuk. Now, they are banking on the former All-Pro receiver to get up to speed and help their team make a playoff push.
Aside from the connection to Daniels, the Commanders needed a receiver. Terry McLaurin tore his patellar tendon against the 49ers on Monday Night Football in Week 6.
Stefon Diggs is their only viable receiver, with rookie Antonio Williams beginning to step it up. It made perfect sense for Aiyuk to join the Commanders.
It's better that he signs with them than with the Los Angeles Rams or the Seattle Seahawks. I had thought Aiyuk might've considered them for a petty incentive since they are the 49ers' divisional rival.
In any case, Aiyuk lands on a team, despite a bunch of 49ers fans believing he was never going to get picked up. The reality is, Aiyuk burning his bridge with the 49ers isn't that serious.
Yes, it's immature, weird, and annoying, but that's all social media. He wasn't toxic in the locker room or anything. It doesn't significantly detract from a team's interest in him.
So, of course, a team was going to give him a chance, especially a wide receiver-needy one like the Commanders. It's the NFL. If anyone has intriguing talent despite their baggage, they will be on a team.
He just couldn't be on the 49ers anymore. He took shots at them throughout the Summer. There's no coming back from that. In the end, the 49ers handled the Aiyuk situation perfectly.
This two and a half year weirdness is finally over. Both sides seem to be in a good spot. Although the 49ers are in a dramatically better spot with Mike Evans.

title: Why the 49ers Should Be Thankful Brock Purdy Is Their Franchise QB
full_text:
It's Thanksgiving for our American readers this week, so don't forget to be thankful that Brock Purdy is the franchise quarterback for the San Francisco 49ers.
There are many reasons for this. He's taken San Francisco to the NFC Championship Game, the Super Bowl and more recently the NFC Divisional Round. That's some effort.
But when looking beyond that, he's always played at a high level, and the level is even higher this year. The 49ers should be thankful that Purdy’s statistics reflect his effectiveness as a quarterback, as he's recorded 2,624 passing yards across 10 games, with a 71.0% completion rate and 23 touchdowns. His 118.2 passer rating speaks volumes.
But this points to a bigger reason to appreciate Purdy. Beyond his performances on game day, he embodies exactly what the 49ers, or any NFL franchise, would want in a quarterback.
His focus remains solely on football , with no distractions or unnecessary drama. Instead, he is constantly looking for ways to improve, whether through marginal adjustments or significant gains. This relentless desire to develop is undoubtedly one of his greatest qualities.
San Francisco lucked into a quarterback who was selected as the last pick of the draft and has established himself as an elite quarterback in the league. Yes, it helps that Kyle Shanahan of all people is his head coach, but all of Purdy's attitude and mentality towards the game is entirely down to him.
This mental aspect of the game is something that can't be taught, requiring natural composure, resilience and self-belief. His ability to handle pressure, learn, not be bothered by setbacks and maintain confidence separates him from many others.
The 49ers have their franchise quarterback for the years to come, and the Purdy era is well and truly underway. It's an exciting time to watch Purdy let it rip, whether he's connecting with future Hall of Famers like Mike Evans and Christian McCaffrey or making the most of opportunities with depth pieces such as Brandin Cooks and Jake Tonges.
But don't forget what he promised this offseason: he wants to win a Super Bowl for the city of San Francisco .
With the 49ers sitting at 9-1 and defeating opponents that mainstream media expected them to lose to, Purdy is certainly backing up those words. He's giving everything he has to deliver on that promise, and the city has every reason to believe in what he and this team are building.

title: Kyle Juszczyk Opens Up On When He Joined the 49ers Back in 2017
full_text:
San Francisco 49ers fullback Kyle Juszczyk is one of the oldest players on the roster, yet his decade-long stint in red and gold speaks volumes.
Juszczyk meets the criteria for what is considered a fan favorite . Not only has he been loyal to a franchise for over 10 years, but he has also earned this through his hard work, reliability, and consistent contributions to the team's success.
Juszczyk recalled joining the 49ers in free agency in 2017, the year Kyle Shanahan and John Lynch began their roles as head coach and general manager, respectively.
"What a different time. It felt like I was going to college again. I'd done my four years in Baltimore, which were like my college years, and now I was starting over again," said Juszczyk to NBC Sports Bay Area .
"It was a whole new regime, with a new head coach, new general manager and a whole new roster. I think we carried over about three players. It really was taking a chance and a risk by going to play with Kyle and trying to start something new and beautiful out here.
"Right away, meeting with Kyle and John, I knew these were the type of guys I wanted to go down that path with and start this journey alongside.
"It was really unique to be one of the very first players here and try to help lay the groundwork and foundation for what this organisation would look like for years to come."
Working with Shanahan for 10 years is something only he and George Kittle have achieved, giving him a core familiarity with how Shanahan galvanises the team to unleash their full potential. Juszczyk explained what makes Shanahan so special, highlighting his ability to motivate players, build strong relationships and bring out the best in everyone around him.
"What always resonated with me, probably because we're not that far apart in age, was his ability to connect with players on a youthful or friendship level, while also being an authority figure, a coach and a teacher," he added.
"He was always able to find that fine line between the two, and I think that's one of his greatest strengths as a coach."
And now Juszczyk will feature on the 49ers' 10-year wall, a historic moment for someone who arrived in his fifth season and then spent the next decade ( and maybe longer , though his contract expires this season) in San Francisco.

title: What the 49ers Can Expect from their Rookies in the Playoff Run
full_text:
The San Francisco 49ers have seven more games in the regular season and then a potential playoff run is coming. What are the expectations for the 2026 rookie draft class for the stretch run?
Stribling is supposed to return to practice around Week 14. So, he could return around Week 15 or 16. Even then, the room is now deep enough that he will likely just be a depth receiver.
Height is the 49ers fourth rusher. He is a depth option who is mostly a pass rusher. However, he ranks 10th in pass rush productivity and 11th in win rate amongst rookie edge rushers. The goal is for him to be more productive as a pass rusher.
Black has already exceeded expectations. However, the impact he has on McCaffrey has to remain. Black allows the 49ers to use McCaffrey in more beneficial ways without asking him to take on the tough carries.
Halton is out for the season due to an injury . Despite that, his rookie season will be viewed as a massive success due to the production he brought.
Willis is the backup left guard. Connor Colby has been rocky but not bad enough to warrant a benching. Still, he was the weak link on the line prior to the Colton McKivitz injury. There is a chance we see Willis at some point this year.
Injuries and the release of Jack Jones have pushed Prysock onto the field in a limited variety recently. The goal is for Prysock to continue to hold off Nate Hobbs for the third outside cornerback role. More than that, the 49ers trusting him in dime scenarios would help.
Dugger has done more than expected already. The goal for him is to be as good moving away from the football as he is when he is coming downhill towards the football. That is where Dugger is best.
The McKivitz injury opens the door for Cruz to play. However, all indications are that they want this year to be developmental.
The rookie UDFA has been a reliable option against the run. He just has to stay healthy and continue to hold down this role. The return of C.J. West could limit his snap counts down the stretch run.

title: The Teams that are Most Likely to Sign Former 49ers WR Brandon Aiyuk
full_text:
The unnecessary drama between Brandon Aiyuk and the San Francisco 49ers ended on Monday. Aiyuk has officially been cut and will look to sign with a new team. Let's explore the four teams he will likely sign with.
This is the team most likely to be interested in Aiyuk. He's been pining to join the Commanders all offseason, even making videos so far, even though he was already on the team.
There was a spat where Aiyuk and Jayden Daniels had a back-and-forth on social media in the Summer. But it seems it never went any deeper than that, as the two have reportedly mended fences .
Since there is no beef between them, signing Aiyuk is back on the table. With Terry McLaurin out for the season, the Commanders could use another receiver.
Stefon Diggs and rookie Antonio Williams aren't enough for them. Adding Aiyuk to form a trio could elevate their offense and give them a real shot at winning the NFC East after Week 11.
The most wide receiver depserate team in the league right now is the Los Angeles Rams. Star receiver Puka Nacua is most likely done for the season.
And there's no telling when Davante Adams will be back. Even if he returns in the next few weeks, the Rams can't have Adams as their only option. Aiyuk joining them makes perfect sense.
He goes into an offense that needs him and will funnel targets to him. That will boost his value in the offseason. Aiyuk also has the petty incentive of joining the 49ers' division rival. I'm sure that will be motivating.
Another team that Aiyuk can sign with for the petty incentive is the Seattle Seahawks. It won't be as good as the Rams since their quarterback and offense are whonky.
But he can still be a good fit since they need another receiver to complement Jaxon Smith-Njigba. Aiyuk would instantly be their No. 2 receiver, assuming he can come close to his level before his ACL tear.
Plus, offensive coordinator Brian Fleury knows him. He'll know how to get Aiyuk to fit and thrive in the offense. He should open things up as well.
Another desperate team that needs a wide receiver is the Las Vegas Raiders. They have no one noteworthy. Most of their targets go to their running backs and tight ends.
Rookie Fernando Mendoza needs a go-to receiver. Aiyuk can be that. Head coach Klint Kubiak is also familiar with Aiyuk from 2023, the year Aiyuk became an All-Pro.
If Aiyuk's social media behavior doesn't translate into the locker room, then he can help with Mendoza's development and provide a big boost to the Raiders' offense.

title: 49ers Could Face Tough Decision With Dominick Puni this Offseason
full_text:
One thing the San Francisco 49ers have not done under Kyle Shanahan and John Lynch is extend the interior offensive line. However, Dominick Puni is going to make their philosophy a lot tougher to stick to, according to Nick Wagoner of ESPN .
Wagoner called Puni the 49ers' clear extension candidate this offseason.
“Puni, who will be eligible for an extension for the first time this offseason, is the clear choice based on consistency and production,” wrote Wagoner.
The 49ers have not paid an interior lineman historically, but Puni might be the best option they have had so far. More than the 49ers' offensive line has a lot of long-term questions, making the team more apt to extend their guard to a big-money deal.
The 49ers have had a decent track record of letting linemen leave in free agency and then filling their hole without much issue.
They let Laken Tomlinson walk after 2021, and that might have been their biggest miss. He is still starting this year for the Green Bay Packers. Still, he has been on five teams since leaving San Francisco and has signed with four different teams in four different seasons after signing a big deal with the New York Jets.
Aaron Banks replaced Tomlinson in 2022. Now, Tomlinson has sent Banks to the bench two years into his big extension with the Packers. Green Bay regrets signing Banks.
The 49ers let Spencer Burford leave after starting at both guard spots. So far, Las Vegas has not been happy with his production. Tomlinson is the only potential miss, and even then the 49ers can say they felt good about letting him walk.
So, they could say that their philosophy has worked and they will stick to it. At the same time, Puni is the best interior lineman they have seen since Tomlinson, and he is likely a better option than him as well.
Puni is someone they drafted and developed. Beyond that, the age of Jake Brendel and Trent Williams, combined with the injury questions to Colton McKivitz, add instability to the line. They do not have a trusted left guard yet. So, Puni could be the one piece that the team builds around in the future.
Peter Skoronski set the market at $25M per year. With the way that Puni is playing, he will likely be approaching that number. Will the 49ers make the move?

title: 49ers Have 5 Options After Colton McKivitz Loss
full_text:
The San Francisco 49ers are going to be without right tackle Colton McKivitz for the rest of the season. This is going to present the team with a tough challenge in replacing him. What are the best options for the team?
This is the most likely option for the time being. Lowe stepped into the spot in Week 11 when McKivitz went down. The big issue is that he is 27 years old and in his fifth year in the NFL. He has 1,415 snaps at left tackle and 276 on the right side. That includes his snaps for the 49ers this year. It is a bit of a new spot for a player signed to be Trent Williams' insurance.
They have Isaac Alarcon and Foster Sarrell on the practice squad. However, Alarcon is from the international program and is still viewed as a bit raw. Sarrell is the name to know. He has 300 career snaps at right tackle, which is more than Lowe. He spent four years on the Los Angeles Chargers. The issue with Sarrell is he signed a month or so ago.
Pleasants has been on the IR with a knee injury. He is expected to be back at some point, but the team has not opened his window. Perhaps it is because they are light on designated-to-return spots, and they were unsure they needed Pleasants. Pleasants has been in the NFL since 2020 and has plenty of right tackle experience in training camp. He might end up being the best option through the playoffs.
Since the other options are not favorable, they could look to poach a player from another practice squad and add him to their roster. Wanya Morris, KT Leveston, Fred Johnson, Kiran Amegadjie, and Bobby Hart are options on practice squads and have NFL experience at right tackle. They could step into the extra roster spot.
There are also some free agents still around. It would be reminiscent of adding Eric Kendricks last year when Fred Warner went down. Names to consider include Kelvin Beachum, Cam Robinson, and Cornelius Lucas. All three could be added to the practice squad as well.

title: 4 Winners, 3 Losers From 49ers' Victory Against Vikings: Kyle Shanahan Evolves
full_text:
MEXICO CITY -- What a win for the San Francisco 49ers in Week 11 against the Minnesota Vikings.
It took a collective effort for them to look as great as they did, but a few players would've liked to have done better. That said, here are the four winners and three losers from the 49ers' victory against the Vikings.
Finally, Kyle Shanahan got the better of Brian Flores . His scheme had been an extremely challenging one for Shanahan to crack. But in this game, Shanahan evolved.
He stepped up and created the perfect game plan for his players to execute. Shanahan made Flores' defense look weak. Now, you have to wonder if he's the one who created the blueprint against Flores.
In case anyone forgot, Mike Evans has been the best free agent signing for the 49ers under Kyle Shanahan and John Lynch. He was phenomenal against the Vikings, tallying six catches on seven targets for 109 yards and a score.
Evans is the reason the 49ers have gotten over the hump against both the Seattle Seahawks and the Vikings. There's no such thing as an extremely difficult defense with Evans in the fold.
Every quarterback struggles against the Vikings' defense, especially Brock Purdy. He has more interceptions than touchdowns against them, with Flores at the helm.
But he finally got over the hump along with Shanahan. He picked the Vikings apart throughout the game. He was incredible in this game and helped take the lead as the MVP favorite.
After Evans' touchdown catch, Ji'Ayir Brown had the best play of the game with his pick-six. Brown floated in a zone in the middle of the field and baited Kirk Cousins to throw it.
Brown perfectly broke on the pass and intercepted Cousins to take it back for a touchdown. The game was over after that score. It was by far the best play of his career.
Colton McKivitz's 2026 season is over after he suffered a gruesome ankle fracture in the middle of the second quarter. It's similar to the injury Fred Warner had last year.
McKivitz was having the best season of his career. Who could've foreseen him ever becoming a cornerstone player in the 49ers' offense? He was abysmal a few seasons ago.
His loss cannot be overstated. It's not far off if the 49ers lose a star player like Trent Williams. Now that he's out, the 49ers will turn to Vederian Lowe, which will certainly limit their offense at times.
It looks like Demarcus Robinson may be the odd man out at wide receiver. He was a healthy scratch, which means he's being phased out of the offense. It's a bummer for him because he was playing well before he suffered a high ankle sprain and was placed on Injured Reserve.
He had a sizable role, but with Keenan Allen in the fold and Jordan Watkins stepping up in the last few games, there's no room for him in the offense any longer. He might not be seen again unless an injury occurs.
It's been a very quiet return to the 49ers for DeForest Buckner. He should've flashed a few times by now, but he has been silent. Even Nick Bosa stepped it up in this game.
No one should start being too concerned about Buckner. But if the 49ers' defense wants to be stronger, they'll need Buckner to be a major factor.

title: 49ers Should Be Thankful Jauan Jennings Rejected Trade to Return
full_text:
MEXICO CITY — Several San Francisco 49ers performed at an elite level in the sensational win over the Minnesota Vikings in Mexico City.
Brock Purdy was terrific, Mike Evans was a monster, and George Kittle is a bulldozer. They were a significant reason the 49ers won that game. But there were other players who played a key role as well.
That includes newly acquired receiver Keenan Allen. He may not have had the stats to prove how impactful he was, but make no mistake: he was solid. Allen fits the 49ers’ offense perfectly.
And with Jauan Jennings sharing the same field as them, the 49ers should be thankful he rejected a reunion. If he didn’t reject it, they wouldn’t have acquired Allen from the Colts.
The Vikings were open to trading Jennings to the 49ers, but Jennings wasn’t open to it. He was content, if not more than happy, with playing for the Vikings. It was strange.
“When we got on a FaceTime with J.J., it went well. It was awesome,” Kyle Shanahan said. “We talked about a lot of stuff, and he ended up saying that he was happy with where he was. It wasn't just like a definite no first, but he was like, ‘Man, Kyle, I'm pretty happy here and liking stuff.’”
Nevertheless, the 49ers moved on and honed in on Allen. He’s clearly a better player than Jennings, especially for what the 49ers need, which is a sharp route-running receiver.
Jennings has never been a good route runner. He’s been effective because he’s tough and is arguably a product of Shanahan. He was a free agent for over two months before the Vikings signed him.
No one wanted to add Jennings to their teams for two months. That tells you all you need to know about what every team thinks about him, including the Vikings. He’s decent, and nothing more.
Look at his performance against the 49ers. He barely did anything. If he hid his name on the back of his jersey, you would’ve thought he was a practice squad player the Vikings brought up.
He’s probably kicking himself, too. Had he accepted the trade, he would’ve been thriving. It would’ve worked with the 49ers, but Allen provides a much better boost to the offense than Jennings.
If there’s a crucial down they need to convert, they can depend on him. It doesn’t have to always be Mike Evans. There’s a pick of the litter for Purdy in those scenarios.
It worked out better for the 49ers, and it’s thanks to Jennings rejecting the reunion trade.

title: Positive Signs Emerge at Buccaneers’ Wednesday Practice
full_text:
The Tampa Bay Buccaneers are still trying to win the NFC South and make the playoffs. But for all intents and purposes, their Week 12 game on Monday Night Football is a playoff game already.
The Bucs face off against the Carolina Panthers on Monday Night Football. The Panthers have a two-game lead in the division at 5-5, while the Bucs sit at 3-7. If the Bucs beat the Panthers, they sweep Carolina and move within one game of the division — lose, and their playoff chances are almost certainly over three games back.
The Bucs will need everyone they can muster to help win that game. And the good news is that they could have some crucial players for that contest.
Cornerback Jacob Parrish was back at practice on Wednesday after leaving the game with a back injury on Sunday. Parrish was replaced by Benjamin Morrison, who was also injured in that game — Morrison was not at practice, but Parrish was.
Parrish has been one of the best corners in football this season, netting 14 passes defended and two interceptions so far this year. He's a crucial part of the defense, so having him will be important.
Perhaps the bigger story, however, is that wideout Jalen McMillan began his 21-day practice window. McMillan injured his knee in the preseason and had a procedure to rectify it, but he re-injured that knee during Tampa Bay's Week 2 game against the Cleveland Browns. He's been out since then, but now, he could return as soon as Monday.
McMillan isn't guaranteed to be back. But if he is, he'd be very valuable — Tampa Bay's wide receiver corps has been very lackluster so far this season. McMillan has been strong against man coverage and is a good separator when he plays, so the Bucs could really use his skill set as soon as possible.
The Bucs will play the Panthers at 8:15 p.m. on Monday. Whether or not Parrish or McMillan plays remains to be seen, but it's very encouraging to see them at practice.

title: Todd Bowles Says Buccaneers Are 'Running Out of Time'
full_text:
It might appear that the Tampa Bay Buccaneers 2026 season is a loss when you look at their 3-7 record, but they are still in the playoff mix as they sit just two games back of the NFC South lead with an all-important prime time matchup against the Carolina Panthers on deck.
There have been positives and negatives to take away from how the Bucs have performed this season, but head coach Todd Bowles doesn't believe that it's one thing — or even a couple — that is keeping this team from having a better record through 10 games.
“It’s few more than one or two things, but you know, the effort is not even a question,” Bowles said on Movin’ The Chains on SiriusXM NFL Radio . “The guys’ gonna fight every week. It’s just about cleaning up the little things and it’s the guy here or there and, you know, we’re running out of time... You know, you gotta correct those things.”
Bowles isn't wrong in his statement. The players have been fighting their tail off, but it has come to no avail.
However, it is worrisome that even Bowles is noticing that the Bucs haven't been able to take care of the little things, given the point of the season we are in.
But one thing is for sure — the Bucs are running out of time, and they must have a fire lit under them to finish the season strong if they hope to make the postseason.
Being just two games out of first place in the division should be motivation enough to go out there and get it right. On top of that, Tampa Bay has one of the easiest schedules remaining, with games against the Panthers, the Los Angeles Rams, the Los Angeles Chargers, the New Orleans Saints and the Atlanta Falcons, who have a combined winning percentage of just .333.
Things are lining up for the Bucs to win the majority of their remaining games, but they must make sure everything is buttoned up in order to do so.
They will have to battle injuries and somehow figure out how to improve their passing game if they hope to rip off a winning streak.
There is minimal room for error for this Bucs team, but they clearly are better than their record shows. If they want to hush the doubters and turn things around, they will need to get the little things right the rest of the way.

title: This Buccaneers Rookie is Turning Heads in 2026
full_text:
The Tampa Bay Buccaneers defense has been the strong suit of the team this season, the opposite of what we thought heading into the season.
The likes of Zyon McCollum and Jacob Parrish have been the big players on defense, but as a whole, the unit has exceeded expectations, becoming one of the top defenses in the league through the midway point of the season.
One player in particular has taken the bull by the horns — rookie linebacker Josiah Trotter.
Trotter has gone vastly unnoticed in his rookie season, mainly due to the Bucs underwhelming on the season. However, he is now starting to get the attention he rightfully deserves.
NFL analyst Ben Fennell took to X to point out how well Trotter has been playing and highlighting his natural instincts, particularly against the run.
Bucs Josiah Trotter is one of the most gifted rookie LBs I've ever seen/studied. 21 years old lol Dude has an insanely quick/confident trigger on his run reads... but isn't ever out of control - feels run action so so well. pic.twitter.com/ueuA95kTmj
Fennell's post made it's way around the web, and led to others chiming in on Trotter.
"Bucs are so bad he probably isn’t getting the attention he deserves, but he’s right up there behind Reese for DROY runner up imo," NFL analyst Jon Ledyard posted .
CBS Sports' JP Acosta also chimed in — "Real ones knew."
There were worries about Trotter's game when he was selected in the NFL Draft by the Bucs, but he has since quelled all worries since taking over as a full-time starter for the defense.
Trotter has been one of the best linebackers in the league against the run and has also shown great promise as a blitzer, creating pressure in the backfield. He has also improved drastically from his collegiate days when it comes to securing tackles, only being knocked for six missed tackles on the season.
He is also the only rookie defender to have a pick-six.
All signs point towards Trotter having a great career in the NFL with how he has performed so far, but he will have to improve in certain areas, most notably when it comes to coverage in space.
Trotter has been performing well up to the levels of Arvell Reese and Jacob Rodriguez, with Sonny Styles and Anthony Hill Jr. also performing above expectations early in their careers.
The 2025 linebacker class is looking like one of the best in quite some time, and for Trotter to be a part of that means the Bucs have a good one for years to come.

title: This Stat is a Huge Reason Why Baker Mayfield Has Been Struggling
full_text:
The Tampa Bay Buccaneers ' offense has struggled all year. The run game has been a success, but the passing game is among the league's worst and has hurt Tampa Bay week in and week out.
There are a lot of reasons why the offense is struggling. The play calling has been lackluster from offensive coordinator Zac Robinson, and the lack of talent in the wide receiving corps has made facilitating the passing game quite difficult. A big part of the equation, however, is quarterback Baker Mayfield.
Mayfield — whom the Bucs extended on a three-year, $55 million per year deal this offseason — has played very poor football dating back to the latter half of 2025. There are plenty of reasons for that, with injuries and decision-making being key factors, but there's another huge reason why he's struggled this year.
When Mayfield gets pressured by opposing defenses, he tends to get sacked. And that kills Tampa Bay's offense.
Sacks are not solely the fault of the offensive line. They certainly play a role, but sacks are just as much a quarterback stat as they are an offensive line stat — maybe even more so.
If the quarterback gets the ball out in good rhythm, he will naturally avoid sacks. That includes throwing it to receivers and throwing the football away, and obviously, it also accounts for mobility in the pocket and shedding rushers. Sacks are incredible swings in the defense's favor — the more a quarterback can avoid them of his own volition, the better the entire offense is.
Pressure-to-sack ratio, then, asks how often a quarterback is sacked when he is pressured. Good quarterbacks avoid getting sacked when pressured, either by getting the ball out or evading the defender. It's an important stat to gauge how long a quarterback holds the ball and how often he is costing the offense by going down.
Baker Mayfield, historically, is very, very bad at this. This year, he's 34th of 34 quarterbacks in pressure-to-sack ratio, getting sacked on 22 of his 80 pressured dropbacks, per SumerSports (27.5%). His best year since 2022 was 2025, when his 15.5% was ranked 16th of 45, but in that same time span, he's had seasons ranked 42nd of 46 (2024, 23.5%) and 44th of 47 (2022, 26.7%).
If you look cumulatively since 2022, he's ranked 63rd of 88 among quarterbacks with at least 100 dropbacks (20.5%). If you narrow that further and only go from quarterbacks with a comparable number of dropbacks to Mayfield — within 25% either way of his 2,509 dropbacks since 2022 — he's dead last, 19th of 19 quarterbacks.
This problem has plagued Mayfield his entire career. It's a big reason why he's been able to excel with strong coordinators, but when he's dealing with worse situations in coaching and the team's wide-receiving talent, he's unable to elevate the offense by himself as a player.
Perhaps the worst part of this equation is that Mayfield is 31 years old and is playing in his ninth NFL season. This aspect of the game gets less and less fixable every year he's in the league — this is simply who he is, and it's a major negative aspect of his game that anyone starting him has to deal with.
Right now, that team is the Bucs. They committed to Mayfield before the offseason with a three-year, $55 million extension, and after a better year on this front last year, he's regressed back to his usual ways.
Mayfield is currently dealing with a foot injury, which makes his mobility tougher than it would be when healthy. He moved around well in Detroit, but he still took a few sacks, including a strip sack and a crucial sack on fourth-and-12 to essentially end the game.
The Bucs play the Panthers on Monday night at 8:15. Mayfield will have to find ways to avoid going to the ground, because if he doesn't, this passing offense will continue to suffer.

title: Buccaneers Could Be in Serious Trouble After Two Players Need MRIs
full_text:
The Tampa Bay Buccaneers play arguably the most important game of the season on Monday night when they face off against the Carolina Panthers — a win keeps them alive in the NFC South, and a loss almost certainly ends their season.
Bad news for the Bucs? They might have a very, very thin secondary for that matchup.
Defensive back Jacob Parrish left the Detroit game early with a back injury, and he was replaced by cornerback Benjamin Morrison. Morrison gave up two touchdowns during the game, but he also injured his hamstring and had to leave as well.
Head coach Todd Bowles gave an update on both players on Monday, and it seems the injuries are at least worrisome enough that they need to get second looks.
Bowles confirmed on Monday that both Parrish and Morrison are getting MRIs to gauge the severity of their injuries.
"They're both getting MRIs today, so we'll have a better update later this afternoon," Bowles said.
The results of those MRIs won't be known until Wednesday, but the Bucs will have been hoping to get some good news. Parrish has been one of the best cornerbacks in football this year, and while Morrison struggled against Detroit, he provides good depth for the team in case of an emergency and has played well in spurts prior to that game this year.
So who's next if both aren't healthy? It's Kevin Knowles, who was brought in this offseason to play special teams. Behind him will have to be either Ayden Garnes, an undrafted free agent who made the team this offseason, or Josh Hayes, a veteran Bucs player who is still on injured reserve and in the middle of his 21-day practice window.
Either way, losing just one of Parrish or Morrison would be unfortunate, given the importance of the Panthers game next Monday. Parrish is the crucial player, though, so it will be interesting to see if he practices on Wednesday ahead of the Monday matchup.
The Bucs play the Panthers at 8:15 on Monday Night Football.

title: Buccaneers Play Most Important Game of Their Season Next Week
full_text:
The Tampa Bay Buccaneers are no strangers to pressure or to the prime-time lights. They've won their division close in a few of Todd Bowles' seasons as head coach, and they've had to play in prime time plenty.
On Monday, they'll face both. The Bucs play the division-leading Carolina Panthers at home on Monday Night Football, and it comes after Bowles and the Bucs lost their Week 11 game against the Detroit Lions to fall to 3-7 on the year.
The game is not just important. It's arguably the most important game the Bucs will play all year, and that's something the coaching staff knows as well.
With the Atlanta Falcons' bye week, the NFC South is now all caught up on games played. And after winning two games in a row, the Carolina Panther are two games out from the entire rest of the field.
Simply put, this game against the Panthers is the singular most-important game the Bucs will have all year. A win puts Tampa Bay within one game of the NFC South lead and gives them the ultimate tiebreaker over the Panthers — if Tampa Bay can keep it close for the rest of the year, they'll hold the match point over Carolina at season's end.
Lose, though? The Panthers will be three games out from Tampa Bay, and the two will have split the series, eliminating that tiebreaker for the Bucs. If the Panthers emerge victorious on Monday Night Football, Tampa Bay's season is as good as over at 3-8.
The Bucs know that. Bowles said as much on Monday.
"Yeah, [the players are] aware of it. They understand," Bowles said. "They know where we stand. It starts with us in this room, so we've got to correct everything and turn that thing around. We've got to do it a game at a time."
The Bucs' entire playoff hopes hinge on this game. And if Tampa Bay doesn't win it, any hope Bowles has of retaining his job as head coach is probably gone, too, so he'll really be looking to win this game on Monday night.
Things went well for the Bucs last time they played Carolina on the road. Will it be the case at home? If Tampa Bay wants to stay alive, it simply must be.

title: Bucs' Best Pass Rusher Played Just 19 Snaps, and Todd  Bowles' Explanation Is Concerning
full_text:
The Tampa Bay Buccaneers lost their game to the Detroit Lions 31-21 in a game that wasn't as close as the score makes it seem. The offense struggled mightily in all respects, and while the defense did their job for most of the game, some lapses allowed the Lions to put up some big points.
It wasn't all doom and gloom for the Bucs, though. One of their second-year players in his first NFL season, David Walker, has been shining, and he currently leads the team both in pressure rate and with sacks — he has five on the year.
Despite that, though, Walker isn't getting a lot of playing time. He only played 19 snaps on Sunday despite getting the team's only sack and making a big special teams play, and he was outsnapped by Yaya Diaby, Rueben Bain Jr. and Anthony Nelson on the day.
Head coach Todd Bowles was asked about why Walker's snap count was so low, and his answer was certainly an interesting one.
"Yeah, based off personnel yesterday, obviously, with that being more of a running team and putting bigger guys in there, we needed bigger guys on the field," Bowles said. "But David is a big part of everything we're doing. We love him to death, and he actually played the run well. He can get engulfed sometimes because of size, and you've got to be careful of that, but as he gets the system down more, he plays more and more. We love everything he's doing."
It is true that Walker is a bit smaller for an outside linebacker, and it's also true that Detroit has been very successful running behind running back Jahmyr Gibbs.
But Walker's pressure rate is arguably worth much more than potential size problems at the edge, and the Lions' passing offense excelled without much pressure coming it way — quarterback Jared Goff completed 71.4% of his passes for 279 yards and two touchdowns on the day, and Walker could have really been needed there.
There are also other smaller players who struggle against the run and who played much more than Walker did. Defensive tackle Calijah Kancey, who is notably undersized himself, played 30 snaps on the day — 52% of all defensive snaps.
Walker also had nine total pass reps on the day. Of those nine pass reps, he spent three of them dropping back in coverage, so those are more snaps where he isn't involved in pressuring the quarterback.
Walker has proved that, at least this season, he is the team's best pass rusher. He may be undersized, but he should be on the field far, far more often, and he's certainly done enough to prove it over these first 10 games in Tampa Bay.
The Bucs play the Carolina Panthers on Monday night. It will be interesting to see whether or not Walker gets more snaps.

title: Todd Bowles Gives Explanation For Crucial Part of Loss to Lions
full_text:
The Tampa Bay Buccaneers didn't just lose one way in their 31-21 defeat to the Detroit Lions. They faltered on offense, defense and in coaching, and that all created the environment to bring the Bucs down to 3-7.
There was one specific issue, however, that fans and pundits alike noticed across the game, and it cost the Bucs dearly throughout the entire contest.
The Bucs had two delay-of-game penalties because they were unable to get the play off in time. Additionally, multiple other plays saw the Bucs leave the huddle with 10 or less seconds remaining — this included a crucial 4th & 12, which resulted in a sack as the team hurried to get the play off.
This has been a problem all year, but it was particularly noticeable against the Lions on Sunday.
Head coach Todd Bowles spoke on Monday after the loss, and when asked about this specific issue, he didn't have a particularly thorough answer.
"It's a combination of everything," Bowles said Monday. "We gotta get out of the huddle quicker, we gotta get to the line quicker, we gotta put the play in quicker. It's a combination of everything."
That answer doesn't clear up the problem, and leads one to wonder what exactly has been happening with this issue across the season so far.
The most likely culprit is that offensive coordinator Zac Robinson is getting the play calls in too late, which causes the offensive operation to slow down. There is a chance that quarterback Baker Mayfield is having trouble relaying the play, but his job is generally to repeat what Robinson is saying through the headset. If the Buccaneers aren't getting to the line fast enough, as Bowles said, too, that could also be a personnel issue with players not knowing where to go once the huddle breaks.
No matter how it's spun, these are typically things that work themselves out in preseason and training camp, and the fact that the Bucs are struggling with this in Week 11 is a rough look.
If the play call comes in late, the offensive operation is completely thrown off. Mayfield needs time to read the defense and make protections, and if the clock is winding down, he has less time to do that. Additionally, pre-snap motion takes time to develop, and that aspect has to be rushed as well if the play isn't in quickly enough.
The Bucs play the Carolina Panthers on Monday Night Football. If they lose that game, their playoff hopes will be all but dashed, so they'll want to fix this issue — and many others — ahead of that game.

title: The Buccaneers' 2026 Season Isn't Dead Yet
full_text:
The Tampa Bay Buccaneers have dropped to 3-7 on the year following their 10-point loss to the Detroit Lions at Ford Field.
The Bucs made the game close for the majority of the contest before falling behind late and securing a touchdown to make it a 10-point game, but they ultimately weren't able to do enough through the full 60 minutes of the game to come away with a much-needed victory.
It was a gut punch for the team as they look to find some sort of rhythm to try and come back to take over the NFC South and make the playoffs.
However, even with the loss to the Lions, Tampa Bay isn't quite dead in the water just yet.
Following the Bucs' loss to the Lions, they currently have a 36% chance of making the playoffs, according to The Athletic . However, they have an important matchup on Monday Night Football in Week 12 against the Carolina Panthers that could have a major impact on their chances of reaching the postseason.
With a win and sweep of the Panthers on primetime, the Bucs' playoff chances would climb back up to 49%, but if they drop that game, their chances fall drastically to 10% — making it a must-win game.
The Panthers just narrowly avoided a loss to the Baltimore Ravens at home, but with the win, they extended their lead over the Bucs in the division to two games.
Fortunately for Tampa Bay, they seem to have the Panthers figured out this season, as they whalloped them 43-13 in Carolina in their first matchup back in Week 7 after a tremendous game from Bucky Irving and the running attack. So, they should have confidence that they can come out and do much of the same.
If the Bucs can come away with a victory to close the gap on the Panthers, their schedule lines up for them to continue increasing their odds of making the postseason with games against the Atlanta Falcons, Los Angeles Chargers, Baltimore Ravens, New Orleans Saints and Los Angeles Rams, who have a combined record of 17-34 (.333 winning percentage).
The Bucs are straddling the line at the midway point of the season and will need a strong finish to the season if they hope to salvage it. It won't be easy, as every team is pushing for its own goals to end the season, and the Bucs might have some issues with key players being hurt on the defensive side of the ball.
However, they find themselves still in the thick of things, and if they are able to overcome the injuries and the deficiencies on offense, they can make some noise down the home stretch and into the playoffs.

title: Overreactions From Buccaneers' Week 11 Loss to Lions
full_text:
The Tampa Bay Buccaneers dropped yet another game on Sunday, losing to the Detroit Lions on the road. That's their seventh loss of the year, and it puts them at 3-7 on the season.
Miraculously, the Bucs are two games out of the NFC South and have a chance to narrow the gap next Monday against the Carolina Panthers. But does that even matter any more with the game we just watched?
As always, we have no qualms overreacting to Week 11. Here are three of our overreactions after Tampa Bay's loss to the Lions:
The Tampa Bay Buccaneers trusted Baker Mayfield this offseason by giving him a three-year extension worth $55 million a year. They did this in hopes that he would return to the quarterback we saw in 2024 and the first half of 2025, as opposed to the quarterback we saw in the back half of 2025.
So far, all of his faults have remained, and they're very present. Mayfield struggles presnap to identify blitz patterns, and it has gotten him sacked on more than one occasion. When he drops back, he holds on to the ball far, far too long, and that also creates sacks — he was strip sacked on the first play of the game, and he finished the game with a staggering 36.4% pressure-to-sack ratio.
Per PFF, Baker Mayfield was under pressure on just 25 percent of his dropbacks - 11 dropbacks under pressure. He managed to throw the ball - just release the football from his hand - on only 4 of those dropbacks. 1 completion. Took 4 sacks for a pressure to sack rate of 36.4%
He didn't make any bad decisions with the football on Sunday as he has in the past, but we've seen that recently, too. And at his age — and with is tendency to play through injuries — this is likely who he is at this point.
All of those flaws will not get better at this point in his career. He may succeed with a better coordinator and better wideouts, but Baker Mayfield will always have these problems, and they will continue to lose the Bucs games in the future.
The Bucs have tolerated these problems, and they seem to be okay tolerating them more after extending him. But how long will that last?
If Bucky Irving isn't firing, this offense is moving nowhere.
Irving had exactly 100 yards from scrimmage on Sunday, but he generated explosives to get the ball downfield and he scored a touchdown for Tampa Bay as well to keep them in the game. He's an elite running back who can do it all, but if he's shut down, Tampa Bay has quite literally nothing else.
There are no receivers to dominate the game, nor can Mayfield play well enough to elevate the rest of the team. Teams will begin to hone in on Irving far more than they already have — he is the nexus of the entire paltry offense, and if that nexus is destroyed, Tampa Bay simply has nothing to offer.
The Bucs have to find a way to be more varied offensively. Irving has been carrying the team on his back, and he cannot do that every week.
There has been, and remains, talk about the NFC South. The Bucs are two games back from the Carolina Panthers as it stands, and if they beat the Panthers on Monday Night Football next week, they'll be just one game back and have a shot at the playoffs.
It wouldn't really matter if they made it, though. This offense is so anemic that any visitor in the first round would trample this team, and changes would almost certainly be made in the offseason. The Bucs would limp to the postseason at best, and everyone would know the resulting outcome.
Change will come in Tampa Bay, whether or not they make the playoffs. The iteration of the Buccaneers must die for a new, better team to be born, and that's abundantly clear now after Sunday's loss.
